# Changelog

## Unreleased

- VaR explorer: turning on **Include matured positions** no longer makes the scope tree disappear (the tree library refused the switch's own "of which matured" column); a screen's own tree measure with a label is accepted.

- **The module runtime** (2.9.11.i2 + i3, wave 1; new Maven module `drishti-module-runtime`,
  [KERNEL_AND_MODULES.md section 10.4](docs/architecture/KERNEL_AND_MODULES.md#104-one-module-runtime-library-two-hosts),
  [DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md section 1.5](docs/guides/DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md#15-the-module-runtime)): the `.dmod` package (pack, unpack, the
  `DMOD.MF` hash list), the `module.yaml` manifest with every field of the design, discovery from the module folders (`active.yaml` or the
  highest version), the checks V1–V8 refusing with plain words (manifest, hashes, no executables, no kernel API classes in a jar, API ranges,
  dependencies with cycles and missing ones, licence, claims against reserved names and other modules, data needs, memory budget), a class
  loader and a child Spring context per module, the live route table (200, 308, 404 off, 410 removed), the registry of contributions and
  the unload sequence in the design's order with a class-loader leak check. A library only: the kernel with no modules behaves as before.
- **Kernel-controlled data bindings** ([KERNEL_AND_MODULES.md](docs/architecture/KERNEL_AND_MODULES.md) section 5;
  [ADMIN_GUIDE.md](docs/guides/ADMIN_GUIDE.md) section 23; [DATA_LAKE_GUIDE.md](docs/guides/DATA_LAKE_GUIDE.md) section 6.1):
  `config/bindings.yaml` is the one home of which connectors serve each kind (one binding per kind, shared by every module: `read` in
  order, `union`, `live`, `write`, `demo`; never a host or a credential). A kind resolves by the site's binding, the distribution's default
  (a pack's route), a lake by convention (`AUTO`), the demo lake (`DEMO`), else `UNBOUND`; states `BOUND`, `AUTO`, `DEMO`, `STALE`,
  `MISMATCH`, `UNBOUND`, `COMPUTED`. An unbound required need switches off exactly the functions that use it, with the reason
  (`404 DRS-1026`). **Admin → Data bindings** (mock-up A): one row per kind, the unbound-required banner, propose and a second
  administrator's approve, reject or withdraw (four eyes, audited), applied without a restart; refusals `422 DRS-1029`.
  `GET /api/v1/admin/bindings`, Health's `bindings` block, `drishti.bindings.file`, `drishti.bindings.refresh-seconds`. **Upgrade:** a site
  without the file gets one at its next start from its connector files' `kinds:` lists (kept as `bindings.yaml.bak` when rewritten); the
  lists are still read this release, each listed as deprecated in Health, and removed in the next.
- **Contracts name no connector:** `storage:` (connector, plugin, path) is replaced by a connector-free `binding-hint:` (lake table,
  partitions, promoted columns, `computed: true`) in all 125 contracts, the schema, `drishti.py contract` and the generated contract, sample
  and pack-guide pages.
- **Kernel API 0.2:** `DrishtiModule`, `ModuleContext` (`Kinds`, `KindWriter`), `ModuleSettings`, `KindProvider`, `BindingState`,
  `AiToolProvider`, `@ModuleApi`; `ApprovalSource` moved into the kernel API (`com.ash.drishti.kernel.api.approvals`). Banking's
  `var-positions` and `var-system-baskets` are `KindProvider`s (computed kinds) instead of source plugins; banking declares its data needs.
- **Explain → Why it moved answers in about a second, not a minute** (the drill's failing Explain test, and "Why it moved looks broken"):
  opening the earlier date ran the load's maturity check, which read every trade (about 8,000) one document at a time because one union
  connector of `trade` (a source system with no table yet, such as Calypso in a lake without it) made the union's columns unreadable. A union
  member that holds nothing of the kind is now left out of the columnar read (it adds no rows; documents would find none there either).
  The drawer's From and To dates and their Explain button wrap inside the drawer instead of running off its edge.
- **Model editor: no inline styles** on the Relationships tab (the drawn paths' height and the DAX box take the editors' classes): the
  console's CSP no longer refuses six `style` attributes there.
- **Tests: one page-load budget of 10 s** (owner 2026-11-10): the page walk (`DRISHTI_PAGEWALK_BUDGET`, was 5 s) and Admin → Engines'
  budget test (was 1 s; the server's 400 ms per-engine probe is unchanged). **Page-load statistics:** every page a browser test opens is
  timed (`DRISHTI_PAGELOAD_LOG`, `drishti-console/tests/pageload_log.py`); the drill prints p95 and median per page, slowest first, and
  writes them to [BENCHMARK.md](docs/admin/BENCHMARK.md) section 18.2 (`tools/drillkit/pageloads.py`). Slow pages are reported, not failed.
- **VaR explorer: include matured items.** A switch beside Explain (`<drishti-switch>`, new in drishti-inputs) adds back the positions or trades,
  at the input's grain, that the load left out because they had matured. Off whenever the page opens; on, the tiles, a band with **Back to official**,
  the method strip, the tree's **of which matured** column and the path's CSV and JSON Lines say *includes N matured …*. The server computes it
  (`matured=true` on `/var/scope`, `/var/scope/path`, `/var/tree`), per request; the official record, captures and limit use never include them.
  A load keeps about 2.3 KB of heap a matured record (2.7 KB more in a mapped date's hot-file header), none beyond 1% of the date's records.
- **Fixes before the drill:** `lake build --format iceberg` sends a promoted id list (`TRADE_IDS`) as its JSON text, as the Delta writers store it, instead of
  refusing the rows as a bad vector; a Delta connector of the older form (a `root`, no lake file) that finds no tables no longer marks every search partial;
  `lake-name` is in the Delta connector's settings catalogue; the console's engine catalogue copy and sitemap list Data loads › Upload.
- **Duplicates folded, behaviour unchanged:** the loaders' line parsing (`LoadLine`), `ReferenceScanner`, `HttpFetcher` and `BoundedCache` in `drishti-common`; `MethodChoices` and `PlaygroundSheets` for FRTB and SIMM;
  `ForwardingTabularSource`, `ReadingFileIO`, `CallTally`; one real-IP rule (`drishti-console/core/hostrule.py`, loaded by `tools/hostaddr.py`), `tools/clitable.py`, the IAM policy steps in `deploy/aws/lib`, `shotlib.start_pack_servers`. Duplicated lines: Java 4523 to 3613, Python 612 to 318.
- **BI modelling depth (2.9.11.i1b):** many-to-many through a declared `bridges:` table (semi-join, never double-counted, totals from each level's own rows, row rules and masks inside the join); both-ways filtering per relationship with a per-measure override, and an ambiguous filter path refused at save with its reason and the fix; relationships named, `via:` per measure; Rachana `calc` grows `ignore = [table] | GROUP`, `keep` narrowing `ignore`, `by`/`having`, `filter =`; `sum_by`, `min_by`, `max_by` (the context transition, grain written; a measure that does not add is refused in `sum_by`); a calculated table may be related in the model that produces it (a self-read refused); a calculation group's template that cannot apply reads *not applicable, and why*; model-level measure functions; `tools/drishti.py bi dax` and the model editor's Tables tab convert common DAX to Rachana and name what they cannot; the Tables tab is table first (name and filter columns, bridges grid, paths drawn on a refusal or on request).

- **Copy-paste ratchet and code volume:** `tools/duplicates.py` runs PMD's copy-paste detector over Java, JavaScript and Python at 100 tokens (`tools/cpd/pom.xml`, outside the
  root build, nothing that ships); the gate fails if any language has more duplicated lines than `tools/cpd/baseline.txt`, which is only lowered. `tools/code_volume.py` writes lines of code per
  release from git into `docs/admin/BENCHMARK.md` section 22.
- **Kernel boundary (P1):** the core names no banking string (`tools/domain_strings_allowed.yaml` is empty); banking's words go through `DomainVocabulary` and the
  console's new plugin hooks (reserved words, console commands, phone pages, connector actions, the view toolbar slot). New `drishti-kernel-api` jar (kernel API 0.1) holds
  the SPIs of KERNEL_AND_MODULES section 2.3, with `ApiSurfaceTest` pinning the surface; `KernelWithoutModulesTest` boots the kernel with no banking on the class path.
- **Pivot rows show entity names** (desk, book, legal entity), as the VaR tree does, with the id in the tooltip. Figures are unchanged.
- **Screenshot scripts** t33, t37 and var follow the current pivot field pane, the Explain drawer and the basket sheet.
- **Mock-ups** for including matured items on the VaR explorer: `docs/lenses/mockups/var-matured/`.

### Operations

- **One home for start and stop scripts.** `bin/start-cluster`, `bin/stop-cluster` (`.sh`, `.ps1`, `.cmd`) and `bin/status --cluster FILE` start, stop and show a cluster on one machine from a cluster file (default `drishti-stack/stack.yaml`, the same format). `drishti-stack/` is configuration only. **`drishti-stack/start.sh`, `stop.sh` and `status.sh` are gone: run `bin/start-cluster.sh`, `bin/stop-cluster.sh` and `bin/status.sh --cluster drishti-stack/stack.yaml`.** The server jar copy moves to `data/stack/server.jar`. `deploy/bin/drishti-node` is now `bin/drishti-node`.
- **The file is the connector.** The file in `config/connectors/` is the only truth; every Admin save writes it, with its history and audit entry. At the first start of this release each node folds connector edits an earlier release kept in the content store into its own files; a file changed since then is kept and the edit is saved beside it as `<name>.yaml.content-store-<date>.bak`, logged and audited. The override marks, *Remove override* and its Health warning are gone. On a cluster a save applies to its node: Admin → Health warns when nodes' connector files differ.
- **Iceberg on `iceberg-core`, one engine.** Metadata, manifests, planning, commits and the REST client now come from Apache Iceberg's library with Drishti's `FileIO` and Parquet reader; no Hadoop at run time. `engine: library`, `DRISHTI_ICEBERG_ENGINE` and Azure/GCS/HDFS roots are gone (the setting is ignored, those roots are refused by name). Interop is proved both ways with every special partition character.
- **Python reads Delta only through Delta Kernel** (`tools/lake/deltaread.py`); delta-rs stays for writes.
- **Connector fixes from the data-standards review:** ActiveMQ no longer treats a Map/Object/Stream message as a delete; JDBC keeps integers beyond a long exact and reads binary as base64; Mongo reads Decimal128 NaN and Infinity; Kafka maps Avro decimal, date and timestamp logical types; an uncompressed Parquet page of the wrong size is an error; AWS keeps the SDK's checksums.


### Data loads

- **Admin → Data loads → Upload** (split view): upload a data file or pick one in the inbox folder, a searchable **Table** picker filled from the file name (kind, pack and connector shown read-only), the exact `.ready` live beside the form, checks against a sample (contract, key, grain and id, `DRS-5210`, hierarchy columns) as pass, warning or refused, and Push: data first, `.ready` last. A replace of a date that already holds rows names the systems and counts, offers a tar or append, and needs a tick. `drishti.py dataload ready`; `.ready` parsing from text and one writer; settings `drishti.dataload.upload.*`; **File drop** in drishti-inputs.
- A dropped file on the Inbox board, and **Build its .ready** on a Waiting card, open Upload filled in.

### VaR

- **What happened to matured items:** Explain's Inputs & lineage says how many records were excluded as matured (per source system and grain) and flags live positions holding trades past their maturity, with the list of positions; "could not be checked" when `TRADE_IDS` or the trade feed is missing. A flag only: no figure changes. Also on Admin → Health and in `provenance.matured`; `/api/v1/risk/var/scope/matured` pages the list.

### Docs

- **Plan:** i2 and i3 become one release with one drill after i1 + i1b, in four waves, with deploy built once, cluster-first.
- **Source file limit:** 2,000 lines (was 1,500); `SourceFileSizeTest`, the console's checks and the guides.
- **Roadmap:** every visual lives in Drishti Elements; a Drishti Elements Playground (live pages with editable data) closes the BI depth release.
- **Roadmap:** a BI depth release (2.9.11.i1b) after i1: many-to-many and both-ways relationships, Rachana filter-context control, a decomposition tree; the comparison with Power BI lists it as planned.
- **Drishti BI and Power BI compared** (`docs/strategy/BI_AND_POWER_BI.md`, opened from Help through the Reports guide): an area-by-area comparison with each Drishti item labelled built or planned, clustered compute behind BI, and Power BI facts checked against Microsoft's documentation.

### Test data

- The demo's VaR inputs are at **position grain** for all three systems (Endur, Calypso, Murex) on every date: `market-risk/scenario-pv` per position (a position under two limit letters is one record per letter, `<position>@<division>/<letter>`); the `pnl-vector` demo table is gone (86 tables). Calypso and Murex positions are valued in USD with `TRADE_CURRENCY` their trades' own, so VaR, ES and component VaR are unchanged. The engine keeps both grains; the generator keeps them by flag. A position named in the Trade column or as `TRD:` counts as the position; a trade inside one answers in words. `PF-LISTED` now reads the product types and `PF-PARTIAL-FILLS` holds whole positions (`Fungible positions under review`), the demo having no trade-level records.

- **Scenario PVs at position grain:** `data/testdata/position-grain/` holds 2026-09-30 for Endur, Calypso and Murex (`GRAIN: POSITION`, 7,984 positions, 509 scenarios), kept out of the demo lake.

## Unreleased

### BI depth: visuals

- **Decomposition tree** (`decomposition` report visual, `Decomposition` in drishti-tree): one measure split level by level, the next split the reader's choice, every figure the pivot engine's for that slice (`POST /api/v1/pivot/decompose`); a split of a non-additive measure says *Σ standalone − diversification = parent*, with component VaR beside standalone when the source has it.
- **Linked brushing:** drag across a line, area, histogram or scatter in a report to select a range; the other visuals filter to it, VaR recomputed; `selection: crossfilter` keeps one selection per visual. A selection has a clear button, and Esc clears it (`rangeBrush` in drishti-chart).
- **New visuals:** `sunburst`, `icicle` (drishti-tree's modes, in reports; an additive size, a colour read per node) and `calendar` (drishti-chart).
- **Playground page** of every element in the gallery (`/elements`, tab Playground page, side list of elements): the visual live, its data (an editable grid) and options below, its HTML and JavaScript editable and drawn in a sandboxed frame (no same origin, no network: no cookie, storage, page or `/api`); an error names its line, also when thrown inside a library, and keeps the last good drawing greyed; Reset. Every visual has its page, the server-side grids with a stand-in datasource and the risk presets with their libraries; a grid's page now carries its rows.
- **Every visual in a library:** a guard fails a screen, plugin or report script that draws by hand (existing cases are listed and only shrink).

### Testing and the drill

- **The page walk:** every drill opens every sitemap page and every top-bar link (the product's and each lens's) as the administrator over the cached VaR demo lake, and fails on an error answer, a server error page, a console error, an uncaught exception, an empty page or a page over 5 s; the key pages are measured at 1366 and 1920 px, dark and light (no sideways scroll, no overlapping controls, labels beside their controls, no oversized field groups). `test_page_walk_browser.py`; `DRISHTI_PAGEWALK_BASE` walks a running console.
- **`/admin` answers at once:** it opens the first Admin tab the person may open instead of the not-found page.
- **Found by the page walk:** Admin → Python workers threw on opening (its requests table carried the Approvals queue's `data-approvals` hook, so the queue's script started on it); the market-risk cube's limit bar drew with inline styles the Content Security Policy refused (now set through the CSSOM).
- **The VaR proof runs in seconds:** an in-process golden test covers all three demo dates, the 509 and 250 windows, USD and EUR, every hierarchy and all 28 system baskets. The server-against-server API comparison now runs for releases only.
- **`tools/drill.sh --affected [--base REF]`** runs only the Maven modules and test files a diff can reach, for builders; shared infrastructure, and anything it cannot place, selects more. `tools/docs/shots_affected.py` does the same for screenshots.
- **Cached demo lakes:** built once per hash of the test data, generators and lake code, and reused by every test stack and check.
- **A faster full drill:** the Java 25 lane compiles everything and runs only the tests of what a JDK version can change, the browser lane has more workers under a memory floor, and heavy jobs follow a memory budget instead of strict order. Before and after are in docs/admin/BENCHMARK.md.

### Fixes

- **Forms laid out again (query by form, the alert form, Admin filters):** a form in columns put each group in a narrow column and
  stretched every field box to its row's tallest, so labels floated far from their controls. In drishti-inputs a group now takes the row and
  lays its fields out in columns, a field's parts sit side by side with each label on its control, nothing is stretched, and a server-drawn
  form in a page's bar takes the room left (the Data loads filter was one narrow column). Browser tests measure it.
- **Engines menu removed: pages live in their lens/Views; switches in Admin → Engines.** The VaR, exposure, FRTB-SA and SIMM pages are
  under **Risk** (in the full product's bar and the Risk and Trading lenses), each shown while its engine runs and the person's role opens
  it (the engine catalogue's `opens:`, one rule for its pages and its command words); the Pivot stays under Views, uploads under Admin → Data loads.
- **Admin → Engines no longer waits on a slow answer:** the page asks the server's answers together, each within 0.8 s, and fills in a late
  one when it comes (or says the server is not answering).
- **Connectors no longer stuck on a frozen copy of their settings:** a pack reload could write a connector's generated file into the shared Admin overlay, where it then outranked the file for good, so a later move of the demo lake left those connectors on the old folder (`FUND` listed nothing). The server's own writes now go to the file, and an older generated file that names tables its lake lost follows its pack's template (`.bak` kept). Admin → Connectors marks a connector whose override is in force, shows what it changes against the file and offers Remove override; Health warns while a node has any. A search names a connector it cannot reach instead of showing an empty list, and a Delta connector with neither `lake:` nor `root:` is refused rather than reading the demo folder.
- **The demo's trade feed keeps step with its VaR records:** `lake demo` moves a trade's `MATURITY_DATE` with the other dates, so the matured-items check does not flag live trades on a moved demo. The committed test data is unchanged.
- **The demo's VaR no longer drifts with the day it is built:** `lake demo` moves `MATURITY_DATE` on dated records with the other dates, so moving the demo no longer matures records that are live on the test data's own date.
- **Demo-lake setups had no system baskets:** the seed follows `DRISHTI_DEMO_ENABLED`, which these setups turn off. `bin/start-server --demo`, the IntelliJ demo-lakes configuration, the deployment guide's settings and `drishti-stack` now set `DRISHTI_VAR_SYSTEM_BASKETS_SEED=true`.
- **IntelliJ run configurations:** the server configurations ran the `drishti-server` module, which has no domain modules on its class path since the split, so VAR and every banking function said *not installed*. They now run `drishti-app`, and *Drishti build server jar* builds it; a test keeps them so.

### Breaking

- **The `risk-hierarchy` kind is removed (HIER):** every VaR and exposure hierarchy is built by the server from the trades' **promoted
  columns**, as the pack's `hierarchies:` block (or `drishti.var.hierarchies`) configures them, any number of them: MGMT
  `DIVISION > DESK > TT_BOOK`, LEGAL `LEGAL_ENTITY > DESK > TT_BOOK` and LL `LIMIT_LETTER > DESK` in the market-risk pack, with the same
  node ids as before (`MGMT~DESK-RATES`, `LL~LL-0003/DESK-RATES`), so `var-limit` rows, captures, links and saved views keep working. A
  site that sent `risk-hierarchy` rows now puts the level columns on every `scenario-pv`, `pnl-vector` (and `exposure-path`) row,
  promotes them in the connector's `layout.<kind>.columns`, and configures `hierarchies:`; the setting `source:` is refused
  (`DRS-5213`), `drishti.var.kinds.hierarchy` and `drishti.ccr.exposure.kinds.hierarchy` are gone, and a data-load file of the kind is
  refused saying what replaces it. With no hierarchy configured the engines build no tree. A connector file written before still naming
  the kind is kept as it is, the kind listed as obsolete. The demo lake needs a rebuild (it holds a `risk-hierarchy` table no connector reads).
  [VAR_GUIDE.md section 15.14](docs/guides/VAR_GUIDE.md#1514-hierarchies-from-promoted-columns).
- **LEGAL's node ids are paths** (`ids: path` in the market-risk pack): `LEGAL~LE-NY`, `LEGAL~LE-NY/DESK-RATES`,
  `LEGAL~LE-NY/DESK-RATES/BOOK-RATES-1`, so a desk booking into two legal entities on a date is a node under each and never refuses the
  date (with `ids: leaf` it was `DRS-5213`). MGMT keeps leaf ids, LL is unchanged, `LE:LE-NY` still means the trades booked to the entity,
  and every VaR, ES, component and limit is as before (golden test). A site whose `var-limit` rows of LEGAL name desks or books by leaf id
  (`LEGAL~DESK-RATES`) re-keys them to the path; the demo's rows are re-keyed.
- **The `portfolio` kind is removed: the system baskets are managed in Drishti.** The bank's own baskets (`PORT:<id>`, the *System
  baskets* list) no longer come from a data feed: they are kept in the basket store beside people's baskets, under the system scope
  (`var/system-baskets/<ID>.json` in the content store; the one Drishti database later, with people's baskets), created, edited and
  retired in the basket sheet by the holders of the new permission `var:system-baskets`, and imported or exported as YAML
  (`drishti.py var baskets export [--scope system]`, `drishti.py var baskets import FILE [--apply]`). The demo's 28 (the same ids, names,
  owners and definitions) are the market-risk pack's seed (`seeds/system-baskets.yaml`), imported once into an empty system scope at the
  first start (`drishti.var.system-baskets.seed`, following `DRISHTI_DEMO_ENABLED`); their VaR, ES and limit use on the demo date, and
  `PORT PF-RATES-DESK`'s page, are unchanged (golden test). Gone: the contract, the test data (`data/testdata/market-risk/portfolio/`),
  the sample, the lake tables and connector kinds, the route and `drishti.var.kinds.portfolio`; a data-load file of the kind is refused
  saying what replaces it. `PORT <id> <GO>`, `PORT <GO>`, `PORT:<id>` and `VAR PORT <id>` work as before, served from the store (the kind
  `system-basket`, the `var-system-baskets` connector; an old `/v/portfolio/<id>` link opens it); an unknown id is `404 DRS-5221`. Limits
  stay `var-limit` rows (`HIERARCHY` `PORTFOLIO`). People's baskets (`BASKET:<owner>/<name>`) are unchanged. A site that loaded
  `portfolio` rows exports them as the import file once and imports it.
  [VAR_GUIDE.md section 5.7](docs/guides/VAR_GUIDE.md#57-system-baskets).

### Features

- **System baskets in the basket sheet:** a holder of `var:system-baskets` sees *System basket* under *Construct your basket* (a
  drishti-inputs form: id, name, description, owner, type with its node or rule, rolls up to, valid from and to): **Save system basket**
  (a basket from the sheet's positions and trades, a hierarchy from its node, a rule from its condition; the next version when it exists),
  **Retire**; *Edit a copy* on a system basket fills it. Checked on save (`422 DRS-5220`: an unknown node, a rule that does not read, a
  position the date does not hold, an id that exists); every change audited (`var-system-basket-create`, `-edit`, `-retire`, `-import`)
  and its owner told in their inbox. The server has no reusable four-eyes flow for content-store records, so audit and the owner's
  notice are the control. API: `/api/v1/risk/var/system-baskets` (list, one, save, retire, export, import).
- **Module permissions on roles:** a role carries `permissions` (today `var:system-baskets`): in configuration and packs
  (`permissions: [var:system-baskets]`), in Admin → Roles (*Permissions*) and the role API; kept as a power row (no schema change);
  every administrator holds them ([ACCESS_MODEL.md section 8](docs/architecture/ACCESS_MODEL.md#8-as-built-the-backend-phase-1-of-the-split)).

- **(Blank) nodes:** a row whose level column is empty, or whose source does not promote it, sits under a **(Blank)** node at that level,
  under its real parent, the deeper levels beneath it (Power BI's convention): never refused, never dropped, the totals complete. The
  name is `empty-label` per hierarchy, else `drishti.var.hierarchy.empty-label` (default `(Blank)`); the id is always a path (`~` for the
  empty value: `MGMT~DIV-MARKETS/~`), so two (Blank) desks never collide; no limit unless a `var-limit` row names it. The explorer shows
  it muted and in italics with a `?` (the trades without a value and the fix). A level column a source does not promote is a `DRS-5211`
  warning (provenance, Admin → Health *Hierarchy warnings*, the log), replacing the hierarchy skipped before; a column no source promotes
  and no pack names is a typo, refused (`DRS-5213`). `/api/v1/health`'s `hierarchiesSkipped` is now `hierarchyWarnings`.
- **Node names from the reference entities:** a node is named by its `desk`, `book` or `legal-entity` record (the level's name is the
  kind), else by its value.
- **`var-limit`:** a row of a node its hierarchy can build but with no positions on the date shows as *limit, no positions*
  (`limitsNoPositions` of the tree); one its hierarchy cannot build is said with the reason (`DRS-5212`). The exposure paths carry
  `DIVISION`.

### Pivot: the fields made manageable

- **The View picker in front of one compact line is how every pivot opens** (Views → Pivot, the MR and CCR cubes, the Pivot under a page's
  table and above search results; the mock-ups and their build checklist: [LENSES.md section 6.4.4](docs/architecture/LENSES.md#644-pivot-fields-the-view-picker-the-compact-line-and-the-panes)).
  No field list on screen: Rows · Columns · Filters · Values on one line, a picker behind each (`R`, `C`, `V`, `F`), a hierarchy as one chip
  (`⋔ MGMT ▾ Desk › Book`) with a level stepper (`Alt+↑`, `Alt+↓`), the lit measure toggles as the values; the grid gets the screen.
  **Customize ›** (`\`) opens the Fields and Build panes (Power BI's), which close to a rail; the BI designer keeps its panes. A preset, a
  Sutra's `pivot: { mode: … }` or the address (`mode=views|compact|panes`) chooses; old addresses and saved views open as they were.
- **Views:** ready-made layouts per preset (`views:` in `pivot-presets.yaml`; the MR cube's six: by risk class × desk, desk, book, limit
  letter, top contributors, trades in my scope; keys `1`–`9`), *My views*, *Shared with me* and **Save view as…** Personal or Shared

  checked by the server); a rate is never summed and a text is counted (shown off with the reason); VaR and ES say they are computed per

### Added

- **`bin/`: one home for starting and stopping Drishti, on Windows, Linux and macOS.** Seven scripts, `start-server`, `stop-server`,
  `start-console`, `stop-console`, `status`, `start-all` and `stop-all`, each as a `.sh` (Linux and macOS: bash 3.2 and the BSD userland),
  a `.ps1` (Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7) and a `.cmd` that runs the `.ps1` from `cmd` or a double-click, with the same options
  and `--help`.
  - `start-server` finds Java 21+ (`DRISHTI_JAVA_HOME`, `JAVA_HOME`, the `PATH`, `java_home` on macOS), the newest server jar, sets the
    temporary folder, the native memory and diagnostic flags and the logs under the data folder, waits for the health URL and prints the
    LAN address; `--background`, `--port`, `--heap`, `--env-file` (secrets off the command line, values never printed), `--demo` (the
    development secrets, marked not for production).
  - **Clusters:** `--node <name>` with `--node-dir` (the node's Drishti\*net folder, made when missing), `--node-data` (its own data
    folder; two nodes on one folder are refused), `--seed <host:port>` and `--advertise` (the machine's real LAN address by default;
    loopback and wildcard addresses refused). Pid, log and temporary folder are per node, so several nodes run on one machine.
  - `start-console --server` takes one server or a cluster's entry nodes (comma-separated): the console uses the first that answers
    and learns the other members.
  - The stops act on the pid file only (never by name): graceful, then forced after a timeout; a stale pid file is removed and said so;
    `--node`, `--all-nodes`. `status` shows pid, state, port, health and LAN address.

### Changed

  is `--server`, `-Stop` calls `stop-server`). The pid file moved from `data/server.pid` to `data/run/server.pid`.

### Drishti Elements, and one way for each job (2.9.11.e)

- **Security: one name, one definition across the domain folders.** A table or model defined twice (`config/tables/bi/` and
  `config/tables/banking/`, or a file and a stored item), a BI file of one id in two folders (`reports/` and `reports/banking/`, the same
  for notebooks, Python items, tables and models) and a pack in two domain folders of one packs root are **refused, both**: neither is
  read, never one picked (the server had used the last one read, so a report could read a second `trades-basic` model without the row
  rules and masks of the first). The table layer's check says `DRS-9610 ... is defined twice: <file> and <file>; neither is read`; the
  BI folder lists each refused file under Health › BI problems and Admin › Artifacts; a pack named twice stops the server at start
  (and keeps its last good version on a hot reload, with the problem on Health) naming both folders. The Python resolver
  (`core/pack_paths.py`) refuses the same, and the shipped packs are checked to hold each name once.
- **Fixed: a grid cell edited while its row is out of view opens over its cell** (drishti-grid): the editor started before the rows
  were drawn at the new scroll, stayed hidden, and its focus scrolled the grid back, so the cell never came into view (Build › Tables &
  models, *+ Computed column* on a table of many columns opened an editor nobody could see); the rows in view are drawn first.
- **Fixed: a Form's Select with an `aria-label` hook names its combobox** (drishti-inputs): the label went onto the `<drishti-select>`
  element as well, so one field was two labelled things (the Build workbench's enumerated options, the BI tile pickers).
- **Fixed: an embedded live report follows its live tables again**: the server describes a report's model by its `datasets` (each with
  its mode) since the table layer, and the frozen 1.x `<drishti-report>` reads `dataset.tables`, so it took every report for static; the
  embed route names the model's datasets as `tables` for the frozen element (the console viewer follows each visual's standing query).
- **Fixed: the World lens's map landing draws the US sectors and the largest funds** (the capital-markets switch was set only on the
  explorer landing), and on a phone the known-at field takes a row of its own under the business date (its date and time were 19 px wide)
  and a table's rows-per-page Select is finger-sized (its control stayed 24 px tall).
- **The terminal's query form on the one server-drawn form** ([ELEMENTS.md section 8.2](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md#82-as-built-drishti-inputs-drishti-data-and-the-grids-cell-editing)):
  `core/forms.py`'s `form_host` sends the criteria through `core/form_kit.host` (`data-di-form` + `data-schema`), and `drishti_form.js`
  finds the `Form` with `formOf(host, {widgets})`; its own `new Form` path and the `data-qf-schema` attribute are deleted. `formOf`
  called with `widgets` on a `Form` already drawn draws its fields again with them, the values kept. The page's GET address and every
  criterion's name (`op.`, `v.`, `v2.`, `cs.<path>`) are unchanged.
- **The Admin forms, part 2, on drishti-inputs' `Form`** ([ELEMENTS.md section 12.3, sixth pass](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md#123-every-designer-editor-and-authoring-tool-on-the-kit-the-standing-rule-of-31)):
  Users, Roles, Access, Audit, Configuration (search and *Propose a change*), Connectors (the list's filters and the connector editor),
  Artifacts (filters, a BI file), Packs (the archive, the signature, the breaking-change box), a pack's *Load a data file*, Lakes,
  Drishti*net (seed, map filter, *Explain a request*, nodes per role, this node's tags, the file's YAML), Capacity (the plan's inputs, the
  growth sliders, the workbook's inputs), Health's busy override, Engines, Edits, Compute, Inbox, Caches, the uninstall dialogs and the
  banking module's Scopes draw no control of their own: the server builds each form's schema (`core/admin_forms.py`, `core/form_kit.py`,
  new; a template calls `admin_form(...)`), every field keeps its old name and data attributes, so routes, scripts and tests read the
  same names. **Fixed with it**: an unticked box in a JSON body is `false`, never missing (a role's powers, a user's *Enabled*, Lakes'
  *Bind* and *Tell*); a new user without a first password, a role or user name that does not fit, an Edits switch without a reason are

  page form's submit while a field has a problem), the field types `file` and `range`, a text field's `password` and `search`

- **Selects on drishti-inputs' `Select`** ([ELEMENTS.md section 8.2](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md#82-as-built-drishti-inputs-drishti-data-and-the-grids-cell-editing)):
  a `Form`'s select field (every form on `Form`: the Admin screens, the alert form, the query form, BI's panes, the editors) is a

  condition and date preset (drishti-inputs' panels: one opened from inside another keeps it open). **A guard**
  (`tests/test_native_select_guard.py`) fails on a raw `<select>` in a console page, script, library source or plugin page; its allow-list (69 files:
  the libraries without drishti-inputs, the renderer's harness, the gallery, the screens of the native-select sweep) only shrinks.
- **The native-select sweep, first half: the libraries and BI on `Select`** ([ELEMENTS.md section 8.2](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md#82-as-built-drishti-inputs-drishti-data-and-the-grids-cell-editing)):
  drishti-grid (a table's rows per page, the phone pivot's measure), drishti-chart (the studio's options, the map's metric), drishti-graph's
  group, size and colour pickers and drishti-tree's size-by and move-to draw drishti-inputs' `Select`, so those four libraries require

  `value`, `disabled` and `focus()` reach the control, and a named one's field reads and sets it (`form.elements.<name>.value`). The guard's
  allow-list: 69 files and 149 selects → 39 and 78 (and to none with the screens below). Names, `data-*` hooks and the saved YAML are unchanged.
- **The screens outside BI on `Select`** ([ELEMENTS.md section 15](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md#15-build-checklist)): every native

  cards, workspaces, the column filter, the controls' dropdown, the table and model editors, the field history, the pack screens, the
  record forms' enum and lookup cells (it opens on the value; a pick saves), the refresh interval, the table chart, and the banking
  plugin's trading landing, market-risk ladder and scenario matrix is drishti-inputs' `<drishti-select>`: search on a long list,

  the theme as YAML is BI Studio's YAML panel (Visual, YAML, Both), both ways: an edit is read by the server after a pause, a line that does
  not read is marked and the theme keeps its last good version; the hand-made YAML writer and the text area are deleted (`dumpYaml` writes it).
- **The Phone and Tablet orders on the kit's `LayoutModel`** ([ELEMENTS.md section 8.9](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md#89-as-built-drishti-designer-the-designer-kit)):

  row's `data-node`), follows a `Selection` both ways, and moves by drag (before, after, inside) or Alt+arrows with the host's `canDrop`

- **The workbench's menus on drishti-inputs** (Add panel, Bind field, File, Ship, the command palette, a dropped field's kinds): `Listbox`

- **Fixed: an unchecked "Active" saved as active.** The alert form, a scheduled report and a subscription read a missing `enabled` field

- **The alert form on drishti-inputs' `Form`** ([ELEMENTS.md section 12.3, fifth pass](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md#123-every-designer-editor-and-authoring-tool-on-the-kit-the-standing-rule-of-31)):

- **No bespoke UI, the editors' rows on drishti-grid editing** ([ELEMENTS.md section 12.3, fifth pass](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md#123-every-designer-editor-and-authoring-tool-on-the-kit-the-standing-rule-of-31)):

- **drishti-graph and drishti-tree, two new Drishti Elements libraries** (ELEMENTS.md section 8.8; the owner's picks: g5 option A and
  g6 option B the defaults, the other options modes of the same components). **drishti-graph**: networks cyclic or acyclic on a canvas
  for thousands of nodes (5,000 nodes and 20,000 edges: the force layout 2.2 to 2.7 s in Node, settling on screen in 4.7 s with the
  page responsive, a full frame 11 to 17 ms); force (seeded Barnes-Hut), layered, radial, circular, grouped and preset layouts,
  animated unless motion is reduced; zoom, pan, minimap, fit; neighbours expanded on demand through a host's hook; the shortest path;
  groups folded by an attribute (a non-additive measure never summed); filters by type; size and colour by a measure with the legend;
  edge width by weight; pin, multi-select and the lasso; Explain; linked selection with drishti-grid through drishti-core's bus;
  export PNG, SVG, CSV and JSON; the arrow keys between neighbours and the adjacency table (▦) as the text alternative; live changes
  throttled; three modes: `inspector` (default), `table` (the Nodes, Edges and Path tables linked both ways) and `terminal` (the
  `GRAPH>` command line with Tab completion, history and function keys); the lineage preset (sources → tables → models → reports, status
  badges). **drishti-tree**: hierarchies as the indented tree grid on drishti-grid's tree data (default), an org chart, a sunburst and an
  icicle (additive sizes only); search with breadcrumbs; non-additive measures (◆) asked of the server and never summed, the
  children's sum beside; Explain; re-parenting in an edit mode that proposes the moves as one four-eyes proposal. drishti-risk's presets:
  the counterparty structure graph and the VaR hierarchy tree. Gallery demos for both (every mode), fixture harnesses, Node and browser
  tests.
- **The one-off graphs moved onto drishti-graph, the old code deleted**: the view's graph panel (the counterparty hierarchy, F3 HIER;
  the console, the client renderer and the embed draw it; drishti-chart's ECharts graph option is gone), the **data map** (DATAMAP: the
  domains as frames of the grouped layout, **Layered** the lineage DAG of the joins, the layout in the address; the drawn SVG, its CSS
  and the server's layout code are gone) and Build › New pack's graph of kinds and links. The same nodes and edges as before (the data
  map's are checked against the server's model in the browser test). linkGrid, the selection event and the shared colour theme
  (`visualTheme`) moved from drishti-chart into drishti-core, where every component uses them.

  every figure the server's (nothing summed in the browser), a book's positions and a position's trades asked when the row opens
  (*computing…* until then), *+ basket* and the direction chip, the current scope marked, what is open and the column widths kept;
  the explorer's own riskGrid tree code is deleted. drishti-tree gains generic hooks for it: `chrome: false` (the view alone),
  `grid` (the node's cell, a measure's `column`, more columns, a row's class and data, widths given and kept, `fitRows`), lazy
  children (`loadChildren`, `lazyText`, `HierarchyModel.addChildren`) and a quiet `select`.
- **The other hand-built trees are drishti-tree too** (ELEMENTS.md section 8.8, no bespoke UI on any screen): the **Drishti Risk

  desks, a node's name the link to the VaR explorer at that scope); the **exposure explorer's scope tree** (the bank, legal entities,
  counterparties, netting sets and a set's trades asked when it opens; peak PFE not additive, every figure the server's; a click opens

  their ancestors, masked values as sent). Deleted: `rl-tree`'s rows, `xx-tree`'s rows, twisties and open-state bookkeeping, the raw
  viewer's own tree and their CSS. **A tree's filter is in the address again** (`?tf.<panel id>=<words>`; treeTables' `address` hook):
  a reload or a shared link shows the same rows, as before the move. **drishti-grid**: rows that open and close (a tree, groups, a
  pivot) are 44 px high on a touch screen (a phone, a tablet; inside the row line), with a 44 px twisty.

- **The Build workbench's shape tree is drishti-tree** (no bespoke UI in an authoring tool): a Design's Shape section draws its fields
  with drishti-tree's new **outline** (`TreeOutline`, `drishti_tree-outline.js`: a `Tree` in grid mode without chrome for a narrow
  panel; marks after a node's label (type, role badge with its reason, conflict, presence, examples), a row class, a filter that keeps
  the matches and the nodes above them, a tree's keys on the rows (Home/End, Right/Left to open, close and go up, Enter or Space to
  open a branch or show a leaf's detail), the detail under the tree with the host's buttons, the host's keys first; `outlineFilter`
  and `outlineKey` pure and tested in Node). Same nodes, counts, conflicts and rare fields, filter, Expand and Collapse, Enter for a
  field's reason, `S` and `B`, a field dragged onto the canvas. The hand-built `role=tree` list and its CSS (`.bs-tree`, `.bs-row`,
  `.bs-detail` and the rest) are deleted; `window.Drishti.ShapeTree` keeps its `show(report)` and gains `fieldAt(element)`.
- **Tables with children are drishti-tree** (RACHANA_REFERENCE.md › Tree rows in the browser): a Sutra table or ladder with
  `children:` is drawn by drishti-tree's new **table tree** (`treeTables`, `TreePanel`, `drishti_tree-panel.js`) in the console, the
  client renderer and the embed (`elements-tree`), from the server's rows (texts, tones, links; nothing summed): the **tree grid** on
  drishti-grid's tree data (+/−, a filter keeping the ancestors of a match, the grid's column menus) or the **org chart** of the same
  rows, a tree that is one chain opening as it; mode, open rows and filter survive a live patch; the server's table stays hidden for
  print and pages without scripts. Deleted: the console's hand-built toggles, filter and funnels on trees (`drishti_tree-rows.js`
  part 1), drishti-grid's `tree` and `treeVisibility`, `.tr-q`, `.tr-bar`, `.tr-count`. The renderer requires drishti-tree; the embed v2
  serves drishti-graph's and drishti-tree's modules. **GLEIF**: an entity's parents chain (`PAR`) is now a tree from the ultimate parent
  down to the entity (highlighted), opening as an org chart; a group's tree (`TREE`) opens as the tree grid with the org chart a click away.

- **No bespoke UI: the BI designer's own panes** ([ELEMENTS.md section 12.3](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md#123-every-designer-editor-and-authoring-tool-on-the-kit-the-standing-rule-of-31)):

  `dock` and `collapsible` parts, link, toggle and choice actions with the host's `attrs`, `setLabel`, `showAction`, objects with an

  headers); the audit (`pivot.explain`) moved to the explainer; `drishti.py pivot explain` and tutorial 37 use the one Explain.

  scenario and in the reported one); the FRTB screen's Total column is back, the server's figure (never summed in the browser).

  (`TemplateStamp.keepPristine`), so it still counts as unedited and keeps following its pack's template; an edited one stays edited.
- **drishti-insight 0.1.0** (library 6, in the Elements manifest, so packing and the gallery include it): the one Explain, the one

  (deleted), and the workbook export (`workbookLinks`, `exportWorkbook`); `base.html` loads the bundle once (Explain only for someone
  signed in). Tests: `tests/elements/insight.test.mjs`; the keymap and Explain tests read the library's sources.
- **The Elements 1.x npm package retired**: `tools/elements_package.py`, `core/element_package.py` and `web/elements/package/` deleted,

  (and the renderer 1.2.0 files as they were); the per-library packages replace the package.
- **`tools/drishti.py` split**: its command tree is `tools/drishti_parser.py` (`build_parser(h)`), the commands stay in `drishti.py`
  (1,495 → about 1,135 lines).
- **drishti-grid**: the row model is chosen in `drishti_grid-model-base.js` (`rowModelFor`), keeping `drishti_grid.js` under the
  modules' 530-line cap.
- **Tests**: `test_docs_rot.py` knows the figures capture's test-only variables (`DRISHTI_FIGURES_OUT`, `DRISHTI_FIGURES_BASELINE`).

- **drishti-grid: tree data on server-side rows** ([ELEMENTS.md section 8](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md), the AG Grid migration
  guide): `treeData` with a `datasource`, `isServerSideGroup(row)` and `getServerSideGroupKey(row)` — the server answers the tree one
  level at a time (`treeData: true` in the block request, `groupKeys` the path of the node whose children are asked); a node is a row
  with the server's figures, a closed node reopens from its cached blocks, a sort or filter asks every open level again,
  `refresh({keys})` asks one node's level, `groupDefaultExpanded` and expand/collapse all open levels as they load, the body draws a
  `treegrid` with `aria-level` and `aria-expanded`. `memoryDatasource` answers tree requests with `getDataPath`. The AG Grid-style
  adapter maps `treeData` with `rowModelType: 'serverSide'`, `isServerSideGroup` and `getServerSideGroupKey` (no longer reported as
  unsupported); the adapter harness's `?mode=server-tree` and the gallery's "Server-side tree data" demo show it. Tests:
  `tests/elements/tree.test.mjs`, `ag-adapter.test.mjs`, `test_elements_grid_browser.py`.
- **A single-choice select in drishti-inputs, and the VaR and exposure screens' pickers on it** (ELEMENTS.md 8.2 and 12.2). `Select`,
  `<drishti-select>` (`drishti_select.js`): the WAI-ARIA select-only combobox over the library's one listbox and popover (groups,
  disabled options); Down, Up, Enter, Space, Alt+Down open, Home and End, Page Up and Down, type-ahead, Enter, Space or Alt+Up pick,
  Escape and Tab close without picking; a long list (more than 8, or `search: true`) has a search field on top; in markup its options
  are `<option>` and `<optgroup>` children; `name` makes a hidden input for a plain form; `setOptions`, `setDisabled`, `drishti:change`
  `{value, option}`. Every native select of the VaR family and the exposure screens is now one: the VaR explorer's currency (its "More…"
  group), scenarios, horizon, VaR and ES confidence and hierarchy (a hierarchy skipped on the date disabled, with why), the basket
  sheet's saved baskets (searchable, asked when opened), the playground's horizon, confidences, currency and workbook size (a refused
  size disabled with its reason), the stress window's hierarchy and window, the period statistics' measure, and the exposure explorer's
  pre-deal form (netting set, candidate, method, whose figures). `terminal/_risk_elements.html` loads drishti-inputs; the gallery has a
  Select demo; the harness and `test_elements_inputs_browser.py` test it by keyboard, type-ahead, search and ARIA; the screens' browser
  tests pick through it (`tests/select_helpers.py`).

- **The console's pickers on drishti-inputs** ([ELEMENTS.md section 8.2](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md#82-as-built-drishti-inputs-drishti-data-and-the-grids-cell-editing)):
  the as-of date in the top bar is a business-date picker keyed by the server's holidays (T-1, month-end, a weekend or holiday refused
  in words); every date field of the terminal, BI and Admin pages (and the ones scripts make: BI's statement, designer and slicer

  the query forms' long enums, a Sutra's multi-select and BI's drop-down slicer are `MultiSelect`; a Sutra's date control is
  `DatePicker` and its date range `DateRangePicker` with the server's presets (open-ended allowed); the history page's range is a
  `DateRangePicker` whose presets open the server's ranges; the people picker (`Drishti.People.attach(input, opts)`, four screens),
  the comment box's `@` and `{` lists and the record forms' entity field are drishti-inputs' combobox. Deleted: the console's
  multi-select (`drishti_multiselect.js`, 106 lines, now a 40-line loader for the frozen renderer 1.2.0), the hand-made listboxes of
  the people picker, the comment box and the entity field, the native date handling of the top bar, and their CSS (`.ms-*`,
  `.ctl-pop`, `.shr-list`, `.fm-entity-list`). **drishti-inputs 0.2.0**: `upgradeDateInput`, `upgradeCheckboxes` and `upgradeFields`
  (a page's own fields upgraded in place: the field keeps its name, id and value, its `value` setter moves the picker, the picker's
  changes come back as `input` and `change` events, `hidden`, `disabled`, `min` and `max` followed, a required or unreadable date stops
  the submit); `Combobox` on a page's own field and in a `suggest` mode; `DateRangePicker` with presets given whole and `openEnded`;
  44 px targets on touch screens. The renderer 2.0.0 and the embeds load drishti-inputs for the controls (its style sheet in the view
  sheet, raised to 29 KB gzip on purpose). A guard fails a console script that draws its own multi-select or picker list.

- **drishti-designer 0.1.0, the designer kit** (the product owner, 2026-11-07: "duplicated code will make the system unmaintainable";

- **The demo lake's layout, the owner's decision** (`config/lakes/demo.yaml` and its jar copy; DATA_LAKE_GUIDE.md section 2): `risk.scenario-pv`
  partitioned by `SCENARIO_SET_ID, GRAIN` after the business date, sorted by `LEGAL_ENTITY, DIVISION, DESK, TT_BOOK, TRADE_ID`, zstd
  (vectors too), 256 MB files, 16 MB row groups, 30 days' time travel, maintenance (compaction to 256 MB, vacuum after 7 days,
  checkpoints); `trading.trade_calypso` and `trading.trade_murex` partitioned by `PRODUCT_GROUP` instead of `PRODUCT_TYPE` (50+ product
  types each; `PRODUCT_TYPE` stays promoted); every trade table compacted and vacuumed after 7 days. The trading pack's recommended
  entries follow (tools/packgen/banking/make_packs.py). An existing demo lake is rebuilt with `drishti.py lake demo` to take it; a load
  into an old-layout table is refused, naming both, until then. VaR figures are equal on either layout.

- **The demo lake's move no longer changes the shipped `config/lakes/demo.yaml`** (found on the owner's stack after 2.9.11.d: at the
  first start after the move the file was re-written in block style, quotes added, and 43 tables appended, so `git status` showed it
  modified and the drill's clean-tree check would fail). Two causes: the shipped file lacked the 37 tables the example packs'
  connectors read from the demo lake (climate, genomics, liquidity, operational risk, retail), and the code that moves old connector
  files to `lake: demo` (`LakeFiles.adoptDemo`) re-serialised the whole file to add any entry. Now the shipped file (and its jar copy)
  holds every table a shipped pack's connector reads, checked by a test and filled by `LakesCli pack-tables --lake demo --packs
  config/packs,examples/packs --write`; a lake file is written only when an entry is really missing (a site's own connector naming a
  kind the packs no longer have, or the data inbox's first load into a table), and then only that entry is added at the end of
  `tables:` in the file's compact style, every other line and comment kept byte for byte (`tables: {}` of an empty lake becomes the
  block). A start that finds nothing to add writes nothing (docs/admin/OPERATIONS.md, "The lakes' folders"). Found on the way: a
  results reader of the older form (`var-results`, `exposure-results`: `risk-results` tables, same old root) was moved to `lake: demo`
  and its table added to the demo lake, where it would have read `data/delta/demo/risk-results`; such a connector reads another shipped
  lake's tables and is now left as it is.

- **Drishti Elements, the design, decided by the product owner** ([ELEMENTS.md](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md)): the console's JavaScript as eight libraries (drishti-core, -inputs, -grid, -chart, -data, -insight, -renderer, -risk; 1 to 5 without a Drishti server), the measured inventory (116 of 258 scripts and modules, about 21,000 lines, fold into them; about 10 grids and 22 chart scripts into one each), the grid's three layouts (wells, panel, terminal: VaR screens default to terminal) and its server-side pivot with non-additive totals from the server, an AG Grid-style adapter for the Enterprise pivot API from public documentation only, one chart spec over ECharts with the risk kinds and maps (world to every country's first-level regions), packaging and licensing per domain module, the documentation of every library (guide, generated API reference, tutorial, gallery, AG Grid migration guide), the guards and the migration order; the decisions (Vega retired, the grid on phones, a standalone Excel writer, the adapter's scope, both options of g2, g3 and g4 built as modes with A the default); mock-ups [g1](docs/architecture/mockups/elements/g1-pivot-grid.html), [g2](docs/architecture/mockups/elements/g2-charts.html), [g3](docs/architecture/mockups/elements/g3-maps.html) and [g4](docs/architecture/mockups/elements/g4-gallery.html).
- **Drishti Elements distributed** ([ELEMENTS.md section 8.7](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md#87-as-built-the-distribution); the guide
  [Using Drishti Elements in your app](docs/guides/EMBED_GUIDE.md#13-drishti-elements-libraries-in-your-own-app)): other applications take the libraries as files kept
  inside the organisation, never from a public CDN or registry. `drishti.py elements pack --libs core,grid,chart [--theme dark]`
  writes one JavaScript file and one style sheet with exactly those libraries and what they require (core+grid+chart: 1.8 MB, 555 KB
  gzip with ECharts; 50 KB CSS), naming what is inside; the banking module's library is refused unless `--include-domain banking`.
  `drishti.py elements dist` writes `drishti-elements-<version>.zip` (every library's ES modules, bundle, sheets, TypeScript
  declarations generated from the typed JSDoc, README and licence notice; the token sheet and one sheet per theme; the engines and map
  shapes; the changelog lines; SRI hashes of every file; 3.3 MB) and the npm tarballs `@drishti/elements-<name>` for an internal
  Artifactory or Nexus registry; `./mvnw -P elements -pl drishti-elements package` builds the WebJar
  (`META-INF/resources/webjars/drishti-elements/<version>/`). The three forms hold the same bytes and are reproducible. Apps override
  any design token after the sheet for their own theme. The manifest's duplicate entries of drishti-inputs and drishti-data are gone and
  it gains `assets` (the folders a library reads at run time).
- **Drishti Elements, the foundation** ([ELEMENTS.md section 8.1](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md#81-as-built-the-foundation-drishti-core-and-the-grids-engine)):
  `static/elements/` with a manifest of the libraries and their versions, ES modules per library and one bundled file each written by
  an offline Python build (`tools/elements/build.py`, `--check`), a loader (`Drishti.elements.load('drishti-grid')`), and the API
  reference generated from the typed JSDoc ([ELEMENTS_API.md](docs/guides/ELEMENTS_API.md), `tools/docs/elements_api.py --check`).
- **drishti-core 1.0.0**: numbers by the server's rules (half up on the decimal value, the true minus, the named formats generated from
  `formats.yaml`, compact, percent, basis points, currency, a locale's separators), business dates and ranges, the theme tokens
  generated from `drishti_tokens.css` with WCAG contrast arithmetic, an API client (errors in words with their DRS code, GET retries,
  abort, time limit, the as-of header), an event bus, a focus trap, a live region and a roving tab index, keys and key maps, dialogs,
  drawers and toasts. Folded in and deleted: `drishti_resize.js` and `build/drishti_grid-keys.js` (`Drishti.resize` and
  `Drishti.GridKeys` keep their names); the alerts' and the workbench's toasts, the table editors' dialog and the number helpers of
  twelve screens now call drishti-core (a value that rounds to zero reads `0`, never `−0`).
- **drishti-grid 0.1.0, the engine** (no look yet): columns and the searchable field list, sort and filter models, the client-side row
  model (typed indexes, row groups with figures from their members) and the server-side one (block requests with sort, filter, group
  keys, values and pivot, a cache, refresh, abort), virtual scrolling for a million rows, the pivot in the server's own view and answer
  (row and column groups, totals and subtotals above or below, open and closed groups, top N with Others, member and value filters,
  pivot result columns), non-additive measures never summed in the browser (asked of the server and merged by coordinates), the
  wells, selection with range figures that warn on a non-additive column, copy as TSV, CSV and a standalone .xlsx writer, the keys,
  the Explain hook and the layout-neutral state. **Events and live data**: typed events on the bus and as DOM events (cell click,
  double-click and edit, selection, range, sort, filter, pivot, groups, expand and collapse, column move, resize, pin and hide, row data
  updated, server blocks loaded or failed, Explain opened); transactions by row id applied in place with a stable order under sort and
  filter, batched for high-frequency feeds, each changed cell's direction kept for its flash; live feeds over Server-Sent Events or a
  WebSocket; the server-side model's invalidate, purge and data-changed notice; group and pivot totals changed by difference, and
  non-additive ones asked of the server again, debounced. 40 unit tests in Node (`tests/elements/`), and the 1,000,000-row figures in
  [BENCHMARK.md](docs/admin/BENCHMARK.md).
- **drishti-grid 0.2.0, the visual layer** ([ELEMENTS.md section 8.1](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md#81-as-built-the-foundation-drishti-core-and-the-grids-engine)):
  `new Grid(element, options)` and `<drishti-grid>` (no framework, no shadow root) draw the engine in the three layouts of g1, all
  built: `wells` (the default: fields with search and the four wells above the grid, Explain in a drawer that follows the selection),
  `panel` (a side tool panel with grouped fields, checkboxes, the wells two by two, pivot mode, grand total column, subtotals above and
  deferred update) and `terminal` (a command line read both ways, one lane of wells, Explain in a split pane with the steps, the worst
  scenarios and the trend, function keys F2 to F10); densities comfortable, compact and terminal apart from the layout; light and dark
  from drishti-core's tokens. Drag chips between wells (or move them from a chip's menu by the keyboard), aggregation per value (the
  server's for a non-additive one), member and value filters, top N, collapsible pivot column groups, the grand totals and any column
  pinned, the column menu, the context menu (Explain, copy, copy with headers, CSV and Excel, chart the range, the rows behind a cell
  in a dialog, group, pin), row checkboxes, ranges by drag or Shift+click with the status bar (count, sum, average, min, max; a sum of
  VaR is refused with a warning), ◆ non-additive totals with a hover note, colour scales and data bars, Explain on E and F2, the full
  keyboard with grid or treegrid roles and announcements, the flash of live changes (still under reduced motion), loading placeholders
  for server blocks, virtual rows and columns; on a phone (O2) the first column pinned and a pivot as one value column with a measure
  switcher. Nothing inline: it runs under a strict CSP. A static fixture harness (`drishti_harness.html`, synthetic data, no server) in
  every layout, density and theme; 12 more Node tests and one browser test file against the harness (`test_elements_grid_browser.py`).
  The engine's pivot header rows (an open group's label line, subtotals below) no longer repeat the subtotal's figures.
- **drishti-inputs 0.1.0** ([ELEMENTS.md section 8.2](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md#82-as-built-drishti-inputs-drishti-data-and-the-grids-cell-editing)):
  business-date pickers keyed by holiday calendars (rules with weekend rolls, n-th weekdays and Easter, or the server's dates; unions
  such as US+UK; T-1, month-end, typed `T-3`, `ME`, `6 Nov 2026`; non-business days refused in words), a date-range picker with twelve
  presets that move with the business date, a tree picker (compact partial selection, children from the server with loading and
  Retry, search), a multi-select (search, chips, select-all, a limit), a combobox with server type-ahead (debounced, aborted, cached,
  in order), forms from a JSON-schema-like description (validation in words, conditional fields, repeatable groups, the server's
  checks, a four-eyes submit that files a proposal and waits), a filter bar that emits the filter model on a bus for grids and charts,
  and the code editor over the vendored CodeMirror (Rachana, YAML and Python; completion from the function catalogue through a hook;
  lint marks and a problems list; read-only; a side-by-side or unified diff). Each a class and a web component.
- **drishti-data 0.1.0**: one data-source contract for grids and charts (in memory, REST pages, Drishti's server-side rows, Arrow,
  live; any source is the grid's datasource as it is), the live client over Server-Sent Events or a WebSocket (reconnect with a
  jittered back-off, a heartbeat, resume from the last event id, states for a status line), backpressure into the grid's
  `applyTransactionAsync` (one batch at a time, the rest folded by row id), and the Arrow client (Flight over HTTP where a server
  offers it, else Arrow over HTTP, else JSON; columns read without a copy where they can be, rows as views, column types for a grid).
  The grid's own SSE and WebSocket feeds are gone: the live client is the one connection.
- **drishti-grid 0.3.0, cell editing**: editors per type (text, a number in the grid's locale read loosely, a date through
  drishti-inputs' business-date picker, a select, a checkbox), started by Enter, F2, a double click or typing, saved by Enter or Tab,
  Escape to cancel; validation in words (required, min, max, length, options, the column's rule); each change one edit transaction
  (`cellValueChanged`, `editTransaction`) with undo and redo; a paste of a range from Excel (quoted cells, one value filling a range);
  Delete over a range; a write-back hook (applied, refused with the old values back, or proposed) and four eyes (cells marked until a
  proposal is decided). `grid.followFilters(bus)` follows a filter bar.
- **drishti-grid 0.4.0, the AG Grid-style adapter** ([ELEMENTS.md section 6](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md#6-the-ag-grid-style-adapter),
  [the migration guide](docs/guides/EMBED_GUIDE.md#14-moving-an-ag-grid-enterprise-pivot-app)): an application written for AG Grid Enterprise's pivoting moves to
  drishti-grid by changing one call, `createGridFromAgOptions(el, gridOptions)`. Drishti never uses AG Grid; the adapter is written from
  its public documentation only. Column definitions (defaults, types, groups, getters, formatters, comparators, classes and safe styles),
  row grouping, pivoting (`rowGroup`, `pivot`, `aggFunc` with built-in, function and `aggFuncs` aggregations, `'drishti:server'` for a
  non-additive measure whose every total is the server's), the totals and open levels, `sideBar` as the panel layout, the server-side
  row model (`serverSideDatasource.getRows` with AG's request, in pivot mode each open level and `pivotResultFields` made into the
  pivot), tree data, the common grid API calls (options at run time, transactions, selection, nodes, CSV and Excel, filter and column
  state both ways, sizing, expand and collapse, the wells, `refreshServerSide`) and AG-named events from the grid's own. Every option not
  taken in full is named once in the console with drishti-grid's way and listed by `reportUnsupported()`. The mapping's one home is the
  code (`drishti_grid-ag-map.js`): the gallery's AG Grid tab (now live, with an adapter demo) and the guide's option table are
  generated from it. The grid gained `registerAggFunc`, a column's `cellClass`, `cellStyle` and `system`, the pivot's `grandTotalRow`
  and the view's `grandColumn` and `columnGroupTotals`. 12 Node tests (`ag-adapter.test.mjs`, one in `gallery.test.mjs`) and a browser
  test against a static harness configured purely with AG-shaped options (`drishti_ag-harness.html`).
- **drishti-core 1.1.0**: the sort and filter model moved in from the grid as the contract every library shares (with
  `FILTER_CHANNEL` and `filterRows`), the element maker and placements, reading typed and pasted numbers in a locale, and loading a
  library's vendored engine (`loadScript`, `loadStyle`, `staticUrl`). One static harness page for inputs, data and editing
  (`drishti-inputs/drishti_harness.html`), 23 more Node tests (`inputs`, `data`, `grid-edit`) and one browser test file
  (`test_elements_inputs_browser.py`). The console's pickers, forms, editors, live connections and Arrow reader that move onto these
  later are listed in ELEMENTS.md 8.2.
- **drishti-chart 0.1.0, with maps** ([ELEMENTS.md section 8.3](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md#83-as-built-drishti-chart-its-maps-and-drishti-risk)):
  one engine-neutral spec over the vendored ECharts (kind, data inline or a server's answer, encodings x, y, series, size and colour,
  drishti-core's formats, axes, legend, annotations as lines, bands, points and texts, conditional marks and colours, interactions);
  the kinds line, area, bar (grouped, stacked, stacked to 100%, horizontal), scatter, bubble, histogram, waterfall, box plot, heatmap
  (sequential and diverging), candlestick, pie, donut, gauge, treemap, sankey, layers and the map; `new Chart(el, spec, options)` and
  `<drishti-chart>` in the two modes of g2, `card` (the default) and `studio` (the kind rail, the chart with its table, the spec beside
  it with options that change both); the shared theme and the three densities; crosshair tooltips, legend toggles, drag-to-zoom with an
  overview window, the keyboard (arrows walk the marks, Enter explains, T the table), **a click on any mark explains it** through the
  grid's hook and drawing and selects its rows, the data table (▦, the accessible alternative), export (PNG at 2×, SVG drawn off screen,
  CSV, the spec), **linked selection with drishti-grid** through drishti-core's bus (`linkGrid`), live updates by row id, throttled.
  **Maps**: the world in Equal Earth, a double-click opens a country's first-level regions loaded on demand from the vendored Natural
  Earth files (the United States in Albers with Alaska and Hawaii as insets, Canada's provinces and territories, every other country

  and the two modes of g3, `ranking` (the default: legend, top ten with bars, the selected place with Explain and "Drill into
  regions ›") and `table` (a floating legend and card, a world inset, a sortable table under the map). **Vega-Lite is translated** into
  the spec (O1): the marks, encodings, aggregates, bins, layers, filters and calculations Drishti's visuals use, the rest named; the
  vendored Vega stays until the screens move. Nothing inline (a strict CSP holds).
- **drishti-risk 0.1.0** (the banking module's, licensed with it): `risk.pnl-distribution` (VaR and ES lines, the tail in red),

  from the typed JSDoc; an event log; a status line with the bundle's size, the tests and a keyboard/ARIA smoke check; and the
  documentation page (runnable examples with "Open in playground", the API from the JSDoc, the keys and roles, the changelog). Demos of
  every component on this build: drishti-core's formats, theme, bus, overlays, Explain, API client and accessibility helpers; the grid in
  its layouts and densities, the pivot, server-side rows, live updates from a manual feed, editing, export; every chart kind, the
  studio, the maps in both modes, linked selection, a live chart, Vega-Lite translated; the four risk kinds; drishti-inputs' and
  drishti-data's demos appear with those libraries. `tools/docs/elements_api.py` writes the gallery's catalogue
  (`drishti_catalogue.js`) from the same parse as ELEMENTS_API.md, `--check` covering both; ELEMENTS_API.md now lists every library's
  types (a `@typedef` was read as `@type` and dropped). 9 Node tests (`gallery.test.mjs`), the routes' tests and one browser file
  (`test_elements_gallery_browser.py`, 5 tests, about 18 s).
- **drishti-renderer 2.0.0: the client renderer rebuilt on the Elements libraries** ([CLIENT_RENDERER.md section 3](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md#302-the-renderer-as-an-elements-library),
  [ELEMENTS.md section 8.5](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md#85-as-built-drishti-renderer-200)). The product owner's rule: no renderer-private
  grid, chart, format, live or input code; the console and the renderer draw panels with the same components. Tables, trees, drills, the
  pivot kind and every chart's Data table are **drishti-grid's document table** (the server's table, element for element 1.2.0's markup,
  with sort, filter, paging, trees and drills); the nested pivot in `behaviours: 'console'` is **drishti-grid's grid with tree data** (new:
  `treeData`, `getDataPath`); every chart is **drishti-chart's panel charts** (the console's options, series for series; the only place an
  engine is called); the element maker, the rules for untrusted data (`attrAllowed`, `safeUrl`), formats (half up) and the API client
  are **drishti-core's**; streams and Elements' one connection per page are **drishti-data's `LiveClient`** (new: SSE over fetch so a
  bearer travels, an address asked at each connect, the event name in each message, `parseSse`). The renderer's `m/format.js`,
  `m/tables.js`, `m/charts.js`, `m/draw.js` and its stream and channel code are gone from the current version; **1.2.0 stays served,
  frozen, for existing embedders** (Elements 2.2 still points at it; Elements 2.3 at 2.0.0). Public entry `static/render/2.0.0/drishti-render.js`
  (the 1.x API unchanged, plus `insight` hooks for About); `/embed/v2/elements/<library>/…` serves the libraries to other origins.
  **One rounding rule**: the panel macros' computed figures (a share, a progress, a width, a heat bucket) round half up as the server and
  the renderer do (`core/half_up.py`). Parity against the console's macros: 476 pairs, no difference beyond the intentional ones (CLIENT_RENDERER.md 14.4). Tests: Node (`data.test.mjs` fetch transport;
  `chart.test.mjs` panel series against the frozen 1.2.0 builders; `doc-table.test.mjs` markup against the frozen `tables.js`;
  `tree.test.mjs`), the render browser files moved to the libraries, and a static harness (`drishti-renderer/drishti_harness.html`, the
  parity suite's ViewModels from `tools/elements/renderer_fixtures.py`) with a four-test browser file (`test_elements_renderer_browser.py`, about 5 s).
- **One search** (lean & streamlined): `core/search.py` behind one console route, `GET /api/search?in=command|help|all`, answers the command
  line's type-ahead (`in=command`, the server's order kept), Help's search box and results page and `/what` (`in=help`), and a new **global
  search** (`in=all`): entities, commands, screens, Help pages and things you can build, grouped by kind, best group and best match first,
  each source in parallel and a failing one named in `failed` while the rest answer. It follows entitlements (the server's), the menus'
  rules (screens), Help's rule (pages), the BI catalogue (reports and boards), the edition, the lens and the engine switches.
  **Removed:** the console's `GET /api/suggest`, the command line's own type-ahead in `api_routes.py` and `Library.search` (one search
  instead of three). One client component, `drishti_search-box.js`, runs the command line, Help's box and the global search (`Alt+K`, or
  the top bar's new search button): ARIA combobox and listbox, debounced, a stale request aborted. Tests: `test_search.py`; 14 test files
  repointed to `/api/search`.
- **One keymap**: `drishti_keys.js` holds every key a page answers, with its scope (dialog, panel, screen, global; the most specific
  wins), its area, a description, and the rule that **a key never acts while you type** in a field. **`?` lists the keys of the screen
  you are on** (and the footer's new **Keys** button; on a view `?` stays About this page), from the same registrations; History's own keys
  dialog is replaced by it. Every page-level key handler moves into it (the VaR screen's B, M, H, N and Alt+B
  included); left outside, each with its reason: the engines menu's filter box (widget-internal), the drill-down's fallback for a host
  page without the keymap. **BI and the Pivot are folded in too** (the eleven BI and Pivot scripts that bound keys on the page on
  their own: BI's `/` and `g` then `h c w r` (`g h` now opens the Build home), the designer's Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y and Escape, the tab
  lists' arrows, the kiosk's K, arrows, P and Escape, the run drawer's Escape, the statement preview's Page Up and Down, the tooltip
  page's Escape, the Pivot's r c v f s, g, x, 1 to 9 and e, its cards' w i u, l and m), and so is the one Explain's E, ? and Escape;
  **BI's own Keys dialog (`#biKeys`) is deleted**: the rail's Keys button and `?` open the keymap's list, which describes the visuals'
  and the designer's own keys. A table's, a panel's zoom and About this page's own keys stay on their widgets and are described to the
  keymap so the list shows them; the allow-list keeps only the engines menu's filter box and the drill-down's fallback.
  - **`test_keymap.py`** (static, in the gate): every registration names a scope and an area, chords are written canonically, no two
    claim one key in one scope and area, ids are unique, no script binds keys on document or window outside the allow-list (and the
    allow-list has no stale entry), widget keys are described. **`test_keymap_browser.py`**: the `?` list (open, focus, Esc, the footer
    button, `?` typed in a field is a character) and the global search (Alt+K from anywhere, grouped answer, ↓ Enter opens, Esc twice).
  - **Timings** (the demo data, one real server, develop's console and this one side by side, requests interleaved, 21 each, median):
    the command line's type-ahead is unchanged, the same answers in the same order (`/api/suggest` 3.4 to 7.2 ms, `/api/search?in=command`
    3.5 to 7.3 ms over `TRD`, `TRD MX-2`, `CPTY north`, `VAR`, `MX-20000001`); Help's results page is unchanged (81 to 105 ms before,
    83 to 114 ms after, over `keyboard`, `value at risk`, `connector`); Help's box (`in=help`) 37 to 60 ms; the new global search
    (`in=all`) 92 to 96 ms, most of it Help's full-text scan (a word index for Help is the next step if it must be faster).
- **Docs:** USER_GUIDE (Keyboard: the `?` list and the rules; *Search everything (Alt+K)*), API_GUIDE (`/api/search`; `/api/suggest`
  removed), RELEASE_NOTES (upgrade note), Help addresses `/help/keyboard` and `/help/global-search`.
