- **One Approvals queue** (SHARED_SCREENS.md section 2, the approved mock-up e2-approvals A with B's due-soon items; lean & streamlined):
  every four-eyes item in one inbox, **Views → Approvals** (`/approvals`, a count on the top bar): Sutra proposals, corrections
  (write-back), BI items, pivot functions, stress windows, regulatory report sign-offs and compute packages. **Due soon** (a report run near
  its filing date, `drishti.approvals.due-days`) is pinned on top; filters *Data · Screens · Risk · Access*, *Mine sent*, *Done*. The item
  shows **what changes** (a diff with the maker's reason; a Sutra's with its moved panels and the workbench's evidence), its **effect if
  approved** (the impact service's answer for a corrected record, the published reports a BI change breaks, a node's stressed VaR under
  each window, the files a signed run releases) and the **rules**; **Approve**, **Reject** with a reason, **Withdraw** your own, or **ask a
  question** (a thread on the item; the maker is told without the text). The maker never approves their own; everything is audited.
  - **One server API**, `/api/v1/approvals` (list, count, item, approve, reject, withdraw, questions): each kind is an `ApprovalSource` in its
    own package (`SutraApprovals`, `ChangeApprovals`, `BiApprovals`, `FunctionApprovals`, `StressWindowApprovals`, `VarReportApprovals`,
    `ComputeApprovals`) keeping its rules; the queue keeps nothing per person (session isolation) and keeps the question threads.
  - **One CLI**, `drishti.py approvals list|show|approve|reject|withdraw|ask`; a new token scope `approve`.
  - **Removed** (folded into the queue): the endpoints `POST /api/v1/sutras/proposals/{id}/approve|reject|withdraw`,
    `/api/v1/changes/{id}/approve|reject|withdraw`, `/api/v1/bi/items/{id}/approve|reject`, `/api/v1/admin/compute/requests/{id}/approve|reject`,
    `/api/v1/pivot/functions/{owner}/{ref}/approve`, `/api/v1/var/stress-window/proposals/{id}/decision`, and the sign-off actions of
    `/api/v1/var/reports/{report}/runs/{period}/signoff` (the maker's narrative is `/narrative`); the console pages *Build → Govern →
    Reviews* (`/build/reviews`, `/build/reviews/{id}`) and *Review → Changes* (`/review/changes`), which redirect (301) to the queue; the
    approve and reject buttons of the BI item page, Admin → Compute, the pivot's Functions panel, the stress window screen and the report
    sign-off screen (each now links to its item in the queue); the CLI commands `design approve|reject`, `change approve|reject|withdraw`,
    `pivot functions approve`, `var stress-window --decide` and `var report sign`; the console's `/build/review-count`.
  - Tests: `ApprovalQueueTest` (two people each see their own queue, due soon first, decisions audited, question threads only for who may
    see the item), `ApprovalApiTest` (the API over real Sutra proposals, with security on), `test_approvals.py`, `test_approvals_browser.py`
    (every button of the queue), `test_approvalscli.py`; 21 Java and 14 console test files repointed.
- **One alert engine** (lean & streamlined): the measure-alert service is the engine (`com.ash.drishti.server.alerts.AlertService`,
  settings `drishti.alerts.*`): rules on a visual, a dataset or model measure, an entity's field or **a Rachana-EL rule on one entity**
  (the new condition `rule`), looked at on a schedule, after a data load or live; delivered as before (inbox, email, chat bridges, webhooks,
  text). **One lifecycle** for every alert raised, the platform's included: **raised → acknowledged → resolved** (by itself when the number
  comes back, or by hand with a note), **owners** (who acknowledged it; a platform alert can be assigned), **snooze** (a breach while snoozed
  is held and raised when the snooze ends; a snoozed platform series tells nobody). The Alerts page lists *Raised for you* beside your rules.
  - **One API**, `/api/v1/alerts` (raised, acknowledge, resolve, snooze, assign, rules, suggestions, the notification stream) and
    `/api/v1/admin/alerts` (everyone's rules, the board tiles that notify, the platform alerts).
  - **Folded and deleted:** the entity-rule engine (`AlertEngine`, `AlertRule`, `AlertEvent`, the identity store's `AlertHistory`, its table
    `drishti_alert` and the setting `drishti.alerts.keep`); its rules are **converted at start, once,** into rules of the engine (a field
    source, the condition `rule`; live when the source pushes changes, else after each load of the kind). The platform alerts keep reading the
    server's meters (`config/alerts/platform-alerts.yaml`, unchanged) and are listed, acknowledged, snoozed and assigned by the engine; their
    own controller is gone. A data load's *alerts* step hands the kind to the engine (`n alerts to look`). Endpoints removed:
    `/api/v1/me/alerts`, `/api/v1/me/alerts/rules/**`, `/api/v1/me/alerts/suggestions/{kind}`, `/api/v1/me/measure-alerts/**`,
    `/api/v1/admin/measure-alerts/**`; the stream moved from `/api/v1/me/alerts/stream` to `/api/v1/alerts/stream` (its `alert` event is
    gone: an alert raised is a `notice` of type `alert`).
  - Tests: `AlertServiceTest` (the lifecycle, snooze, the converter, the rule condition, the platform alerts for administrators only),
    `AlertsAndMonitorsTest`, `FieldMaskingTest`, `LoadsApiTest`, `PlatformMetricsApiTest` repointed; console `test_alert_routes.py`,
    `test_monitors_alerts.py`.

  - **The Pivot's Why did it move? card (W) is on the one Explain** too: the card keeps its choices (the two cells or dates, the split,

    explains a figure** (the grid's key); expand by another field moved to **Shift+E**. The two dates of *Why did it move?* are

  every table of the VaR explorer (the scope tree as tree data, the path, the history, the contributions, the captures, the
  currencies), parametric VaR, the basket's sheet (now drishti-grid's cell editing: typing, Enter, Tab, Delete, undo; the paste with
  headings stays the sheet's) and its what-if, the VaR Playground (its six header rows pinned), backtesting, the regulatory screens, the
  stress window, the scenario matrix, the MR lens, the risk landing, the exposure explorer and its counterparty screens, FRTB-SA and
  SIMM is a `<drishti-grid>` in the **terminal layout** (the product owner's default for VaR screens) made by drishti-risk's preset
  `riskGrid` (figures never summed in the browser); every chart is drishti-chart or a drishti-risk kind (`riskChart`): the P&L
  distribution from the server's bins with VaR, ES and the fitted normal, the backtest with the server's zone, count and multiplier, the
  exposure profile with the server's EEPE. **Deleted**: `drishti_var-charts.js` (208 lines) and `drishti_exposure-charts.js` (126), the
  screens' hand-built tables, SVG drawing, sheet editor and playground canvas, and their CSS (2,524 lines out and 1,822 in under `web/`, libraries
  included). Commands, addresses, keys and saved views unchanged. Market-risk code stays in drishti-risk (the owner's domain rule):
  drishti-risk 0.2.0 gains the grid and chart presets, the figures in words (`riskMoney`, `riskSigned`, `riskInt`, `riskPct`: the texts
  the screens printed before), `textColumn` and `moneyColumn`; the generic libraries only generic hooks: drishti-grid 0.4.0 (a column's
  `cellClass` and `cellRenderer`, a row's `getRowClass` and `getRowData`, `fitRows`, `chrome: false`, `pinnedTopRows` with
  `pinnedCellClicked`, a tree node's own row in its cell context), drishti-chart 0.2.0 (the histogram of a server's bins). A
  before-and-after comparison of sixteen screens and tabs (`tests/screen_figures.py`, `tests/test_var_family_figures_browser.py`, run on
  demand) and every family browser file on the new selectors with its assertions kept.
- **The first global search no longer waits on Help** (Alt+K): it read every Help page's text, rendering them all on the event loop
  (about 12 s on a cold console, longer on a busy machine); the console now renders them once in a worker thread as it starts, Help's
  search renders what is missing off the event loop, and the rendered pages are shared by every pack set's library. **The Approvals
  queue drops a stale list**: an answer to an older filter that arrives after a newer one no longer replaces it.
- **The console's CSS on design tokens, the look unchanged** ([ELEMENTS.md 4.1, Design tokens](docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md#design-tokens)):
  `drishti_tokens.css` is the one home of every colour and scale. Each hard-coded colour became a token whose value in every theme is
  what its rule drew: fixed colours (white labels on coloured fills, the navigation band, scrims, the theme menu's swatches, FRTB-SA's
  Terminal colours), the landings' and Capacity's hues per theme, elevations, and the print palette (last in the file, with no
  `!important`). The type scale (53 steps in px: a library or an embedded view draws the same size on a host page whose root text is not 16px,
  as the Elements' harnesses' 13px; 7 relative steps, 10 fluid display sizes), spacing (52 px steps up to 32px),
  radii, layers (14 `--d-z-*`), breakpoints (24 `--d-bp-*`) and the Elements' densities are tokens of exactly the values in use;
  grid and chart take their density sizes from them. Gone: rules of removed screens (the old Studio, the BI model designer and layer
  wizard, the browser Python console, the top bar's clock and desk name, the exposure sparkline, unused tone and text utilities), the
  `[hidden]` rules of console-only sheets that Bootstrap's own covers, rules repeated twice, the theme button's hidden label, and
  fallbacks of tokens that never existed (`--d-text`, `--d-fg`, `--d-mono`, `--d-border-strong`: the value they drew is written).
  `!important` removed where specificity or order does it; the rest is on an allow-list with a reason each. The embedded view, report
  and renderer sheets write the fixed tokens into their rules, so their size is unchanged. Numbers (90 sheets): lines 9,404 → 9,256;
  distinct hex colours outside the token file 75 → 0 and `rgb()` 15 → 0 (194 distinct hex in all the CSS, every one now in the token
  file); literal font sizes 69 → 0; `!important` 149 → 97; `@media` widths 25 → 24 breakpoints. The forms', pickers' and record forms'
  sheets (`drishti_form.css`, `drishti_controls.css`, `drishti_record-forms.css`) are tokenised too, their rules otherwise as the inputs
  conversion left them; the line count after the pickers' own deletions is 9,213.
  - **Proof the look did not change** (`tools/dev/css_visual_check.py`, [TEST_HARNESS.md 3.14](docs/architecture/TEST_HARNESS.md#314-the-css-visual-check)):
    landing, the VaR explorer, Pivot, a BI report, Build home, Admin and Help at 1440 px and landing, VaR and Help at 390 px, in all ten
    themes, before and after against one server, compared pixel by pixel: 100 pictures, 76 identical, 23 within the anti-aliasing
    tolerance (the VaR charts' edges, as between two runs of the same tree), 1 different (a BI report's timing footer, whose width
    follows a measured time; identical when taken again). Again after the inputs conversion merged and its three sheets were tokenised:
    71 identical, 28 within tolerance, 1 different (a BI chart caught mid-redraw; identical when taken again). No picture differs
    because of the CSS.
  - **Guards** (`test_css_tokens.py`, a quick file check): no colour literal outside the token file, font sizes only from the type scale,
    `@media` widths only from the breakpoints, no undefined `--d-*`, and `!important` only on its allow-list, which only shrinks.
  - **Left for the forms work**: the stacked-label rules repeated in eighteen forms, with the seven checkbox-row classes that escape them
    with `!important`: one form-label convention once wip/e-forms has converted the forms.

### Domain modules, the access registry and lenses (2.9.11.f)

- **Domain modules, phase 1: the backend split** ([DOMAIN_MODULES.md](docs/architecture/DOMAIN_MODULES.md), [ACCESS_MODEL.md](docs/architecture/ACCESS_MODEL.md)).
  The core knows no industry: banking is a module. New Maven modules: **drishti-registry** (the access registry), **drishti-compute-banking**
  (VaR and ES, parametric, components, backtesting, exposure, FRTB-SA, SIMM, beta and correlation: `com.ash.drishti.banking.compute`, pure
  maths), **drishti-banking** (the VaR, exposure, FRTB-SA, SIMM, sensitivities, MR cube and official-results services, storage and API:
  `com.ash.drishti.banking`) and **drishti-app** (the runnable jar, at its old path `drishti-server/target/drishti-server-<version>-exec.jar`).
  The six places where the core used banking code are SPIs now (`PivotSourceProvider`, `CacheGroup`, `CapacityFigures`, `HealthFigures`,
  `OfficialReaders.OfficialResults`, the edition's words); `ArchitectureRulesTest` fails the build when the core imports a domain, a
  domain another, a domain's compute Spring or the server, or anything but the registry reads the access model. VaR, exposure and the BI
  parity answers are unchanged.
- **The access registry** (drishti-registry: `AccessRegistry`, `EmbeddedAccessRegistry`, `AccessStore`, `YamlAccessStore`): licence →
  module → lens → function → permission, decided in one place. Each module's jar ships its manifest (`META-INF/drishti/module.yaml`:
  packages, engines, packs, connectors, API, functions) and its lenses (with the modules they need and the functions they bundle); a module
  is on when installed, licensed and enabled. No `config/access/licence.yaml` is the **development licence** (every module, unsigned), so an
  existing installation changes nothing. A module that is off loads no bean, engine, job or API (`@ConditionalOnModule`), its packs and
  connectors do not load, its API answers `404 DRS-1025`, and Admin → Engines says why its engines are not installed.
- **Admin → Modules over REST**: `GET/POST /api/v1/admin/modules` (states, what each brings, the licence, the lenses; the switch, with a
  reason, audited, written to `config/modules/<module>.yaml`, taken at the next start); `GET /api/v1/modules` (the modules loaded and the
  lenses open to the caller). New settings `drishti.modules.dir`, `drishti.modules.<module>.enabled`, `drishti.modules.watch-seconds`,
  `drishti.access.dir` (CONFIGURATION.md; OPERATIONS.md section 22).
- **Functions** (command words such as VAR, TRD, EQV, EXP) are the finest unit of access: each belongs to one module (a word no module
  declares is the core's), lenses bundle them, and the mnemonic switches (Admin → Commands) are decided by the registry: a function is on
  when its module is on and no administrator turned it off; its API then answers `404 DRS-1026` (and `403 DRS-1027` is wired for per-person
  grants in 2.9.11.i).
- **The banking API is under `/api/v1/risk/…`** (`/risk/var`, `/risk/exposure`, `/risk/frtb`, `/risk/simm`, `/risk/sensitivities`,
  `/risk/risk-factors`, `/risk/mr`); the old paths are answered as the new ones for this release (`Deprecation: true` and a `Link` to the
  new path), then removed. Connector files naming the moved engine classes keep working for this release.
- **Packs name their domain** (`domain: core | banking | economy | capitalmarkets` in `pack.yaml`; ids and folders unchanged): a pack loads
  only while a module of its domain is on. A **capitalmarkets** module (content only, shipped with the core) holds the us-equities and
  funds packs and the market data's functions (CRV, FX, EQV ...; the market-data pack stays banking's while its engines read it); GLEIF is
  core reference data; economy keeps world-economy and news-and-markets. The Market lens needs capital markets and banking.
- **Editions as lenses**: the risk, trading, market and world editions are lenses of the registry; an edition opened as a lens is offered
  only while its modules are on.
- **Domain modules, phase 2 (first half): the console follows the modules** ([DOMAIN_MODULES.md](docs/architecture/DOMAIN_MODULES.md)
  section 8, [ACCESS_MODEL.md](docs/architecture/ACCESS_MODEL.md) section 8; OPERATIONS.md section 22). The console asks the server and
  nothing else: the public about answer now lists the `modules` loaded, and `GET /api/v1/modules` answers, as the person, the modules not
  loaded (with why), the lenses open to them (with the modules and functions each needs) and the **functions they may not use** (each with
  its module and the words to say). A module that is off, or a function off for the person, is gone from every door the console draws:
  its pages and routes answer 404, menus (sitemap `domain:` tags, now drawn by the module's state; a new `requires: module:<id>`), the
  Engines menu, the Admin strip, search, the command line and its type-ahead, Help (its guides, tutorials and section) and the Build home
  leave it out, and typed anyway it says *VRES is not available to you: ask your administrator*.
- **Domain modules, phase 2 (second half, first steps): the moves.** The banking console code, pages, scripts and styles live in
  `drishti-console/plugins/banking/` (`routes/`, `templates/`, `static/`, the landings' code, the Build types, the engine calls), the
  World landing in `plugins/economy/`; the console finds a module's templates after its own and serves a module's files at the same
  `/static/...` addresses, gated by module and lens. The banking engines are the module's: their catalogue entries in drishti-banking's
  `META-INF/drishti/engines.yaml` (and the console's `plugins/banking/engines.yaml`), their jar files in its `engines/`; a server without
  the module lists none of them. Rule 4 of the boundaries as a check: `tools/domain_strings.py` counts the banking names in the core's
  code against an allow list that only shrinks. `EngineRegistryTest` and `EngineFilesTest` run in drishti-banking (they use its engines).
- **Domain modules, phase 2 (second half): the banking module's configuration in its own places.**
  - **Packs in domain folders**: the shipped packs are `config/packs/<domain>/<pack>` (`core/{core,gleif,compute-demo}`,
    `banking/{trading,market-data,market-risk,counterparty-risk}`, `economy/{world-economy,news-and-markets}`,
    `capitalmarkets/{us-equities,funds}`); a pack's `domain:` names its folder. One rule says where a pack is: a packs root holds packs
    directly or one level down in domain folders (a folder with no `pack.yaml` of its own), in Java `com.ash.drishti.api.PackFolders`
    (the pack loader, the reloader and its watchers, Admin -> Packs, deploy and roll back, the Sutra CLI, the lake files' pack tables) and
    in Python `drishti-console/core/pack_paths.py` (the console, the tools, the generators, the tests). `drishti.packs.dir` is unchanged
    (`config/packs`); installed and example packs stay flat. Upgrade: a site's own pack folder under `config/packs` keeps working where it
    is; links to `config/packs/<pack>/...` in a site's documents need the domain folder.
  - **Token declarations from the module**: the banking module's read-only POSTs and its `risk:write` scope are in its jar
    (`META-INF/drishti/token-scopes.yaml`), merged by the core (`ModuleTokenScopes`) only while the module is on: with banking off no
    token can be given `risk:write`. The core's new `compute:write` scope keeps your what-if sandboxes and cancels your own computations
    (`risk:write` still does too).
  - **Help's Risk measures section** is the banking plugin's (`drishti-console/plugins/banking/help.yaml`: its head, placed after Get
    started, and its pages); the core's `help.yaml` and the sitemap no longer name it.
  - **Banking lakes, reports, BI items, tables and models in banking folders**: `config/lakes/banking/{var,ccr}-official.yaml` (a lake
    file may sit in a domain folder; the jar copies are drishti-banking's, listed in its `drishti/lakes/shipped.txt`), the regulatory
    report definitions `config/reports/banking/` (`drishti.regulatory.reports-dir`'s default), `config/bi/reports/banking/`,
    `config/bi/python/banking/`, `config/bi/notebooks/banking/` and `config/tables/banking/` (the banking tables are `banking.<name>`,
    were `bi.<name>`; a site's model or report naming `bi.trading_risk_trades` and the other moved tables needs the new name). A domain
    folder named after a module is read only while the module is on: with banking off, BI lists none of its reports, tables or models.
  - **Editions folded into lenses**: `config/editions/` is gone. A lens's file is `config/lenses/<module>/<lens>.yaml` (risk, trading,
    market: banking; world: economy), the feature presets `config/lenses/features.yaml`, the folder `drishti.lens-dir`
    (`DRISHTI_LENS_DIR`, was `DRISHTI_EDITIONS_DIR`; the console's `lens.dir`). A lens names its packs by module, so World is economy
    with capital markets: with capitalmarkets off, its packs, functions, cards and the World landing's companies, filings and funds are
    gone. Home's cards and chips are the registry lens's (`cards:`, `chips:` in the module's `lenses.yaml`, answered per person by
    `/api/v1/modules`), each shown only while its function is on; the Public sector lens has its eight cards and four chips.
    `drishti.edition` and `drishti.lenses` are unchanged. Upgrade: move a site's own edition file to `config/lenses/<module>/`.
    The guide is now the lenses guide, [LENSES.md](docs/guides/ADMIN_GUIDE.md#12-what-a-lens-is) (was LENSES.md; Help → Lenses guide, the old address
    `editions` redirects): what a lens is, an instance lens and people's lenses, each shipped lens (Risk, Trading, Market, World,
    Public sector) with its modules, packs, cards and chips, customising, your own lens, clusters, troubleshooting, upgrading, the design.
  - **A server without the banking jar**: `config/modules/banking.yaml` names the module (`module: {id, domain, title}`), so a server
    built or started without drishti-banking knows it and shows it off as *not installed*: none of its packs, lakes, tables, models or
    reports load (they used to load, and their engine connectors failed). With the jar, the jar's manifest is the module, as before.
  - **The command line's examples follow the person**: the placeholder (`TRD MX-20000001, CPTY north …`, a lens's `menus.placeholder`)
    keeps only the examples whose function the person may use; with banking off its examples go, with capitalmarkets off World's `USEQ`
    and `FUND` ones (none left: blank). Admin -> Engines' menu line no longer names banking's engines.
- **Static assets by module**: each module's console part is `drishti-console/plugins/<module>/plugin.yaml` (its routers, engines, words,
  pages, templates, static files, and the parts it adds to a core screen). An off module's scripts, styles and Elements library are not
  served (404), and neither to a person whose lens does not use the module (the World lens gets no banking file). The Elements manifest
  carries each library's `module` (drishti-risk: banking) and the loader refuses a library of a module the page does not list
  (`<meta name="drishti-modules">`, `configure({modules})`, `refused(name)`).
- **The console's cycles C1 to C7 are broken in place** (no screen moved yet): the banking routers are included from the plugin's list;
  commands, retired links, the type-ahead, the Pivot presets' word grammar and the landing rules are hooks the module fills
  (`core/plugins.py`); one workbook streamer (`core/workbook_stream.py`); the core client has one engine call (`BackendClient.engine`) and
  the banking calls are the module's own (`plugins/banking/risk_api.py`), **on `/api/v1/risk/…`**; the market landing's figures moved to the
  banking routes, Admin → Saved VaR baskets to the VaR routes, the Pivot draws the MR lens through the plugin's `screens:`. A static test
  (`test_module_boundaries.py`) fails when the core imports a module's code, includes its templates or names its files.


### The public sector: the first new domain, government data and free news

- **Part of the economy module, with a lens of its own** (PUBLIC_SECTOR_GUIDE.md; one module, the owner's decision of 2026-11-07): ten
  functions (`WDI`, `WDIS`, `CBANK`, `CBSER`, `NSTAT`, `OECD`, `OECDS`, `PRESS`, `PREL`, `GDELT`) in the economy's manifest, the
  **Public sector** lens, and the free news (`PRESS`, `PREL`, `GDELT`) in the World lens. The economy module off: all its packs,
  connectors, functions and both lenses are gone, banking, capital markets and GLEIF untouched (`EconomyModuleOffTest`,
  `PublicSectorLensTest`).
- **Six packs** with `domain: economy`, each with its kinds, data contracts (worked examples under docs/contracts/samples), README,
  pack guide and Sutras built from the UI kit only: **world-development** (World Bank WDI: a country's profile with the world map by GDP
  per head, every indicator's history), **central-banks** (FRED and the Bank of Canada: a bank's policy rate, its last move and its
  series), **national-statistics** (Statistics Canada by vector), **oecd** (the members' leading indicator, unemployment, inflation and
  growth, a map by inflation), **official-news** (the press releases of the Fed, ECB, Bank of Canada, Bank of England, SEC, OSFI, the US
  Federal Register and the Canada Gazette, each a link) and **gdelt-events** (a country's day in the world's news: events, tone,
  conflict, CAMEO categories, a map by tone, the top stories).
- **Six daily feeds on drishti-feeds** (`config/feeds/<pack>.yaml`, `tools/feeds/sources/`): incremental (the source's last update, each
  series from its last observation, releases already seen, the GDELT days after the last), JSON Lines into `worldlake` and `newslake`,
  whose lake files now ship with exactly these tables (`tools/test_empty_lakes.py` says only these packs read them). Every source's
  licence and terms are in the feed file (`options.sources`); the Bank of England, OSFI and the Canada Gazette are internal only and their
  releases say so. FRED's key is `DRISHTI_FRED_API_KEY`; without it the Bank of Canada still loads. One publisher down or a day GDELT
  skipped never fails a run.
- **One fetcher of the World Bank's WDI**: the world-development feed. Besides its ten headline indicators (the profile) it pulls, as
  series only, every `kind: wdi` code of `tools/realdata/sources.yaml` back to that file's `years.first` (`options.series-from`) and the
  world, its seven regions and four income groups (`options.aggregates`; an aggregate's series has no `WDI_PROFILE`, now optional in the
  contract). world-economy reads WDI from that feed's latest output (`publicsector.wdi_rows`, written into its cache in the API's shape,
  so the normaliser is unchanged) and never calls the WDI API; with no output it fails saying `run feed run world-development first`.
  `--no-wdi` is gone and world-economy loads all twelve of its kinds again (economy, macro-indicator, economic-forecast, labour-market
  and fiscal-position are back); it runs after world-development by schedule (06:30, then 06:45). `--scope` widens WGI and IMF series
  only: a new WDI code goes into `sources.yaml`. Tested on world-development output written from its recorded fixtures
  (`tools/feeds/tests/test_wdi_one_fetcher.py`).
- **Tests on recorded fixtures** (`tools/feeds/tests/test_publicsector.py`, never the network) and a browser test of the six screens on a
  scratch lake loaded from them (`test_public_sector_browser.py`); `tools/packgen/publicsector/make.py` writes the samples and READMEs.
- **Docs**: the Public sector guide and Tutorial 46 (two Help entries), the External data page's public-sector rows and section, the
  contract pages, OPERATIONS' modules.

### The pre-deal service and the exposure what-if in Java

- **The pre-deal check is a service of the exposure engine** (EXPOSURE_GUIDE.md section 18.9): `POST /api/v1/exposure/predeal` and the
  command `PREDEAL <counterparty> LIKE <trade> [<notional>] [REVERSE] [IN <netting set>]` (or, without a template, `PREDEAL <counterparty>
  <asset class> <notional> <maturity> [MTM <amount>]`), `GET /api/v1/exposure/predeal/grammar`, `drishti.py exposure predeal "PREDEAL …"`.
  The what-if with the trade added is held to the counterparty's stored credit limit on its measure (`PFE 95 peak` at its confidence;
  EEPE, EPE, peak EE) and to each tenor bucket's limit (`BUCKETS`, read from `credit-limit` now), and answers **approve** (exact data,
  within the limit and every bucket), **decline** (exact, over the limit or a bucket) or **refer** with the reason: a proxy answer (the
  `addon` method) only refers, never approves; so does no limit on record, a limit on a measure the engine does not compute, netting sets
  the person does not see, a stale run, the netting set not certain, or no exposure for the counterparty. Every answer shows the method
  and the template trade (copied: id, product, notional, the factor and side; or described), the limit before and after with the
  headroom and the buckets, and the exposure before, with and incremental; SA-CCR's incremental EAD says **under construction**
  (2.9.11.k). Computed as the person (a template only of a trade they see trade by trade, `403` otherwise; a counterparty they see none of
  `403`); every check audited (`ccr-predeal`, with its check id, decision, method, command and limit use). Code: `ExposurePreDeal`,
  `ExposurePreDealCommand`, `ExposurePreDealController` in the counterparty-risk server package `com.ash.drishti.server.exposure`.
- **Counterparties → Pre-deal check, the screen** (`/predeal`; `PREDEAL <GO>`, the menu item that ran `XWIF`, and **Pre-deal check ›**
  in the exposure explorer at a counterparty or a netting set; EXPOSURE_GUIDE.md sections 7 and 18.9, after the CCR cube mock-up C):
  the trade as a drishti-inputs Form (counterparty, netting set, a booked trade to copy or the trade described, the notional as money,
  the side), the server's verdict (approve, refer or decline with the lamp and the reasons; the limit and each tenor bucket within, near
  or over with before, with the trade, increment, use and headroom; EPE and EAD before and after), the one Explain of the check, and the
  what-if (the profile overlay with the limit and the incremental PFE per tenor on drishti-chart through drishti-risk; the figures and the
  table by tenor on drishti-grid). Every number is the server's; a typed command checks at once; a phone layout; gone with the banking
  module. The registry item `pre-deal-screen` is retired.
- **One limit rule, the server's** (new setting `drishti.risk.limit-near`, 0.8, in `config/engines/var.yaml`; `RiskLimits` in the banking
  module): every limit the module holds a figure to says **within**, **near** (from that share) or **breach** (over 100%) in the answer
  itself: each VaR scope and node (`limitStatus`, `limitNear`), the official record's nodes (read with the record), the VaR what-if
  (`limit`: the scope's limit, the use before and after, `statusBefore`, `status`), the pre-deal check's credit limit and tenor buckets,
  and the sensitivity ladder's cells (now `within` rather than `ok`). `MrSensitivities.NEAR` and exposure's `limit-near` are folded into
  it. **The Trading landing shows the server's status and computes none**: the book rows, the desk headline, the Breaches and Near limit
  tiles, the desk head's limit use by book and day, and both halves of the new-trade check (the VaR half reads the what-if's own `limit`;
  the console no longer divides by the book's limit). `limit_state` and the setting `trading.near-limit` are removed.
- **Every limit bar draws the server's status** (within green, near amber, breach red; a row without a status has no tone): the VaR
  explorer's limit tile and its scope tree's bars (the explorer's own amber at 75% and red at 90% are deleted), drishti-risk's VaR
  hierarchy tree (`LIMIT_USE_BANDS` 0.75/0.9/1 is replaced by `LIMIT_STATUS_TONES` on the node's `LIMIT_STATUS`; `limitBreaches` reads
  the status), the Risk home (its bars, pills and heat-map cells, and the VaR and credit breach counts, which counted a use of 100% as a
  breach), the MR cube's limit tile (its near tick at the server's `limitNear`), the exposure explorer's limit tile, bar and chip (its
  own amber was over 90%) and the market-risk pack's Home fact *a book over its limit inside a desk within its own*. drishti-tree's
  `bar` takes a status instead of bands (`{status, tones, words, max}`; `bandTone` becomes `statusTone`). The server adds the status
  where it was missing: the MR cube's headline (`limitStatus`, `limitNear`) and an exposure counterparty's credit limit (`status`,
  `near`).
- **One way to check a trade**: the exposure explorer's Pre-deal tab, its form and the console's what-if proxy (`POST /api/exposure/what-if`)
  are removed; the tab's address (`/exposure?scope=…&tab=predeal`) opens the check at that counterparty or netting set. The API and
  `drishti.py exposure whatif` keep the what-if alone.
- **The pre-deal answer says near** (by `drishti.risk.limit-near`, the one limit rule above): the limit and each bucket `within`, `near`
  (from that share: still approved, the reason says which) or `breach`; also `headroomBefore` and `near` on the limit, `increment`,
  `useBefore` and `headroomAfter` on each bucket, and with the exact method the IMM EAD (`ead`, α × EEPE) before, with and incremental.
  The one Explain explains a check (kind `predeal`: `ExposurePreDealExplainer`; the check made again, not audited twice).
- **Drishti Elements**: drishti-inputs' Form takes `doneText` ('' says nothing after a submit, for a page that shows the answer) and a
  field without help no longer prints "null"; drishti-risk's `risk.exposure-profile` takes `eepe: false` (an answer without EEPE, such as
  the proxy's: none drawn, never computed in the page).
- **The Trading landing's new-trade check** asks the pre-deal service for its exposure half: the decision, the limit use and every figure
  are the server's (the console no longer divides by the limit or picks the netting set); when the copied trade has no paths on the run
  the same check is asked described, and refers. Its verdict shows *Refer to credit* and *Declined: over the limit* with the reason.
- **The exact pre-deal exposure what-if (`POST /api/v1/exposure/what-if`, method `paths`) is computed by the Java exposure engine**
  (EXPOSURE_GUIDE.md sections 7, 18.7 and 19.5; COUNTERPARTY_ENGINES.md 6.4). `ExposureWhatIfMath` (`drishti-compute`) adds each
  candidate's paths to its netting set's value path by path and computes the set's collateral and exposure again with `ExposureMath`, the
  same code as every exposure figure; `ExposureWhatIfPaths` reads the scope and each joined netting set as the asker. The same request and
  the same answer field by field (only the `engine` and `note` texts say Java); no sandbox, no reactive connector, no compute workers: it
  answers on every server that runs exposure. Parity: the Python engine's answers on a book of four netting sets (margined with
  thresholds, MTA, IA, rounding and IM; unmargined with IA; no CSA; collateral posted), six what-ifs over the three collateral models,
  both rank rules, an unwind and a horizon change, recorded before it was retired (`ccr/whatif-parity.json`, `tools/ccr/`), are given
  again to the cent (`ExposureWhatIfMathTest`). A `copyOf` is made only of a trade the asker sees trade by trade (`403` otherwise).
- **The Python exposure engine is retired:** `drishti_compute.exposure` (`measures.py`, `whatif.py`) and its tests, the compute pool
  `exposure` and `DRISHTI_COMPUTE_EXPOSURE_WORKERS`, the counterparty-risk pack's reactive connector `exposure-whatif` with its kind,
  contract and command `XWIF`, the `exposure-result` parameters `detail` and `sets` (`ExposureWhatIfInputs`), and `DRS-5446`. A
  never-edited `exposure-whatif.yaml` connector file is removed at start (kept beside it as `.retired-<time>.bak`); an edited one stays,
  its kind listed as obsolete.
- **Tests**: `ExposurePreDealApiTest` (the what-if equal to a full recompute with the trade booked, figure by figure and date by date;
  approve; decline on the limit and on a bucket; refer on a proxy, no limit, a measure not computed and no exposure; two people at once
  with their own entitlements; the grammar; the audit); the console's trading check, menus and under-construction tests; `test_expcli`.

### drishti-feeds: external data into the lakes, every day

- **drishti-feeds: one module to pull external data into the lakes every day** ([EXTERNAL_DATA.md](docs/guides/EXTERNAL_DATA.md), Help → Data
  → External data feeds: one guide for the feeds and their sources). A feed is a feed file (`config/feeds/<feed>.yaml`: the source, its datasets and the pack, kind and table
  each loads, the target lake, the daily schedule, the licence with its redistribution and internal-only flag, API keys as `${ENV}`
  names only) and a `Feed` class in `tools/feeds/sources/` that pulls. The base class (`tools/feeds/feedbase.py`) does the rest:
  incremental pulls from a state file (`data/datafeeds/<feed>/state.json`, saved only when the whole run succeeds), the polite client
  (one User-Agent `DRISHTI_FEEDS_USER_AGENT` naming Drishti, no personal address; a pause between requests; retries with back-off
  and `Retry-After`; a download cache, so a broken run resumes), JSONL.gz per dataset and business date under
  `data/datafeeds/<feed>/<date>/` with a manifest of rows and SHA-256, a lock per feed, and a re-run of a date that replaces it whole.
- **Three load routes, no new writer**: `java` (the default: `lake build --engine java`, the parallel loader `LakeLoad` from the
  server's jar), `python` (`lake build`) and `inbox` (the files and their `.ready` with `lake:`, `sha256` and `rows` dropped into the
  data inbox; several tables or dates as one tar of `<table>/<date>/` folders). Every route replaces the dates it loads; a table new to
  the lake file gets its pack's recommended entry first (and the dataset's key as its id).
- **`drishti.py feed list|run|status|schedule`** (`tools/feeds/cli.py`; the wrappers `tools/feeds/feed.sh` and
  `tools/windows/feed.ps1`): `feed run <feed>|--all [--date D | --since D] [--load java|python|inbox|none] [--dry-run] [--snapshot]`,
  scheduler exit codes (0 ok, 1 failed, 2 refused, 3 locked, 4 partial) and one log line per run; `feed schedule --cron | --systemd |
  --windows` prints ready-to-use daily entries. Every run appends a line to the run ledger `data/datafeeds/ledger.jsonl`.
- **Admin → Data loads → Feeds**: every feed's last run, last success, rows, duration, failures and last error, and Run now
  (`GET /api/v1/admin/feeds`, `POST /api/v1/admin/feeds/{feed}/run`, audited; console tables on drishti-grid). A failed run raises
  the platform alert `data-feed-failed` through the one alert engine (the gauge `drishti.datafeed.failed`; a later success closes it;
  the same rule for Prometheus). Server settings `drishti.feeds.config`, `root`, `python`, `sample-seconds`.
- **The public-data refresh scripts are folded into the feeds** (no second way): `tools/publicdata/` is gone; its pack sources live
  in `tools/feeds/sources/` and run as the feeds `gleif` (into the new **`referencelake`**, core reference data: `config/lakes/referencelake.yaml`,
  `data/delta/referencelake/`, shipped empty like the other lakes), `us-equities` and `funds` (into `capitalmarket`; the index
  members now include the **Russell 2000 from IWM's** N-PORT holdings beside the Dow 30 from DIA and the S&P 500 from SPY),
  `yahoo-prices` (internal only, off as shipped), `world-economy` (internal only for the IMF forecasts, into `worldlake`),
  `news-and-markets` (internal only, into `newslake`) and `market-data` (incremental by day from its state, each document under its own
  date, `--since` for a backfill, into `capitalmarket`). The World Bank's WDI belongs to the public sector's world-development feed:
  world-economy reads it from that feed's output (see "One fetcher of the World Bank's WDI" above).
  Refreshing a pack's committed demo snapshot in `data/testdata` is `feed run <feed> --snapshot` (with `--internal-ok` for
  internal-only data), writing exactly where the scripts wrote. Their per-pack `.sh` and `.ps1` wrappers are replaced by the one
  wrapper per system; `DRISHTI_SEC_USER_AGENT` and `DRISHTI_GLEIF_USER_AGENT` are replaced by `DRISHTI_FEEDS_USER_AGENT`; the
  sources' downloads and builds move from `<data>/publicdata/` to `<data>/datafeeds/sources/`; `DRISHTI_LIVE_FETCH` is replaced by
  pytest's `--live` for the hand-run smokes.
- **Tests on recorded responses only**: every feed's pull, incremental state, an idempotent re-run, retries, the lock, the ledger and
  status, the inbox route's `.ready` and tar, the java and python routes into a temporary lake, the command line and the schedule
  output; Admin → Feeds in the console and the server; one `--live` smoke per feed for a person to run.

### Fixes (the train's bulk drill)

- **Delta lakes follow the Delta protocol's path rules exactly, tested against delta-rs both ways**
  ([DATA_LAKE_GUIDE.md section 14](docs/guides/DATA_LAKE_GUIDE.md#14-delta-protocol-compliance)). The native reader decoded Delta Kernel's
  plain file paths a second time, so a table with a Hive-escaped partition folder (Spark's and Databricks' `PRODUCT_GROUP=100%25`,
  `a%3Ab`) or one delta-rs wrote (`Money%20market`) could not be read; only a `java.nio` `file://` URI is decoded now
  (`LocalPaths.decodeUri`). The Java lake writer and the parallel loader take Kernel's target folder, which Kernel hands as a URI,
  decoded once (`LakeWriter.targetDirectory`): folders are Spark's Hive-escaped names and `add.path` is encoded exactly once (a value
  `100%` failed the load; the loader wrote `Money%2520market` in the log for the folder `Money market`). An empty partition value is
  null in `__HIVE_DEFAULT_PARTITION__`, as Spark writes it (Java writer, loader, Python writer). `lake build` refuses a partition column
  name a folder would change (`PRODUCT GROUP`, `a=b`, `a/b`). `tools/lake/test_delta_interop.py`: delta-rs writes and Drishti's Java
  reader reads; Drishti's three writers write and delta-rs, `pyarrow.dataset` and the Java reader read; 47 partition values (space, `%`,
  a literal `%2F`, `:`, `/`, `..`, `\`, control characters, quotes, Unicode, emoji, 200 characters, the sentinel text, empty, null);
  `LakeWriterTest`, `LocalPathsTest`. Upgrade: reload tables the parallel loader wrote since 2026-11-07 21:27 with such values
  (RELEASE_NOTES, upgrade step 13).
- **Column-mapped Delta tables (mode `name` or `id`, as Databricks writes them) are read correctly by every server path**: the fast
  paths that read Parquet columns by name (the id map and type-ahead, columns with partition values, vectors with partition texts, one
  entity's vector, the one-document read's id filter) read each column by its physical name (`col-<uuid>`), and the business date, a
  partition column, the load id's and a key range's statistics are looked up by it (`DeltaTable.Layout.phys`); before, such a table's
  columns read as empty. `DeltaColumnMappingTest`: column-mapped copies (written by delta-rs) of the layout, partitioned and vector
  fixtures answer exactly what the plain tables answer, both engines.
- **Python reads deletion vectors, column mapping and v2 checkpoints**: `tools/lake/deltaread.py` reads a table with delta-rs when its
  pyarrow reader reads it completely, else with Delta Kernel through the server's exec jar
  (`com.ash.drishti.deltalake.read.DeltaRowsCli`). delta-rs 1.6.6, the latest release, refuses deletion vectors and v2 checkpoints and
  reads a column-mapped table of reader version 2 as all nulls. `lake maintain`'s relayout and the Delta-to-Iceberg copy read through
  it. Fixtures `tools/lake/testdata/delta-features` (real deletion-vector files written by Kernel, a column-mapped table, a table only a
  checkpoint describes); `test_delta_interop.py`: Python returns exactly what the Java reader returns
  ([DATA_LAKE_GUIDE.md section 14.3](docs/guides/DATA_LAKE_GUIDE.md#143-table-features)).

- **The MR cube's capped measures are deterministic**: stressed VaR (`drishti.cube.mr.stressed-max-cells`, 100) and SBM
  (`sbm-max-cells`, 60) were counted per evaluation, and cells already cached by an earlier view were not counted, so which cells got a
  figure depended on what was asked before and in what order (desks × currency alone: stressed VaR on 100 of 186 cells; after the same
  rows by nothing and by risk class: 131), and a row's diversification summed whatever parts had one. A provider now declares a capped
  measure (`PivotProvider.cap`); the pivot engine lays the grid out without it, then computes it for the view's first N cells in the
  grid's order (row by row as shown, each row's columns left to right), each cell asked alone through the cache; every other cell carries
  the note, even when its figure is cached. Nothing is counted in shared state, so parallel queries get the same answer. A
  diversification (`diversification`, `diversificationByColumn`) is `null` when the total or a part with members has no figure, never a
  partial sum; a sort or a top N by a capped measure is refused in words. Every figure computed is the engine's own for the cell's scope,
  as before (`CappedMeasureTest`, `VarMrCubeCapTest`; PIVOT_GUIDE sections 9 and 29.2).
- **Iceberg tables follow the Iceberg spec exactly, tested against the Apache Iceberg Java library both ways**
  ([DATA_LAKE_GUIDE.md section 15](docs/guides/DATA_LAKE_GUIDE.md#15-iceberg-spec-compliance)). drishti-iceberg percent-decoded a
  `file:` data file path holding a `%` (`FileAccess`, and `relocate`'s matching), so a table the library, pyiceberg or Spark partitioned
  by a value such as `a/b`, `100%`, `a:b` or `é` (folders `g=a%2Fb`, `g=100%25`, `g=a%3Ab`, `g=%C3%A9`) failed with *no such file*;
  paths are opened as written now. Expiring snapshots removed a snapshot a tag named and left the tag dangling (the library could no
  longer load the table): expiry keeps every branch's and tag's snapshot, and removing snapshots removes the refs and statistics entries
  that named them. Moving `main` dropped its retention settings (`min-snapshots-to-keep`, `max-snapshot-age-ms`). Delete files were matched
  to data files by a text key, so an equality delete of the null partition also deleted rows of the partition holding the text `null`.
  The library engine turned a root with a space, `%` or non-ASCII letters into `java.nio`'s encoded URI, so Hadoop wrote the lake into a
  folder named `my%20lake` beside the root. Drishti's writers left the other partition values null in a table another engine had
  re-partitioned (its files then vanished from pruned reads): such a table is refused for writing, by name. A stale Hadoop
  `.version-hint.text.crc` made the library log a checksum error after each Drishti commit. `lake maintain`'s figures read gzip-compressed
  metadata files. `IcebergSpecInteropTest` (26 partition values under eight transforms, position and equality deletes, a tag and a branch
  through expiry, a root with a space, `%` and unicode, a re-partitioned table), `LiteralPathsTest`, `TableUpdateRefsTest`,
  `test_maintain_iceberg.py`. Upgrade: RELEASE_NOTES, upgrade step 14.
- **The old explain endpoints answer for one release**: `GET /api/v1/var/explain`, `/api/v1/var/explain/matrix` and
  `/api/v1/pivot/mr/explain` (and their `/api/v1/risk/...` paths) answered `404` since the one Explain replaced them; like every other
  moved path of this release they now answer with the 2.9.11.d body (the one Explain's `why.answer`, its `matrix`, and the MR cube's
  `factorOverlay` note), `Deprecation: true` and a `Link` to `/api/v1/explain?kind=var&part=why` (`&view=matrix`)
  (`VarExplainApiTest`, against the recorded 2.9.11.d shape; API_GUIDE, RELEASE_NOTES).

- **Drishti's lake writer and a partition value with a space**: Kernel hands a partition's folder percent-encoded
  (`PRODUCT_GROUP=Fixed%20income`); the writer wrote the file there while every read looked in `Fixed income`, so a Calypso or Murex
  trade load by `PRODUCT_GROUP` failed with "the write failed, nothing was committed". The writer now decodes a `file:` URI exactly as the
  reads do (`LakeWriterTest`).
- **The public-sector feeds keep their working history as JSON Lines** (the data standard): a series' points, the kept releases and
  GDELT's per-day country aggregates under `<data>/datafeeds/<feed>/history/` are `.jsonl`, a row a line.
- **A pack filled by a feed counts as served without the demo connector**: `PacksServedWithoutDemoTest` accepts a Delta connector
  reading the lake an enabled feed loads the kind into (the six public-sector packs, `worldlake` and `newslake`); PACK_DEVELOPER_GUIDE
  step 16 says so.
- **A table's `highlight`**: a `table` panel accepts `highlight` (an expression per row, as a ladder has), which the GLEIF entity's
  parents chain uses for the entity itself; Rachana refused it with DRS-2023 (`PackSutrasTest`; RACHANA_REFERENCE's table options).
- Tests brought up to date: the demo lake's trades by `PRODUCT_TYPE` (Endur) and `PRODUCT_GROUP` (Calypso, Murex); the engines' and
  publishers' sources found in their domain modules; `css_visual_check.py` names the demo lake's variable through `lakeconfig`; importing
  `drishti-stack/stack.py` in a test leaves no `__pycache__` in the checkout.

### Fixes (pushing into a new lake)

- **A table created by its first load gets its kind's key as `id:`**
  ([DATA_LAKE_GUIDE.md sections 3.4, 4.0 and 5.1](docs/guides/DATA_LAKE_GUIDE.md#34-pushing-data-from-your-own-programs)). A lake made
  by the data inbox (or a table it added) copied the pack's entry without `id:`, so every row was rejected (*no id (field 'id' is missing
  or empty)*) unless the `.ready` file gave `key:`. The entry now takes the `.ready` file's `key:`, else the pack's ingest key, else the
  single `key:` field of the kind's data contract (`PackEntry.contractKey`, `feedroute.contract_key`); the parallel loader falls back to
  the pack's key for an entry still without `id:`. A tar into a new lake works the same way.
- **A tar may mix the tables of one kind**: a tar's folder may be a table name (`trade_endur`, `trade_calypso`, `trade_murex`), which
  resolves to its kind and connector, as well as a kind name; names compare with `_` and `-` alike (`risk_hierarchy` is the kind
  `risk-hierarchy`). The inbox adds each table's entry to the lake (it used to add only the kind's first). Java `Routes`, Python
  `feedroute` (which now reads a lake-form pack's `lake-tables:`) and `lake build`'s tars alike.
- **`lake build --engine java --key`** passes the key to the loader for a lake of `config/lakes/` (it was dropped, and an entry without
  `id:` rejected every row).
- Tests: `NewLakeKeysTest` (the real loader: one file and a tar of `trade_endur`, `trade_calypso` and `risk_hierarchy` over two dates
  into a lake that does not exist, every row landed, the archive again replaced), `test_feedroute.py`, `test_javaload.py`.

The five new lakes ship as lake files with no tables (`config/lakes/<lake>.yaml` and their jar copies), and **nothing shipped points at them**: every connector, rule and setting reads `demo` (guarded by `tools/test_empty_lakes.py`); a site points at them itself. The demo lake's one-time move and `build_demo_lakes` treat a folder holding only its README.md as empty.

- **Demo and real data never mix** (DATA_LAKE_GUIDE.md section 6; found on tutorial 45's real run, where the demo ComSwap `TRD 1000001`
  still opened after `trade-endur` was pointed at risklake). The cause was the packs' sample documents: the `demo` connector serves
  every kind and, on a live read, is asked before the (non-live) lake connectors. Now, once a kind's routed connector or any Delta or
  Iceberg connector serving it names a lake other than `demo`, the samples no longer answer for that kind, by id or in a search
  (`SourceRouter.ownLake`); a server whose connectors all read `demo` is unchanged, and the published results lakes (`var-official`,
  `ccr-official`) do not count. Admin → Health marks a pack *DEGRADED* when its connectors read more than one lake
  (`packs[].lakes`, `packs[].lakeWarning`: *trading's connectors read different lakes: demo (trade-calypso, trade-murex); risklake
  (trade-endur)…*). Tutorial 45 keeps `union: true` in its `trade-endur.yaml` (a connector file replaces the pack's template whole).

    system; every Delta table is measured before and after (version, data files, rows, every data file present); any difference or error
    moves everything back; it refuses, saying why, when the target exists, when anything there belongs to no lake, across file systems,
    for an Iceberg table, for a table that does not open, or while a build or load holds the lake's lock; it never deletes; it runs once,
    recorded in `data/delta/demo/_drishti-lake/relocated.json`.
  - **`lake:` in a `.ready` file** names the lake a file goes to, over a rule's `lake:` and the inbox's default; a lake with no file yet is
    **created** by the load (`config/lakes/<lake>.yaml`: format delta, root `${drishti.data.dir:./data}/delta/<lake>`, the routed pack's
    recommended entry), its tables at `data/delta/<lake>/<domain>/<table>` (`risklake/trading/trade_endur`, `risklake/risk/scenario-pv`).
    The Data loads page, the load report (`warning`) and `drishti.py dataload status` say *loaded into risklake, but no connector reads
    it: point market-risk's connectors at it (lake: risklake) and restart* (`SourceRegistry.lakesRead`).
  - **Connectors: two forms, both permanent** (product owner, 2026-11-07): `lake: <name>` (the lake file's root: a folder, `s3://...` or
    `mem://...`) or an explicit `root:` path or URI with `domain`, `table.<kind>` and `layout.<kind>.*` (tables no lake file describes, a
    vendor's Delta table on S3), with no warning. A connector that gives both uses its own values over the lake file's, said in the log,
    by `lake check` and on Admin → Connectors (a warning on the field). Before: such a connector was refused, and the path form warned.
  - **The connectors generated with the demo lake's old root follow it:** once the demo lake is moved, the server rewrites each connector
    file whose `root:` is the demo lake's old default (`${DRISHTI_DELTA_ROOT:./data/delta}` and its variants) to `lake: demo` with
    `lake-tables:` (`LakeFiles.adoptDemo`, also the first step of `lake migrate-config`), the file kept beside it
    (`<name>.yaml.before-lake-<time>.bak`), a table the demo lake file lacks added from the connector's layout; a `var-pv-stream`
    connector's `lake:` folder of that form becomes `lake: demo` (the plugin takes a lake's name; the market-risk pack's `pv-updates`
    ships `lake: demo`). A Delta connector with neither `root` nor `lake` reads `<data>/delta/demo`. An Iceberg lake file without a root is
    at `<data>/iceberg/<lake>`.
  - **One place spells where lakes are:** drishti-lakeconfig (`Lakes.defaultRoot`, `Lakes.DEMO_ROOT_ENV`) and `tools/lake/lakeconfig.py`
    (`root()`, `DEMO_ROOT_ENV`, `DEMO_ROOT_REF`); `lake demo`, `build_demo_lakes.py`, `bulk_trades.py`, `varcli`, `packmake`, the pack
    generators, the doc-shot and bench harnesses, `drishti-stack` and `schemakit` resolve through it. The guard `tools/test_lake_paths.py`
    fails on a lake folder or the demo root's variable spelled in code (Java, Python, JavaScript) outside the lake configuration.
  - **The command-line loaders read `lake:` too** (`tools/lake/feedroute.py`, `lake build`): a `.ready` file's `lake:` names a lake of
    `config/lakes/` (`--lake` on the command line wins); its keys are the inbox's, one list (`test_feedroute.py` compares them with
    `ReadyNote.KEYS`).
  - **Fixed:** an archive's rollback undid the load in the folder named like the inbox's lake (`demo`) rather than the lake's root.
  - **Tools follow:** `build_demo_lakes.py`, `lake demo`, `load-delta.sh`/`.ps1`, `bulk_trades.py`, `varcli` and `start-server.ps1` default

    Windows CI and `deploy/lake-maintenance.yaml` name `data/delta/demo`.

- **One Python runtime: every Python run on the server's compute pools** (SYNTHESIS A11, Brief 3; PYTHON_COMPUTE.md section 19; lean & streamlined):
  - **The pool `python`** (`config/compute/compute.yaml`) runs code people write: python visuals and Python measures of reports, boards and alerts,
    Transforms behind Python datasets, Python-driven tables and models, the Notebook's Python cells, the Transform editor's step-by-step run, a frame's
    profile and an item's own tests. Its engine is `drishti_compute.items` (the console's worker logic, moved into the compute SDK). The server's one
    door is `PythonRuns` (also the one `TransformRunner`); `PythonFrames` reads every run's rows **as the person running it**; `PythonTestRuns` runs an
    item's `tests:` on the pool, so **publishing a Python item with a failing test is refused whichever way it is asked** (before: the console's gate only).
    New server routes `GET /api/v1/bi/python/runtime`, `POST /api/v1/bi/python/{check, visual, cell, steps, profile}`,
    `POST /api/v1/tables/editor/python/run` and `GET /api/v1/tables/editor/python/runtime`; the plan's Python tier is `python` (was `console`).
  - **Safety:** a new pool setting `isolation: strict` (Linux, fork mode): the worker leaves the network at start (a user and network namespace with no
    interface) and each request's child is held by **Landlock** to the Python installation and its own scratch folder before its code runs (C++ file and
    socket calls included: `pyarrow.fs` cannot read a home folder); the item's own CPU and memory limits; the import guard and audit hook; **pinned
    libraries** (`config/compute/locks/python.lock`, every file's sha256, written by the new `tools/python_lock.py` from `python.in`): the server checks
    the pool's interpreter against the pins and refuses every run, naming each package, while one differs; **every run audited** (`python-run`); a
    Transform's or Python table's rows **checked against their contract** (columns and types; the sample run also keys and never-empty columns), refused in
    words (`DRS-9075`); text the contract declares a date or a timestamp is read as one first (dates reach Python as ISO text). Where the strict sandbox cannot be had (**Windows**, a Linux without Landlock or user namespaces) code does not run and says why.
  - **Compute:** requests and results carry **files** as they are (`ComputeRequest.files`, `ComputeResult.files`, over Drishti*net too), for Arrow
    frames of any type and a Transform's Parquet.
  - **Enabled:** the Python-driven table editor's **Sample run** and its Notebook's **Run cells on the server**, and the Notebook page's **Python cells**
    (`POST /bi/notebook/python`); `python-table-runs` removed from the under-construction registry.
  - **Deleted from the console** (2,089 lines): `core/pyrunner.py`, `core/pyrunner_worker.py`, `core/transform_cli.py`, `core/pytests.py`,
    `core/python_items.py`, the quant stand-in `core/quant/`, the Py-node endpoint `routes/pynode_routes.py` (`/internal/py/*`), the snippet examples'
    pandas runner in `core/prep_snippets.py`, and the `bi.python.*` settings; its Python routes pass to the server. **Deleted from the server:**
    `ProcessTransformRunner`, `ConsolePythonRunner` and `drishti.bi.transform.python`, `runner`, `work-dir`, `console-url`, `console-token`.
    A static test bans compute libraries (pandas, NumPy, SciPy, polars, DuckDB, statsmodels, scikit-learn) in the console's code
    (`tests/test_console_runs_no_compute.py`, in the gate). `statsmodels` left the default `python-packages` (it was never installed or pinned).
  - Tests: `drishti-compute/src/test/python/test_items.py` (every interface, the sandbox's refusals in words, the kernel's refusal of a C++ read, a
    limit stopping one request), `PythonRunsTest` (refusals until safe, the pin check, a measure, a Transform and failures through a strict worker, the
    audit); the console's tests now check what it passes to the server; the browser tests run a Notebook cell, the editor's sample run and its
    contract check on a real pool; `tests/test_python_runtime_answers.py` shows the Python model `desk-pnl-vs-exposure-py` answering each
    reader from their own inputs and every tile of the board `python-wall` drawing on the pool (refusals before; owner-approved; skipped with the
    reason where the sandbox or the pinned interpreter is missing). The BI foundation parity fixtures are unchanged (compute off).
- **The Trading lens is configuration** (product panel A19, TRADING_LENS.md section 3.7): `trading.yaml` unhides `DPNL`, `PNL` and `SENS`

  counted in every drill's Java lanes, against budgets from a measured run with headroom (cold 590 ms, budget 3,000 ms; warm p95 18 ms,
  budget 100 ms; 0.9 MB allocated, budget 4 MiB).

- **The old BI code deleted; pivot formulas are Rachana** (BI_FOUNDATION_2911E.md section 11, the deletion; the product owner: no
  critique, delete the old, fold the formulas within d). Deleted: `DatasetParser` version 1, `DatasetDefParser`'s `rachana: 2` form,
  `ModelDefParser`'s `datasets:` form, DEL's checker, lowering, printer and catalogue (`bi/expr/functions.yaml`), `ExprParser`,
  `LegacySources`, `StableIds`, the converters and `drishti.py bi migrate --expressions` / `--models`, and the pivot's
  `FormulaParser` (7,873 lines removed and 1,467 added outside the docs, net 6,406 fewer; 6,000 fewer in main code). BI's folder refuses `datasets/` and `models/` in the old forms (`DRS-9196`). A pivot formula
  is read by Rachana's one parser (`FormulaLowering`; `count()` with no argument counts the rows); saved formulas (views, their versions,
  formula functions) are rewritten into Rachana at start, in place, once, audited (`PivotFormulaMigration`). A promoted run writes a table
  that reads it (`from: { run }`). Build → New pack writes a deep kind's BI as tables of the table layer (`config/bi/tables/`) and a
  `rachana: 3` model, and a pack's `config/bi/tables/` is loaded as table items. A pack's table that would break someone else's
  published report is held, as a dataset was. `tables migrate` reads BI's first expression syntax (an item without `expressions: 2`:
  `&&`, `||`, `!`, `c ? a : b`, `[Measure]`) with Rachana's parser, so an installation that never ran the removed `bi migrate --expressions`
  still migrates. **Parity:** the 76 formulas recorded on the old parser
  (1,801 SQL-path cells, 76 Java answers) give the same answers in their Rachana text (19 rewritten), but one changed by the product owner's decision (2026-11-07):
  `count(where = CCY in [])`, refused on the old SQL path, answers 0 on both paths (an empty list matches nothing); BiFoundationParityTest (6,468
  answers) and BiParityTest (13 cases) exact. `ModelDefTest` on `rachana: 3` tables and a model. Docs: BI_LANGUAGE_REFERENCE out of Help
  (Q27; `/help/expressions` leads to Rachana's expressions, `/help/sql` to the API guide's Drishti SQL), RACHANA_REFERENCE (`count()`),
  PIVOT_GUIDE (formulas in Rachana), BI_GUIDE (what BI reads; packs' BI content), CLI_GUIDE (`bi migrate`), SCHEMA_TO_PACK, tutorial 17
  and OPERATIONS (back up `config/tables`), tutorial 37 (formula language), FUNCTIONS.md regenerated.
- Decided (product owner, 2026-11-07, decision A, overriding BI_DESIGN 8.5's "security binds to the dataset"): **nobody sees more data
  after the upgrade.** A row rule on one fact also limits the related rows of another fact of the model: the new rule function
  `related_rows('alias')` (Rachana's catalogue, rule scope) keeps a table's rows that share a key (a dimension both reference, or a
  reference between them) with the rows of that alias the reader sees, written by BI's engine as `EXISTS` over the other table at the
  question's dates with that table's own rules; a rule it cannot honour (no such alias, no shared key) refuses the question.
  `tables migrate` writes `related_rows('<fact>')` on each other table of a `rachana: 1` dataset for the role whose rule named that fact
  (where it wrote `true` before; a rule naming several tables, or this table and another, gives `false`). A live table's history follows its
  table's rules on its group columns (a history without groups refuses a limited reader). Read outside BI's engine (a table on its own
  through the table layer) the rule lets no row through. A model that already said `may-see-all` keeps it: the shipped `trading-risk` is
  unchanged, and BiFoundationParityTest stays exact. MultiFactTest (the desk head sees her desk's limits only) and LiveHistoryTest (her
  desk's samples only; refused without groups) keep their limits; NoMoreRowsAfterMigrationTest migrates every shipped sample of
  `bi/before-tables` and checks every recorded case as `rita`, `hana` and `ann`: no answer has more rows than before. BI_DESIGN 8.5 and
  example 8 corrected; RACHANA_REFERENCE (`related_rows`), TABLES_GUIDE, RELEASE_NOTES, TROUBLESHOOTING. A per-table exposure access
  design goes to 2.9.11.h's security discussion.
- **Removed: BI's authoring screens of the old forms** (decided 2026-11-07: one way per job; EDITORS.md, where the model diagram is
  a later read-only picture). The dataset wizard (`wizard_routes.py`, `drishti_bi-wizard*.js`, `drishti_bi-wizard.css`), the new-dataset
  wizard (`drishti_bi-dataset-layer.js`, `drishti_bi-dataset-steps.js`), the model designer (`drishti_bi-model-designer.js` and its
  `-tabs`, `-fields`, `-calc`, `-ai` scripts; `model_routes.py`'s compose, parse, measure, new, contract and dataset-yaml calls), the 2.1
  dataset page and Model view (`dataset.html`, `model.html`, `drishti_bi-model.js`) and the Datasets page's *Start a model from the packs*:
  they wrote `rachana: 1` and `2` files, which BI refuses (`DRS-9196`). Their addresses redirect to Build › Tables & models (`/bi/md/<item>`
  → the model, `/bi/datasets/new[-layer]` → a new table, `?edit=<item>` → that table) or to the table's page (`/bi/d/`, `/bi/m/`). *Make it
  a model* writes a `rachana: 3` model. The test stacks seed tables and models of the layer (`bi_samples.migrate_texts`). The tests of the
  removed screens are deleted; the tutorials' picture scripts that drove them (`tools/docs/shots` t10, t11, t13, t15, t18, t44) go with
  the 2.9.11.g documentation rewrite.
- **Fixed (BI on the table layer, found by the server suite):** `tables migrate` kept a dataset's `hidden-for: { roles, columns }` as
  those columns' `hidden-for` (it was lost), a narrowing's `columns: [a, b]` as those columns of the base (it was dropped, so every base
  column showed), a `rachana: 1` dataset's audience on its tables (they were open to every reader), and refuses a `keep:` other than
  `latest by <column>`, a group aggregate it does not know and a grouped dataset's rule on a column it is not grouped by, as BI did.
  BI reads a column's `unit:` as its currency again (a column of the table or an ISO code), so the currency guard (`DRS-9158`) works; a
  column's `hidden-for` hides it from those roles; a table over a table may only read the base's columns (`DRS-9105`). A model of the
  layer goes through the publish gate after the layer's checks (one name in the catalogue, the safeguard, the contract against its
  published version). A model a reader may not open is never answered by a table of that name. A table built on a model is the model's
  consumer in lineage and impact. A refresh asked of a table refreshed on its own schedule is that table's run, in its history. The
  dataset page lists each table's row rules. Build › Tables & models lists a file of the tables folder once (BI reads that folder too).
  The AI's prompts call a model's table a table. `tables migrate` keeps a `rachana: 1` dataset's refresh schedule on its tables (a table's own
  first) and its expected values of a measure that is one aggregate of a table as that table's tests (`agg: count`, `agg: sum, column: …`).
  A model's review shows the first rows of its fact table; a model's delete confirmation counts what reads it (its lineage); an entity view
  on a model's table opens the entity's kind (a model's describe says it: `entity`); the catalogue's Datasets tab lists tables.
- Decided (product owner, 2026-11-06): **tables use look-ups, models join**. The table editor says *look-up* (Source and look-ups, + Look-up); combining tables row by row is a model's relationships (EDITORS.md section 2, VIRTUAL_TABLES.md V10a, TABLES_GUIDE).
- **The switch: BI reads the table layer** (BI_FOUNDATION_2911E.md section 7.3, step 5). The shipped datasets and models were migrated
  with `drishti.py tables migrate` (dry run first: 34 items converted, 0 refused; 103 expressions, 22 rewritten DEL into Rachana) into
  `config/tables/bi/` (24 tables and 10 models); `config/bi/datasets` and `config/bi/models` are gone and the two live reports name their
  models. BI's folder reads `config/tables` (`drishti.tables.root`): a table is an item of the kind `table`, a model of the kind `model`, as
  the editors store them; BI's models read published tables of both kinds. A table is said in BI's terms by `LayerTables` (the source's
  paths as columns, a grain as BI's `each`, `keep: { latest }` as one row per key, rules and masked columns as BI's security, a table over a
  table as BI's narrowing, `materialize: { live }` as BI's live mode); a model's `history:` samples its live tables (Q14).
  **One parser:** BI reads Rachana only (`Expressions` over Rachana's parser; `NodeLowering` lowers Rachana's tree to BI's compiler tree and
  `NodeText` writes it back as Rachana); DSQL's inline expressions become Rachana (`SqlToRachana`); the expression check runs Rachana's
  checked mode; the pivot measures BI hands the engine come from Rachana's tree. **TablesService reads BI's item store** beside the files
  (`BiItemTableStore`), so the pivot, Sutras and Flight see the tables and models the editors publish. **Parity:** `BiFoundationParityTest`
  reproduces all 6,468 recorded answers (23 files) value for value; one difference was found and fixed at its cause: the pivot engine's
  formulas compared a value with `None` by SQL's rule (never true), so `Open MTM`'s totals (`... && TRADE_STATUS != null`, the migrator's
  rewrite of Q1) were empty; `x == None` and `x != None` now test for a missing value in the formula's Java and SQL forms.

- **The editors of the table layer** (docs/architecture/SHARED_SCREENS.md groups 1 to 4; TABLES_GUIDE.md section 11): **Build › Tables & models** (`/build/tables`, also on BI's rail). One shell: the objects with search | the editor with the **live YAML below it** (a visual edit is written back by the layer's own writer, the file's header kept, the edited line highlighted; a YAML edit is checked as typed and shows in the visual side; an invalid line is marked and the visual side keeps the last valid version) | a **preview read on the server as you** (rows, the totals of the number columns by the pivot engine, checks, the cost of a join across connectors, Used by). Visual / YAML / Both remembered per person (the server's preference store); Validate, Preview, History, Impact, Save draft and **Propose for review** (BI's four-eyes review: the item kinds `table` and `model` in the layer's form, approved through the layer's checks); **+ New** steps for a table (columns suggested from a sample of the source), a model (the four questions) and a Python-driven table. The **table editor**: the source and its look-ups as rows with the cross-connector cost (`drishti.tables.scan-warn-rows`), columns as a checklist with computed columns in Rachana (type-ahead from the function catalogue), and a **Text** toggle (the table as one Rachana statement, read back on the server). The **model editor**: Overview, Tables, Fields, Measures (each **?** opens its card: formula, plain words, a worked value, used by; **adds up?** from the pivot engine's functions), Hierarchies, Row rules, Masks and the **Access** matrix. The **Python-driven table editor**: the build function beside its output contract, inputs, schedule, pool and limits, templates (join and derive, resample, statistics per group, an approved feed) and **Notebook → Turn into table**; the **sample run on the server's compute pool `python`** (see *One Python runtime* above). The API is `/api/v1/tables/editor/*`.

- **Resizable panels and columns on every screen**, one shared component (`static/js/drishti_resize.js`, `static/css/drishti_resize.css`), declared by markup (`data-resize="panel"`, `data-resize="columns"`): splitters on the VaR explorer's Scopes panel, the exposure explorer, Help's contents list, the Build workbench (Data and Details), the pivot's Fields, the BI report designer's panes, the BI model designer and a view's Context column; column resize on the VaR tree (CSS-grid rows), every data table, BI grids and matrices and the pivot grid (HTML tables). Widths are kept per person and per mode in the browser (the VaR explorer with Parametric on or off), never on the server; a double-click or `Home` resets; `←` `→` move a focused line; a column has a least width; off on phones. The designer grid's column edge, the workspace divider and the screen grid's split now use the same component and their own handles are gone. USER_GUIDE "Resize panels and columns". The render tests compare the library's drawing without the console's resize handles (its splitters and column handles are console chrome; the grid's split is compared by its name) and their console page loads the component as `base.html` does (CLIENT_RENDERER.md section 14.1).

- **Fix (identity, SQLite):** two identity databases read at the same moment in one JVM could swap the times of their rows (created, updated, last sign-in). Hibernate's `TIMESTAMP_UTC` reads every instant through one calendar shared by the whole JVM, and the SQLite driver sets each row's time on it; on SQLite the identity database now reads instants as `TIMESTAMP` in UTC, a calendar per read (the same epoch milliseconds are stored, so existing databases read unchanged; PostgreSQL unchanged). This was the last cause of `NetLastAdminTest`'s flakes: the node that disabled the seeded administrator had read a peer's newer seeded record in place of its own and wrote it back. A test reads two SQLite databases at once.

Same tests and assertions (TEST_HARNESS section 3.12).

### Tests and the drill

- **The browser-test harness ([TEST_HARNESS.md](docs/architecture/TEST_HARNESS.md), ARCHITECTURE.md section 22, BENCHMARK.md
  section 18).** The drill's browser lane is handed out by test (`--dist loadgroup`): a file that keeps a server or state is one group
  on one worker, a small independent test marked `spread` is a unit of its own. Each worker starts one Chromium (contexts reused per
  width and reset between tests), one stand-in console and a pool that keeps at most one idle real server; the pack ViewModels are
  bound once per run for every worker. The two render suites are split into one spread test per pack Sutra, their pages drawn four at
  a time and served over HTTP on the worker's port. Pages wait on a settled signal (`Drishti.settled`: charts drawn, nothing
  aria-busy, no request unanswered, the page quiet; inert for people) instead of fixed pauses. Scratch ports come in blocks of 1,250
  per worker (up to 12 workers). The lane's workers come from the memory available (`drill_plan.py workers`), its memory is sampled
  (`drill_monitor.py`), and every browser file over 300 s is flagged (`drill_plan.py budget`, `tools/drill-budgets.txt`).
  `test_browser_rules.py` checks the rules for browser tests on the source. The console parses a pack's YAML once while its files
  are unchanged (a cold page spent about a second of the event loop on it, for every user).
- **The quick file checks run in the gate.** Every test that only reads files is marked `static` (the Java launch guard, the asset
  names, the branding guard, the under-construction registry, the front-end policy, the browser-test rules, the scratch ports, the
  contrast of the themes, no shared user state, the console does not aggregate, the engines' help pages, the settings catalogue, the
  command catalog; in the tools the READMEs, the pack guides, the IDE run configurations, the exports' JSON Lines and the Knowledge
  pages). The gate's new `gate-checks` job runs them (`drill_plan.py static`), in about half a minute; the console lanes run
  `-m "not static"` and the tools' lanes leave them out. Before, the Java launch guard ran in the browser lane, because its text names
  Chromium, and failed a drill an hour in. A static test starts nothing: `test_browser_rules.py` checks it (TEST_HARNESS.md rule 11).
- **`tools/drill.sh --gate`** runs the gate alone, on any branch, and stops (a check of a few minutes before a drill). Measured: the
  whole gate 145 s, its quick file checks 32 s.
- **The browser lane measured three times with the harness** (TEST_HARNESS.md section 5, BENCHMARK.md section 18): 1,515 s,
  1,735 s and 1,554 s on 9 workers, against 3,654 to 3,768 s for develop's lane on 3 workers in the last drill; about 36 GB at its
  peak, at least 10.8 GB left available. **Fixed:** the refresh test read the freshness label after a fixed 1.1 s pause and, on a
  loaded lane, read "stale"; it now waits for the label. The docs-rot check counts a variable the console tests' helper modules read
  (the harness's `DRISHTI_BROWSER_PROFILE`, `DRISHTI_BROWSER_PAGES_AT_ONCE`) as read.
