### Part C: virtual tables for every consumer (decided 2026-11-04)

- **The decisions (VIRTUAL_TABLES.md section 10, status decided).** V1 to V5 as recommended, V6 (built with the DEL fold: one migration,
  one parity proof, two drills), and V7 to V15: many tables over one source with reads shared per request, new tables offered never made,
  editors and reading as the source, models across connectors with the scan warning, dates as the source has them, names unique across
  virtual and stored tables, Sutras reading tables, DuckDB the one SQL engine reached only through the existing executors, one grammar.
- **Reading a table (TABLES_GUIDE.md section 7a).** `tables.read.TableReads`: a table resolved to its root source (a table over a table
  reads its base's source with the base's grain and filter, its own added), the source's documents read once per business date and
  known-at time for every table over it within one request, the rows computed by the preview's one computation
  (`Preview.rows(table, doc, ...)`, now shared), the reader's access applied; a reader's condition in Rachana over the table's columns
  (a masked column cannot filter); dates: none is the latest, a date not held is refused, an undated source is today's rows, known-at
  refused where the source keeps no history; more than `drishti.tables.read-max-rows` (2,000,000) refused, never cut short. It is the
  layer's `ModelAnswers.Rows` too, so a model's answer reads the same rows.
- **One access rule.** `answer.TableAccess`: a table's rules for the reader's roles, the table and its columns hidden from a role, the masks
  for a reader without the raw power; `ModelAnswers` now asks it (moved out of `ModelAnswers`, not copied).
- **Names and joins.** `Catalogue.clashes` refuses a virtual table named like a stored table (`DRS-9616`); `tables check --stored`.
  `read.ScanEstimate` warns of a large unfiltered side of a model's join across connectors.
- **New tables offered.** `read.TableOffer` and `drishti.py tables offer NAME --sample FILE (--kind K | --lake L --table T) [--grain]
  [--write]`: one typed column per scalar field of a sample, the id key when unique, the lists of objects as grains to choose; `--write`
  accepts it as a new file, refused when the name is taken.
- **Codes.** `DRS-9615` (a read refused, HTTP 422), `DRS-9616` (a name clash, 409) and `DRS-9609` (no such table, 404) in the server's
  error codes, TABLES_GUIDE.md and API_GUIDE.md.
- **The server reads virtual tables (V5).** `server.tables.TablesService` (`drishti.tables.root`, `read-max-rows`, `scan-warn-rows`): the
  catalogue read again when a file under it changes, a table named like a stored kind or lake table refused at load and never served, and
  the reads of one request for one person over `DataViewService.walk` (the kind's entitlement, the edition, the person's masks on every
  document; a row rule knows `user.name`, `user.roles`, `user.desk`, `user.desks`, `user.email` as BI's do; rules off while security is
  off). A column masked at the source for the reader is masked in the table.
- **The pivot reads virtual tables.** Source `table:<domain>.<name>` (PIVOT_GUIDE.md section 3): listed with the kinds a person may open,
  its columns as fields (masked ones left out), staged in the pivot engine's executor. `StagedRows` is the one staging of rows in hand
  (moved out of `PanelSources`, which uses it too).
- **Sutras read virtual tables (V13, in 2.9.11.e).** `source: { table: <domain>.<name>, where, limit, as-of }` on any panel that reads
  data (RACHANA_REFERENCE.md, TABLES_GUIDE.md section 7a; the Sutra schema): the rows, read for the page's viewer through the table layer
  (`TableRows`, the engine's one port to it), are `$src`; `where` keeps rows with the page's context; a page built for nobody in particular
  reads no table. **The viewer through the view pipeline** (its own commit, mechanical): one `ViewerContext` (user, roles, attributes, raw
  power, masks, kinds) per request, made by `Entitlements.viewer`, passed with every call of `ViewPipeline`, the screen, live streams and
  explain in place of the masks-and-kinds pair, never kept shared. `TablesService` reads for a `ViewerContext` (the viewer's masks and kinds,
  so an embedded app's masks hold too). `SutraTableSourceTest`: two people with different row rules and masks on the same page, in turn and
  sixteen at once, each get their own rows and masks.
- **A declared mask always holds (a leak fixed).** A column a virtual table declares `masked: true`, and a column a BI dataset lists under
  `security.masked`, was masked only when the installation masked some field of its own (`drishti.security.redact` not empty): "raw" was
  read as "nothing masked for this person". It is now the raw power itself (`Entitlements.rawPower`: a role with `raw`, never through an
  embedded app), so a declared mask holds for every reader without it, whatever `redact` names. The `ViewerContext`'s `raw`, the tables'
  reads and BI's `DatasetService.masks` use it; BI's per-reader result key names it. **For the parity test:** in an installation with an
  empty `redact` (the shipped one is not empty, so the shipped demo's figures do not change), readers without the raw power now see masked:
  `trading-risk-counterparties` and `counterparty-exposure-counterparties` NAME and RATING, `trading-risk-trades` COUNTERPARTY,
  `counterparty-exposure-official` NODE_NAME, `live-trading` and `live-trading-trade` TRADER_ID (and through them the models
  trading-risk, counterparty-exposure, live-trading and desk-pnl-vs-exposure-py). `DeclaredMasksTest` (empty `redact`: masked without the raw
  power, shown with it, for a table and a BI dataset).
- **The large-join threshold (V10, decided).** `drishti.tables.scan-warn-rows` for the installation, and `scan-warn-rows:` in a
  `.model.yaml` for that model (checked: a whole number above zero); CONFIGURATION.md regenerated.
- **The pivot keeps what it staged.** `TablesService.version` names a read without making it (the definitions, the table, the date, the
  source kind's data version, who reads); `TableSources` keeps each open's fields and staging by that version, so a view opened again on
  unchanged data reads nothing, and reads its rows only if the staged table was dropped (`StagedRows` takes the rows lazily). A source
  without a data version is read on every open.
- **Screens: decided (VIRTUAL_TABLES.md section 11).** Of the table editor's mock-ups A, B and C (`docs/lenses/mockups/virtual-tables/`),
  the product owner chose B and C with a switch (`BC.html`): Visual (B: the document, the columns, the rows) by default, YAML (C: the
  definition as text with checks) for experts, both editing the one draft; unsaved text that does not parse cannot switch back until
  fixed; each person's last choice remembered. The model editor's mock-ups `model-A.html` (lists), `model-B.html` (diagram, measures,
  answer; recommended) and `model-C.html` (measures first) follow the same Visual-and-YAML idea. Refined the same day: a live YAML panel
  below every visual view (updated by each visual edit, collapsible, its state remembered per person), editable in place or full screen
  with the edit right (a valid edit updates the visual part at once; invalid text shows its error at the line while the visual part keeps
  the last valid version), read-only without it; models get B (diagram) and C (measures) behind one switch (`model-BC.html`); `BC.html`
  shows the panel open, collapsed, with an error and read-only. A and the single-option mock-ups kept for the record. Not built yet.
- **Build fixes on the branch.** Error Prone's `ReturnValueIgnored` (`lang.Compiler`) and `JavaTimeDefaultTimeZone` (`lang.SqlLowering`,
  the preview's evaluator) and `NullTernary` (`ModelAnswersTest`), which stopped `drishti-bicompute` and `drishti-tables` compiling.
- **Tests.** `TableReadsTest` (shared reads, rules, masks, hidden columns, conditions, a table over a table, dates, the limit),
  `TableOfferTest` (the offer and its grain pass the checks and preview; name clashes; the scan warning), `TablesCliTest` (offer, `--stored`),
  `tools/test_tablescli.py`, `PivotTablesApiTest` (a table as a pivot source with its kind's counts and its masks; two tables over one
  kind read it once; stored names).

## 2.9.11.a — The pivot engine with pivots over documents in Rachana paths; one Engines menu and the Help hub; the data inbox; the in-memory lake in its own module (2026-11-03)

### The data inbox

- **The data inbox: files dropped in a folder are loaded into the lake by themselves (DATALOAD_INBOX.md; DATA_GUIDE.md section 7;
  OPERATIONS.md 11.4; TOOLS.md 5.3a; API_GUIDE.md, Data loads).** Put JSON Lines files or archives (`.jsonl`, `.ndjson`, `.json`; plain,
  `.gz`, `.zst`; `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`) in `<data>/dataload/inbox` with a `<file>.ready` beside each (or one `ready.all`);
  every `interval` (10 minutes) the owner node takes the whole ready, stable batch at once into `inprocess/<run>/` (a run id is its start
  time and node, `20261103T150000Z-drishti-main`), skips a file whose SHA-256 was loaded before, routes each file by its `.ready` or the
  first rule of `config/dataload.yaml`, loads the files of each table with the parallel lake loader (`LakeLoad`) started as a child Java
  process with its own heap (`loader-heap`), records every step in `ledger/`, moves each file with its marker and a report to
  `outbox/<day>/<run>/` (or `failed/` with the reason), and announces each pack, kind and business date through `LoadService`, as
  `POST /api/v1/packs/{pack}/loads` does. Runs never overlap: a cycle due while a run loads is recorded as *skipped: run … still loading
  (n min)*, and Load now says the same. Crash-safe: a stopped server's run is finished at the next cycle, never loaded twice. One runner
  per folder (`owner`, plus `inbox.lock` with a heartbeat). Busy protection skips a cycle when the server is short. In a cluster
  every signal is passed on to the other live members by `loads.LoadForwarding` (the path a person's announcement already took, now one
  class for both), as the owner node: `node:<id>` with the service role, signed with the cluster key; the receiving `LoadController`
  takes such a signed node signal as an administrator's. A file of lake rows or loader rows is refused with the reason (`RowForms`): the
  parallel loader has no reader for those forms.
- **A data-load signal makes a new table readable at once (the Delta connector).** A connector whose domain had no table when it started
  (the first load into an empty lake) found the new table only at its next periodic reindex, so the signal's verify said *not found*;
  the signal's refresh (`purgeCaches`, `refreshVersions`) now looks for new tables (`NewTables`, tested by `NewTablesTest`) and lists one it finds at once. Found by the data
  inbox's end-to-end check.
- New module `drishti-dataload` (plain Java: `Inbox`, `Claims`, `Ledger`, `Routes`, `ReadyNote`, `LoaderProcess`, `Outbox`, `Recovery`,
  `Cycle`, `DataInbox`); the server's wiring is `server.dataload` (`DataLoadConfiguration`, `DataLoadController`). New engine `dataload`
  in the catalogue, `config/engines/dataload.yaml` (off as shipped; every key in CONFIGURATION.md), `config/dataload.yaml` (the routing
  rules; the demo packs' rules commented). New endpoints `GET /api/v1/admin/dataload`, `POST /api/v1/admin/dataload/run` and
  `POST /api/v1/admin/dataload/retry` (administrators; the `POST`s in the `loads:write` scope). New command `drishti.py dataload
  status|run|retry`. `LakeLoad.reads(name)` tells whether the loader reads a file name. Two new rules in `ArchitectureRulesTest`
  (`dataInboxIsPlainJava`, `dataInboxWritesNoTable`). The Admin screen comes after its mock-ups.

### Menus, Help and fixes

- **Pivot: "show values as" on views of several dimensions.** % of row, % of column, % of parent and rank split a cell's key at its
  first `|`, but a key of several coordinates holds `|` too, so on a view with two or more row or column dimensions they read the wrong
  total (or none). The cell is now split by the row and column keys themselves; `ShowAsTest` checks every share against its own total.

- **Pivot: a JSON Lines export** (PIVOT_GUIDE.md, Export). The pivot screen and `POST /api/v1/pivot/export` offer `jsonl` beside Excel, CSV and
  Arrow: one object a cell and measure, and the rows of a cell one object a row, so every export of the console offers the data standard.

- **One Engines menu (mock-up engines-menu/A; USER_GUIDE.md, The top bar).** The Engines menu replaces the VaR and Exposure top-level
  menus (and the VaR and Exposure entries of Views): a column per compute engine running in the cluster (VaR `VAR`, Exposure `EXP`,
  FRTB-SA `FRSA`, SIMM `SIMM`), its command word in the column's head, every page one click away with its command on the right. It is
  drawn only for a role that opens an engine (`opens:` per engine in `drishti-console/config/menus.yaml`: `role:<name>` or
  `pack:<name>`; administrators open every engine). The same rule, in one place (`core/menus.py` `engine_refused`), drops an engine's
  command words from the type-ahead for a role that does not open it and refuses them when typed, in words ("VaR is not opened for
  your role; ask an administrator."), so the bar is Views, Engines, BI, Build, Admin, Help for a risk administrator and
  Views, BI, Build, Help for a role that opens none. Past four running engines (`search-over`) a search box filters the pages by name,
  description or command (Enter opens the first); administrators see *Admin → Engines* and, at the foot, the engines running on no
  server, greyed. On a phone the columns fold into a drawer, one engine open at a time, 44 px rows. Drishti Risk's bar is Views,
  Engines, BI, Admin, Help; Drishti Trading keeps its subject menus after Engines.
- **The help centre reorganised (mock-up help-hub/A; USER_GUIDE.md, Help).** The front door of `/help` is a search box, a "most used"
  row (User guide, VaR guide, Tutorials, What's new) and a tile per section: Get started, Risk measures, Analytics and BI, Data, Build,
  Operate, Reference and Knowledge, with Internal for administrators. A tile opens its section's page (`/help/section/<id>`): its pages
  grouped, every guide on one row with its tutorial beside it, a search of that section only (`/help/search?section=<id>`). Help is
  documentation, not data: a running engine's pages are open to anyone who can open Help, signed out included; an engine that runs
  nowhere has its pages left out (an administrator sees them greyed). Config-driven: `drishti-console/config/help.yaml` now has `sections:` with `groups:`, a page's `engine:` and `pair:`,
  `most-used:`, `aliases:` (old section names: a pack guide's `category:`, an edition's `help.categories`, `/help#cat-<id>`) and
  `documents:` (the section of an unlisted document by folder); every page belongs to exactly one section (a test checks it). Page
  addresses, retired slugs and F1 are unchanged; the editions' `help.categories` name the new sections.
- **Menu items for pages a build holds show again with FastAPI 0.142.** A menu item's `route:` requirement read the app's routes by
  their `path`, which FastAPI 0.142's included routers no longer carry, so the VaR Playground, Backtesting, FRTB-SA and SIMM items were
  left out; the routers are now walked into.
- **The in-memory lake is its own module, `drishti-memlake` (IN_MEMORY_LAKE.md section 16; ARCHITECTURE.md §13,
  PACK_DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md §1.1 and §1.3).** Plain Java with no Spring: the `mem://` storage (`ChunkPool`, `MemoryStorage`,
  `MemoryStores`, from `drishti-lakeio` `com.ash.drishti.lakeio.mem`, now `com.ash.drishti.memlake.store`) and the service (`MemoryLake`,
  `MemoryTable`, `ReplenishSource`, `MemoryCompactor`, `MemoryBinding`, `Retention`, `HostChecks`, from `drishti-server`
  `com.ash.drishti.server.memlake`, now `com.ash.drishti.memlake`). The settings record is `MemoryLakeSettings` (was the server's
  `MemoryLakeProperties`); the server keeps only `MemoryLakeConfiguration` (binds `drishti.lake.memory.*`, the beans, the cron parser, the
  memory budget and busy protection) and `MemoryLakeController`. Expiring a memory table's old versions moved from the Delta writer's
  `TableUpkeep` to `memlake.MemoryUpkeep` (`TableUpkeep.shape` no longer takes a store). The settings and the REST API are unchanged.
- **The lake engines reach `mem://` through `drishti-lakeio`'s storage providers.** New `lakeio.StorageProvider` (a scheme, its storage,
  whether it is memory-only) and `lakeio.StorageProviders` (found with `ServiceLoader`); `drishti-memlake` registers `mem`. The native
  Delta engine, the lake writer, the Iceberg engine's file access and the Delta and Iceberg connectors ask `StorageProviders` and never
  name the module; two new rules in `ArchitectureRulesTest` (`memoryLakeIsPlainJava`, `lakeReadersDoNotSeeTheMemoryLake`) keep it so. The
  memory-lake tests moved with the code (`DeltaInMemoryTest`, `IcebergInMemoryTest`, `MemoryRatiosTest`, `MemoryLakeTest`,
  `RetentionTest`, `MemoryStorageTest`, `MemoryStorageContractTest`); `drishti-lakeio` and `drishti-deltalake` publish test jars for them.

### Fixes and smaller changes

- **Fixed: answers that arrive late no longer undo what you did meanwhile.** The dataset wizard's YAML and checks show the newest
  form: an older check answering last (a slow server) had put back the title it was asked about, so the dataset saved under the old
  name. The VaR regulatory report keeps a comment typed while the previous action's answer was on its way (it was emptied). In the
  BI Runs tab, the run drawer keeps the focus when it is redrawn, and Esc closes it when the focus has fallen to the page (a button it
  was on became disabled while it worked); before, Esc did nothing and the drawer stayed over the list. A BI report's visual that
  is being asked again (a selection, a slicer, a drill) no longer takes a pushed answer to its old question, which drew the old
  figures and ended its busy state early. The top bar's bell is marked `data-alerts-live` once the live feed has said hello (alerts,
  notices and write-back edits reach the tab from then on); a zoomed panel is marked `data-table-fitting` while its tables wait to
  fit its new height.

- **Flaky browser tests fixed at the cause (the drill's `data/drill/flakes.log`).** The exposure and VaR browser tests build their
  scratch lakes with the Python writer (`lake demo --engine deltalake`): `auto` started Drishti's Java writer in a new JVM for every
  table and business day, hundreds per lake, and the exposure lake outran its 900 s limit beside the other workers. The scratch BI
  stacks wait for their server and console until they answer (up to ten minutes, as `wb_live.py` does) and stop waiting at once when
  the process has exited; they had 150 s and 120 s. The catalogue tests type into the catalogue's own search box (`input[data-search]`;
  the Engines menu's items carry `data-search` too). The renderer parity test waits until no part of the page is busy, not a fixed
  time, and prints what differs. The write-back test waits for the other browser's live feed, not 1.5 s; the zoom tests wait for the
  fit, not 350 ms; the BI Runs test waits for the drawer to close before it clicks under it; the pack wizard's resumed draft is read
  with an auto-waiting expectation.


- **About:** the headline (*See what your data hasn't told you yet.*) is centred with the rest of the page's opening on a wide
  screen; it had been drawn flush left. The VaR card and the risk area name the basket sheet, which replaced the selection tray.

- **The release drill is faster and stops sooner (tools/drill.sh; PACK_DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md §2.6, TOOLS.md).** A gate of a few
  minutes runs first, every job at once: the licence headers, the generated documents and data that must be current (settings
  catalogue, data contracts and their pages, data samples, the packs' generated content, the Python API reference), the docs and
  help console tests, and one Java 21 build of the working tree (Javadoc with doclint, Spotless, Maven threads) that runs only the
  rule tests: every `drishti-it` test, `TokenScopeGuardTest` and `ArrowAnswersTest`; its jar is the one the console starts. Its first
  failure stops the drill. Then everything else at once: the console suite in a browser lane (few workers, normal priority) and an
  other lane (more workers, lower priority), each giving its files to the workers longest first from the durations the last runs
  recorded (`data/drill/durations.json`); the Python tool tests; the Java 21 verify in a copy of the committed tree (its `config/`
  and `data/` compared by content before and after); and the Java 25 verify, in its own copy, once the lighter jobs have finished.
  A failed console test runs once more file by file and every failed file is re-run (two at a time in the other lane, one in the
  browser lane), each under a time limit of twice the file's recorded time, at least ten minutes; tests listed in
  `tools/drill-known.txt` are reported as accepted and do not fail the drill. The first failure no re-run can change stops the other
  jobs (`--keep-going` runs them to the end). **Fixed:** every command of the Python tool tests and of the Java runs now fails the
  drill when it fails; before, a job ran as `job || ...`, where bash ignores errexit, so only each job's last command counted (the
  trading pack's generated Sutra fragments and `data/testdata/testdata.yaml` had been reported stale in the tool log without
  failing it). The data samples' pages (`sample_docs.py --check`) and `contracts.py check` are now
  checked by the drill too. The console suite needs pytest-xdist 3.7 or newer.

### The pivot engine

- **Pivots over entity documents (PIVOT_ENGINE.md 6.7; PIVOT_GUIDE.md, Documents).** A pivot field is a Rachana path, parsed by
  Rachana's own parser: `$.PRODUCT_TYPE`, `$.LEGS[0].CURRENCY`, `$.LEGS[*].NOTIONAL` (one row per leg), `$.LEGS[?@.LEG_TYPE == 'FIXED'][*].NOTIONAL`,
  `size($.LEGS)`. The field list follows the documents' shape (each list a grain of its own) and takes a typed path; a view has one grain,
  the finest list it uses; a coarser figure counts each parent once (new built-ins `sum_once`, `count_once`, `avg_once`); two separate lists
  are refused; a filter on a list keeps the parents with any (or, with `~all`, all) elements matching. Three routes, fastest first: a
  promoted column, a BI dataset table's cached layer, DuckDB JSON over the documents; the cell's provenance names it. An administrator sees
  the most used typed paths with Promote and Add to dataset (`GET /api/v1/pivot/paths`). The guide's six worked examples and tutorial 33's
  new step carry the demo lake's real figures and pictures (`tools/docs/shots/t33.py`).
- **Chart any table: Top N, Others and the split cap by the pivot engine.** The chart asks the engine for a level's top N (`top: {field:
  {n, by}}`) and draws its *Others* member, whose figures come from its own rows; the browser merges no cells any more (its `combine`
  and the extra sum and count of an average are gone).
- **Client renderer 1.2.0.** A table that offers Pivot is the table and a link to the pivot screen, as the console draws it (the Table |
  Pivot switch, `pivotTab` and the `pivot` behaviour module are gone); 1.1.0, 1.0.0 and 0.1.0 stay served, unchanged. The pivot grid sets
  its indents and conditional formats through the CSSOM, so a host's CSP that refuses inline styles is respected.
- **Nothing else aggregates: the Sutra `pivot` panel and Chart any table on the pivot engine.** A `pivot` panel's cells, subtotals and
  totals are computed by the engine's in-memory provider (`RowsProvider`, the built-ins' own states; equal to the tabular provider on the same
  rows) and its nested rows drawn by the one pivot grid (`pivot-grid.js`, the Pivot screen's, which now replaces `pivot-core.js`). *Chart any
  table* sends the shown rows' chart fields to the new `POST /api/v1/pivot/inline` (at most 100,000 rows) and draws the engine's answer;
  *Chart all N* on a panel offers *Chart every row*. `pivot-engine.js` is now only the engine's browser client (query, inline, layout,
  formats): its in-browser `cube` and filters are deleted, as is the old nested grid.
- **One pivot: the old Pivot tab retired onto the pivot engine (product owner, 2026-11-02: no dual machinery).** A table or ladder whose
  Sutra says `pivot:` and a search whose kind's pack says `pivot:` now carry **Pivot**, which opens the pivot screen on the panel's own rows
  (`panel/<kind>/<panel>/<id>`) or on the kind, with the Sutra's or the pack's arrangement as the opening view; an author promotes a page
  table's view to its Sutra at `/api/v1/pivot/promote`; *Chart all N* asks the pivot engine. Retired: the browser-computed Pivot tab
  (`pivot.js` of the tab, its saved arrangements `/api/v1/me/pivots`), the search pivot (`/api/v1/search/pivot/**`, `SearchPivot`,
  `PivotCube`) and the panel records endpoint; the pivot screen now owns `/api/pivot` and `static/js/pivot.js`. `drishti.pivot.enabled` is
  the old name of the engine's switch (`config/engines/pivot.yaml`); `drishti.pivot.max-row-keys`, `max-column-keys`, `document-scan`,
  `drill-page` and `budget` are gone. Embedded views: Elements 1.4.4.
- **The pivot engine as a compute engine; the direct lake route; currencies and units.** `config/engines/pivot.yaml` with its catalogue
  entry (the MR cube needs it); large Delta and Iceberg tables read straight from their Parquet files by DuckDB (masked columns never
  read, the filters repeated on the raw columns for statistics skipping); money converted at the view's rates or refused per cell when it
  mixes currencies, a sum of a rate or percentage refused; the architecture rule test (only `drishti-bicompute` aggregates for a pivot).
- **The pivot engine, phase P1 (2.9.11.a; PIVOT_GUIDE.md, tutorial 33, ARCHITECTURE.md#26-the-pivot-engine).** A new module `drishti-bicompute` (plain
  Java): views of declarative cell sets compiled to one `GROUP BY GROUPING SETS` statement per restriction, functions with start, add,
  merge and finish (mergeable: sum, count, avg, min, max, wavg, variance and standard deviation; holistic and exact: median, percentile,
  distinct count), partial states merged in a fixed order, a partial-state cache in the one memory budget (`pivot.states`), the
  split-and-merge harness. Any Data view table (read for the person, masks applied, staged in memory) or VaR (`source: var`, every cell the
  VaR engine's answer for its scope) as a pivot: `PIVOT <GO>`, Views → Pivot, Pivot on a Data view table; nested rows opened lazily (only
  open nodes computed), expand by another field per member, top N with an Others of its own members, sorting per level, the provenance of
  every cell, the scan estimate, a chart that never stacks a non-additive measure, Excel with outline levels, SUM formulas only where a
  figure adds up and a Provenance sheet, CSV, Arrow, saved and shared views, cell references, compare two dates. `/api/v1/pivot`,
  `drishti.py pivot`, `drishti.pivot.*` settings, codes DRS-5701 to DRS-5705 and DRS-9507.

## 2.9.11 — Sensitivities and market-risk capital; the basket as a sheet; the in-memory lake; compute engines; busy protection (2026-11-03)

- **Fixed (drill): the release drill's console findings.** The sign-in page, which sends its form in the background for busy protection,
  marks the page while the form is on its way (`html[data-signing-in]`), and the browser tests wait on it as on a navigation (they had
  run on before the sign-in was answered, then read the sign-in page). The basket workbook (`POST /api/var/basket/sheet.xlsx`) answers a
  body that is not a JSON object with 400 or 415 in words, never 500. Admin → Engines' switches fill with the fill tokens and its data
  travel in an attribute (no inline script); the SIMM screen names the product from `ui.product`. `POST /net/engines` is in the API
  guide. `make_sutras.py` writes the phone layouts of the shared deal fragments, the counterparty, the netting set and the Endur commodity
  swap (they had been added by hand, so `--check` failed); `testdata.yaml` regenerated. Tutorials 30 to 32 gain their pictures
  (`screenshots.py --guide t30`, `t31`, `t32`), what you should see at every step and their next steps; the tutorials card counts
  past thirty. FRSA's capital stack draws each bar to its length (the width was a style attribute, which the console's CSP blocks).
  The SIMM screen's list of netting sets follows the page's date (`asOf`), as its breakdown did. Admin → Health no longer fails (500)
  when the in-memory lake is on: a memory store's gauge reads its use against its cap. The example memory connector
  (`config/connectors.examples/memory/news-store.yaml`) says `domain: ""`: without it the pack's template added `domain: news` and the
  connector looked under `mem://news/news`, so every news page read *no source holds*.
- **Fixed: the stress window page read the current window a month late on a demo lake.** `lake demo` moved a stress scenario set's
  window and days with the business dates (HS-STRESS-2008 became 2008-08-01 to 2009-07-31 on a lake ending 2026-11-02) while the long
  history's days stay as they are; a stress set's period of history now stays 2008-07-01 to 2009-06-30, as VAR_GUIDE.md section 18.9
  says, and only its business date moves.
- **The stress window page draws across the page again:** its outer box used the class `sw`, which the terminal style sheet also uses for a
  small legend swatch (14 by 3 pixels), so the page shrank to a narrow column; the box is now `sw-page`. New browser test
  `test_stress_window_browser.py`. VAR_GUIDE.md section 18.9 opens with a plain-words explanation: what the stress window is, what the
  screen shows, the data it uses and where it is useful.
- **Forms, write-back:** a form opened before the page knew whether its person may submit (a quick open, a phone) now gets its Submit
  button and its note when that answer arrives; before, it stayed without Submit until the page was reloaded.
- **VaR, Ad-hoc scopes:** a saved basket's or portfolio's name stays visible; its Edit, Delete and + basket buttons sit after the name
  instead of over it, on one line: showing them never changes the row's height, so the rows below never move under the pointer.

- **Busy protection judges memory by what is left, not only a share:** new heavy work waits for memory only when the heap after a collection is past its level **and** less than `memory-free-min-mb` (768 MB) is left; `DRISHTI_ADMISSION_ENABLED` switches it off (the console's own tests do, their servers running a 768 MB heap).

- **Compute engines on or off per server, each with its own configuration file (2.9.11 row 14; COMPUTE_ENGINES.md, OPERATIONS.md
  section 21).** VaR (with regulatory VaR), exposure, the position sensitivities, FRTB-SA, SIMM and the in-memory lake each have a file,
  `config/engines/<engine>.yaml` (`DRISHTI_ENGINES_DIR`; the same file inside the jar), holding the switch `drishti.engines.<engine>.enabled`
  and every setting under its old key; `application.yaml` imports them and no longer holds them; SA-CCR, FVA and the two cubes have their
  file and switch, shown "not installed". The old switch names (`drishti.var.enabled`, `drishti.ccr.exposure.enabled`,
  `drishti.frtb.enabled`, `drishti.simm.enabled`) still decide when a site sets them, with one warning at start (DRS-1024); the
  environment variables are unchanged; an edition's `var: off` presets the new switch; nothing is required on upgrade. Off, an engine is
  not started (no date, cache, thread or capture), its API answers `404 DRS-1020` in words (was 403), and when no server of the cluster
  runs it its words, menus, Help pages, Home cards, pages, playgrounds, BI datasets and `drishti.py` commands (exit 3) disappear.
  Dependencies are enforced with words (FRTB-SA needs VaR and the sensitivities, SIMM the sensitivities; DRS-1021; a server started with
  a need off starts with the engine `blocked`, DRS-1022). **Admin → Engines** (mock-up A): the engines with switch, state, memory,
  threads, needs, used by and where each switch is set; a staged change reviewed in a side panel (dependency check, what disappears,
  live or restart) and applied with a required reason, written to the engine's file (only `enabled` and `changed`, comments kept,
  atomic, refused when edited by hand since, DRS-1023), audited, in History; off is live with a 30 s drain, on is live except the
  in-memory lake ("restart needed"); an edit of the file by hand takes effect too. In a cluster each node publishes its engines in its
  digest, an engine's request goes to a node that runs it, and the Cluster tab changes another node's engine (signed, audited on both).
  `drishti.py server engines list|show|on|off|history` (`admin engines` the same). CONFIGURATION.md has an Engines area, checked.
- **Docs: the pivot engine designed (design, not built; PIVOT_ENGINE.md, mock-ups A, B and C in docs/architecture/mockups/pivot/,
  the plan's proposed 2.9.11.a).** One generalised, very large-scale pivot for all of Drishti in a new `drishti-bicompute` module:
  measure providers (DuckDB tabular, VaR vectors, FRTB-SA, SIMM, later CCR), mergeable, sketch and holistic measures, custom
  aggregation functions (start, add, merge, finish) with a split-and-merge harness and a playground, expand and collapse, charts,
  Excel and CSV export, BI and the MR cube on it; the MR cube (2.9.11 row 3) moved to after it.
- **Construct your basket is one sheet like Excel; baskets are edited, amended and deleted (2.9.11 rows 10 and 12; VAR_GUIDE.md
  sections 3.5 and 5.8, tutorial 25 steps 5 and 7).** The chip tray is retired (mock-up D): a column per kind of part (trade, position,
  portfolio, book, desk, each configured hierarchy's word such as the limit letter, counterparty) and the Op column (+ or −), filled by
  typing, by the type-ahead (a hint lands in its kind's column), by **+ basket** on any explorer row, or by pasting whole columns from
  Excel (a first row of headings places each column); only the rows in view are drawn, so 10,000 ids scroll as fast as ten. **Start from
  the whole bank** is one checkbox (`BANK - DESK:COMM - TRD:XYZ`); a minus in the Op column or a leading `-` takes away, and a minus that
  takes nothing away, or a + row under the whole bank, is flagged in words. Every check and figure is the server's: `POST
  /api/v1/var/basket/sheet` takes the columns as lists and answers each cell found or not found with the reason (not live, outside your
  view, a masked counterparty, one id a cell) and the basket's VaR, ES, sum of the parts, diversification and trades; **Remove the not
  found**; **Download as .xlsx** (`POST /api/v1/var/basket/sheet.xlsx`). A saved basket keeps the sheet's lists (to 20,000 rows; its
  scope composed when read) and opens back into the sheet column by column (`GET /api/v1/var/basket/sheet?scope=`). In *Ad-hoc scopes* a
  basket of yours has **Edit** (Save keeps its name as the next version; a basket changed since is `409`) and **Delete**; an
  administrator edits anyone's, saved under its owner, audited (`var-basket-edit`) and told in the owner's inbox; a portfolio (the bank's
  feed) and a basket shared with you have **Edit a copy**. The what-if trades, save with read-only sharing, Open without saving, Alt+B and
  the count on the link are kept.
- **Designs: IFRS 9 expected credit loss and financial crime (docs only; product owner, 2026-11-02).**
  [IFRS9_ECL.md](docs/architecture/IFRS9_ECL.md) designs the impairment engine (staging with SICR, backstop, exemption and cure; PD from
  curves or migration matrices; LGD with collateral; EAD with CCF; EIR discounting; weighted scenarios; overlays with four eyes; POCI;
  why the provision moved in exact steps; contracts, playground, hand-built cases). [FINANCIAL_CRIME.md](docs/architecture/FINANCIAL_CRIME.md)
  designs the FCU engines (trade surveillance, transaction monitoring with threshold tuning, network analytics, customer risk rating,
  sanctions and PEP screening, fraud scoring, alerts and cases, FINTRAC STR, LCTR and EFTR, rule effectiveness, data protection). The
  plan proposes 2.9.20 (IFRS 9) and 2.9.21 and 2.9.22 (financial crime, split in two), placement to confirm.
- **VaR by trader on the server (2.9.11 row 9; [VAR_GUIDE.md section 11.3](docs/guides/VAR_GUIDE.md#113-path-and-contributions)).**
  `GET /api/v1/var/scope/contributions?by=attribute:<COLUMN>` groups every trade of the scope by its value of a trade column and sums
  each group's vector in Java over all its trades (never cut to `max-parts`), so the groups' component VaR adds up to the scope's VaR. The
  column is the VaR book's own (`COUNTERPARTY`, `STRATEGY`, a hierarchy's level column) or one the trade valuations keep (`TRADER_ID`,
  joined by trade id; the new setting `drishti.var.kinds.valuation`, `trade-valuation`). A role that sees the column masked gets no groups,
  `masked: true` and a note. The Trading landing's VaR by trader asks it (`by=attribute:TRADER_ID`) and only shows the rows: a desk with
  more trades than the contributions page now counts every trade.
- **The VaR what-if in Java (2.9.11 row 11; [VAR_GUIDE.md section 8.2](docs/guides/VAR_GUIDE.md#82-the-what-if-the-java-engine)).**
  `POST /api/v1/var/what-if` keeps its request and answer and is computed by the server's VaR engine (`VarWhatIfMath`: before and after
  VaR, ES and stressed VaR, each trade's standalone, incremental and component VaR), with no sandbox and no compute workers, so it answers
  with `DRISHTI_COMPUTE_ENABLED=false`. Parity with the Python engine it replaces: its answers on the demo's DESK-RATES (three trades:
  an unwind, a half, a double) are frozen in a test and given again to the cent. An item may also copy any scope (`"copyOf":
  "BOOK:BOOK-RATES-3"`) or bring a vector priced elsewhere (`"pnl": [...]`); `drishti.py var whatif SCOPE --copy TRADE=FACTOR
  [--trades FILE.json]` posts to it. **Retired:** the Python VaR engine (`drishti_compute.var`, its tests and the compute pool `var`,
  `DRISHTI_COMPUTE_VAR_WORKERS`), the computed kind `var-whatif` with its connector, contract and command `VWIF` (the menus' *What-if*
  entries, the editions' lists and chips; the Trading landing's new-trade check now needs the word `VAR` and `XWIF`), and `DRS-5205`.
  **Upgrade:** a connector file generated from a pack's template that the pack no longer has and that nobody edited is removed at start
  (kept beside it as `.retired-<time>.bak` and in the history); an edited `var-whatif.yaml` stays, its kind listed as obsolete under
  Admin → Connectors → Template updates.

- **ISDA SIMM, computed per netting set, collect and post (2.9.11 row 4; [SIMM_GUIDE.md](docs/guides/SIMM_GUIDE.md), tutorial 32).** The
  server's Java engine computes SIMM from the same position sensitivities as FRTB-SA: each netting set's trades from the netting-set
  records, its CSA's version, regimes, calculation currency and add-ons when the CSA carries them; delta, vega, curvature and base
  correlation per risk class with the concentration factor at the rules' grain (per currency for rates, per issuer and seniority for
  credit, per factor otherwise), f_kl and g_bc, every bucket's net capped at its K, the residual buckets outside the root, vega σ from the
  risk weight × HVR, HVR_IR⁻² on rates curvature; the risk classes within a product class with ψ and the four product classes added; the
  CSA's fixed, notional and multiplier add-ons. Post is every sensitivity negated. **ISDA's numbers are licensed: none ships.** The bank
  installs one parameter file a version in `drishti.simm.parameters-dir` (the structure `docs/architecture/capital-parameters/simm.yaml`,
  every number empty); a version with a number missing is refused (`DRS-5333`) and every figure carries the version and the file's
  SHA-256. `SIMM` opens the netting-set list with each one's breakdown and the margin against the counterparty's call (`crif-external`);
  netting sets without sensitivities show the stored figure, labelled; any VaR scope is an analytic. `PLAY SIMM <netting set>`: the
  Choices panel (the version, concentration, HVR), the side, a switch compared in words, recipes replayed to the cent (`PLAY SIMM RUN
  <id>`), and the workbook of live formulas with the switches and the side as Config cells (recalculated by LibreOffice in the tests and
  equal to the engine to the cent); the template workbook has every parameter cell empty. API `/api/v1/simm/...`; CLI `drishti.py simm`,
  `play simm`; settings `drishti.simm.*` (`enabled` switches it off); codes `DRS-5331` to `DRS-5336`. The tests use a toy parameter file
  (not ISDA's).
- **FRTB-SA, computed for any scope (2.9.11 rows 1 and 2; [FRTB_SA_GUIDE.md](docs/guides/FRTB_SA_GUIDE.md), tutorial 30).** Position
  sensitivities (`SENS`) and the factor dictionary (`RFAC`) are kinds of the market-risk pack, served by risk-store and loaded by `lake
  demo`; the server's Java engine computes the FRTB standardised approach from them: the sensitivities-based method (delta, vega and
  curvature per risk class with the two curvature sides, the three correlation scenarios and the binding one, the alternative
  specification), the default risk charge (from the `default-risk` input; *not computed* without it) and the residual risk add-on
  (from the `residual-risk` input, or derived from the positions' product types and notionals), with Euler contributions that add up.
  Parameters are the market-risk pack's `capital/frtb-sa-sbm.yaml` and `frtb-sa-drc-rrao.yaml` (MAR21.46's published GIRR table by
  default), checked at start and hashed into every answer. `FRSA <scope>` opens the capital screen (the stack, the scenarios, the bucket
  drill, the contributions); `PLAY FRTB <scope>` the playground: every method choice a switch, a switch compared side by side with the
  difference explained by step, the workbook of live formulas with the switches as Config cells (recalculated by LibreOffice in the tests
  and equal to the engine to the cent, with the defaults and each switch flipped), and recipes replayed to the cent (`PLAY FRTB RUN <id>`).
  API `/api/v1/sensitivities`, `/api/v1/risk-factors`, `/api/v1/frtb/...`; CLI `drishti.py sens`, `frtb`, `play frtb`; settings
  `drishti.frtb.*`. The factor names give GIRR curvature per currency (`IR/CURVE/<ccy>`) and commodity curvature per commodity
  (`CM/PRICE/<commodity>`), with the cross-currency basis and inflation without a tenor; vega horizons follow MAR21.92. Planned
  contracts `default-risk` (DRCI) and `residual-risk` (RRAI); the capital-input regime `BCBS-MAR`. Refusal codes `DRS-5321` to `DRS-5329`.
- **The in-memory lake: data that never touches a disk** (2.9.11 row 13, on Java 21; docs/guides/DATA_LAKE_GUIDE.md, tutorial 30).
  Feeds that may not, by contract, be saved on a disk are held as ordinary Delta tables whose files live in the server's memory: a
  `MemoryStorage` for `mem://<store>/…` beside local disk and S3 (direct buffers in a reused 1 MB chunk pool under a hard cap per store,
  released explicitly on Java 21, reference-counted files so readers on an old version finish, truly exclusive commits; the same Storage
  contract suite as local disk). The native Delta engine, the lake writer (rows from memory, no staged file; zstd by default, byte-equal
  Parquet with `codec: snappy`) and Iceberg's file access read and write it; the Delta connector with `root: mem://<store>` reads it
  unchanged. **Replenish jobs** (`drishti.lake.memory.tables`) fill each table from a URL, a file, a connector's documents or the news
  connector by ids, in `replace`, `append` or `merge` mode, on a schedule or cron, on the source's signal, at start in warm-up order,
  after an eviction and on demand; every run is in a values-free history. The **eviction ladder** frees old versions, then whole unpinned
  tables least recently read first, then refuses the write with the table whole at its previous version. **Automated compaction** merges
  small files, drops replaced rows and re-sorts appends, only with headroom under the cap. **The guard** (`DRS-5219`): a memory-only
  connector keeps no disk cache, id-map files or index segments; scheduled reports, a share's picture or e-mail, notes copying values and
  Ask are refused; BI run results are not stored; DuckDB does not spill; a user's download is allowed, streamed and audited without
  values. **News first**: `config/connectors.examples/memory/news-store.yaml` and `config/examples/in-memory-lake.yaml` move the
  news-and-markets pack to `mem://news`; the sentinel scan (markers through pages, a download and a refused report, then the data folder,
  the temporary folder and the logs searched) finds none. Admin → Lakes and Health (store use, refusals, pinned tables, the direct-memory
  limit against the caps, swap, heap dumps, JFR, the temporary folder), a gauge per store in busy protection, the off-heap pool in the
  memory budget; `drishti.py lake memory status|jobs|refill`; node.yaml `memory-stores` binds a store and its pack to its owner node and
  the others forward; the launchers raise `-XX:MaxDirectMemorySize` by the stores' caps (`tools/lake/memory_caps.py`,
  `DRISHTI_LAKE_MEMORY_MB`). Measured on the demo tables: 4 to 42 times smaller than the decoded rows, 1.6 to 3.9 times smaller than the
  disk lake (RESOURCES_AND_SCALE.md 5.8).

- **Busy protection: refuse politely, never fall over** (2.9.11 row 8; mock-up A). One gate in front of new sign-ins, VaR and exposure
  date loads, Data view downloads, BI runs and bulk loads reads the heap after the last collection, each engine's loads against
  `load-threads`, the open dates' heap against their safety net, the requests answered at once and the free disk; past a wait level the
  new work is answered `503` with `Retry-After` and `DRS-9501` (sign-in), `DRS-9502` (a date), `DRS-9503` (a download), `DRS-9504` (a BI
  run) or `DRS-9505` (a bulk load), in calm words. Defaults: new heavy work waits over 85% of the heap after a collection, new sign-ins over
  92%; people signed in keep working (open dates are never gated). A refusal is remembered for its `Retry-After`, so a crowd gets one
  decision; it lifts as soon as its cause clears. The console shows the message in place with a countdown ring, Try now and Cancel, and
  tries again by itself three times (sign-in, the VaR and exposure panels, the Data view's Download card); nothing else on the screen
  changes. `drishti.py data get --wait` (and `DRISHTI_WAIT_BUSY=1` for every command) waits and tries again, printing the same words.
  Admin → Health gains the Busy protection card (memory after clean-up, loads running, request handlers busy, disk, with warn and wait
  markers; the last refusals) and the operator override (Automatic, Let everything through, Hold all new heavy work; a reason required,
  ends by itself, audited as `busy-override`); `GET /api/v1/admin/busy`, `PUT /api/v1/admin/busy/override`. Settings `drishti.admission.*`
  (OPERATIONS.md 12.5, CONFIGURATION.md).
- **One competitive analysis.** The older comparison page (`/about/competitive`, from `drishti-console/config/competitive.yaml`: product categories, no vendors) is retired; its address leads to the Help guide *Competitive analysis* (`docs/strategy/COMPETITIVE_ANALYSIS.md`, vendor by vendor, administrators only). Administrators reach it from the Help menu, the Help centre and About; the footer link is gone; `competitive.yaml` and its CONFIGURATION entry removed.
- **Why it moved follows the active theme.** The VaR page's *Why it moved* view drew in the renderer library's own default palette (parchment whenever the computer was in light mode) instead of the theme picked in the console; it now takes the active theme and follows a switch at once.
- **Construct your basket opens only when asked** (the link, Alt+B or + basket), never by itself when a basket kept in the browser or a saved basket opens.
- **Sensitivities and market-risk capital (design):** checked against Basel MAR21–23 and ISDA SIMM 2.8+2512 before the engine is
  built. Curvature now takes an up and a down term per factor with the larger bucket charge kept, floors the across-bucket sum at zero
  and applies the correlation scenarios to the squared correlations; the curvature factors and shocks are stated per class (commodity
  added to the parallel shift); the estimate from gamma is written out as a second-order approximation; the FX ÷ 1.5 is limited to
  options not referencing the reporting currency. SIMM concentration is applied per currency, per issuer or per factor (not per bucket),
  with the f and g adjustments, the always-capped bucket net, residual buckets and the equity/FX/commodity vega volatility; the SIMM
  parameter file no longer carries a correlation across product classes (they add). DRC and RRAO paragraph references corrected; RRAO's
  listed/cleared exclusion limited to other residual risks. Hand-built cases 9 to 11 added; cases 1 to 6 recomputed unchanged. The
  playground explanations follow. A new section *Checked against the rules* lists each point.
- **FRTB and SIMM data contracts (design):** `docs/contracts/FRTB.md` and `SIMM.md` rewritten to the sensitivities design: the shared
  input is `position-sensitivity` (SENS) with the `risk-factor` dictionary (RFAC), replacing the earlier per-trade `sensitivity` table;
  units, signs and the per-class delivery rules; draft default-risk and residual-risk inputs; the parameter files with version and hash;
  the method switches, the playground recipe and workbook; refusals with their words; sizing at 300,000 trades and 2.3 million positions.
  New `FRTB_DATA_STRUCTURES.md`: every field, the naming standard, the bucket grids, the computed records, worked JSON Lines records of
  each kind and the mapping from CRIF and bump reports. SIMM follows 2.8+2512 with its numbers shipped empty.
- **Drill:** stops at once with the remedy when `drishti-console/.venv` is missing (a new worktree).
- **Decks:** the roadmap as it stands (built: the regulatory foundation, the VaR Playground, why VaR moved, the Data view, the phone; next: sensitivities and market-risk capital), hot-dates 10, the 200K and 1M benchmarks measured.
- **Tests:** the direct-memory soak test no longer calls AssertJ from its 72 worker threads (on Java 25 they waited on its class initialisation for ever).

## 2.9.10.a — Admin → Capacity; the cluster under load; three VaR dates in the demo; the competitive analysis (2026-11-01)

### Admin → Capacity

- **Admin → Capacity**, after Caches (administrators; the editions' `admin.pages` gain `capacity`; OPERATIONS.md 12.4). It opens on
  **today against the plan**: heap, RAM, disk and cores each with a state in words (room, tight, short, not measured) and a headroom bar
  (what the plan needs against what this server has, a tick where it is now, a Why? with the sum and every figure in it); **what breaks
  first** in a sentence with its symptom and the fix (`-Xmx`, `drishti.var.open-heap-mb`, the disk, the cores); this server beside the
  plan (positions, dates open, the open dates' heap and the safety net, heap after GC, `-Xmx`, RSS, machine memory and cores, disk free,
  people and requests a second); growth at ×1 to ×3 the trades with sliders for the intraday share, dates in memory and users; the
  warnings. **Edit the plan** shows the planner: the inputs grouped (changed ones yellow, Reset to defaults, Use this server's figures),
  the four answers, what the heap holds, every result with its Why?, the settings in three forms with the YAML block, every JVM argument
  with its condition and the command line, each with Copy. **Download the working (.xlsx)** gives the planner workbook with every result
  a live formula, its inputs as on the screen, this server's live figures, or both side by side (a Live column stamped with its time),
  audited as `capacity-workbook-downloaded`. Phone tiers (must, glance, more folded, desk), dark and light, F1 to the guide.
- **One planner file, three evaluators.** `drishti-server/src/main/resources/capacity/planner.yaml` holds the inputs, coefficients,
  results, settings, JVM arguments, warnings, calibration and the Explain examples; `tools/sizing_planner.py` now reads it (the workbook
  is byte-for-byte as before) and also writes the server's workbook template (`capacity/template/`) and shared test vectors (every named
  figure at three shapes), which the browser's evaluator (`capacity.js`, under Node) and the Python one are checked against.
  RESOURCES_AND_SCALE.md 9.7.
- **API**: `GET /api/v1/admin/capacity` (the planner as JSON), `GET /api/v1/admin/capacity/live` (the measured figures with their time
  and the planner inputs they stand for), `GET /api/v1/admin/capacity.xlsx?inputs=plan|live|both&<Input>=…`; `GET /api/v1/admin/health`'s
  `server.rssMb` (resident memory from `VmRSS`, Linux; null elsewhere). The server's request activity also counts the people who asked
  something in the last 5 minutes and today's busiest minute.
- **CLI**: `drishti.py admin capacity [--live] [--set Name=value] [--all] [--json] [--xlsx FILE --inputs plan|live|both]`.

### Large workbook downloads

- **A streamed answer may take 30 minutes.** `spring.mvc.async.request-timeout` (`DRISHTI_ASYNC_TIMEOUT`, `30m`) replaces the
  servlet container's 30-second limit for streamed answers: the VaR Playground's workbook for a whole bank (7,089 positions, about
  106 MB of formulas), the Why it moved working, the capacity workbook and BI exports arrived cut short and would not open. Test:
  `StreamedDownloadTimeoutTest`.

### Three VaR dates in the demo

- **Three VaR dates in the demo data.** The committed VaR inputs are written for 2026-09-28, 2026-09-29 and 2026-09-30, each
  in files of its own, so *Why it moved* shows real waterfalls on the demo: each date's positions from that date's trades (31 and 37
  trades leave), the scenario window a day further on with every day keeping its move (the factor model's earlier days), and book
  `BOOK-FI-3` moved from the credit desk to the fixed income desk on 2026-09-29. Limits are the newest date's; the stress set, the desk
  P&L and the long P&L history stay on the newest date. 2026-09-30's files are byte for byte as before (the bank's VaR 112,041,646);
  the bank's VaR is 112,405,919 on 09-28 and 112,575,052 on 09-29. The test data grows by 32.8 MB to 181 MB. The browser test of the tab
  builds the three dates in one `lake demo`; contracts and sample pages read the newest date. On the demo the bank's VaR falls 533,406
  from 09-29 to 09-30 (trades out −531,668, market −1,738) and rises 169,133 from 09-28 to 09-29 (trades out −866,479, market
  +1,035,612); `DESK:CREDIT` and `DESK:FI` show the book's move as a hierarchy step (−12,532,037 and +19,620,151). VAR_GUIDE.md sections
  3.11 and 22.1.

### Competitive analysis, for administrators

- **A full competitive analysis, internal.** `docs/strategy/COMPETITIVE_ANALYSIS.md`: Drishti's position, its five strongest
  differentiators and five biggest gaps, and the first and long-term pitches; built today against planned, with evidence levels
  (measured, designed, claimed, not verified); banking, finance and risk (risk aggregation cubes, trading-platform risk modules,
  enterprise market and credit risk, regulatory reporting, governance, buy-side) with a capability matrix, each competitor's strengths,
  where Drishti wins and loses and how to position it, the vendor stacks Drishti could replace once the plan is built, and what still
  decides deals; general data and analytics (BI, semantic layers, lakehouses, real-time engines, app builders, Grafana, AI assistants)
  with its own matrix; pricing observations from public sources; risks and upkeep; every source with the date read. Marked
  "Internal — not for customers".
- **Help pages for administrators only.** A help catalogue entry may carry `roles:` (`roles: [admin]` for the competitive analysis):
  only an administrator, or a person holding one of the roles, sees it in the Help index and in search and opens it; for everyone else
  it is not listed, not found and its address answers 404 (`Guide.permits`, `visible()` in the help routes). docs/README.md's map of the
  help centre lists the pages everyone sees, so the internal page is in no customer-facing index (`test_docs_help_map.py`); tests:
  `test_help.py` (an administrator sees it, a viewer gets 404, a listed role opens it).

### 2.9.11 and 2.9.12 groundwork

- **Sensitivities and market-risk capital: the design and the data, nothing built.** The design note
  `docs/guides/FRTB_SA_GUIDE.md`: position sensitivities and the factor dictionary, the FRTB standardised approach
  step by step (SBM delta, vega and curvature per risk class, the three correlation scenarios, DRC, RRAO), ISDA SIMM's structure, where
  each number comes from, the API, command line and screens planned, the FRTB-SA and SIMM playgrounds, and eight hand-built test cases.
  The planned contracts `position-sensitivity` (SENS) and `risk-factor` (RFAC) of the market-risk pack with their generated pages and
  sample pages; the parameter files in draft (`docs/architecture/capital-parameters/`: MAR21, MAR22–23 with their paragraphs; SIMM's
  structure with every licensed number empty). Demo data from the VaR factor model: `tools/packgen/sensitivity/` writes 8,052 sensitivity
  records (Murex and Calypso by position, Endur by trade) and 855 factors under `data/testdata/market-risk/`, run by `make_testdata.py`,
  not loaded by `lake demo` until the kinds have a command; the sample pages tool shows planned kinds with demo data as their own group.
  Mock-ups for the product owner to choose (three options each): the FRTB-SA capital screen, SIMM, and the factor dictionary with the
  load's quality (`docs/lenses/mockups/frtb-sa/`, `simm/`, `risk-factors/`).
### The cluster's contribution tables under load

- **A contribution table asks each remote shard once.** On a sharded date, contributions by position and by trade fetched each
  position's or trade's vector from its shard's owner in turn: about 2,000 signed `POST /api/v1/var/partial` calls one after the other
  for a desk of 2,000 positions held elsewhere. The table's reads are now fetched ahead (`VarBook.readAhead`,
  `ShardedVectors.batched`): one call per remote shard of up to 1,024 row sets (each set sent as its runs, 8 bytes a position), the
  shards side by side, through the new members-only `POST /api/v1/var/partials` (the same signature, label, data-version and access
  checks as `/partial`, in `token-never`). Every part is the same to the bit as the one read alone (`ShardReadAheadTest`, on one member and
  on each of three).
- **A scope's standalone sums too.** The sum of the parts' standalone VaR behind a headline (the bank minus a desk, a basket) computed
  each position's vector with a call to its owner, on the vector-sum pool: with every pool thread waiting on owners, the first requests
  of a date on a member waited past the client's 60 s. These reads are fetched ahead as well, a step of 1,024 positions or trades.
- **Measured** (three members, 200,000 positions, Java 21, `-Xmx4g`): contributions p95 0.88 / 1.35 / 2.53 s at 50 / 100 / 200 users
  (10.4 / 15.8 / 13.9 s before), no error in any window (17 timeouts at 50 users before), 226 / 249 / 231 requests a second (123 / 161 /
  148), no pinned virtual thread.
- **One deadline per gather.** The calls made for one answer share `drishti.var.sharding.call-timeout-seconds` (30 s): the first owner
  gets its share of the time left and its replica the rest, so a stalled owner becomes an answer from the replica or a clear
  `503 DRS-5215` inside the client's 60 s, never a client timeout.
- **No pinned carrier while a skeleton streams.** `ShardSkeleton.write` copies the hot file's sections with positional reads into a
  64 KB buffer and the stream's own `write`, no longer through `Channels.newChannel(out)` (whose `synchronized` write pinned a virtual
  thread's carrier on Java 21 when the reader was slow). The same bytes.
- Docs: VAR_SHARDING.md section 15 (contributions under load), BENCHMARK.md section 4.3 (the cluster rows, results in
  `tools/bench/results/2.9.10a-200k-cluster.jsonl`), API_GUIDE.md (`/partials`).


## 2.9.10 — Memory, scale and mobile; why VaR moved (2026-11-01)

*2.9.9 and 2.9.10 are released together as 2.9.10.*

### Memory, scale and mobile

- **A sizing planner for one server.** `docs/architecture/Drishti-Sizing-Planner.xlsx`, written by `tools/sizing_planner.py` (standard
  library; `--check` guards drift, `tools/test_sizing_planner.py` its formulas and figures): type positions, dates in memory, users and
  the Java version, and read the heap term by term, `-Xmx`, RAM, disk by folder, cores, the settings with their keys, the JVM arguments
  as one command line, and warnings; every constant on its own tab with its source and status, calibrated to the 1,000,000-position
  re-benchmark (RESOURCES_AND_SCALE.md section 9.7). The defaults are a production shape (300,000 trades, 39% updated
  intraday in 10 batches), with today's intraday layer on the heap and its batches in the lake; Explain gives the results for it and for
  the 1,000,000-position benchmark. A cluster version comes later.

- **The VaR Playground's Explain tab in plain words.** The workbook's Explain tab opens with what VaR answers, how to read the tabs, and
  signs and units; each of the ten steps starts with a sentence in plain language before its formula and cells; and every term of Main
  (each input, derived cell and result), Config (each column), Data, FX, PnL and Provenance is explained: what it is, why it matters,
  what changing it does, and its cell and value. Titles and text wrap at the top of their rows (styles `wrap` and `label.wrap`).
- **The VaR page's Playground link carries the date** (`asOf`) beside the scope, currency, measure, horizon, confidences and set.
- **VaR memory: node members as runs.** A hierarchy node's members (`OrdinalSet`) are kept as the sorted runs of its books' and cells'
  ordinals, not as a bitmap of the whole date: at 1,000,000 trades and 27,024 nodes that is about 2.5 MB a date instead of 1.69 GB. Every
  query and set operation answers the same in both forms (bit-exact; `OrdinalSetRunsTest`); an intraday layer's nodes stay runs.
- **VaR CPU: a scope's parts summed run by run.** The totals over a scope's positions (`sumStandalone`, the count) walk the scope's runs
  a position at a time, and whether a position is whole is a binary search over runs or a scan of its own bits, never a scan to the end of
  the scope's run (`BitSet.nextClearBit`, 89% of the CPU of the 1,000,000-position benchmark). Answers unchanged to the bit.
- **VaR and exposure: refusals for room remembered.** A date refused for room (`DRS-5204`, `DRS-5218`; exposure `DRS-5445`) is
  remembered for `drishti.var.refusal-ttl-seconds` (300; exposure `drishti.ccr.exposure.refusal-ttl-seconds`): asked again, `503` at
  once with `Retry-After`, without reading the lake (fifty requests at once make one load). Forgotten when room is freed, the inputs
  change or the time is up; listed in the status (`refusedForRoom`) and in Admin → Caches (`var.refusals`, purgeable). Tests:
  `RefusalsTest`, `VarRefusalRememberedTest`.
- **VaR: mapped dates bounded by the disk, not a quarter of the heap.** `memory-budget-mb` now applies to the heap tier only. A mapped
  build reserves three times its largest hot file, at least 256 MB when none exists yet (the estimate was 0), and checks the disk every
  64 MB while the rows stream in: a date that would leave the disk under the guard is refused with `DRS-5204` naming the bytes needed and
  free, its spill and part file deleted. The page cache is advisory: the status compares the open hot files with the memory beside the
  heap (`memory`). Test: `VarDiskBudgetRefusalTest`.
- **VaR and exposure: least recently used dates leave first; `hot-dates` 10.** `drishti.var.hot-dates` and
  `drishti.ccr.exposure.hot-dates` default to 10 (were 2) and count dates. Every request stamps its date; the least recently used leaves
  first; the date just used, the newest business date and the dates pinned in memory always stay. A byte safety net,
  `drishti.var.open-heap-mb` (0: automatic, 0.4 x heap - 512 MB - load-threads x 1.6 GB, at least a tenth of the heap; exposure its own),
  closes the least recently used dates' currency books, then stress books, then whole dates, never a protected one. Every book reports
  `heapBytes()`; Admin → Caches `var.dates` shows every open book's heap. One shared class for both engines (`OpenDates`). Test:
  `VarEvictionLruTest`.
- **Pinned dates.** `drishti.var.pinned` (and `drishti.ccr.exposure.pinned`): `month-end`, `quarter-end`, `year-end`,
  `fiscal-year-end` (with `drishti.var.fiscal-year-end`, `MM-DD`), `stress-window` and named `dates`, each with `back` and `keep`
  (`disk`: the hot file built in the background after the official record and never trimmed; `memory`: open, protected, counted in
  `hot-dates`); the last business day in every calendar of `drishti.business-date.calendar` (a New York or Toronto holiday moves it back).
  Off by default. Listed with reasons and build state in `GET /api/v1/var/status` and `GET /api/v1/exposure/status`. Test:
  `PinnedDatesTest`.
- **VaR memory: aggregates read from the hot file.** A mapped date's book, cell and node aggregates (`AGGS`, float64) are mapped when the
  hot file opens, like the position rows, instead of read onto the heap (642 MB a date at 1,000,000 positions): the heap keeps the key
  to row index; a node's vector is a copy of its row, the same float64 bits. An intraday layer keeps only its changed aggregates and reads
  the rest from the morning's mapping. The file format is unchanged (earlier files open as they are); `AGGS` is checked by
  `VarHotFile.verify` with the matrices. Every book reports `heapBytes()` (`VarHeapPerDateTest`: 5.7 MB a date at 10,000 positions,
  about 14.8 MB before; node runs 49 KB instead of 706 KB of bitmaps). The build writes the `AGGS` section a batch of rows at a time
  instead of one `byte[]` of every aggregate (642 MB less at the load's peak at 1,000,000 positions); the file's bytes are unchanged.
- **A date in use stays open over the byte safety net.** The net never closes a date (or its currency and stress books) read in the
  last `-Ddrishti.open-dates.net-grace-seconds` (120): at a heap whose automatic net is smaller than one date, two dates asked in turn
  by many users closed each other and loaded again at once, and the loads' working memory ran out. Idle dates still leave; a new load
  without room is still refused (`DRS-5204`). Found by the 1,000,000-position re-benchmark at `-Xmx6g`. Test: `VarEvictionLruTest`.
- **The Parquet footer cache weighed in bytes.** Parsed footers are weighed at about 700 bytes a column chunk and bounded by
  `-Ddrishti.parquet.footer-cache-mb` (64), replacing `-Ddrishti.parquet.footer-cache-groups` (50,000 row groups, which held 385 MB
  at 1,000,000 positions). Test: `ParquetFootersWeightTest`.
- **The sizing formula corrected** (VAR_GUIDE 27.1, RESOURCES_AND_SCALE 9.5, BENCHMARK 12.1): the heap of a book with node runs and
  mapped aggregates, about 0.77 GB at 1,000,000 positions (3.17 GB measured before); to be confirmed by the 1,000,000-position
  re-benchmark. Tests: `VarHeapPerDateTest` (`-Dvar.heap.positions`, 10,000 by default), `VarEvictDeleteTest` (a hot file deleted only
  once its three mappings are released).
- **The phone display** ([MOBILE_DISPLAY.md](docs/guides/BUILD_GUIDE.md#32-designing-for-phones), [USER_GUIDE.md, On a phone](docs/guides/USER_GUIDE.md#on-a-phone)).
  Every panel has a phone tier: **must** (in full, first), **glance** (a compact form: five rows in chosen columns and sort, a chart as a
  sparkline with its last value and change, the first bars, figures or tab, a map as its places, with *Show all*), **more** (a row under
  *More on this page*, loaded in place when tapped, bound as the viewer with the page's controls and date) or **desk** (named under *On
  desktop*, with the page's link to copy). A phone gets only its must and glance panels; a tablet keeps its layout less the desk panels;
  a desktop is unchanged. *Show everything* gives the whole page for the session, *Why these panels* says which layer set each tier. The
  grammar: `phone:` on a panel, a use and a Sutra, and a fragment's `doc.phone`, checked as `DRS-2059`, carried in the ViewModel's new
  `phone`; the kind defaults (tables and charts glance, provenance and notes more, pivots desk); the site (`ui.phone.rules`,
  `ui.phone.packs`, `ui.phone.kinds`) and the edition (`phone.rules`) set tiers and cap them with `max:`, the cap winning; Drishti Risk
  puts its VaR contribution panels under *More*. The device is the `drishti-device` cookie the browser keeps from its width, or an
  `X-Drishti-Device` header. The VaR and exposure pages and the four edition landings take the same tiers part by part
  (`ui.phone.pages`, an edition's `phone.pages` and `home.phone`). Person pins come later, as decided. Tests: `PhoneReaderTest`,
  `PhoneViewTest`, `test_phone.py`, `test_phone_browser.py` (390 px and 1280 px, dark and light).
- **The lens menus on a phone** (LX1 option C): below 640 px an edition's subject menus fold into one menu named after it (**Risk**,
  **Trading**, **Market**, **World**), first in the bar, a column per subject; a wider screen keeps the subject menus as before. The lens
  documents' checklists say built.
- **Connectors for AWS S3 Tables and Delta Lake on S3, with Python tool scripts.** S3 Tables: the `iceberg` connector with
  `catalog: s3tables` and one setting, `table-bucket-arn`; the S3 Tables Iceberg REST endpoint, SigV4 under `s3tables`, the region,
  the warehouse, the REST prefix and the namespace follow from the ARN (`S3Tables` in drishti-iceberg), kinds are read as S3 Tables
  names (`pnl-vector` is `pnl_vector`), the native engine only, idle until the ARN is set; the loaders and `iceberg-external` take the
  same settings ([ICEBERG_CONNECTOR.md section 20](plugins/drishti-plugin-iceberg/README.md#aws-s3-tables)). Delta Lake on S3: the
  `delta` connector with `root: s3://<bucket>/<prefix>` and credentials from the AWS default chain
  ([DELTA_CONNECTOR.md section 17](plugins/drishti-plugin-delta/README.md#delta-lake-on-aws-s3)). Templates in
  `config/connectors.examples/s3tables/` and `delta-s3/` (`risk-store.yaml`, `trade-endur.yaml`, each folder with its README). Tool
  scripts in Python with `boto3` (no AWS CLI; `.sh` and `.ps1` wrappers): `deploy/aws/s3-tables/` and `deploy/aws/delta-s3/` create,
  check (one table read end to end as Drishti reads it) and remove the buckets, the namespace or prefix and the IAM policy, with
  `--dry-run`, `--region`, `--profile` and `--env`, never printing a credential ([TOOLS.md section 4.14](docs/guides/CLI_REFERENCE.md)).
  Tests: `S3TablesTest` (the settings an ARN gives, the names, the signatures against ones recorded with botocore),
  `S3TablesRestTest` (a stand-in REST endpoint that refuses unsigned requests), `IcebergS3TablesTest`, `DeltaOnAwsS3Test` (the
  template on S3Mock in the JVM), `test_s3_tables.py` and `test_delta_s3.py` (botocore's Stubber). Live runs pending an AWS
  sandbox account.

### Why VaR moved


- **Why VaR moved (RO1).** The VaR page's new tab **Why it moved** (`VAR EXPLAIN <scope>`, or `VAR <scope> EXPLAIN`) splits a scope's
  VaR change between two business dates (default the one before the newest, and the newest) into causes that add up exactly: a chain of
  states S0 to S7, each a full VaR (the earlier date as officially captured, restated, by the later hierarchy and rules, without the trades
  out, on the common scenario days, at the later market, on the later set, with the trades in), each step the difference of two states.
  Each step names its drivers (incremental VaR of the trades out and in, the books moved by the hierarchy, the scenario days that left or
  entered with their rank, each child's component VaR change for the market) and every state its VaR scenario's date in words; an
  order-free view by child also adds up to the change, and the limit-use line splits its change into the VaR's part and the limit's. Only
  the churn is summed. Three views over one answer, **Waterfall** (the default), **Matrix** (every child node, the steps across) and
  **Sentences**, drawn with the standard panel kinds by the console's renderer; the view is kept in the address and the person's settings
  (`varExplainView`); phone tiers; F1 opens the guide's section. **Download the working (.xlsx)**: every state's P&L column, ranks and VaR
  as formulas, each step a difference of cells, the add-up check and checks against the engine to the cent, on the Playground's frame.
  `GET /api/v1/var/explain`, `/explain/matrix`, `/explain.xlsx`; `drishti.py var explain <scope> [--from] [--to] [--matrix] [--xlsx]`;
  settings `drishti.var.explain.*` (the order of the causes, window lines, amendments, top, drivers, cache). The Shapley variant is
  planned. VAR_GUIDE.md section 3.11.
- **Tests and tools.** Browser tests not about the phone display read the whole page (the *Show everything* cookie), the phone
  tests the phone's; the Sutra Next equivalence compares the page drawn without its phone tiers; the scheduler and pack reload tests
  wait for the state they check; the VaR P&L history generator is `tools/packgen/var/pnl_history.py` (it shared a module name with the
  test data's history on multi-day runs); the demo lake's 87 tables in the guides.
- **The plan.** 2.9.9 (memory, scale and mobile) and 2.9.10 (the VaR change explained) ship together as 2.9.10; there is no 2.9.9
  release. Next: 2.9.11 sensitivities and market-risk capital (with the cluster's VaR timeouts), 2.9.12 counterparty engines, 2.9.13
  Java 25 and performance I, 2.9.14 oversight, 2.9.15 regulatory reporting, 2.9.16 native performance II, 2.9.17 XVA and wrong-way risk,
  2.9.18 advanced market risk, 2.9.19 executive. One full drill per release; a second when the first needed fixes, and always for the
  performance releases.

## 2.9.8 — Regulatory VaR reporting begins; the VaR Playground; the Data view; choosing the stress window; the lenses' own menus (2026-11-01)

- **Regulatory VaR reporting** ([REGULATORY_VAR_REPORTING.md](docs/guides/REGULATORY_VAR_REPORTING.md), one document for Canada and the
  US to cell level). The `desk-pnl` kind (`DPNL`: actual and hypothetical P&L per desk and day, its contract and generated demo P&L);
  the regulatory backtest at 99% and 97.5% of the bank and every desk with zone, US capital multiplier and the desks behind each
  exception (`VAR BANK BACKTEST`, `var backtest`); period statistics over the official records with the 60-day and 12-week stressed
  averages (`VAR BANK STATS FY2026`, `var stats`); report definitions in `config/reports/`, frozen runs with each cell's lineage and
  checks, and maker-checker-approver sign-off before xlsx, csv and PDF are released (`VAR REPORT`, `var report`); the pilot pack (the
  annual report's VaR table and the backtesting chart); a demo-only synthetic official history (off by default). Planned input
  contracts (status `planned`): trade cash flows, a risk-type mapping, finance's P&L, capital inputs, Volcker attributes, regulatory
  desks. The two analysis documents were merged into this one guide; VAR_GUIDE keeps summaries and links. Tests: the engine's
  backtest, statistics and runs, `VarRegulatoryApiTest`, `test_var_regulatory_browser.py` (three people sign a run), the CLI.
- **The VaR Playground** (`PLAY VAR`, `/play`, `var playground`; [VAR_GUIDE section 3.10](docs/guides/VAR_GUIDE.md)): a scope or up
  to 50 positions worked cell by cell (500 positions shown, the rest in Rest of scope) with a formula bar and the explanation beside
  the grid; a streamed workbook of real formulas (Main, Config, Data, FX, PnL, Explain, Provenance) at 100, 500, 1,000, 10,000 or all
  positions, its size and recalculation time estimated first. Recalculated by headless LibreOffice, it equals the engine to the cent
  at 1, 50 and 500 positions. Tutorial 25 step 18.
- **The Data view** (`DATA`, Views → Data, `/api/v1/data`, `drishti.py data get`, `tools/datacli.py`): every dataset with source,
  format and dates; a date, columns and filter lines; the row count; the day streamed as `.jsonl.gz` with entitlements and masks
  applied and each download audited. Tutorial 7.
- **Choosing the stress window** (`SWIN`, `var stress-window`; VAR_GUIDE 18.9): the `pnl-history` kind (`PNLH`) anchored to the
  engine's stress P&L, every 250-day window valued as a stressed VaR, the worst against the window in use, an alert past a threshold,
  proposals approved by a second person.
- **The lenses' own menus** (`menus.top`, subject menus in `config/menus.yaml`): Risk, Trading, Market and World put their subject menus
  in the top bar, each item showing its command. `PLAY` and `DATA` are edition words (LENSES.md).
- **One benchmark document** ([BENCHMARK.md](docs/admin/BENCHMARK.md)) replaces SCALE_BENCHMARK and BENCHMARK_2_9_7; figures still to
  be measured say so.
- **Three machines on premises and on AWS** ([CLUSTER_DEPLOYMENT.md section 16](docs/guides/CLUSTER_GUIDE.md)): why three,
  what is shared, failover, sizing from 200K to 10M positions, bill of materials, the AWS reference and monthly cost, fast disks (gp3,
  io2, instance NVMe), ECS on EC2 against Fargate; the three decks carry it.
- **Temporary files under the data folder**: the command line honours `DRISHTI_TMP_DIR`; the release drill keeps every temporary file
  under `data/tmp/drill` (`DRISHTI_DRILL_TMP`) and its Java 25 copy beside the repository (`DRISHTI_DRILL_COPY_DIR`), where git sees no
  repository above it; CONFIGURATION.md lists every process's temp folder.
- **Designs for the next release**: RO1, RO2, the board pack and Market data checks, one screen each with option A as the default view
  and the others a click away, built as Sutras.

The server had published (the API and the CLI were never wrong; a reload showed Published). The item's answers now go through `drishtiBi.itemAnswers` (`bi-lib.js`): a read answered after a later save, publish or move is dropped. `test_bi_publish_order.py` plays the race in Node; `test_bi_wave_b_browser.py` and `test_bi_languages_browser.py`, which failed whenever the read was the slower of the two, pass again.

    the console only, audited `embed-sign-in-window` with the origin, user and time); the token reaches the page by `postMessage` to its

    SSO session lasts, then the button again; an unregistered origin gets the button disabled with `DRS-8002` naming it; on phones a new

  - **Fix: the client-mode "stall" on a shared item opened from an inbox link** was a race: the reply box was usable before its deferred
    script, which in client mode waits behind the renderer's module graph (fetched cold, import by import, in a fresh browser context), so
    a quick Ctrl+Enter was lost. The box and its button now come disabled until wired, and client-drawn pages preload the renderer's
    modules (`modulepreload`). The test passes three times in client and in server mode. Also: a panel's *Expand* button and its
