- **10-day VaR and the confidence chosen, built (row 2b of 2.9.7)** ([VAR_GUIDE.md section 18.6](docs/guides/VAR_GUIDE.md#186-horizons-the-two-10-day-methods-and-the-confidence-chosen-as-built-297)):
  every VaR answer can be read through a lens, computed on demand from the same 1-day scenario P&Ls, nothing new fed or stored.
  **Horizon** 1-day (the default) or 10-day by **√10** (VaR, ES and every vector-derived figure × √10; VaR and ES exactly the 1-day × √10)
  or by **the 10-day sum** (each scenario the sum of 10 consecutive 1-day P&Ls in the scenario set's order, N − 9 overlapping windows:
  509 give 500, 250 give 241; VaR, ES, components, contributions and the P&L path on the windows); the default method a setting,
  `drishti.var.ten-day-method` (`sqrt10`). **Confidence** of VaR and ES from configured lists, `drishti.var.confidences` (95%, 97.5%,
  99%, 99.5%; 99% the default) and `es-confidences` (97.5% the default): another rank of the same sorted vector. A scope's 10-day
  vector is the windowed sum of its summed 1-day vector in a fixed order, the same bits across shards and thread counts (tested). On the
  VaR page: **Horizon**, **Confidence** and **ES** beside the Reporting currency (the approved mock-up), every panel redrawn, the method
  strip naming them, the link `?h=10d&m=sum&q=0.99&esq=0.975`, the person's settings (`varView`) remembering them, full width on a
  phone; **limit use** only at the limit's own horizon and confidence (`var-limit` gains optional `HORIZON` and `CONFIDENCE`, 1D and 0.99
  by default), else *limit is for 1-day 99%: not comparable*; backtest exceptions only at 1 day. Commands `VAR BANK 10D`,
  `VAR BANK 10D SUM`, `VAR BANK 10D SQRT`, `VAR BANK 95`, `VAR BANK 10D SUM 97.5`, `VAR BANK ES 95` (the type-ahead offers them); the API's
  `horizon`, `method`, `confidence`, `esConfidence`; the CLI's `--horizon`, `--method`, `--confidence`, `--es-confidence`; VRES's
  parameters (`VRES BANK~horizon=10d~method=sum`); captures and exports name their lens. Official records unchanged (1-day at the
  configured confidence) and carry **`HORIZON`** (`1D`) and **`METHOD`** (null): published rows `CONTRACT_VERSION` 1.4, contracts
  var-official 1.1, var-result 1.1, var-limit 1.1. BI: `nodes.HORIZON`, `nodes.METHOD`, the measures **VaR confidence** and **ES
  confidence**. The full-revaluation slot (a second vector set, `HORIZON: 10D`) designed, not built. Demo figures (the bank, 2026-09-30):
  1-day 99% **112,041,646** (unchanged), 10-day √10 **354,306,794**, 10-day sum **274,544,283** (the 5th worst of 500 windows), 1-day
  95% **68,355,411**. Docs: VAR_GUIDE, USER_GUIDE, tutorial 25 (a new step), the Market risk Knowledge page (a term and a confusion),

- **Plan: one configuration document (C1–C3)**: CONFIGURATION.md as the one place for every setting of every kind (server, console, connectors, packs, editions, stores, BI runs, write-back), generated from the sources with a drill check, and Help → Configuration in the console with the value in effect for administrators.
- **Resources and scale, built (step 3 of 2.9.7)** ([RESOURCES_AND_SCALE.md section 14](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md#3212-bounded-resources-inside-one-server)):
  - **Fix: the exposure trade-paths cache key** is a SHA-256 digest of the sorted trade ids (a 32-bit hash let two different sets of one
    size share an answer); the lake read runs outside Caffeine's compute.
  - **The viewers' views are bounded** (VaR `drishti.var.view-cache-mb` 64, exposure `drishti.ccr.exposure.view-cache-mb` 16, idle an
    hour) and released with their date (soak audit H10).
  - **Shard books released for age** (`drishti.var.sharding.release-after-seconds`, 900): members announce their open dates; a book of a
    date nobody has open, outside the newest `hot-dates` and unread, is unmapped (soak audit H9: two owners kept each other's dates).
  - **Id-map files released, then deleted** (Delta and Iceberg, soak audit H3): a map leaving the cache is unmapped once its readers are
    done; older versions are unmapped before they are deleted (the previous version kept); a sweep at start; each connector's folder
    capped by `id-map-disk.max-gb` (5). Before, deleted files stayed mapped (disk held on Linux, failed deletes on Windows).
  - **Id-map disk safeguards and `id-map-disk.ttl`** (Delta and Iceberg, one class `IdMapFolder` in `drishti-api`): the cap never evicts a
    map mapped, being read, written or mapped in the last five minutes, or of a date open in VaR or exposure (the engines register their
    open dates through `DatesInUse`), so a date in use is never evicted and rebuilt in a loop; a date whose map alone is over the cap is
    kept, warned about once per date and version (log and Admin → Caches **Dates**) naming the setting to raise. New
    `id-map-disk.ttl` (default off; at least `24h`, refused at start below that): drops maps unused (mapped or read) that long, ±10% per
    file, never the latest and previous dates, today's, an open date or a map being read, nor a mapped map when no engine can vouch;
    on the connector's scheduler, unmapped then deleted, a failed delete (Windows) tried again. Admin → Caches says why each map went:
    `expired (ttl)`, `evicted (max-gb)`, `replaced (new version)`. **Idle mappings released** (`id-map-disk.idle-release`, 30m, at
    least 5m): a map not read that long is unmapped, its file kept and mapped again at the next read (never while read, never an open
    date), so the heap caches' mapped maps no longer hold the folder above `max-gb`: it converges back under the cap; only maps in use
    can exceed it (`idMapsInUseOverCap`). Tests: `IdMapFolderTest` (13), `DeltaDocStalenessTest` and
    `IcebergDocStalenessTest` (the document cache never serves stale data: new after a signal, new after `refresh-seconds` without one,
    old only as of the old version), `CacheAdminTest`. Docs: [OPERATIONS.md section 12.3](docs/guides/OPERATIONS_GUIDE.md#145-disk-caches-per-connector)
    (sizing: about 75 MB per million ids per date), CONFIGURATION, DELTA_CONNECTOR, ICEBERG_CONNECTOR.
  - **BI layers' retention** (`drishti.bi.query.store-max-dates` 260, `store-max-gb` 50): the oldest dates beyond, then the least
    recently built beyond the cap, never a table's newest; at start and every ten minutes.
  - **The small maps that only grew are bounded** (VaR's built-ahead status, official indexes, BI's per-date generations and epochs,
    parsed datasets, write-back overlays (soak H11), the Kafka and message-state weights).
  - **The heap tier's position vectors** are kept within a quarter of `drishti.var.memory-budget-mb` a date (before: unbounded).
  - **Logs rotate, dumps are capped, console leftovers go:** `drishti.logging.file` (100 MB a file, 1 GB in all, compressed; the stack
    sets it per node, standard output to `<node>.out`), `drishti.disk.max-dumps` (2), the console's crash folders removed at start.
  - **No pinning on Java 21 where the guard missed it:** the PV stream's apply and flush (a `ReentrantLock`, the date loaded first),
    Iceberg's delete files and Redis's dictionaries (`SingleFlight`); `NoBlockingUnderSynchronizedTest` now checks synchronous cache
    loaders and the engines' lake reads too.
  - **Admin → Caches as designed (O1), purge a date (O2), here or the cluster (PO-6):** every cache of the server (VaR, exposure, BI,
    pack access, the mapped id maps besides the engine and connectors) with where it lives, size against its limit, age, hit rate,
    freshness, dates and last purge, under the memory and disk totals. `GET /api/v1/admin/caches` now answers `{memory, disk, caches}`
    (each row keeps `name`, `type`, `stats`); new `GET /api/v1/admin/caches/{name}/dates`; `POST .../purge?date=D&scope=cluster`;
    `SourcePlugin.purgeDate` (Delta, Iceberg); CLI `server caches --dates NAME`, `purge NAME --date D --cluster`.
  - **Announce a load from the UI (O4), forwarded over Drishti\*net (PO-5):** Admin → Packs → Data loads → Announce a load (audited
    `load-announced`); a `ready` load announced on one member is passed on once to every other live member (`forwardedTo`).
  - **Reload one date (O3):** `POST /api/v1/var/reload?date=D`, `POST /api/v1/exposure/reload?date=D`; `drishti.py var reload --date D`,
    `exposure reload --date D`.
  - **Compact object headers on Java 25, generational ZGC on 21 (D5, PO-8):** every JVM started through `tools/javacmd.py` (the stack,
    loaders, tests) gets `-XX:+UseCompactObjectHeaders` on 25; the Docker and ECS images add it on 25 and `-XX:+ZGenerational` on 21.
  - **Hot files kept across restarts in the server images (PO-10):** `DRISHTI_VAR_KEEP_HOT_FILES`, `DRISHTI_EXPOSURE_KEEP_HOT_FILES`.
  - **Decisions recorded:** RESOURCES_AND_SCALE section 12, PO-1 to PO-11 as recommended (product owner, 2026-10-30); not built in this
    step: D1 (the mapped skeleton; what remains is in section 14.23), D8, PO-11.
  - **The VaR skeleton's id maps encoded (D2):** four hash maps of boxed ordinals a date become sorted indexes: the heap of two open
    dates of 100,000 trades 161 MB to 117 MB (-27%); a lookup 0.33 µs (a binary search).
  - **One cache budget (D3, PO-2):** `drishti.memory.cache-share` (0.5 of the heap) in weighted pools sets the maxima of the Delta
    connectors' shared caches and the engines' answers (VaR and exposure answers now weighed in bytes); halved for a minute when the heap
    after a collection passes `drishti.memory.squeeze-at` (0.85); a build guard against new count-only caches.
  - **The console's log lines carry a timestamp (D9).**
  - **A fixed reduction order (PO-7):** any scope's VaR is equal to the bit whatever the server's core count (blocks aligned to the
    ordinal, sized from the set, added in order); measured within +3.2% at 8 and 24 threads, desks and baskets 17 to 41% faster.
  - **The version watch (O9, PO-9):** an open VaR or exposure date notices a lake change without a signal within
    `drishti.var.version-check` / `drishti.ccr.exposure.version-check` (30 s), reloads in the background, and warns meanwhile.
  - **The soak (O8), short form in CI:** `VarResourcesSoakTest` (dates and versions in turn: every holder bounded, the heap flat).
  - **Health → Disk (O7):** every folder against its cap and the free space against the guard (`disk` in `GET /api/v1/admin/health`).
  - **Hot files bounded in GB, and a free-space guard (O5):** `drishti.var.tier.max-disk-gb` (0: half the disk) and
    `drishti.ccr.exposure.max-disk-gb` (0: a quarter; it wins over the retention, PO-3), least recently used first; a build that would
    leave the disk under `drishti.disk.min-free-percent` (10) / `min-free-gb` (20) is refused with the new `503 DRS-5218`.
  - **Date loads off the common pool:** VaR, shard books and exposure load on pools of their own (`drishti.var.load-threads`,
    `drishti.ccr.exposure.load-threads`, 2 each).
- **The client-side renderer, phase 2: the console draws its entity page with it** ([CLIENT_RENDERER.md section 16](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md#301-one-page-renderer-one-embed-renderer),
  [ADR-022](docs/architecture/adr/022-one-renderer-in-the-browser.md)). **Drishti Render 1.0.0** (`static/render/1.0.0/`; 0.1.0 stays
  served, unchanged). **`ui.render`** (CONFIGURATION.md): `ui.render.mode` `server` (default this release) or `client`, page by page
  (`ui.render.pages`: `view`, `pane`); `?render=server|client` compares the two on one address. On a client page the entity page
  (`/v/{kind}/{id}`, what `/go`, a share and a history day open, a workspace pane) embeds its ViewModel as the page arranges it (the
  reader's layout, saved pivots, grid) and `static/js/view-render.js` draws it into the page's own `.view`; the page's scripts are
  deferred after it, so every console behaviour runs on the drawn view unchanged: the per-column funnels and their address, Chart any
  table, the drill's address and Back, Customize, layout mode, the download menu, the Pivot tab's grid, the nested-pivot grid, controls,
  row events, refresh and computed panels. **Live** goes through the library's `subscribe()` on the tab's channel with a new `vm:`
  subscription whose panel patches are panels (JSON), no HTML. **About this page** is drawn by the library from JSON
  (`/v/{kind}/{id}/about?format=json`). `/v/.../panels`, `/events` and `/children` answer each panel's JSON beside its HTML. **The library
  gained**: `behaviours: 'console'` (the console's own funnels, Chart any table, Pivot grid, nested pivot, drills in place, zoom and
  controls, loaded beside it and started in its container: one implementation each), `about: true` (a side sheet in the container),
  `navigation: 'follow'`, `subscribe(fn)` for a host's own channel, `drawPanel`/`drawStrip`/`drawAbout`/`drawCharts`, `DRS-9106` and
  `DRS-9107`. **Elements 2.0 and the embed API v2** beside v1 (unchanged) for one release (ELEMENTS.md section 19): `<drishti-view>`,
  `<drishti-panel>` and the alias `<drishti-screen>` on the renderer, with 1.x's API; `/embed/v2/views/{kind}/{id}` answers the ViewModel,

  and `/embed/v2/elements/2/drishti-elements.js`; the demo host's `/?elements=2`. **The contract**: the server stamps `"contract": "1.0"`
  on every ViewModel (`ViewModel.CONTRACT`, required in the schema). **Three console fixes phase 1 found**: a panel with no `data` and
  `empty: false` no longer breaks the macros; a candlestick's candles carry `openText` ... `volumeText` and both renderers print them; an
  `hbar` bar list no longer widens the page (long labels cut with an ellipsis and a title, long values widen their own column), which
  stopped `funds/fund`, `trading/murex/xccy-swap` and `world-economy/.../region` scrolling sideways; a narrow panel's header now wraps its
  tools (`funds/fund` at 1280 px). Customize, Outline and Grid redraw a client page's body with the library after a step
  (`drishtiFreshGrid`), and the library's About carries *Ask about this page*. The whole browser suite run once in client mode: every
  failure listed with its cause in CLIENT_RENDERER.md 16.5 (one open: the first client page a new context opens from the inbox's link
  stalls before its module runs). Not moved, and why: the Studio and
  Build previews, Compare, search, monitors and exports (CLIENT_RENDERER.md 16.1). Tests: `test_render_console_browser.py` (every captured
  view, edge case and pack Sutra on the console's page in both modes, and each behaviour in both), `test_render_behaviours_browser.py`,
  `test_embed_elements2_browser.py`, `test_render_phase2.py`, `ViewModelSchemaTest` (the stamp, the candle texts). Docs:
  CLIENT_RENDERER.md, ADR-022, ELEMENTS.md (architecture 19, guide), API_GUIDE (embed v2, `contract`), VIEWMODEL.md, GENUI.md 9 (streams
  the JSON messages), CONFIGURATION (`ui.render`), USER_GUIDE.

- **Design: resources and scale** ([RESOURCES_AND_SCALE.md](docs/guides/CLUSTER_GUIDE.md#15-sizing-memory-cpu-and-disk), design, not built): the single
  design for memory, CPU and disk. An inventory of every cache and memory-mapped file read in the code, flagging the unbounded and
  count-only ones (role views, shard books, id-map files, BI layers on disk, hot files bounded by file count, exposure hot files kept by
  the retention); freshness without a signal (an engine's open date is not re-checked: a version watch, O9, proposed); the heap skeleton
  (D1: memory-map it, recommended over encoding or sharding it), one cache budget, releases with the date, compact headers, the collector
  per role, the CPU items with pinning found on Java 21 and where SIMD would and would not help; disk caps with a free-space guard,
  Admin → Caches and Health → Disk as designed, metrics and alerts; capacity at 2.3M and 10M positions before and after D1; the benchmark,
  profiling and soak method; the build order and eleven decisions. Docs corrected beside it: ARCHITECTURE 14 (Admin → Caches does not show
  every cache) and 16.3 (an open VaR date is not re-checked without a signal; Delta's date version is a stamp of the date's files);
  PERFORMANCE (the Docker image runs ZGC without `-XX:+ZGenerational`).

- **Plan: caches, disk and loads visible and bounded (O1–O8)**: Admin → Caches with each cache's place, size against its limit, TTL, hit rate and dates; purge a date; reload one date; announce a load from the UI; hot files bounded in GB with a free-space guard; old id-map versions removed; Admin → Health → Disk; a soak test that keeps memory and disk flat.

- **ARCHITECTURE.md 16.2 and 16.3:** choosing a data mechanism (the lake, computed kinds, Python workers, BI, the hot file and sharding) with the four-question check a measure passes before it uses the heavy one; and how memory-mapped data follows the lake (the data-load signal, the inputs' digest from the tables' data versions, provenance on every answer).

- **Plan: the order of the rest of 2.9.7 and a memory and CPU diet** (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN): the renderer, then the benchmark with profiling (JFR, heap histograms) on Java 21 and 25 as the baseline, then ten measured improvements (the heap skeleton per shard, dictionary-encoded ids, one cache budget, released maps, compact headers on 25, the renderer, fewer JSON passes, faster cold loads, quieter logs, unpinned virtual threads on 21), the benchmark again, soak-proofing, the fixes and the release; Java 21 and 25 both stay supported.

### Drishti Trading: the fourth edition, "my" scoping, its three landings, four lenses (2026-10-30)

- **Drishti Trading** (`drishti.edition: trading`, `config/editions/trading.yaml`), for traders and desk heads: the five packs of Drishti
  Risk (allow-only) and 33 commands (the blotter `TRD` … `ITRD`; `BOOK`, `DESK`, `TRDR`, `POS`; `VLIM`, `VWIF`, `VRES`, `TVAL`, `PNLV`,
  `HIER`, `PORT`; `CPTY`, `GRP`, `NSET`, `NSMTM`, `CPMTM`, `LIM`, `XWIF`, `EXP`; `CRV`, `FX`, `FXV`, `EQ`, `EQX`, `CMD`, `CMDC`, `BND`,
  `CDS`) with the words `VAR`, `EXP`, `BI`, `FUNC`, `WHAT`; regulatory, stress, collateral operations and macro economics left out;
  Build, Studio, forms and the data map off; the trading and VaR BI datasets; branding "Drishti Trading". `PSUM`, `PSTRIP` and `PBOOK`
  are the compute-demo sample pack's, not a trading pack: left out.
- **"My" scoping, configured**: `trading.people` (the edition file, the console's `application.local.yaml` on top) maps a person to a
  trader (their books) or a desk (`role: desk-head`); else a trader record matching their user or name; else a **View as** picker whose
  choice is kept in their settings (`tradingView`, a new key of `/api/v1/me/settings`, validated). An administrator may always pick. The
  first landing follows the trading role (`trading.landing-by-role`), below the person's own choice. Scoping never widens access: every
  read is the person's, with their roles and masks.
- **Its Home**: the three approved mock-ups in the terminal look with a green accent. **Trader desk**: P&L today (MtM change against the
  business day before, from the trade valuations on both dates; none without the day before, said), my VaR (intraday when updated) and the
  highest limit use of my books, DV01 (only when the data has it), trades today (new, amended, cancelled from `TRADE_ACTION`,
  `TRADE_STATUS` and `SOURCE_UPDATE_TIME`), **Check a new trade** (one VaR what-if on the book and one pre-deal check on the counterparty,
  each the engine's own on a copy of a booked trade of the product scaled to the notional; the exposure engine's add-on proxy, labelled,
  when the exact method cannot run), today's blotter, top positions by VaR contribution, quick commands. **Desk head**: desk P&L, desk
  VaR and limit use, breaches, books near their limit, the largest counterparty's share of the desk's positive MtM; limit use by book over
  the last five business dates from the official VaR records (every cell prints its percentage); by trader (P&L, component VaR, trades;
  masked for a role without raw, said); P&L against VaR from the official history (left out, with a note, without one); overnight
  movers. **Explorer**: the command line, chips, grouped commands, recent Trading commands. Read-only routes
  `/api/home/trading/{me,valuations,blotter,risk,limits,pnl-var,traders}` and `POST /api/home/trading/check` (`DRS-4023` unless the
  edition or lens shows the commands), `plugins/banking/trading_landing.py` (LENSES.md section 6).
- **Four lenses by default**: `drishti.lenses` is `risk,world,market,trading` (server `application.yaml`, the stack, Docker, the AWS
  example); Open, Leave and Switch to across all four; no design link inside the Trading lens.
- **Tests**: `EditionTradingServerTest` (the lens through the real settings API, its commands, `ECON`, `SCN`, `COLL`, `FRTB` refused with
  `DRS-4023`, its BI), `EditionTwoLensesServerTest` with four lenses, `SettingsTest` (`tradingView`); `test_trading_landing.py`;
  eight Trading cases in `test_edition.py`; `test_edition_trading_browser.py` (A, B and C at 390 and 1280 px, every theme, the page-width
  audit, no request outside the console, the check box end to end).

### Arrow where it pays: measured, and Arrow to the browser for the VaR contribution tables (2026-10-30)

- **Measured first** (`tests/test_arrow_bench_var_browser.py`, `tests/test_arrow_bench_bi_browser.py`, opt-in `DRISHTI_ARROW_BENCH=1`;
  scratch server and console): payload bytes raw and gzip, the browser's parse time and click-to-painted, JSON against Arrow, for the
  VaR P&L path, the contribution tables, BI grids of 5,000 and 50,000 trades and a large search. **Arrow kept** for the VaR contribution
  tables by position and by trade (1,173 and 1,281 rows on the demo desk: 692 and 632 KB of JSON become 243 and 244 KB, gzip 21% and
  15% smaller, fetched in 59 to 61 ms against 81 to 91 ms, painted in the same time). **JSON kept** for the P&L path (no smaller, gzip
  larger), a node's few children, and the BI grid (36% smaller raw but 8 to 14% gzip, slower to parse, painted no sooner); **search** is
  HTML drawn on the server (1,000 rows: a 680 KB page, whose rows would be 124 KB as JSON and 74 KB as Arrow: the saving is drawing in the
  browser, left to the client-side renderer, row 2). The numbers and why: `docs/guides/DATA_FORMATS.md` section 6.
- **`Accept: application/vnd.apache.arrow.stream`** on `POST /api/v1/bi/reports/{id}/query` and `GET /api/v1/var/scope/contributions`
  answers the JSON answer as an Arrow IPC stream: its table the record batch (repeated text as dictionaries, booleans, 64-bit integers,
  doubles, nulls), the rest of the answer in the schema's metadata (`drishti.answer`, `drishti.table`). An answer Arrow is not written
  with goes as JSON; without the header nothing changes. Server: `ArrowAnswers`, and `ArrowIpcWriter` gains schema metadata, dictionary
  columns and boolean columns. Console: `core/arrow_answer.py` passes the server's Arrow through and writes it with pyarrow from a JSON
  answer (a BI answer given in time by a run, with the run in `X-Drishti-Ran-As`).
- **In the browser:** `drishtiFetchTable(url, opts)` (`static/js/drishti-table.js`) returns one column-oriented table whichever format came
  back (typed columns, the JSON answer rebuilt cell for cell; 64-bit integers as Numbers where safe and text where not, decimals as exact
  text, dates and timestamps as ISO text keeping their zone); `?tables=json` asks JSON. **Apache Arrow JS 21.1.0** vendored under
  `static/vendor/apache-arrow/21.1.0/` with its LICENSE and NOTICE (no source map, no remote URL; loaded only by the VaR explorer).
- **Tests:** `ArrowAnswersTest` (server: Arrow equal to JSON, dictionaries, booleans, records with keys left out, fallback, negotiation);
  `tests/test_arrow_answer.py` (console: round trips, the server's own stream read by pyarrow, negotiation and fallback on both routes);
  `tests/test_arrow_browser.py` (the explorer drawn the same from Arrow and from JSON, the answers equal through the console, without
  Arrow JS, on a phone, no other host asked, no policy violation).
- **Docs:** `DATA_FORMATS.md` section 6 (where Arrow is used and where it is not, the measurements, how to ask), `API_GUIDE.md`
  (Answers as Arrow: the Accept header), `BI_GUIDE.md` section 14, `VAR_GUIDE.md` section 3.4, `PYTHON_COMPUTE.md` section 14, `VENDOR.md`;
  implementation plan 2.9.7 row 0 built.

### Direct memory: a server no longer runs out after hours (2026-10-28)

- **The fault.** After about 13 hours a cluster node started with `-XX:MaxDirectMemorySize=256m` failed every lake read with
  `OutOfMemoryError: Cannot reserve 8192 bytes of direct buffer memory (allocated: 268430166, limit: 268435456)` (87 times, and on the 27th
  too), and trade pages showed errors. On Java 21, `FileChannel.read` into a heap buffer copies through a temporary direct buffer as
  large as the read and keeps it cached on that (carrier) thread, with no size limit by default; `LocalStorage`'s reader passed the Delta
  kernel's and the Parquet reader's multi-megabyte heap reads straight to the channel, on many threads.
- **The fix.** `ChannelIo` (`drishti-api`): file-channel reads and writes of heap buffers go in 128 KB slices through a bounded pool of
  reusable direct buffers (64 at most, 8 MB); when all are busy the transfer is sliced through the JDK's own buffer at 128 KB. Used by
  `LocalStorage` (every Delta, Iceberg and Parquet read), the lake loader's sort runs, rejects and outputs, the Delta and Iceberg local
  writers' streams, VaR and exposure hot files (whole-section reads and writes; `ShardSkeleton` through them), compute results
  (`ArrowIpc`, read and written in slices), day index segments, the JSON Lines connector's 4 MB scan blocks, and the content store
  (`FileContentStore.get` without `Files.readAllBytes`; the version check hashes the file in 64 KB pieces; `exists()` for a run's answer
  instead of reading it). Kafka consumers fetch at most 4 MB (`fetch.max.bytes`) and 1 MB a partition by default (`client.*` overrides).
  Throughput holds (a 128 MB file in the page cache, Java 21, old then new: 8 MB reads 8.1 to 9.5 GB/s on one thread and 11.8 to
  25.3 GB/s on eight; 1 MB reads 10.7 to 10.8 and 41.8 to 55.6; 64 KB reads 11.4 to 10.4 and 57.4 to 55.0).
- **Launch flags.** `-Djdk.nio.maxCachedBufferSize=262144` in every server and loader launcher (`drishti-stack/stack.py`, the Docker and
  ECS server images, the ECS lake task, `tools/windows/start-server.ps1`, `load-iceberg.ps1`, `load-cassandra.ps1`, every
  `tools/load-*.sh`, the IntelliJ run configurations, and `tools/javacmd.py`'s `java_cmd`), with `-XX:NativeMemoryTracking=summary`; the
  production launchers add a heap dump on OutOfMemoryError (`dumps/`) and a rotated GC log (`gc-%p.log`, 5 x 20 MB), making both folders
  first. OPERATIONS.md 12.1a, CONFIGURATION.md *JVM flags for a long run*, PERFORMANCE.md; `tools/test_launcher_memory.py` checks them.
- **Admin → Health: Memory and files.** A row with direct memory against `MaxDirectMemorySize` (amber with a warning from 80%), mapped
  memory, heap, live threads, open files against the limit and (Linux) descriptors still open on deleted files; the same figures under
  `server` in `GET /api/v1/admin/health` (`ProcessResources`).
- **Proof.** `DirectMemorySoakTest` (drishti-lakeio: 24 platform and 48 virtual threads reading 2 to 4 MB ranges of local files through
  `LocalStorage` for 12 s in a JVM with `-XX:MaxDirectMemorySize=64m`) and `HotFileDirectMemorySoakTest` (drishti-compute: the same threads
  opening three dates' VaR hot files of 9,000 trades for 10 s at 32m) run in their own surefire executions, without the launch flag.
  Against develop's code they fail within two seconds with the production error; with the fix direct memory stays flat, under 8 MB and
  5 MB. `ChannelIoTest`, `ProcessResourcesTest`, the Health API and console tests cover the rest.

### The parallel lake loader

- **One duplicate-record rule for both loaders (2026-10-29, product owner).** When one id appears more than once on one business date
  in one load, `lake build`'s Python path and the parallel loader now write the same table: the copy with the latest `COMPUTED_AT` is
  kept (`--latest-by` / `source.latest-by` / the pack's `ingest.<kind>.latest-by` name another ISO-timestamp field; `''` turns it off),
  else the last one read in one deterministic order (files sorted by path whatever order `--from` gives, then line order); the others
  are dropped, counted per date in `duplicates` and named in `duplicateExamples` (`kept`, `dropped` as `file:line`); a load never fails
  for them. Before, both copies were written, in an order that differed between the paths (`PythonPathEqualityTest` failed when a plain
  copy of a test file sat beside its `.gz`). `rows` and the partitions now count the rows written; `accepted` still every valid document.
  Code: `tools/lake/stage.py` (`instant_micros`, `Stager.resolve`), `jsonstream.input_files` (one sort by path), `build.py`,
  `javaload.py`; `drishti-lakeload` `Latest` (new), `RowParser`, `ParseWorker`, `LoadReport.resolveDuplicates`, `DateWriter`.
  Tests: `PythonPathEqualityTest.duplicatesAcrossAndWithinFilesKeepTheSameCopyOnBothPathsAndBothFormats` (with and without
  `COMPUTED_AT`, Delta and Iceberg), `LatestTest`, `test_build.py` (last read, latest, the timestamp rule), `test_javaload.py`. Docs:
  TOOLS.md sections 4.3, 4.6 and 4.13, PARALLEL_LOADER.md section 13 (decision 9).

- **A config-driven, multi-threaded Java loader of JSON Lines into Delta or Iceberg (2026-10-28; the release's top item).** New module
  `drishti-lakeload` (`com.ash.drishti.lakeload.LakeLoad`, in the server's exec jar), for the bank's scenario-PV load (2.3M positions x
  510 scenarios, 20+ GB): readers (a plain file in byte ranges, ranged GETs on S3; a `.gz` or `.zst` decompressed as a stream by one
  reader, multi-member gzip included), parsers (streaming Jackson, the document re-written byte for byte as `lake build` keeps it, vectors
  straight to `double[]`), sorted runs spilled to `memory.spill-dir`, writers merging key ranges into Parquet files of
  `file-size-mb`, and **one commit per business date** (a Delta version replacing the date through Kernel; an Iceberg overwrite of the
  date). Memory bounded by `memory.budget-mb` (queue, sort buffers, writers), the spill space checked before reading, the spill removed
  however the load ends; the summary reports each stage's throughput (decompress its own), the peak heap and the MB spilled. Each date
  sorted by `LEGAL_ENTITY`, `DESK`, id by default (shard-aligned files, statistics a reader can prune by) and a **load manifest** listing
  each file's first and last keys for the cluster's VaR shards. The vector column BYTE_STREAM_SPLIT + ZSTD. Folder or `s3://` in, folder
  or `s3://` out, credentials only from the AWS chain; Windows with Java only. Design, decisions and the 2.3M estimate:
  [PARALLEL_LOADER.md](docs/architecture/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md#10-the-parallel-lake-loader-drishti-lakeload); every key: [TOOLS.md section 4.13](docs/guides/CLI_REFERENCE.md#713-the-parallel-lake-loader).
- **`drishti.py lake build --engine java`** runs the build in the loader (`tools/lake/javaload.py`; `--loader-set KEY=VALUE`; Delta or
  Iceberg; `--from s3://` and a Delta `--lake s3://`); the Python path stays the default: the loader runs only when asked (`--engine java`,
  or `--java-above-mb N` for `--engine auto` to pick it for at least N MB of JSON Lines in `overwrite-dates` mode). `lake build` also takes a POSIX lock beside its `flock`, so it
  and a loader run on its own exclude each other.
- **Measured** at the machine's limit, 10,000 positions x 510 scenarios (54 MB of JSON in eight gzip files) on 24 cores: 0.2 s warm
  (about 50,000 rows/s); a 24 MB budget and a `-Xmx192m` JVM give the identical table. 2.3M estimated at 1 to 5 minutes on a 16 to 32
  vCPU server (an estimate, to be measured on a real server: release item 3).
- Equal to the Python path: `PythonPathEqualityTest` runs `lake build` both ways on Delta and Iceberg (synthetic positions and the
  market-risk pack's scenario PVs) and compares every row, document, column and vector; the Delta and Iceberg connectors read both alike.
- Supporting changes: `ParquetDataWriter` (drishti-iceberg) takes `double[]` list values, UTF-8 text and per-column options
  (BYTE_STREAM_SPLIT, no dictionary, no statistics, a codec); `LakeWriter.engineFor` and `LakeWriter.removals` are public; Iceberg
  relayout (`lake maintain`) leaves a table laid out by `drishti.layout.sort-by` in its order.

### VaR sharding across Drishti*net

- **VaR sharded across Drishti\*net (off by default; product owner's design of 2026-10-28).** With the market-risk pack's new `sharding:`
  block (`enabled`, `key: [LEGAL_ENTITY, DESK]`, `kinds`, `target-shard-mb`, `replicas`) or `drishti.var.sharding.*`, each date's trades
  are cut into a shard map of legal entity and desk ranges near the target size (a desk never split, the same on every member), each shard
  owned by `replicas` members by rendezvous hashing (no consensus protocol; owners move only once the membership has been stable for
  `stable-seconds`; zones, pins, a coordinator-only member), each owner building only its shards from the lake (the Delta and Iceberg
  connectors skip files by the key column's statistics, every row checked) into its own hot file (a `RANG` section). Every member puts the
  date together from its shards and the others' skeletons: the same trades, positions and nodes as one server, **every node's aggregate to
  the bit**; any other scope's rows are summed shard by shard by one ready owner (`POST /api/v1/var/partial`, signed, one hop, as the
  caller), exactly one answer per shard, added in shard order. No live owner: `503 DRS-5215`, never a partial VaR; another data version:
  `409 DRS-5216`; data that does not cut along the key: `422 DRS-5217`. Handover through readiness in the capability digest (a new
  `services` field) and a grace period; `drishti.py var shards --drain` before a scale-in. `GET /api/v1/var/shards`, `drishti.py var
  shards`, `provenance.shards`. Measured equal to one server to the cent (VaR, ES, contributions, the P&L path, the tree, intraday, the
  official record) on three members in USD and EUR on Delta and Iceberg (`VarShardClusterTest`); `ShardMapTest`, `ShardOwnersTest`,
  `ShardGatherTest`, `ShardAssemblyTest`, `VarShardHandoverTest`, `VarShardingSettingsTest`, `VarShardSingleNodeTest`. The machinery
  (shard map, ownership, handover, gather with its completeness check, readiness) is measure-agnostic (`compute.shard`, `server.shard`,
  `ShardedMeasure`), VaR its first measure. Docs: [VAR_SHARDING.md](docs/architecture/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md#13-var-sharding-how-it-is-built), VAR_GUIDE.md section 28,
  DRISHTI_NET.md, NET.md, CONFIGURATION.md, TROUBLESHOOTING.md, TOOLS.md, CLI_GUIDE.md. Open: an Admin → Health "Shards" panel (mock-ups
  first).
- **Fixed (drill): a reporting currency could keep answering without the day's intraday updates.** The official capture reads every
  currency as the morning run; when it built a currency first (it runs after a full-run data-load signal) its morning book became
  everyone's book in that currency until the date was dropped (`intraday: null`, the morning figures); a batch applied while a currency was
  being built was lost the same way. On one server as on a member (the drill's `VarShardClusterTest`: member A's `BANK - TRD:T4` in EUR, 5
  positions and VaR 802 against 6 and 1,268). Now a currency keeps its morning run per date and data version and every answer puts the
  USD date's layer on it as the USD date holds it then (applied incrementally per batch as before). A date whose updates cannot be read is
  answered with a warning saying so, never silently from the morning run. `VarIntradayApiTest` reproduces it on one server;
  `VarShardClusterTest` now waits, as a client would, until every server's answers list the batches in USD and EUR. VAR_GUIDE.md sections
  8.4 and 28, VAR_SHARDING.md sections 7 and 12.
- **Fixed (drill): the intraday batches are listed in one stable order.** `intraday.batches` followed the order the signals applied them
  in, so one server and a member (or two runs) could list `["B-I2","B-I1"]` and `["B-I1","B-I2"]`. Now everywhere (the answers'
  `intraday`, the provenance, `drishti.py var intraday`, the data-load signal's log): by each batch's newest `COMPUTED_AT`, then by
  `BATCH_ID`, oldest first, the newest 20; `batchCount` counts every batch applied (`VarIntraday.BATCH_ORDER`, `VarIntradayTest`).
- **Fixed (drill): `POST /api/v1/var/partial` and `POST /api/v1/var/shards/drain` are in `token-never`** (`TokenScopeGuardTest`): the
  first is the members' signed channel made as the caller (like `/compute/peer/**`), the second an administrator's action (like
  `/var/reload`). API_GUIDE.md, VAR_SHARDING.md section 10.
- **Test: `VarShardClusterTest`'s join no longer depends on the random node ids.** With three members and two owners per shard the third
  member owned neither shard about one run in nine (seen once in five runs); its node id is now fixed and S1 pinned to it.
- **Fixed: a reload landing while an intraday batch was applied could bring the dropped date back.** The data-load signal applied the
  batch on the date it had read and then put the result in place unconditionally; a reload in between (another input's signal, an
  administrator's reload) dropped the date and retired its morning book, and the batch then published the old book and layer over the
  reload. Now the layer is published only over the very date it was built on; otherwise the signal says `superseded` and the date, as
  loaded again, reads its updates (this batch included, once) from the lake. A refused update's label likewise. `VarIntradayApiTest`
  reloads the date at that moment, deterministically. VAR_GUIDE.md section 8.4.
- **Test (drill): `VarIntradayApiTest`'s few hundred batches compared the intraday date with a date read before its full run reached the
  connector.** The one-run date was overwritten and read after a fixed 1.5 s (the connector's 1 s refresh), with no data-load signal; under
  load the read still saw the old snapshot, so the expected side was that date's morning run (`MGMT~BANK` `[52,168,…]` against the right
  `[106,307,…]`). The intraday side was correct. The test now loads that date first, writes the full run, waits until the date's version
  shows it and sends its signal, as a loader does; the full-run test waits for both tables' versions.
- **Fixed (drill): a member stopped answering BANK when both owners of a shard were down.** With every owner of S0 stopped, `VAR BANK`
  answered `503 DRS-5215` on the member left once a rebalancing round had passed: the round dropped the date to put it together again,
  and putting it together needed S0's skeleton. Now a date is never dropped to be put together again: the replacement is put together
  beside it and swapped in, in one step, once complete; meanwhile the date loaded answers every node's aggregate, the shards held here and
  the others' rows at its own data versions, and only the scopes that need the missing shard's rows answer `DRS-5215`. A shard book the
  date loaded reads is released only after a replacement without it is in place (before, releasing even an *older* version of a shard
  dropped a date that read the newer one); a member that finds itself stale puts the date together again the same way. Answers still
  never mix data versions: each partial is asked at the version its date was put together from. `VarShardClusterTest` runs the rounds
  and a forced replacement with both owners down (BANK answered `503` before the fix, every time). VAR_SHARDING.md sections 7 and 8.

### Drishti*net

- **Fixed (drill): a user-state change made while a peer was suspected for a moment never reached it.** `StateSync` queued a change only
  for the peers routable at that moment; a member suspected during a busy server's pause and then heard again never "joins" again, so no
  catch-up brought the change either. The drill's `NetLastAdminTest` saw a node keep the seeded administrator enabled after another node
  disabled it (`only ada and bob left enabled` failed under load). Now a change (settings, layouts, pivots, workspaces, sessions, users,
  roles, tokens) is queued for every member that is not gone, suspected or drained included, and sent once it is alive; a dead member
  still drops its queue and gets the catch-up when it comes back. The last-administrator rule itself was right: it relies on every node
  seeing every change. `NetLastAdminTest` marks the peer suspect at the moment of the change (the change was queued for nobody before the
  fix). DRISHTI_NET.md section N7.

## 2.9.5 — Iceberg as a full alternative to Delta; VaR hierarchies by columns (limit letters); connector files that upgrade themselves safely (2026-10-28)

### Hierarchies

- **Configurable hierarchies; the limit letters (2026-10-28; product owner's decisions 1 to 8).** The VaR and exposure engines build
  the hierarchies the market-risk pack's new `hierarchies:` block names (`drishti.var.hierarchies` wins over it; neither: MGMT and LEGAL
  from the rows, as before). A hierarchy comes from the `risk-hierarchy` rows (book-based, as before; its `HIERARCHY` and `LEVEL` enums
  are open now) or from the trades' own columns: the demo adds **LL, the limit letters** (`LIMIT_LETTER > DESK`), whose nodes are every
  distinct path of the rows' values, so a letter may hold part of a book. Node ids are paths (`LL~LL-0003/DESK-RATES`) or, with
  `ids: leaf`, the value (refused when a value has two parents). A configured `word` names a node in any scope (`LL:LL-0003`,
  `LL:LL-0003/DESK-RATES`, also in exposure). The engine sums each **cell** (a run of one book's trades with the same level values)
  once, so a letter is as fast as a desk; a position whose trades sit under two letters is split (`<position>@<letter>`) and counted.
  Hot file format 3 (the `CELL` section) only for a date with cells; the hierarchies' configuration is in the hot file's digest.
  - **Limits:** the new dated kind `var-limit` (`VLIM`, JSONL; `HIERARCHY`, `NODE_ID`, `LIMIT_VAR` in USD) for a hierarchy whose
    `limits: var-limit`; a node without a row shows no limit (never zero); a row naming no node is said (`DRS-5212`).
  - **Data without the column (product owner, 2026-10-28):** a source that does not keep a level column (P&L vectors or exposure paths
    written before the letters) **skips that hierarchy alone**: the date, MGMT, LEGAL, exposure and the official captures answer as
    before, and a `DRS-5211` warning names the hierarchy, the column, the kind and the fix, in the provenance, Admin → Health (*Hierarchy
    skipped*) and the log; its tree answers `DRS-5214` with the reason and the explorer lists it disabled. A row that leaves the column
    empty is still refused and listed; a bad configuration `DRS-5213`. `HierarchyColumnMissingTest`, `HierarchyUpgradeWithoutLettersTest`.
  - **Official records** of every configured hierarchy (VaR: 131 nodes on the test data, 88 + 43), the membership lines with `{"row": "cell"}`;
    exposure's official nodes for a column hierarchy are rules over the trades' values.
  - **The explorer:** the hierarchy selector lists the date's hierarchies by title (the tree's `hierarchyInfo`), the choice kept in the
    link (`hierarchy=LL`), an unknown one shows MGMT with a note; `VAR LL LL-0003` and the search find letters.
  - **Data, regenerated by the generators:** `LIMIT_LETTER` on every P&L-vector, scenario-PV and exposure-path row (12 letters, two
    books split), the `var-limit` rows, the intraday and Kafka samples; P&L-vector ids are now `PNL-<trade or position>-<set>` (the
    earlier `PV-` ids are still read: lakes and captures written before).
  - **Tests:** `ColumnHierarchyTest`, `HierarchyConfigTest`, `HierarchyEquivalenceTest` (MGMT and LEGAL from columns equal the rows'
    trees: ids, parents, levels, members, aggregates to the bit, VaR, ES, components and worst scenarios to the cent, USD and EUR, limits;
    every letter the sum of its rows), `VarHierarchyApiTest`, `HierarchyColumnMissingTest`, `ExposureOfficialHierarchiesTest`.
  - **Docs:** VAR_GUIDE sections 5.2, 5.3, 12, 15.4, 15.14, 15.15, 19, 20, 23.4, 25, 26.3; EXPOSURE_GUIDE section 20; CONFIGURATION;
    API_GUIDE and TROUBLESHOOTING (`DRS-5211` to `DRS-5214`); the contracts (`pnl-vector`, `scenario-pv`, `exposure-path`,
    `risk-hierarchy`, the new `var-limit`).

### Connector upgrades

- **Connector upgrades are airtight (product owner, after the 2.9.4 drill met a var-whatif file without `ccy`).** A file Drishti writes from
  a pack template carries its fingerprint in its own text (`# drishti-template: pack=… template=… text=…`, so it survives the content-store
  overlay and the history): at an upgrade, a file nobody edited is replaced in full by the new template (changed values included), the
  file before kept beside it (`.before-upgrade-….bak`) and in the history, one log line, audited as `connector-template-upgrade`. An
  edited file gets every key the template has at any depth: settings, kinds, layout lists, description, and a reactive connector's
  `kinds.*.params`, `kinds.*.result`, `reads`, `engine`, `triggers`, `coalesce`, `cache`, `limits`, `history`; its values are never
  overwritten, lists keep their order and gain the missing items. Conflicts are listed in **Admin → Connectors → Template updates** with
  **Use the pack's value** per key (`POST …/template-updates/<name>/use-template-value`). Reset to pack default and Regenerate write a
  stamped file again. **Tests:** `TemplateStampTest`, `TemplateMergeTest`, `TemplateUpdatesTest`, and the upgrade drill stage
  `ConnectorUpgradeTest` (a server on release 2.9.4's generated files, `tools/connector_upgrade_fixture.py`, with an edited risk-store and
  the edited 2.9.3 var-whatif: every unedited file equals the current template, the edits stay, var-result, var-whatif with `ccy` and
  exposure-result answer). **Docs:** CONNECTOR_FILES "Upgrades", OPERATIONS, the Windows QA guide's upgrade note.

### Iceberg

Delta stays the default lake format everywhere; Iceberg is chosen only by configuration (a connector file, `lake build --format iceberg`,
`build_demo_lakes.py --store …=iceberg`, `deploy/aws/iceberg/`).

- **The Iceberg connector answers as the Delta connector on the same rows.** Vector columns (`layout.<kind>.vectors`: the P&L and
  scenario-PV vectors as `list<double>`, a missing element null, never 0) are read in bulk by `vectors()` (both engines, bit for bit)
  and put back into a fetched document in place of their `{"$vector": …}` marker; `documents()` reads a date in one pass; plus
  `tableIdentity()` (the metadata's `table-uuid`, stable after a copy read through `relocate`), `inventory()`, `holdsNone()` and
  `refreshVersions()` (a data-load signal re-reads each table's snapshot at once). `IcebergLoader` writes vector columns from staged
  lines (a list that is not numbers is a reject, counted at the end). **Tests:** `IcebergVectorsTest`, `IcebergParityTest`.
- **Disk caches for Iceberg, as Delta's.** Each date's id map memory-mapped under `<data>/cache/<connector>/idmaps`, documents in a
  RocksDB store under `<data>/cache/<connector>/docs`, both kept across restarts and keyed by the date's files (a commit of another date
  keeps them valid); `id-map-disk.enabled`, `doc-disk-cache.*` (on by default). **Test:** `IcebergDiskCacheTest` (after a restart no data
  file is read for a hit).
- **`lake build --format iceberg`** stages as for Delta and streams the rows to Drishti's Iceberg loader (vector columns kept; only
  `overwrite-dates`; partition columns kept as columns); `--lake s3://…` or a REST catalog through `--iceberg-set` for object storage.
  **`build_demo_lakes.py --store risk=iceberg`** moves every table of the risk domain into Iceberg and writes `risk-store.yaml` to read it
  (`risk=delta`, or a full build without `--store risk=…`, puts it back). **Tests:** `test_vectors.py`, `test_stores.py`,
  `test_build_demo_lakes.py`.
- **Admin → Lakes and `lake maintain` for Iceberg.** A lake with `format: iceberg` (or Iceberg tables under a local root) is maintained by
  `IcebergMaintenance`: retention, relayout, snapshot expiry, and **orphan files** (`--remove-orphans --older-than-hours`, 72 at least,
  with a dry run), under the 7-year floor of `risk` and `risk-results` (`--floor-days 2557`: no date dropped and no snapshot expired
  inside it), the ownership rule, schedules and history. The tables list has a **Format** column. **Tests:** `IcebergOrphanFilesTest`,
  `test_maintain_iceberg.py`, `test_admin_lake_maintain.py`.
- **`deploy/aws/iceberg/`**: `load-day.sh` (no publish step: the loader commits), `backfill.sh`, `maintain.sh`, `setup-lifecycle.sh`
  (tiers `data/` by business date beside the Delta rules, never `metadata/`, no expiry; the Delta script now keeps the Iceberg rules too),
  `setup-alarms.sh`, `report.sh`, `setup-iam.sh` with `iam/*.json` (Glue `GetDatabase/GetTable(s)/CreateTable/UpdateTable`, Lake
  Formation `GetDataAccess`), `tables.example`, `check-conditional-writes.sh`, and `check-glue.sh`. **Test:** `test_deploy_aws.py`

- **VaR and exposure on an Iceberg risk lake, equal to Delta to the cent.** The same day written from the very same lines to a Delta
  lake and to an Iceberg lake, read by one connector switched from `plugin: delta` to `plugin: iceberg`, gives the same VaR, ES,
  component and incremental VaR, worst scenarios, limits and limit-letter nodes, in USD and in EUR, and the same EE, PFE, EPE, profiles
  and contributions. Intraday works on Iceberg too: file batches appended to an Iceberg table apply live as on Delta, and the Kafka PV
  stream's windows go to an Iceberg risk lake as one Iceberg append each (`LakeAppends`; on Delta, as before). `--store risk=iceberg`
  now also switches the counterparty-risk pack's `exposure-store.yaml` (it reads `simulation-run` and `exposure-path`, both in the risk
  domain: before, exposure lost its tables once they were moved). Run for real on the demo data: 14 risk tables, 955,124 rows, in
  Iceberg in 579 s; a server on that lake answered `VAR BANK` (USD 124,948,241; EUR 111,265,495, the lake built to end on that day's business date; on the test data's own date, 2026-09-30, Delta and Iceberg both give 112,041,646, tutorial 29), the limit letter `LL:LL-0003` and
  `EXP BANK` from Iceberg and published its official records. **Tests:** `VarFormatEqualityTest`, `ExposureFormatEqualityTest`, `LakeAppendsTest`, `test_stores.py`.
- **Official results to Delta or Iceberg, in a folder or on `s3://`.** `drishti.var.official.format` and

## 2.9.4 — VaR from scenario PVs or P&L, by trade or position, in any currency, intraday from files and Kafka; JSON Lines as the data standard; the decks rewritten (2026-10-27)

- **One download button per panel (2026-10-27).** A panel's CSV and JSON Lines downloads are one **↓** button with a small menu (CSV, JSON Lines) instead of two icons: the second icon wrapped a zoomed panel's header on a phone onto another line, leaving room for five rows (the drill's `test_phone_zoomed_table_fits_without_scrolling`). USER_GUIDE.

- **Upgrade: a computed connector's new parameters too (2026-10-27).** A reactive connector file written before 2.9.4 (var-whatif without the `ccy` parameter) refused the reporting-currency what-if (DRS-5205). The connector template update now also adds the parameters a pack's template gained (`kinds.<kind>.params.<name>`), keeps the file's own, and keeps the file as it was beside it; and it runs once at start, before the server answers, so a request never meets a connector it has not reached yet. `TemplateUpdatesTest`; CONNECTOR_FILES.

- **The basket is on the VaR page only (2026-10-27; product owner).** The top bar's **◫ Basket** button is gone (it did not apply to
  every screen); the VaR explorer keeps **◫ Construct your basket** (now with the count of its parts), the basket strip, **+ basket**
  on rows and the what-if. **Alt+B** opens the tray only where the page offers it (the explorer); elsewhere it does nothing, and the
  landing page's **← Back to** keeps it. The basket's contents still persist in the browser, so it is there when the VaR page opens;
  `var-basket.js` and its CSS load only on the VaR page. No other page had a basket action. **Tests:** `test_var_routes.py`,
  `test_var_explorer_browser.py`. **Docs:** USER_GUIDE (the top bar, the VaR section), VAR_GUIDE section 3.5, tutorial 25.

- **P&L vectors in any currency (2026-10-27; product owner).** On a P&L record `CURRENCY` is now the currency the values are in: a
  vector in CAD is converted to USD per scenario with that scenario's FX (approximate, counted in `tradesWithoutPv`), its `PV` at
  today's rate; no scenario FX for it rejects the row (`DRS-5207`). The trade's own currency is the optional `TRADE_CURRENCY` (scopes,
  rules, Trade currency); `REPORTING_CCY` is a deprecated alias that must equal `CURRENCY` (`DRS-5208`). The generator and the scripts
  write `CURRENCY: USD` and `TRADE_CURRENCY` on P&L records (the bank unchanged); the checker converts a non-USD vector the same way.
  **Tests:** `VarInputsApiTest` (a CAD P&L vector equal to its conversion; a contradicting `REPORTING_CCY` refused). **Docs:** VAR_GUIDE
  sections 15.2 and 15.13, the pnl-vector contract.

- **Upgrading to 2.9.4: connector files get the new columns by themselves (2026-10-27).** A connector file written from a pack's
  template at an earlier first start (`config/connectors/risk-store.yaml`) lacked the columns the VaR inputs gained (`RUN_KIND`,
  `COMPUTED_AT`, `VALUE_TYPE`, `GRAIN`, `SOURCE_SYSTEM`, `POSITION_ID`, `TRADE_IDS`), so a plain upgrade could not read intraday updates
  or the record fields. Connector template updates now treat a layout list that lacks the template's new columns
  (`layout.<kind>.columns`, `.vectors`) as additive: with `template-updates: additive` (the default) the server appends them at start,
  keeps the connector's own columns and order, keeps the file as it was beside it (`<name>.yaml.before-<time>.bak`), logs one line and
  lists it under Admin → Connectors → Template updates; a list that differs only by an administrator's edit stays a conflict. **Upgrade
  notes:** pull, build, rebuild the risk lake (`build_demo_lakes.py --only market-risk`), start: nothing to edit by hand (with
  `template-updates: notify` or `off`, press **Add missing kinds** once). **Tests:** `TemplateUpdatesTest`. **Docs:** CONNECTOR_FILES,
  VAR_GUIDE section 8.4, the Windows QA guide's 2.9.4 section.

- **A configurable scenario window and confidences (2026-10-27; local branch, for the product owner's review: not pushed).**
  **`drishti.var.scenario-window`** (`DRISHTI_VAR_SCENARIO_WINDOW`, default `all`: the whole set, 509 in the demo) or N: the newest N
  scenarios of each date's set, every row (P&L vectors, scenario PVs, scenario FX) cut to them at load; k = ceil(N (1 − α)) (the 3rd
  worst of 250 at 99%, ES the mean of the 7 worst); a shorter set used whole with a warning; N below 20 refused at start; the window in
  the provenance (`scenarioWindow`), in the hot file's digest and in official records (`SCENARIO_WINDOW`, the var-official contract and
  published table). **`drishti.var.confidence`** and **`es-confidence`** gain placeholders (`DRISHTI_VAR_CONFIDENCE` 0.99,
  `DRISHTI_VAR_ES_CONFIDENCE` 0.975) and are refused at start outside (0.5, 1) (they were silently replaced); the provenance states them;
  the console no longer hard-codes 99% or 97.5% (the legends, the tiles while computing, the tab *In other currencies*, the basket's
  what-if), the what-if answer carries its confidences, a Home fact's label reads the answer's. **Per request:** `window=`,
  `confidence=`, `es-confidence=` on `GET /api/v1/var/scope` (`drishti.py var show --window --confidence --es-confidence`) recompute the
  headline from the same vector, labelled (`override`) and never official. Backtesting keeps `history-days` and 99%. **Tests:**
  `VarWindowApiTest`. **Docs:** VAR_GUIDE section 18.5 and settings, CONFIGURATION, USER_GUIDE, the Market risk Knowledge page.

- **Inputs in any form and any grain; every record says what it is (2026-10-27; local branch, for the product owner's review: not
  pushed).** A pricing system may send **scenario PVs or P&L vectors, per trade or per position**, and switch between dates. **2.9.4
  requires every PV or vector record to say what it is**, leading each line: `VALUE_TYPE` (`PV` or `PNL`), `GRAIN` (`TRADE` with a
  `TRADE_ID`, or `POSITION` with a `POSITION_ID`), `CURRENCY` and `SOURCE_SYSTEM` (the value fields keep their names: `SCENARIO_PV`,
  `BASE_PV`, `PNL`; a P&L vector's currency stays `REPORTING_CCY`, USD, and `CURRENCY` is the trade's or position's own). **Older files
  need the fields added:** `drishti.py var convert FILE --set VALUE_TYPE=PNL --set GRAIN=TRADE --set CURRENCY=USD --set
  SOURCE_SYSTEM=MUREX` (or `--infer`); a record without them is refused (`DRS-5208`), as is one whose `VALUE_TYPE` is not its payload or
  `GRAIN` not its id. A position sent whole is used as it is (never derived), placed by its book (`LEGAL_ENTITY`, `DESK`, `TT_BOOK`),
  naming its trades in `TRADE_IDS` for navigation; everything that adds up works on it (tree, portfolios, `LE:`, `DESK:`, `BOOK:`, `CPTY:`,
  baskets, what-if, captures, official records, currencies, intraday files and Kafka keyed by `POSITION_ID`); trade-level features say
  so in words (`TRD:` of a position, contributions by trade, a trade page linking its position). **One source system sends one form and
  one grain on a date** (else the date is refused, `DRS-5210`, as is a supplied position covering a trade also sent on its own); an
  intraday update in another form or grain than the system's morning run is refused and listed. **Optional pins**
  (`drishti.var.inputs: {ENDUR: {form: pv, grain: position}, default: {form: any, grain: any}}`) cross-check the records (`DRS-5209`
  when they disagree). Every answer's provenance has `inputsBySystem` (form, grain, rows, how decided, `tradesWithoutPv`), the status
  too, and the page's *How this number was built*. `drishti.py var intraday --load` routes a mixed file by `VALUE_TYPE`. The test data,
  the samples and every script write the fields (the bank unchanged: 112,041,646 / 160,143,809); `make_var_data.py --position-systems`,
  `--inputs-config`; `tools/pvgen --grain position`, `--position-systems`; the checker reads both grains. **Tests:** `VarInputsApiTest`
  (the same trades as their positions give the same node VaR and ES in all four combinations; a system switching grain; two grains on a
  date refused; records refused with their codes; an intraday update in another grain refused), `VarInputsTest`, `VarPvStreamTest` (a
  Kafka message mixing all four of four systems, a pin disagreeing, a field missing), `test_pvgen.py` (per position equals per trade to
  the cent), `test_varcli.py` (routing, convert). **Docs:** VAR_GUIDE 1.9 (section 15.13 with the 2x2 table, the pin, the currency
  caveat; 15.12's example lines; errors), the contracts, CONFIGURATION, API_GUIDE, TROUBLESHOOTING, USER_GUIDE, the Market risk
  Knowledge page.

- **A stand-in pricing system, JSONL only, and both forms per system (2026-10-27; local branch, for the product owner's review: not
  pushed).** `tools/pvgen` (each with a `.sh` beside it and `tools/windows/pvgen-*.ps1`; pure Python from the console's environment,
  kafka-python for Kafka; `--help`, `--dry-run`, a fixed `--seed`): `morning.py` writes a day's `scenario-pv`, `pnl-vector` and
  `fx-scenario` from the demo's factor model and `scenario_fx.py` (`--out`, or `--lake` with `--server` to load and signal);
  `intraday.py` N small batches of amended, new and cancelled trades, each its own `BATCH_ID`, `RUN_KIND: INTRADAY` and a later
  `COMPUTED_AT` (`--batches`, `--trades-per-batch`, `--mix`, `--plan`, `--lake`, `--server`, `--every 30s`); `publish_kafka.py` the
  same to the PV topic, each message JSONL text of `--per-message` records, a cancel a cancel line (`--rate`, `--seconds`, `--save`); `check.py` recomputes the bank's and
  each desk's VaR and ES from the files with the engine's formula and compares them with the server (exit 1 on a difference over one
  unit). Every file is **JSONL** (`.jsonl`, `--gzip` for `.jsonl.gz`), each line exactly one row of its kind's contract, no other field;
  a Kafka message's value is one such row. **Both forms per system:** `--pv-systems`/`--pnl-systems` (default Endur as scenario PVs,
  Murex and Calypso as P&L vectors), `--all-vectors` every system as P&L vectors exactly as 2.9.3 (the bank on the test data's 2026-09-30 112,035,906 /
  160,132,107, as in 2.9.3); the same flags on `tools/packgen/var/make_var_data.py`. The contracts of `scenario-pv`, `pnl-vector` and `fx-scenario`
  state the delivery format (JSONL, one row a line) with an example line each (a full run's, an intraday amendment, a cancel); the
  demo's morning rows say `COMPUTED_AT` 06:00Z (was 22:30Z: an intraday update must come after the morning run); the committed intraday
  sample `config/packs/market-risk/samples/intraday/I-2026-09-30-001.scenario-pv.jsonl` is what `intraday.py` writes (`--first` numbers a
  second run on). **Upgrading:** a `config/connectors/risk-store.yaml` written before 2.9.4 needs `RUN_KIND,COMPUTED_AT` added to its
  layouts, the server says so (VAR_GUIDE 8.4). **Fixed** on the
  way: a batch sent in both kinds as two loads (each with its signal) applied only its first kind; the engine now tracks each kind of a
  batch apart. **Tests:** `tools/pvgen/test_pvgen.py` (dry runs, the shape and determinism by seed, every written line a JSON object of
  its contract, the sample regenerated byte for byte, the checker against the engine's figures), `test_var_data.py` (the forms per
  system; all vectors reproducing 2.9.3), `VarIntradayApiTest` (a batch in two loads), `VarIntradayTest` (a trade changing form).
  **Docs:** VAR_GUIDE 1.8 (section 15.12 *Producing P&L vectors and scenario PVs*: both forms side by side, one sample line of each kind
  with the intraday marker and a cancel, "this is the contract a pricing system sends"), tutorial 25 step 13 (the intraday script, the
  badge, the check; picture 13), TOOLS, QA_ON_WINDOWS_WITH_CUSTOM_DATA (2.9.4, PowerShell with the venv's python.exe; Kafka optional),
  the contracts and pack guide pages.

- **Intraday updates from Kafka, micro-batched (2026-10-27; local branch, for the product owner's review: not pushed).** The
  market-risk pack's connector **`pv-updates`** (plugin `var-pv-stream`, off by default: `DRISHTI_VAR_PV_STREAM`, `DRISHTI_VAR_PV_TOPIC`,
  `DRISHTI_VAR_PV_WINDOW` default `5m`, `DRISHTI_VAR_PV_MAX_TRADES` default 500) reads a pricing system's PV topic (compacted, keyed by
  `TRADE_ID`, the value one JSONL row of `scenario-pv` or `pnl-vector`, a tombstone a cancel) like the Kafka connector (`KafkaClients`,
  now public, gives it the same consumer settings and security), keeps the latest message per trade over a window (`COMPUTED_AT`, the
  offset breaking a tie), flushes early at `max-trades` or on an administrator's **Apply now** (`POST
  /api/v1/var/intraday/streams/{connector}/apply`, a button on the connector's Admin page; `GET /api/v1/var/intraday/streams`), and
  writes the window to the lake as **one** intraday batch (`K-<date>-<time>-<n>`, Drishti's lake writer, the pack's layout), then raises
  the data-load signal once: the intraday layer applies it as a file. Guards: another business date, before the morning run, or not later
  than what the date holds (a redelivery, a replay after a restart) ignored and counted; another scenario set (`DRS-5203`), a failed
  scenario (`DRS-5206`) or a malformed row (`DRS-5201`) rejected, never filled with zero, listed in the stream's status and the
  provenance's `intradayRejections`. **Tests:** `VarPvStreamTest` (in-process Kafka, no Docker: a window of several trades, latest
  wins, a file batch between windows, an early flush with a tombstone, the guards, files and windows mixed equal to one run to the cent
  in USD, EUR and CAD, a replay writing nothing), `test_var_routes.py`. **Docs:** VAR_GUIDE section 8.4 (Kafka: flow, rules, settings,
  sizing 4–8 KB a message), KAFKA_CONNECTOR section 17, CONFIGURATION, API_GUIDE, USER_GUIDE.

- **The top of the VaR tree named by a setting (2026-10-27; local branch, for the product owner's review: not pushed).**
  **`drishti.var.root-name`** (env `DRISHTI_VAR_ROOT_NAME`, blank by default: the hierarchy data's `NAME`, *Drishti Bank* in the demo)
  names the root node of every hierarchy when a date loads; **`drishti.var.root-names`** (`{MGMT: "…", LEGAL: "…"}`) names one
  hierarchy's root over it. The tree, breadcrumbs, headline, command line, `var-result`, captures and new official records show it;
  records captured before keep their name (append-only). The name is part of the hot file's digest, so a change is not masked by a file
  built before; a running server shows it after a restart (or a reload of the dates). No console text named the root: the page reads the
  node's name. **Tests:** `VarRootNameTest` (both trees renamed, `root-names` winning, nodes below unchanged, blank keeps the data's
  name, the digest). **Docs:** VAR_GUIDE settings, CONFIGURATION (server table and placeholders), USER_GUIDE, the Market risk Knowledge
  page.

- **Intraday updates from files (2026-10-27; local branch, for the product owner's review: not pushed).** A second `BATCH_ID` on a date no
  longer turns today's VaR into yesterday's: a pricing system sends **only the changed trades** during the day (amended, new or
  cancelled), priced over the morning run's scenario set, marked **`RUN_KIND: INTRADAY`** (the contracts of `scenario-pv` and
  `pnl-vector`, with `COMPUTED_AT`; the risk-store layout promotes both), each batch its own `BATCH_ID`, appended to the lake. The
  data-load signal of such a batch applies it **without a reload** (`VarIntraday`, `OverlayVectors`): each updated trade's difference
  goes into its book and every node above it in both hierarchies, the per-trade-currency totals and every reporting currency already
  built (only that trade reconverted); the morning hot file is never changed; the latest `COMPUTED_AT` per trade wins across every batch
  (an update older than the morning run, or than the one held, is ignored and counted); a cancel (`TRADE_STATUS` not live) removes the
  trade; a new trade gets its book and its position by the rules; a trade moved to another book moves; another scenario set is refused
  (`DRS-5203` in `intraday.rejections`); a full run of the date (or a signal with no new intraday batch) reloads as before and drops the
  layer; a restart rebuilds the same from the lake. Only the current P&L per trade is kept, so the work of a batch does not grow with
  the batches before it. Every answer that includes updates says **`intraday`** (`updates`, `trades`, `amended`, `added`, `cancelled`,
  `lastAt`, `batches`, `batchCount`, `rejections`), the VaR page shows an **intraday** badge, and the provenance a row; the official
  records and publishing read the morning run alone (an intraday batch never restates them). `drishti.py var intraday` lists each date's
  layer and `--load FILE.jsonl` appends a batch (`lake build --mode append`) and signals it; `var show` and `var status` say it. The
  demo's morning rows now say `RUN_KIND: FULL` (regenerated; figures unchanged); `lake demo` moves the scenario PVs' valuation dates.
  **Tests:** `VarIntradayTest` (amended, new, cancelled, moved, updated twice, a new trade in an existing position, a cancel and a revival:
  equal to the cent to the final data built as one run, every node in both hierarchies, any scope, every position, the totals in four
  currencies, heap and mapped), `VarIntradayApiTest` (files and signals: a P&L vector amended, a cancel, a new trade, a scenario-PV
  trade updated twice, an older update ignored, another scenario set refused; equal to the cent to the same final data loaded as one run
  in USD, EUR and CAD; the official record the morning run's; a full run drops the layer; 200 batches on one date, the time per batch flat,
  equal to one run and to a restart), `test_varcli.py`, `test_var_routes.py`.
  **Docs:** VAR_GUIDE 1.7 (section 8.4 as built, 15.8, 15.9, 20.2, the CLI), USER_GUIDE (the badge), the Market risk Knowledge page,

- **Reporting currencies built ahead, per-trade-currency totals, the currency picker and Trade currency (2026-10-27; local branch, for
  the product owner's review: not pushed).** The product owner's decisions on the VaR currencies: (1) PVs stay as received, in each
  trade's own currency; (2) **`drishti.var.currencies`** (default `USD, EUR, CAD, JPY, GBP`, env `DRISHTI_VAR_CURRENCIES`) lists the
  reporting currencies **built ahead**: once a date's USD book has loaded, one low-priority background thread builds each listed
  currency's book into its own hot file, so a VaR in it never waits on its first ask (a request meanwhile joins the build, or builds it,
  as before); mapped tier only; **`drishti.var.currency-retention-dates`** (default 5, env `DRISHTI_VAR_CURRENCY_RETENTION_DATES`) keeps
  them for the newest five dates, older ones' files deleted after each build. Measured on the demo lake (8,566 trades): 21.4 MB and 58 to
  148 ms a currency a date (four currencies: 86 MB, 0.37 s, in the background; the USD load 0.58 s); per 100k trades about 250 MB a
  currency a date and 4.3 s for four. `GET /status` says what was built (`currencies.builtAhead`, `tier.currencies`). (3) Every node
  keeps its PVs **summed per trade currency** (`CurrencyTotals`, the hot file's new `CTOT` section, format 2): a node's P&L in any
  currency is `Σ_c [PVsum_c(s) × FX_c→X(s) − PVbase_c × FX_c→X(base)]`, the same to the cent as converting each trade; the headline VaR
  and ES in any currency other than USD come from it, and the new **`GET /api/v1/var/scope/currencies`** (the scope in every listed
  currency, that VaR in the page's currency at today's rate, the difference) and **`GET /api/v1/var/currencies`** (listed, available,
  ready). (4) The VaR page has a **Reporting currency** select in its status line (mock-up A: the listed currencies and More…); every
  panel, the tree, captures and the basket tray follow it; it stays for the tab's session and goes into the link (`ccy=EUR`); the
  command line takes **`VAR … IN EUR`**; the provenance says the reporting currency, the input form, the scenario FX and the cross
  rates via USD; a new tab **In other currencies** (mock-up C's table, loaded only when opened; a click switches the page). (5) Every
  trade page's strip says **Trade currency** (`EUR · as priced` from its scenario PVs, else `USD · as booked`; it takes the place of
  Source, which stays in the deal ticket: the strip holds eight), its Risk group the trade currency and its **Base PV** in it
  (`RISK_LINKS.TRADE_CURRENCY`, `TRADE_CURRENCY_FROM`, `BASE_PV`); the VaR contributions and worst scenarios list it, a position's trades
  too (`TRADES[].TRADE_CURRENCY`, contract), and the derived trade pages label their column Trade currency. The demo lake now moves the
  scenario PVs' valuation dates with the business date (`lake demo --as-of today` rejected them all as valued on another day).
  On the demo lake (2026-10-27) the bank is 126,537,611 / 172,532,570 USD and **110,448,804 / 144,379,703 EUR**; the test data's figures
  are unchanged.
  **Docs:** VAR_GUIDE 1.6 (section 15.11, settings, API, sections 3.1, 3.2, 3.4, 26's format 2 and `CTOT`), USER_GUIDE (the picker,
  `IN <currency>`, Trade currency), CONFIGURATION (the two settings and their placeholders), tutorial 25 (step 1: the picker and the
  tab), the Market risk Knowledge page, the position contract; the VaR guide's and tutorial 25's pictures retaken, two new.
  **Tests:** `CurrencyTotalsTest` (every node's totals equal the trade-level result to the cent in five currencies, heap and mapped;

  six currencies), `VarCurrencyAheadTest` (built ahead, the status, the currencies list, totals against the converted book, the tab, a

- **VaR from scenario PVs, in any reporting currency (2026-10-27; local branch, for the product owner's review: not pushed).** A bank's
  batch may now send a trade's scenario P&L as **scenario PVs** in the trade's own currency (the new kind `scenario-pv`, `SPV`: its PV
  under each of the 509 scenarios and its base PV of the same run) beside or instead of the P&L vector; the VaR engine turns them into
  the trade's USD P&L when it loads the date, `P&L(s) = PV(s) × FX(s) − PV(base) × FX(base)`. Scenario FX is the batch's when it supplies
  it (the new kind `fx-scenario`, `FXS`: USD per unit today and under each scenario), else derived from the FX history of `fx-spot`
  (today's rate moved by each scenario day's 1-day move); every cross goes through USD (the product owner's four decisions). A scenario
  that failed to price rejects its trade with the new **`DRS-5206`** (the scenarios named, never filled with zero); a currency without
  FX, the new **`DRS-5207`**; valuation dates other than the business date, `DRS-5201`. Every answer takes a **reporting currency**,
  `ccy=EUR` on the API and `--ccy EUR` on `drishti.py var` (headline, path, contributions, history, tree, hints, captures and compare,
  the what-if, `var-result` and `var-whatif` with the parameter `ccy`, the official record), and says it in `currency`; the USD book is
  built at load, another currency's on its first ask, from the USD book (`CurrencyBook`, `ScenarioFx`), kept per date on the tiered
  memory (its own hot file under `<hot>/<date>-<CCY>/`); `drishti.var.official.currencies` (default `[USD]`) captures other currencies
  officially beside USD (only USD is published). The provenance says how the vectors met FX (`fx`: per currency `supplied` or
  `derived` and today's rate; `scenarioPvTrades`). The console's picker: the entry above.
  **Test data:** the Endur trades (1,339: 1,089 USD, 246 EUR, 4 CAD) now come as scenario PVs (`tools/packgen/var/scenario_fx.py`), with
  supplied FX for AUD, CAD, CHF, EUR, GBP and JPY; the other 8,233 trades stay P&L vectors; `lake demo` builds 84 tables (was 82). A USD
  trade's P&L from its scenario PVs is its 2.9.3 vector exactly; the EUR and CAD trades now also carry their currency's move on their
  value, so the bank on 2026-09-30 moves from VaR 112,035,906 / ES 160,132,107 to **112,041,646 / 160,143,809**, and on the default
  demo lake (2026-10-26) from 126,544,583 / 172,580,660 to **126,537,611 / 172,532,570**; only the commodity desk, its books, LE-NY,
  Markets and the bank change. In EUR the bank's VaR is 111,837,045 (not 95.4 m at today's rate: the bank's 3.65 bn USD of value moves
  against the euro). Limits and portfolios unchanged.
  **Docs:** VAR_GUIDE contract 1.5 (sections 15.9 scenario PVs, 15.10 reporting currency, settings, errors, CLI, API, official
  records, test data; the figures that moved), tutorial 25 (step 1: scenario PVs and `--ccy`), the Market risk Knowledge page ("From
  scenario PV to the P&L vector" as built, the figures), the two new contracts and `var-result`/`var-whatif`'s `CURRENCY`, the pack's
  guide and README, API_GUIDE and TROUBLESHOOTING (the two codes), CONFIGURATION (the new settings), the demo-table counts.
  **Tests:** `ScenarioFxTest` (the conversion, crosses through USD, supplied over derived, bad rates, a whole book converted),
  `VarCurrencyApiTest` (both forms side by side, a failed scenario, no FX, a valuation date, every answer in a currency, captures,
