## 2.9.1 — Functions (FUNC) for everyone; groupings and analytics computed; External data and complete pack guides; the exposure benchmark (2026-10-26)

- **Groupings and analytics computed instead of stored (2.9.1, Track B of the computed-measures roadmap).** Seven pages that were
  stored copies of figures are computed from the fundamental data when opened, and their stored versions are retired in the same change
  ([GROUPINGS_ANALYTICS_GUIDE.md](docs/guides/GROUPINGS_ANALYTICS_GUIDE.md), [tutorial 27](docs/tutorials/06-groupings-and-analytics.md)):
  - **LEIG** (`lei-group`) and **LEIC** (`lei-country`): computed by the gleif pack's derived connector `gleif-groupings` from every
    legal entity: no 50-member cap on a group (its tree and each member's level from `DIRECT_PARENT`, lapsed registrations new), no
    400-row cap on a country; `LEIG ALL` and `LEIC ALL` computed too. The `lei-group` and `lei-country` snapshots are gone from
    `data/testdata/gleif/` (−0.77 MB); an ultimate parent carries `GLEIF_GROUP_SIZE` (its group's size in GLEIF, an input) and every
    entity its `PROVENANCE`. The type-ahead finds a group by name (`LEIG Ford Motor`); the `lei-group` search form is gone.
  - **SIC** (`sic-sector`): computed by `us-equities-groupings` from the companies, totals of the USD reporters (the strip says how many
    are not summed), net margin new; the `sic-sector` snapshot is gone.
  - **ECG** (`country-group`): computed by `macro-groupings` from the economies (an economy is in its region, its income group and the
    world): GDP and population summed, GDP per capita their ratio, growth weighted by GDP, inflation the members' median; the income
    groups have figures for the first time; every member economy listed. `tools/realdata/build_docs.py` builds no country group.
  - **CORR** (`correlation-matrix`): a set keeps its factors (`EQUITY_IDS`, `FX_IDS`); its correlations are the computed kind
    `correlation-result` (`CORRC`), worked out by the reactive connector `correlation-engine` (a Java engine in the server, no compute
    pool needed) from the factors' daily closes: a window (default every return) and an estimator (Pearson by default, or Ledoit-Wolf)
    picked on the page. `AVERAGE`, `PAIRS`, `WINDOW` and `ESTIMATOR` are removed from the record.
  - **USEQ ratios**: net margin and revenue growth worked out by the company page from `REVENUE`, `NET_INCOME` and `FINANCIALS[]`;
    `NET_MARGIN`, `REVENUE_GROWTH` and `FINANCIALS[].NET_MARGIN` removed from `us-company`, `ROWS[].NET_MARGIN` from `index-membership`.
  - **FACT changes and IDX totals**: a financial fact's change on the year and an index's members' revenue, net income and SIC
    divisions are worked out by the pages; `CHANGE_PCT` and `HISTORY[].CHANGE_PCT` removed from `financial-fact`, `SECTORS`, `REVENUE`,
    `NET_INCOME` and `BY_SECTOR` from `index-membership` (equal on every record).
  - **EQ beta**: the security master's hand-set `BETA` is removed from `equity`; the computed kind `equity-beta` (`EQB`, the reactive
    `equity-analytics`, a Java engine) regresses the equity's daily log returns on its index's, and the equity page's Beta panel shows it
    (the demo's independent price walks give betas near zero; two equities name no index and get a refusal in words).
  - **PXH analytics**: returns over 1, 3 and 6 months and the history, volatility, largest drawdown, beta and correlation against a
    benchmark (`DRISHTI_US_EQUITIES_BENCHMARK`, default SPY), computed by the `yfinance` plugin as the history is read. Internal use only
    and off as shipped, like the prices.
  - **The derived connector** gains `also-group-by` (a member in several groups), `unlisted` (a page over everything keeps only its
    figures), the `median` aggregate, `then` (fields worked out over the page), `sort`, `tree` (a group's own hierarchy) and
    `search-fields` (docs/connectors/types/derived/README.md). The world-economy generator (`tools/packgen/common/packbuild.py`) writes a
    derived connector for a computed kind; the market-data generator writes the correlation engine (`tools/packgen/banking/corr_kinds.py`).
  - **Reconciliation** on the committed data (guide section 18): LEIC and SIC equal on every page; LEIG equal but for 19 groups' levels
    (the stored depth depended on the order members were listed) and one group with an entity fetched for two groups (36 members, stored
    37); ECG within 3% of the World Bank's own aggregates on GDP, 2.1% on population, 0.32 points on growth and 0.5 on inflation, the
    difference being the World Bank's estimates for members that have not reported; CORR's stored pairs were synthetic (computed now:
    0.096, −0.012 and 0.092 averages against stored 0.385, 0.512 and 0.406); USEQ growth differs on 3 companies whose previous fiscal
    year is missing (computed against that year only, empty when it is missing).
  - **The guard:** `tools/contracts.policy.yaml` `computed-in-place:` (LEIG, LEIC, SIC, ECG) and `removed:` (the ratios, the correlation
    figures); `tools/test_contracts.py` fails the build when a stored version returns. Contracts redrafted for the four groupings and
    written for `correlation-result`; `docs/contracts/packs/` and `COMMAND_CATALOG.md` regenerated. Help: two entries (the guide and
    tutorial 27); twenty-seven tutorials.
- **The exposure explorer's browser test (2.9.1).** `drishti-console/tests/test_exposure_explorer_browser.py`, as the VaR explorer's:
  over the committed exposure run in a scratch lake (Delta connector, demo off, compute on) it opens `EXP BANK`, the tree and the
  counterparty board, a counterparty (breadcrumb, tiles, Netting sets), a netting set's Collateral tab (CSA, the signed effect of
  collateral), a trade in its netting set (netting benefit) and Back; By tenor; the q 95/99 and collateralised switches; the pre-deal
  what-if by the proxy and by the exact paths method; a netting set without paths; a phone's width; F1 to the exposure guide. No pictures.
- **The exposure benchmark (2.9.1).** `ExposureTierBenchmark` (drishti-server tests, opt-in like VaR's `VarTierBenchmark`) loads a
  synthetic date as the server does and times the load, the hot file, reopening, the scopes (bank, a counterparty of 20 sets, a set),
  contributions by netting set and by trade, the exact pre-deal arithmetic and the proxy; measured at 10,000 and 100,000 trades (P 100

## 2.8.0 — Data contracts for every command; VaR computed for any scope; Admin → Commands; write-back; branding from configuration (2026-10-26)

- **VaR's official capture at start waits for the lake:** it tried once, before the Delta connector was up, and never again. It now retries every five seconds for up to ten minutes; after that, the next data-load signal captures the date.
- **Drill:** runs the compute worker SDK's Python tests (`drishti-compute/src/test/python`, the VaR what-if engine among them).
- **Write-back W1 to W7 (2.8.0): forms save through connectors, with the edit log on the Drishti database.** A form whose Sutra has
  `save:` (`target: overlay | owned | source`, `approval`, `reason`, `command`/`create` for a connector's `writes:`) gets **Submit…**:
  the draft is saved, the review and confirm sheet shows per record what you saw, what is there now and your change (a field that moved
  is flagged before you send), where it goes, who approves (never you) and what it recomputes, and **Confirm** turns it into change
  requests (`POST /api/v1/changes`, `/changes/preview`). A change waits for approval in `drishti_edit_request` (four eyes, the policy's
  approver roles; **Review → Changes**), then is appended to its record's lane in `drishti_edit_log` and acknowledged only after commit;
  P lanes (64) with one virtual-thread worker each apply in seq order, ownership taken in the database by a conditional update with a
  lease and every append, apply and command fenced by the epoch (a zombie owner writes nothing); the handler re-checks the person's
  rights, masks and the form's rules at apply time and conflicts a change whose fields moved (the three-way difference in words), never
  overwriting. Overlays and owned values are written in the same transaction and laid over every document the router reads (*How this
  view was built* says *Edited here*; a form's row on another kind's page too); a page watching the record updates (live frames, or drawn
  again with *Changed … just now*). In a cluster: a shared PostgreSQL edit log (lanes spread by the ring, forwarding to the owner, failover
  by lease) or an edit primary (the API forwarded to it, overlays followed, *Edits are paused* while it is down); `edit.log: auto` decides.
  Source commands go through the outbox: `SourcePlugin.write`, connector files' `writes:` validated at load (guard and idempotency
  required, unknown `:param` refused: Admin → Connectors and Admin → Edits say why), the JDBC plugin's guarded, idempotent statements,
  `reply` or `next-load` confirmation, resend with the same change id after a failover; File, Delta and Iceberg never write. Every applied
  change publishes `edit.applied` to the reactive connectors (a `write-back` event with the watermark `L<lane> -> seq`, replayed per lane
  from the edit log). **Off by default** at every level: `config/edit/edit.yaml` (`edit.enabled: false`), a form's `save:`, a connector's
  `writes:` switched on by an administrator; the `edit` power on a role (Admin → Roles: *Submit edits*; the shipped `admin` role) and the
  `edit` token scope. New: Admin → Edits, `drishti.py change propose|submit|list|show|approve|reject|withdraw|history` and `edits status`,
  DRS-9301 to DRS-9306, `drishti.edit.file` (`DRISHTI_EDIT_FILE`), the book desk's form submits a trade's correction (one approver),
  tutorial 24, [EDITS.md](docs/guides/APPROVALS_GUIDE.md#7-for-administrators-switching-write-back-on). Decisions taken while building and what is not built (the S3 edit log, the lake fold of
  overlays, the per-column `edit:`): [WRITE_BACK.md section 19](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md#31-collaboration-write-back-and-approvals)
  (WriteBackFlowTest, WriteBackOffTest, EditLogTest, LanesTest, EditTriggersTest, JdbcWritesTest, test_write_back.py,
  test_write_back_browser.py, test_changecli.py). Also: the console's shared live connection now listens for `switches` events, which
  Admin → Commands sends (they were dropped by the hub).

- **Fixed: a flurry of old notices on opening the console.** When the first live stream opened on a server after a quiet spell (a
  restart, or the only tab reopened), InboxHub re-read its window of the last 100 inbox rows for late commits and pushed them all as
  new, so days-old "Run finished" notices toasted at once. Rows already in the inbox when the stream opens now count as delivered
  (InboxHubTest). The console shows at most three toasts at once and folds a burst into "+N more on the bell", and a run's toast no
  longer reads "Run Run finished".
- **Admin → Commands (2.8.0, product owner's option C with option A's side panel).** Every command of the packs, grouped by pack, with
  what it does (the data contract's description), its example, an Everyone switch and greyed role columns for grants per role later;
  a pack switch per pack; changes batched with Undo and "Review N changes", a side panel listing everything each change blocks and a
  reason kept in the audit log; the history; the version of the switches each server holds. A command turned off is **not active**
  everywhere: `403 DRS-1016` (new) for its page, API, typed command, search, exports, BI reads and the compute ask, a "not active" page in
  the console, left out of type-ahead, pick lists and the packs' menus, links to it struck through, panels reading it "not active (turned
  off by an administrator)", open pages told on the live channel. The switches (commands and packs) are kept in the Drishti database
  (`drishti_switch`, `drishti_switch_log`, both schema files) with a hybrid-logical-clock stamp; last writer wins by (stamp, node); their
  hash rides the gossip member entry and a node pulls a peer's switches when it differs (`GET /api/v1/net/switches`), so separate SQLite
  nodes agree, and a node that was down catches up on rejoining. Pack switches moved into the same ledger. Admin API
  `/api/v1/admin/commands` (never a token), `drishti.py server commands list|off|on|history`. docs/admin/USER_MANAGEMENT.md (new), API_GUIDE,
  TROUBLESHOOTING, USER_GUIDE, TOOLS, NET, DATABASE, CONFIGURATION, help centre.

- **Branding from configuration only (product owner, 2026-10-25).** No console template or script, and no server message, writes the
  product's name: it comes from `ui.product` (templates `{{ PRODUCT }}`, scripts `<body data-product>`) and `drishti.branding.product`
  (`Branding.sqlName()`, `Branding.netName()`, `Branding.name(..)`), and features follow it: `<product> SQL`, `<product> Elements`,
  `<product>*net`. New `ui.owner` and `ui.owner_email` name the author on the About page. The fallback fonts are now
  "Product Wordmark" and "Product Tagline" (element sheet rebuilt). Guard tests: `tests/test_branding_guard.py` (console: templates,
  scripts, a rebranded About page) and `BrandingLiteralTest` (drishti-it: string literals of the server's main code). Licence headers,
  header names (`X-Drishti-…`), `DRISHTI_` variables and code identifiers are unchanged. docs/admin/CONFIGURATION.md.
- **VaR complete, part 2** (VAR.md (in git at tag v2.9.5) 1.4, AS BUILT):
  - **Tiered memory** (`drishti.var.tier`, default `mapped`): each loaded date is written once to a local **hot file** under
    `<data folder>/var/hot/<date>/` (format 1: float32 position rows in hierarchy order, the trades of fungible positions, float64 node
    and book aggregates, columns, ids, runs, nodes, a CRC32C per section) and memory-mapped; the heap keeps the aggregates, columns and
    links only (about 80 MB a 100,000-trade date instead of 407 MB of vectors more). The load streams the lake's rows to a spill file, never
    to the heap. A date not open is mapped again from its file (no lake read); the file is rebuilt when the date's inputs change, evicted
    dates are unmapped after a grace, at most `disk-dates` files are kept, and the files are deleted at shutdown and start unless
    `keep-on-shutdown`. Unmapping is safe: a reader guard per matrix (a shared Arena on Java 22+, the cleaner on 21). Node figures are the
    lake's to the bit; any scope within 2⁻²⁴ × the date's gross P&L (the test data: exact; scaled to billions: 5.86 × 10⁻⁸ of the VaR).
    `provenance.tier`, the status's `tier`; `heap` keeps the V1 store. Sharding across Drishti*net is documented as planned (not built).
  - **Benchmark** `VarTierBenchmark` (opt-in): measured at 100,000 trades × 5 dates (first load about 1 s a date, reopening 23 ms, a node
    0.5 ms, the whole bank from float32 rows 3.4 ms, a 50,000-position basket 2.6 ms), extrapolated to 1 M × 50 (about 2.25 GB a date,
    113 GB for 50, the bank in about 35 ms resident) with the command for a server (VAR.md section 12.2, VAR_ENGINE.md section 13.2).
  - **VaR as computed kinds** through reactive connectors: `var-result` (`VRES`, the Java engine, connector `var-engine`) and
    `var-whatif` (`VWIF`, the Python VaR engine `drishti_compute.var` in the new compute pool `var`: hypothetical trades from a private
    sandbox, incremental VaR in order and alone, component VaR and ES after, the stressed window); contracts, about texts, the pack README.
  - **`drishti.py var`**: show, parts, path, history, tree, status, capture, captures, compare, basket, baskets, official, reload, whatif.
  - Docs: VAR.md 1.4, VAR_ENGINE.md (13.2, 18.7), VAR_DATA_MODEL.md (12, 14, 18.5), the new VAR_GUIDE.md and tutorial 25, VAR_EXPLORER,
    CONFIGURATION, API_GUIDE, TOOLS, CLI_GUIDE, the help centre. Tests: MappedVectorsTest, VarHotFileTest, VarTestDataPrecisionTest,

- **Reactive connectors, steps R1 to R4 (2.8.0, [REACTIVE_CONNECTORS.md](docs/architecture/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md#4-reactive-connectors) section 21,
  [REACTIVE_CONNECTOR.md](docs/connectors/types/reactive/README.md), [tutorial 23](docs/tutorials/19-build-a-pack-and-a-screen.md#part-c--computed-panels-a-reactive-connector)):** a connector
  may compute its answer. The built-in plugin `reactive` (in `drishti-compute`) reads a connector file's computation: kinds with typed
  `params:` (int, decimal, text, scope, bool, enum, date, sandbox-ref; defaults, allowed values, bounds, refused in words), `reads:`
  (inputs read through the normal routing **as the person asking**, masks applied; a later read may take its ids from an earlier one),
  `engine:` (a Python engine in a compute pool, cut over every worker of the pool and its Drishti\*net peers with `split` and added up
  with `reduce`; or a Java `ComputeEngine` in the server: Drishti's own always, others with `compute.in-process-java: true`),
  `result:` rules, `triggers:` (`write-back`, `live`, `data-version`, `schedule`, with `affects:`), `coalesce:`, `cache:`, `limits:`. A
  read authorises the viewer, checks the parameters, pins the inputs' data versions, keys the answer with the viewer's view signature (two
  people with different rights never share one), answers from the cache or joins the computation under way (single flight), admits by
  class and per person, computes with progress, validates, stamps (pin, inputs, watermark, trigger, engine, where it ran, result hash)
  and audits (`compute.answer`). Triggers mark results stale and recompute those somebody watches, coalesced (quiet window, maximum wait,
  one more for what arrived meanwhile), ordered by watermark (a late older result is dropped), each event once. Private what-if
  sandboxes (`sbx-…`, frozen copies to share). The SPI is in `drishti-api` (`com.ash.drishti.api.compute`). **On a screen:** a panel's
  `source:` takes `params:` (expressions, evaluated as the viewer; lint `DRS-2012`, `DRS-2057`); the panel is never blank: *computing*
  with a progress bar from the live channel (`compute:<request>`), filled in place when the result lands; *stale* in amber; *failed* or
  *refused* in words; the other panels unaffected; live views rebuild as their viewer; charts in a panel swapped in are drawn. **HTTP and
  CLI:** `POST /api/v1/compute/{connector}/{kind}`, a request's events to its owner only, cancel, `POST /api/v1/compute/events`
  (administrators; the write-back hook), sandboxes, `GET /api/v1/admin/compute/reactive`; `drishti.py compute run|cancel|event|sandboxes|reactive`.
  Connector files, pack templates and the form keep a reactive connector's computation. **The sample:** the `compute-demo` pack
  (synthetic P&L strips; not loaded by default) computes a book's path with the sample Python engine (`PathSumEngine`, new in the SDK)
  and its Java twin, the same number. **Measured:** a cache hit 4.7 µs inside the connector, a miss with a trivial engine 47 µs, a miss
  through a Python worker 2.3 ms; a computed panel from the cache 2.7 ms through the server, the same as a plain panel. Not yet:
  per-event impacts (W6/V5), the disk cache, one as-of per screen (R5), the cluster (R6). Tests: `ReactiveConnectorTest`,
  `PythonBridgeTest`, `ReactiveOverheadTest`, `ReactiveApiTest`, `SutraWiringTest`, `ConnectorFilesTest`, `test_compute_panels.py`, `test_reactive_panels_browser.py`,
  `tools/test_computecli.py`.
- **Banks in the public-data packs:** us-equities gains three lists kept by Drishti (`LISTS` in

  VersaBank) and `IDX BANKS-UK` (HSBC, Barclays, Lloyds, NatWest). A foreign filer's annual report (20-F, 40-F) and IFRS tags are
  read in the currency it reports in (new `CURRENCY` field; totals over many companies add USD reporters only); a Canadian or UK
  company links to its economy; total assets fall back to total equity and liabilities; GLEIF name matching strips EDGAR's

  (National Bank of Canada, Desjardins, EQB, Laurentian, ATB and Canada's other domestic banks GLEIF knows by name; Santander UK,
  Nationwide, Virgin Money, TSB, Metro, Close Brothers, Co-operative Bank, Monzo, Starling, Investec and other UK banks and
  building societies), resolved by legal name and country. The GLEIF mapping download sends `Accept: */*` (the server now

- **Compute workers, steps C1 to C3 (2.8.0, [PYTHON_COMPUTE.md](docs/guides/NOTEBOOK_GUIDE.md),
  [COMPUTE.md](docs/guides/OPERATIONS_GUIDE.md#15-compute-workers)):** a new module, `drishti-compute`: a supervisor of out-of-process Python workers in pools (fork
  mode on Linux, a fresh child per request; warm mode on Windows, reset and recycled), one request per worker, JSON-lines control and
  Arrow files in a per-request scratch folder under `<data dir>/compute/` (removed when the request ends), correlation ids, progress,
  cancellation, wall-time, CPU and memory limits, and an audit-hook sandbox (no sockets, no processes, no writes outside the scratch
  folder). **As many workers as wanted:** the count is configuration per pool and per node (`compute.nodes.<node>`); a request can be
  split into chunks and fanned out over every worker of this node and of the other Drishti\*net nodes that serve the pool, gathered in
  order; fair scheduling by class (interactive, event, batch with its share) and by user (turns, an in-flight limit) with bounded
  queues (`DRS-9203` busy). A pure-Python worker SDK (`drishti_compute`: the engine contract, an Arrow codec with no pyarrow, the
  sample engine echo/sum/sum-vectors). `requires:` on connector files (Python lock with hashes, Java coordinates with sha256 and a
  native-code scan, plugins); locked environments built offline with `pip --require-hashes`, a manifest checked at every worker start,
  read-only; the four-eyes approval (requests and approved items in `drishti_compute_request` and `drishti_compute_approval` of both
  schema files; revocable; audited): a connector with unapproved requirements stays off and says why. **Admin → Compute**; the
  configuration `config/compute/compute.yaml` (off as shipped); errors `DRS-9201` to `DRS-9206`. A load test with a configurable
  worker count (`ComputeLoadTest`; 16 to 64 workers measured, [COMPUTE.md section 9](docs/guides/OPERATIONS_GUIDE.md#155-admin--compute-reactive-connectors-and-when-something-is-wrong)).
  Still planned: the pricer interface, QLRisk and the QuantLib Java worker (C4 to C6), the reactive connectors (R1 to R6).
- **2.8.0 designs (design only, nothing built):** reactive connectors that compute when asked and on events, with point-in-time
  stamps, coalescing and per-user isolation ([REACTIVE_CONNECTORS.md](docs/architecture/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md#4-reactive-connectors)); out-of-process
  Python and Java compute workers with pinned, administrator-approved requirements, QLRisk as the default pricer (design only until
  its API is stable) and QuantLib's own Java binding in an isolated worker ([PYTHON_COMPUTE.md](docs/guides/NOTEBOOK_GUIDE.md));
  a generic VaR engine over precomputed 509-day P&L vectors for any scope, with what-if and full drill-down
  (VAR_ENGINE.md (in git at tag v2.9.5)) and its data model: positions, portfolios, the vector layout in Delta, cubes,
  the in-memory vector store and sizing (VAR_DATA_MODEL.md (in git at tag v2.9.5)).

  reads the YAML once it is (it read the text from before the alert was set; the WIP wait on the model is gone). A screen grid's

  one being stored (`test_areas_split_tabs_and_arrange[light]` reloaded before the split was saved).

  a part added from the UI kit opens its settings in the side panel at once, one plain-word question per parameter of its docstring with
  choices from the record's real fields (*Which number? [NOTIONAL]*, *Which list?*, *Label*, *Format*; `core/designer_settings.py`,
  `GET /designer/settings/{draft}`, step `settings`); a key figure's number is guessed from the record's numbers instead of the
  fragment's `$.VALUE`, which no record holds ("No data available"). A part the person added whose setting names nothing in the record

  keep **Hide**), with an **Undo** toast. One click, drop or double click adds one panel: an add in flight ignores more clicks, a drop on
  a panel inside a panel is handled once, each step carries a nonce the console does once, and a draft's steps run one at a time.

  browser test edits a book page written out in its own design, since the pack's book page is now made of fragments.
  for the alert to be written before it reads the YAML.

- **us-equities refresh script** ([PUBLIC_DATA.md](docs/guides/EXTERNAL_DATA.md), us-equities): `tools/publicdata/us_equities.py`
  with `us-equities.sh` and `tools/windows/publicdata-us-equities.ps1`, the pack's own script like the others (`status`,
  `refresh [wikidata nasdaq sec gleif prices]`, `--years/--since --scope --out --dry-run --internal-ok --offline --cache`). It wraps
  `tools/packgen/us_equities/fetch.py` and `make.py`: a refresh of the committed pack writes exactly what `make.py` writes, then
  `make.py --check`; every cached file is in the shared cache index and each run in the pack's manifest. `--scope` adds tickers or
  `CIK:`, `INDEX:<CODE>=<QID>`, `FILINGS:`, `YEARS:` and `CONCEPT:` to a widened build in the data folder (`--into-pack` only on
  purpose). Prices (Yahoo, through the `us-equities-prices` connector of a running server) are internal only: a snapshot in the data
  folder, refused in committed folders without `--internal-ok`. `make.py` gains `--pack DIR`; its generated guide points at the
  script. Offline tests on a recorded two-company cache.

- **Public-data refresh scripts** ([PUBLIC_DATA.md](docs/guides/EXTERNAL_DATA.md)): one script a pack in `tools/publicdata/`, each
  with `status` and `refresh [SOURCE ...] --years/--since --scope --out --dry-run --internal-ok --offline`, a `.sh` and a
  `tools/windows/publicdata-<pack>.ps1` wrapper. `world_economy.py` wraps `tools/realdata` (World Bank, IMF, UNDP, Factbook; a
  committed refresh writes what `realdata.py all` writes, and is a no-op from an unchanged cache; `--scope` adds World Bank or IMF
  indicators to a build in the data folder); `news_and_markets.py` wraps `capture-market` (more tickers and topics with `--scope`);
  `official_market_data.py` captures ECB FX, the US Treasury par curve, SOFR and the euro short-term rate as `fx-spot`,
  `ir-curve` and `rate-fixing` documents. Shared library `pdbase.py`: polite HTTP (User-Agent, pause, retries), a resumable download
  cache with checksums under `<data>/publicdata/cache`, a manifest per pack, and the internal-only guard (IMF, Yahoo and news data
  never go into a committed folder without `--internal-ok`, refused in words). Tests on recorded responses; one live smoke test
  with `DRISHTI_LIVE_FETCH=1`. Fixed on the way: `realdata.py check` no longer reports the hand-kept `regions.json`;
  `capture-market` can write to a folder without a `testdata.yaml`.

  the chosen counterparty). Masks and roles decide: a masked field is never shown or editable (*Hidden for you*), another role's field
  is locked. Saving keeps a **draft** per person in the content store: `/api/v1/drafts` (CRUD, checked again on the server with the
  same rules, a masked or locked field refused, audited); the page offers "You have 2 drafts on this page" to resume or discard and asks

  it, `DRS-2012`; the schema describes it; the view model carries `refresh` on each panel). The console fetches only the panels that are

  scroll kept; a picked row and what it opened survive, and the panels a pick drives are refreshed by sending that pick again. Each
  refreshing panel has pause, resume and a slower interval; the page has **Pause all**; the choices are kept per person and per screen

  `views.refresh_min_seconds` (default 5). Every panel says how fresh it is ("updated 12 s ago", ticking; "stale" in amber; "trade-endur
  isn't answering; showing data from 10:42"; "live" on a live page). The Sutra designer: Describe's `refresh 30s` takes effect, and

- **Sutra Next, phases 2 and 3 (2.7.0): events, sources over several packs, nested child panels**
  ([SUTRA_NEXT.md](docs/guides/RACHANA_REFERENCE.md#sutra-next-fragments-events-children-sources-layout-and-forms) sections 6 to 8, 14, 15):
  - **`source:` as a mapping** on any panel: `{ kind, id | where | search, limit, as-of, pack }`, read as the viewer (a kind the viewer
    may not open is never fetched: "no access to <kind>"; documents masked before binding; a `where` over a masked field never
    holds); `$src` in Rachana-EL is the record (or records) read. One read per source per request. The text form
    (`source: "link(...)"`) is unchanged. A BI model source is refused (`DRS-2057`): not built yet.
  - **Events**: `emits: [{ name, on: row-click | bar-click, payload: { field: "@.X" | { bind, type } } }]`; `@<panel>.<event>.<field>`
    and `@parent.<event>.<field>` in Rachana-EL; `waits:` (what a panel waiting on an event says). Evaluated on the server per click:
    `POST /api/v1/views/{kind}/{id}/events` `{panel, event, row, selections}` answers the selection's token and seen payload, the
    panels that read it (only those), the clicked panel's children and the selections it cleared. The payload is kept twice: as the
    viewer saw it (drawn, filtered) and as stored (only to look up a source, for the same person); selections travel as `IdTokens`
    (ported from ui-board-preview) that only the same person resolves on the same screen (`403 DRS-5002` otherwise;
    `drishti.views.selection-ttl`, default 30 minutes).
  - **Children**: `children: [{ place: expand-row | detail-right | detail-below | tabs, show: on-select | always | on-expand, source,
    waits, panels }]`; lazy (`GET /api/v1/views/{kind}/{id}/panels/{panel}/children?sel=...`); a new pick replaces them; depth 3.
  - **Lint**: `DRS-2057` (unknown panel, event or payload field, a panel reading its own event, cycles, `$src` without a source, a
    source id reading a number, date or bool field, triggers not built), `DRS-2056` (`@parent` without a parent, depth over 3,
    expand-row under a panel without rows); `DRS-2055` for a fragment whose panels emit without `doc.emits` or read `@parent`
    without `doc.expects`. A `use:` may carry `source`, `when`, `waits` and, for a one-panel fragment, `emits`, `children`, `span`,
    `height`, `area` (anything else is `DRS-2048`).
  - **`?sutra=<name>`** draws a view with another Sutra of the entity's kind (API and console, `DRS-5001` for one of another kind).
  - A `kv` panel with `rows` and no columns lists the plain fields of the record it reads at bind time (`field-list@1` over `$src`).
  - **Console**: `static/js/sutra-wire.js` and `static/css/wire.css`: rows and bars that fire (click, Enter, Space), the picked one

  - **Fragments**: `<name>.v<N>.fragment.yaml` with `fragment: <name>`, used like blocks. The shared library is the Drishti UI kit's

    `region-map`, `source-footer`. An empty optional
    parameter (`code`, `key`, `area`) leaves the key out.
  - **The `doc:` docstring**: summary, description, every parameter with type, default and meaning, emits, expects, examples, since.
    Strict for fragments (`DRS-2055`: not loaded without a complete one); a warning for Sutras and older blocks (`sutra lint --docs` prints
    an incomplete one and counts those without one; never fails on it). `doc:` is a known top-level key of a Sutra and in the schema.
  - **Composite fragments**: a fragment may `use:` other fragments at a pinned version (`name@N`), passing parameters explicitly,
