- **Fix: uninstalling a connector made through Admin** no longer fails with `cannot archive ... NoSuchFileException`: since connector
  edits are a shared overlay in the content store there is no file to move, so the text in force is archived (`ArtifactArchive.archiveText`),
  the overlay removed (kept in the shared history) with any file under it (`ConnectorFiles.removeEverywhere`), and Restore writes it back.
- **Fix: a server started with `DRISHTI_BI_STORE` (the BI store folder) failed at start** with `drishti.bi.store is '<path>': use
  content (the default) or jpa`: Spring's relaxed binding offered the folder as the BI content store's kind too. That value is now
  read as the default (`content`); `drishti.bi.store: jpa` still works.
- **Fix: the connector template updater's loop** sleeps on its own thread, outside the `synchronized` start (NoBlockingUnderSynchronizedTest).
- **Tests: the BI catalogue browser tests follow the catalogue's kind tabs** (`?kind=all`, the Datasets tab instead of the old kind filter).
- **Tests: the W1 model designer stack's reference-store serves book as well as desk** (with three books): a dataset's implicit model
  brings the kinds its references name (DESK, PORTFOLIO), and a connector file without book made every query DRS-9026. The shipped
  `reference-store` template and examples already list book.
- **Fix: a table repainted away before its toolbar was placed** no longer throws in the console (`tables.js`: the strip above the table is
  added only while the table is still on the page).
- **Tests: S3 on three simulators, no Docker.** Adobe S3Mock 4.12.4 in the test JVM (a Maven test dependency; Windows QA included)
  runs the content store's S3 contract (`S3MockContentStoreTest`) and the Iceberg native engine's table on S3
  (`NativeOnS3SimulatorTest`); moto 5.2.3 (`moto[server]`, pinned in `drishti-console/requirements-test.txt`) runs Delta on S3 and
  `lake publish` on S3 (`tools/lake/test_s3_simulators.py`); the MinIO server binary runs both on Linux (`MinioContentStoreTest`, no
  longer Testcontainers), from `DRISHTI_MINIO_BIN` or the git-ignored `tools/cache/minio/`, checksum-verified when downloaded, and
  skips with the reason on Windows, offline, or while MinIO serves no community binary (`410 Gone` today). Every suite probes and
  prints which conditional writes its simulator covers (create-only, update-if-match, delete-if-match, racing writers) and skips
  what it does not: S3Mock's racing creates are not atomic. The drill runs the Python suite too. Shared helpers:
  `com.ash.drishti.testkit.s3` (Java), `tools/lake/s3sim.py` (Python). Docs: CONTENT_STORE.md §7, TOOLS.md §4.12, the Windows QA
  guide §6e.
- **Fix: `lake publish` checked the files on AWS, not on the store it commits to.** With `--storage-option AWS_ENDPOINT_URL=…`
  (MinIO, an S3-compatible store) the file check now uses that endpoint and the keys given, as the commit does; before, it asked
  AWS S3 and failed (`ACCESS_DENIED`).
- **New: data loads overrides saved through Admin apply on every node** (`loads/config/<pack>.yaml` in the content store, read on every
  use; the old `<data>/loads/config` files imported once and kept; `drishti.loads.config-store: file` for one node). Nothing under
  `config/bi` is written by the UI any more (BI content is already in the store), so there is nothing to share there.

- **New: connectors catch up with their pack's template.** A connector file generated from an older template (for example `macro-store`
  without `region-economy`, `risk-store` without `trade-valuation`) is compared with the pack's current template at start and every
  minute: missing kinds and settings are added automatically, keeping every edit (`template-updates: additive`, the default, in
  `config/connectors-settings.yaml`; `notify` only lists; `off`), as a shared edit with the old text in the history, one log line and an
  audit entry. Settings an administrator changed and kinds no pack serves are never changed automatically. **Admin → Connectors →
  Template updates** lists every drifted connector beside its template with *Add missing kinds*, *Regenerate from template*, *Remove
  obsolete kinds* and *Fix all additive*; the Connectors tab shows a count. [CONNECTOR_FILES.md](docs/guides/DATA_GUIDE.md#template-updates).

- **New: connector edits made through Admin reach every node of a cluster.** Files in `config/connectors` stay the base (GitOps); an
  Admin create, edit, enable or disable, restore or delete is a shared edit in the content store (`config/connectors/<name>.yaml`, with
  history) that every node applies over its file within `drishti.store.watch-ms` (2 s), hot-reloading as for a file edit. Admin →
  Connectors marks it *shared edit*; Reset removes it. Placeholders stay unresolved in the store. Two nodes editing one connector get one
  `409 DRS-5032`. `drishti.connectors.store: file` for one node. [CONNECTOR_FILES.md](docs/guides/DATA_GUIDE.md#connector-files-on-a-cluster), CONTENT_STORE.md section 11.

- **New: collaboration, notes, embed apps, pack switches, the audit trail, Sutra proposals and load history on every node of a cluster.** They moved
  into the content store (docs/architecture/CONTENT_STORE.md section 9): one document per comment thread (its comments, sealed revision
  chain, mentions, followers), shares, per-user inbox documents, outbox deliveries claimed by compare-and-set (sent once across nodes),
  holds and seals; `admin/embed-apps/`, `admin/pack-state.json`; the audit trail as per-node day segments merged when read, each node's
  lines hash-chained; `governance/proposals/` decided by compare-and-set; `loads/<pack>.json` (no announcement lost, a late notice sent once). Multi-document changes run as content transactions
  (`TxContentStore`): buffered, version-checked, applied in order with an intent record under `system/tx/` that any node finishes after a
  crash. Each store imports its old tables and files once (a marker under `system/imports/`; the old data is kept). Switches back, one
  node only: `drishti.collab.store` (`jpa`, `file`), `drishti.audit.store`, `drishti.embed.store`, `drishti.packs.state-store` (`jpa`),
  `drishti.governance.store`, `drishti.loads.store` (`file`). Two nodes editing the same item get one `409 DRS-5057`. The backup is now the store root. Options
  for sharing UI-written configuration (`config/connectors`, `config/bi`) are listed for a decision (section 10); nothing built.

- **Changed: Raw document opens on the page, in a viewer, not as raw JSON in a new tab.** In a number's "over time" window, *Where it comes from … Raw document* now opens a dialog with the document as a foldable tree (theme colours, the document's key order, long lists cut at 50 with *Show all*), the field's path highlighted and scrolled to, Search (keys and values), Copy JSON / Copy node and Download (`<kind>-<id>-<date>.json`). Masked values stay `•••` as the server sends them; Esc closes it and returns focus; full screen on a phone. F9's drawer draws the same tree and opens the viewer. The `/api/raw/...` address still works (Ctrl/middle click). No other raw-JSON links were found in the console (provenance, Explain and the history page link none). Test: `tests/test_raw_viewer_browser.py`.

- **Fixed: the console set a healthy server aside because a live stream broke** (`server ... set aside after 2 failed requests in a row: stream broke (ReadError)`, then `console moved from ... to ...`, again and again). A stream that opened and then ended (a server restart, an idle or proxy timeout) no longer counts toward `backend.fail_after`; the console checks that server's health at once, and only a failed check or request counts. A session that moved because its server restarted returns to it once it has been healthy for a minute, instead of staying moved for good (`core/cluster.py`, `core/backend.py`; docs/admin/NET.md, DRISHTI_NET.md). After such a move a screen-designer draft saved on the old server showed `DRS-5006: no design`: drafts and other per-user content are kept on the node that saved them until the central content store.
- **New: the content store, and Designs on every node of a cluster.** Build workbench Designs (with their samples, versions, About, form and share) are kept in the content store, so a console that fails over to another Drishti*net member finds them instead of `404 DRS-5006 no design`. One small interface (get, compare-and-set put, list, delete, changes) with four backends chosen in their own file, `config/store/store.yaml` (examples in `config/store.examples/`): **filesystem** (the default, `data/fstore`; a shared mount on a cluster; visible names only, atomic rename, lock files, Windows retries), **sqlite** and **postgres** (the table `drishti_content`, in the two complete schema files) and **s3** (conditional PUT). Two nodes saving the same Design at once give one success and one `409 DRS-5057`; a bad key is `400 DRS-5058`, an unreachable store `503 DRS-5059`. `drishti.builder.designs.store` is now `content`; at the first start the old `data/designs` folder is imported (idempotent, logged) and renamed `designs-imported-<time>`, and Designs in the identity database are imported once. Every backend passes one contract suite. [CONTENT_STORE.md](docs/architecture/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md#5-the-content-store-user-content-every-node-reaches), [CONFIGURATION.md](docs/admin/CONFIGURATION.md#the-content-store-configstorestoreyaml), DRISHTI_NET.md 11.2.

- **New: BI content and BI runs on every node of a cluster (the content store).** BI workspaces, members, items with their draft body, published versions, revisions, governance events, favourites and last opens, views and settings, and BI runs with their shares, schedules, results and promoted snapshots, now live in the content store (`bi/...`, key layout in CONTENT_STORE.md section 9), so every Drishti*net member sees the same BI content and the same runs. Two nodes saving the same item at once give one success and one `409 DRS-5057`; a run's status and result read from any node; a dead node's unfinished run is adopted by exactly one node through a compare-and-set lease in the store (no shared database needed), and a scheduled run fires on one node only. Workspace membership, item visibility, run visibility, shares and the signature rule on results are unchanged. `drishti.bi.store` (`content` or `jpa`) and `drishti.bi.runs.store` (`content` or `local`) are `content` by default; at the first start the identity database's `drishti_bi_*` and `drishti_bi_run*` rows and `<data>/bi-runs` are imported once (idempotent; a marker keeps deleted items and runs from coming back; rows and files are kept). Listings come from a per-node snapshot at most `drishti.bi.store-list-ttl` (1 s) old. `BiStore` is now an interface (`ContentBiStore`, `JpaBiStore`). [CONTENT_STORE.md](docs/architecture/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md#5-the-content-store-user-content-every-node-reaches) section 9, [BI_RUNS.md](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md#287-bi-runs-every-bi-query-as-a-bounded-visible-job) 13.3, [CONFIGURATION.md](docs/admin/CONFIGURATION.md), DATABASE.md.

- **Changed: a re-run says how it was asked in `rerunData` (`same` or `latest`)**, not `data`, which kept being overwritten: the new run's drawer showed Data "—" instead of its data versions.

- **Fixed (2.6.7 patch): Run again said only "Something went wrong."** A rerun the server answers at once (200 `{run, answer}`) is not kept as a row, so the reloaded list lacked it and the drawer failed in the page. The drawer now shows the new run from the reply (*Done at once: asked again with the latest data / as before, N rows*) and the old row says *superseded by* it; a fault in the page says *Run again failed in the page: <message>* and is logged to the browser console, never a bare "Something went wrong.". The test stand-in answers reruns in the real server's shape. [BI_RUNS_GUIDE.md](docs/guides/REPORTS_GUIDE.md#15-background-runs-long-bi-questions).
- **Fixed: the top bar's business date was unreadable in the Blue, Green and Crimson themes** (dark figures on the coloured gradient); it is now a white field with dark figures, like the command line.

- **Fixed (2.6.7 patch): Run again from a run's drawer looked like it did nothing.** The `Re-run ▾` select is now a labelled choice (*Run again as*: same as before, as of D; with the latest data) and a primary **Run again** button. While the new run goes the button spins and says *Running…*, the new run is highlighted at the top of the list and the drawer switches to it and follows it live; an answer given at once says *Done at once: reused the answer from <time>* with **Open result** (the console lost the run of an inline answer before); the old row says *superseded by* the new run. [BI_RUNS_GUIDE.md](docs/guides/REPORTS_GUIDE.md#15-background-runs-long-bi-questions).
- **The BI catalogue is split by kind (2.6.7 patch).** Tabs on the same page: Reports · Boards · Models · Datasets · Python (Python items, Transforms and notebooks) · All (grouped by kind), each with its count; `/bi/catalogue?kind=reports&sort=use` names the tab (bookmarkable, back and forward walk the tabs, the older `?kind=report` still works); search, filters and sort work inside the tab; with no `kind` the last tab used opens, else Reports. The console asks the server for every kind and for the boards and sorts each item into one tab (`GET /bi/api/catalogue-tabs`); no server change. [BI_GUIDE.md section 6](docs/guides/REPORTS_GUIDE.md#42-the-catalogue).
- **Rerun as of the same date or the latest, and fresh (2.6.7 patch).** `POST /api/v1/bi/runs/{id}/rerun` takes `data: same|latest` (same: as of the run's resolved date, the default; latest: resolved again now through the same as-of rule) and `fresh: true` (computed anew, no reuse or join; the owner only); the run object says `rerunOf`, `data` and `fresh`. API_GUIDE, BI_RUNS 14.1.
- **Fixed (2.6.7 patch): live BI (standing queries, board tiles, live visuals) showed a silent "No data" when a live table names a connector that does not serve its kind.** Starting the live table now says what a build says, `connector 'X' does not serve kind 'Y' (its kinds: ...)` with the fix, as the visual's or subscription's problem (`DRS-9026`), and no empty live table is started.
- **A report visual's answer is shared by access profile (2.6.7 patch).** Viewers with the same roles, masks and row rules (the model's security signature, row part and mask part) reuse or join one run of a visual on the same data and dates; another mask or row rule never gets it, in either order. A visual that depends on who is looking (`user.*`, `me`, `@me`, `${user}`, `USERNAME()` anywhere in the report, its state or query; a personal model; a live or version-1 dataset; no data version) stays personal. BI_RUNS.md 9.3a, BI_RUNS_GUIDE.
- **Fixed (2.6.7 patch): a report's fact table showed no rows ("No data for this selection") while its dimensions showed the latest held date.** A table whose connector does not serve its kind (a connector file generated from an older pack template: `config/connectors/risk-store.yaml` without `trade-valuation`) read nothing and was built, empty, for today; the build now says `connector 'risk-store' does not serve kind 'trade-valuation' (its kinds: ...)` with the fix (add the kind, or take the pack's template again). An empty build for "the latest" is served once and never kept or remembered (no `meta.json`), so the next read asks the source again.
- **As of a date, each table reads its latest business date on or before it (2.6.7 patch).** Facts and dimensions alike, live or not, on a weekend, a holiday or before today's load; an empty partition of a date is never the answer while an earlier date has rows (one whose source cannot say its data version is read again). The BI runs planner's footprint resolves the same dates, and they are part of the run result key (a reused answer is for the same dates). A refresh, a rebuild and a window still read their exact dates.
- **The answer says each table's date (2.6.7 patch).** Answers carry `meta.dataAsOf` (`asked`, each table's date, `aligned`; `meta.asOf` is unchanged); the report's line says *Data as of D* (with *asked A: no later data*) or, when the tables differ, *Data as of: trades D1, prices D2 (asked A)*, and a visual or board tile whose tables differ says it in its foot, in the theme's warning colour.
- **A report's `as-of` setting (2.6.7 patch):** `per-table` (the default), `aligned` (the newest date all of the visual's tables hold, for reconciliations), a fixed date, or a relative name (`last-business-day`, `previous-month`, ...); checked as `DRS-9030`; REPORTS.md section 7.1. A visual pinned to a past date is asked once, not followed.

- **Fixed (2.6.7 patch): on a console of several servers every followed visual said "Not updating · old: stream refused".** A standing query is held
  by the node that took `POST /api/v1/bi/mq/subscribe`, but the stream (`GET /mq/stream`) went to whichever server the console worker that holds
  the browser's channel used, and that node refused it (`DRS-9180`); the console dropped the server's answer and said "stream refused". Now a
  subscription's id names its node (`sq-<node>-<hex>`, as a run's `r-<node>-...`): the console opens the stream on that node's server, and any
  node relays the stream (and a close) from the holder, as the subscriber. A refusal reaches the page with the server's code and reason; on
  `DRS-9180` (the holder restarted) the page subscribes again once and reconnects. The visual's foot says *Reconnecting*, or *Not updating*
  with the reason in words (no "old:").

- **Fixed: a report's visuals failed `DRS-9025` ("you already have 3 queries running") once they became runs.** A report of eight visuals is eight runs and a person's cap (`drishti.bi.query.max-concurrent-per-user`, 3) admits three at once; the others waited the ad-hoc query's 2 s for a place and failed. A run now waits for its place as long as it may run (`max-duration`), so the rest queue and draw in turn.

## 2.6.7 — BI runs, chart any table, Delta and Iceberg side by side, gossip on its own port and HTTP/2; with 2.6.6, the QA release (2026-10-21)

- **Fixed: an oversize upload over HTTP/2 was refused by the client** (`Prohibited header name 'connection'`, Java 25's HttpClient): the 413 now sends `Connection: close` only on HTTP/1.x (2.6.7 turned HTTP/2 on).

- **BI runs integration findings, console side (BIR-09, BIR-10, BIR-12, BIR-13, BIR-14) and Promote in the drawer (2.6.7).** BIR-14: the
  workspace's *Add a member* form and settings live on its **Members** tab; after **Create workspace** the Workspaces page offers *Next: add
  the people who share it* (opens `/bi/w/<id>?tab=members`), and a shared workspace with only you in it says so on its Items tab with an
  **Add members** link; the three browser tests open the Members tab. BIR-12: *Kept until* says *kept (promoted)* or *kept (pinned)* only when
  the run says so; a done run without a date reads "30 days after it was last opened" (the run's or the settings' retention); a run without
  a result says nothing. BIR-13: a reason that already ends with the start of the fix ("…: re-run it") is finished by it, never said twice.
  BIR-09, BIR-10: no data words and no tables draw a dash (or the tables' versions when only those are given), and a report visual's run
  titled with the report's id reads by the visual's and the report's names. **Promote…** (`can.promote`) asks for the name, title and *a
  dataset snapshot* or *a report on it*, sends `POST /runs/{id}/promote {name, title, to}`, then shows *Promoted to name@N* with links to
  the drafts; DRS-9004 and DRS-9108 are said in words. `drishti.py bi runs promote RUN --to dataset|report [--name] [--title]` follows the
  server as built (`--as snapshot` still works). BI_GUIDE.md, BI_RUNS_GUIDE.md, BI_RUNS.md 14.4, tutorial 13.
- **BI runs: the server findings of the integration round (2.6.7, docs/qa/2026-10-21/BI_RUNS_INTEGRATION.md, BI_RUNS.md 18.2b).**
  BIR-07: a stored result is reused after every restart while the data is unchanged. The model part of the data version (the model view's
  hash) was taken of `ResolvedDataset.masked`, a `Set.copyOf` whose iteration order is salted per JVM, so a model with masked columns could
  hash differently after a restart; the hash is now taken of a canonical text (datasets by alias, masks sorted) and the masks keep their
  order (`ModelViewHashTest`, fresh JVMs included). The hash of every model with masks changes once with this release: its layers and stored
  results are built again once.
  BIR-06: report visuals are planned under `Prefer` as model queries are: a heavy visual asks to confirm (`409 DRS-9082`), a slicer on it
  needs a run (`409 DRS-9089`), ad-hoc heavy goes to the background at once; a visual of unknown size waits inline as before (no confirmation
  asked of every visual of a page); without `Prefer` nothing changes (`ModelAcceptanceTest` order 19, `RunServiceTest`).
  BIR-08: a run waiting for confirmation at a restart keeps waiting (a new token in its run object) until its `confirm.ttl`, instead of
  failing `DRS-9085` with a bell; a lapsed or unreplayable one is cancelled quietly (`DRS-9083`, the reason in words, no notice).
  BIR-09: the run object's `data.tables` (table, connector, dates, rows, versions) and `data.words` are filled from the planned footprint
  (`RunDataWords`, kept with the estimate, no new column), so the Runs tab's *Data* column says what was read (`RunDataWordsTest`).
  BIR-10: a report visual's run is titled with the visual's title and its `source.title` is the report's, no longer the report's id
  (`ModelAcceptanceTest` order 19).
  BIR-11: `can` offers only what the server can do now: share, export (not when distribution is off, not for a statement's file) and
  promote; rerun only for runs that can be asked again, schedule only for mq, sql and report runs (`RunCanTest`).
  BIR-13 (server side): a `DRS-9085` row's reason is a plain reason ("…and it could not be started again"), no longer ending with "re-run
  it", which the console's fix line repeated.

- **BI runs in the console: sharing, schedules, export and rollup suggestions (2.6.7, BI_RUNS_GUIDE.md).** The run drawer's **Share…**
  takes people and roles from the people picker (chips; names typed comma separated work too) and lists each recipient with the mode the
  server decided: *sees the same*, *re-masked* or *recomputed as them* (their run named), a refusal said in words with its code; **Unshare**
  per recipient. A recipient sees the run in their Runs tab marked *shared by* its owner, opens and exports their own version. **Schedule…**
  has presets (daily, weekdays, business days, weekly on a day, monthly on the last day or business day, or written out) that write the
  subscription grammar, shows it before saving, and the drawer shows the schedule with its next firing, **Edit**, **Pause**/**Resume** and
  **Remove**. **Export CSV** and **Export Excel** in the drawer, on the run card and above a report drawn from a run. **Admin → BI → Runs**
  lists the rollup suggestions with their YAML, **Accept** (into the model's draft, for review) and **Dismiss**; the **model designer**
  shows a notice linking to its model's open suggestions. **Run as SQL** in the report designer's query panel asks with the inline wait
  and shows the run card past it. CLI: `bi runs unshare`, `bi runs schedules edit`, `bi runs suggestions [list|accept|dismiss]`, `bi runs
  export --format csv|xlsx`, and completion. Help cards `run-share`, `run-schedule`, `run-export`, `run-suggestions`. Not yet: Analyse's
  SQL cells keep asking synchronously.
- **BI runs on a Drishti*net cluster (2.6.7, BI_RUNS.md 13.4, DRISHTI_NET.md).** Runs are named after the member (`r-<node id>-…`).
  `ShardDirectory` is wired to the members alive (`RunCluster`): a heavy run of a model another member owns is submitted there for the
  caller (signed, one hop, on-behalf-of, so their masks hold); a run's result, cancel and actions go to the member that holds it
  (`RunForwardFilter`, `502 DRS-5052` while it cannot be reached); `GET /runs` is scattered and merged (`nodes.failed`); run events are
  relayed. Leases are renewed every `lease.renew`; with one identity database a dead member's unfinished runs are adopted by the model's
  new owner once their lease lapsed, by one conditional update, and started again (attempt + 1); a node whose run was adopted abandons its
  copy. `RunClusterTest` (two servers in one JVM).

- **BI runs: a statement run interrupted by a restart is made again** as its runner from the request it was asked with (preview or
  file), instead of failing with `DRS-9085` (BI_RUNS.md 12.1, 18.2b R7). A replayed run keeps the runner's current signature, so its
  result reads back. `StatementReplayTest`.

- **BI runs: promotion to a dataset snapshot (2.6.7, BI_RUNS.md 9.4, DATASETS.md section 16).** `POST /api/v1/bi/runs/{id}/promote
  {name?, title?, to: dataset|report}`: the runner (with `bi-author`) freezes a finished model query or SQL run as
  `<data>/bi-runs/snapshots/<name>/v<N>/` and gets a draft dataset `source: {run: <name>, version: N, token}` (and a draft report on it).
  The rows are the promoter's view: a column masked for them holds the mask and is declared `masked` for every reader. The snapshot is read
  as a staged table of the model layer, only by the dataset it was promoted to (name and token, else `DRS-9108`); promoting again is the
  next version of the same draft; `promote.versions-keep` versions are kept. `RunPromotionTest`, `ModelAcceptanceTest` order 18.

- **BI runs: sharing, rollup suggestions, export, schedules, statements and the Admin numbers (2.6.7, BI_RUNS.md 18.2b).** **Sharing
  (R6, 9.3):** `POST /api/v1/bi/runs/{id}/share {to: [bob, role:risk-team]}` decides per person from the row part and the mask part of the
  security signature: `same` (equal rights: the stored result), `re-masked` (the same rows, more masks: the extra columns masked as the engine
  masks them, a masked grouping field collapsing its groups) or `recomputed` (a new run as the recipient; equal rights share one
  computation). The decision is taken again at every read, so a recipient never sees more than their rights allow now; a person who may not
  read the model gets no share; notices carry names only. `DELETE /runs/{id}/share/{recipient}`. **Rollup suggestions (8.3a):** repeated
  heavy questions of one model, grain and filters' shape (never values) past `suggest.min-runs` in `suggest.window` and `suggest.min-seconds`
  appear in `GET /api/v1/bi/admin/runs` `suggestions` with the rollup drafted; an administrator accepts (the rollup joins the model's draft
  for review) or dismisses; `built` once the model has it. **Export:** `POST /runs/{id}/export {format: csv|xlsx}`. **Schedules:**
  `POST /runs/{id}/schedule {schedule: "business-days 07:30"}`, `GET/PUT/DELETE /runs/schedules`; each firing runs as the owner now; the
  run object's `schedule`. **Statements** take `Prefer: respond-async` (preview and file). **Admin and metrics (R8):** the gauges
  `drishti.bi.runs.queue`, `running`, `store.bytes`; `/api/v1/bi/engine` `runs`; `admissionWaitP95Ms`, `accuracy.basis` and the snapshot
  storage filled. Not built yet: promotion to a dataset snapshot or a report, and the cluster (R7: leases, forwarding, scatter, adoption).
- **BI runs: the console and the real server together (2.6.7, docs/qa/2026-10-21/BI_RUNS_INTEGRATION.md).** Fixes: a run card whose run
  ended before the card listened now draws the result (it said *Queued* for ever on the real server, BIR-01); *Open* and the inbox notice of
  an MQ or SQL run open it in the Runs tab instead of a 404 (BIR-02); *Who: Shared with me* lists nothing until runs can be shared (BIR-03);
  the Runs tab's storage line is the person's own results, no longer the node's with the largest users' names (BIR-04); `bi mq --async` and
  `bi sql --async` take `--yes` (BIR-05). Open for the server lane: report visuals are not planned, so reports never show the confirm card
  (BIR-06); reuse after a restart failed once of four (BIR-07); a run waiting for confirmation fails `DRS-9085` at a restart (BIR-08).
- **BI runs, the server continued (2.6.7, BI_RUNS.md 18.2b and 14.5).** **The planner (R3):** an MQ or SQL question is sized from metadata
  only (built layers' `meta.json`, the new `SourcePlugin.rowEstimate`: Delta add-action `numRecords`, Iceberg manifest `record_count`; then
  rows per day learnt from builds), never a scan: tiers from the estimate, `409 DRS-9082` with the estimate, a `confirmToken` and the run
  (confirm with `POST /runs/{id}/confirm` or by asking again with the token), `413 DRS-9086` past the local engine's read limit and `409
  DRS-9089` for an interaction that would need a run, all before anything runs; estimates carry a real `basis` (`layers`, `delta-stats`,
  `iceberg-manifests`, `history`, `unknown`); measured rates and the `estimate.ratio` metric learn from finished runs. The synchronous
  `DRS-9029` now comes from the same metadata before any layer is built. **Data version:** a planned question's result is keyed by the
  version of every table and date it reads, so it is reused after a restart while the data is unchanged and never once a date is restated.
  **Store:** `store.max-bytes-per-user` is enforced (a person's oldest results go first). **The console contract (14.5):** `Drishti-Run`
  header on inline answers, `can.discard`, `confirmToken`, `schedule` and `source.model` on the run object, `since=` and comma-separated
  `state=` on the list, Admin's `/admin/runs` in the console's shape. **Fixes:** a slicer's second re-ask on the same visual no longer
  fails `DRS-9080`; an MQ with `options.explain` answers at once with its SQL under `Prefer`; a superseded interaction answers `409
  DRS-9083`, not `500`; an interrupted wait cancels its invisible run (`cancel.release`). `RunPlannerTest`, `RunServiceTest` (restart
  reuse, confirm, refusals), `ModelAcceptanceTest` (all four endpoints with and without `Prefer`), `rowEstimate` in `DeltaLayoutTest` and
  `IcebergSourcePluginTest`.
- **BI runs, the server (2.6.7, docs/architecture/BI_RUNS.md; steps R1, R2, R4, R5 and parts of R3, R7 and R8 as built in its section
  18.2b).** Every BI question can be a bounded, visible job. `POST /api/v1/bi/mq`, `/models/{id}/query`, `/bi/sql` and `/reports/{id}/query`
  accept `Prefer: respond-async[, wait=N]`: done within the wait (2 s) the answer is today's, with `X-Bi-Run`; otherwise `202 {run}` and the
  run continues, visible, with a `bi-run` notice when it ends. Without the header nothing changes. New `/api/v1/bi/runs` endpoints (submit,
  estimate, list, get, result, events, cancel, rerun, keep, delete result, settings, Admin's list and cancel); the run object of section 14.3.
  A run is computed as its runner; its result is reused, and a running twin joined, only under the same key (question, security signature,
  data version), so a result never crosses signatures (both orders tested). Background runs queue fairly (`workers`, `queue.per-user`,
  `DRS-9081`) and run in the `BACKGROUND` class; a question too large for an interactive answer becomes a background run, and a dashboard
  interaction that would need one is `DRS-9089`. Results are kept under `<data>/bi-runs` (FileSwap, retention and budget sweeper). At start
  every unfinished run is started again as its runner or failed `DRS-9085` with a reason, and told. Admission gains class caps
  (`drishti.bi.exec.background-share`, `standing-share`), dataset refresh enters it as background work, and background fragments take at most
  `fragments-share` of a connector's pool. Settings in their own file `config/runs/runs.yaml` (examples in `config/runs.examples/`); the
  `drishti_bi_run`, `drishti_bi_run_share` and `drishti_bi_run_schedule` tables in both identity schema files, kept identical by the new
  `SchemaParityTest`. Metrics `drishti.bi.runs.*`. Not yet: the metadata planner and confirmation, the run engine (a second DuckDB),
  Parquet and Arrow results, sharing, promotion, export, schedules and the cluster (forwarding, leases). `RunStateTest`, `RunsContractTest`,
  `AdmissionClassCapTest`, `RunServiceTest`, `RunStoreTest`, `RunRecordsJdbcTest`.
- **BI runs, the console lane (2.6.7, R1c to R6c of docs/architecture/BI_RUNS.md section 18.2).** A BI workspace has three tabs,
  **Items · Runs · Members** (`?tab=`); the Runs tab lists your runs and the ones shared with you with their status, as-of dates, data
  version, duration, rows and estimate, filtered by status, source, who and since, with a search; rows change live from
  the browser's one live channel (subscription `biruns`, relaying `GET /api/v1/bi/runs/events`; no polling) and each change is announced. A run's drawer shows its source, who ran it, filters, parameters, data
  versions, estimate and actual, tier, retention, shares and schedule, with every action its `can` allows: open (`/bi/run/<id>` opens the
  report with `?run=<id>`, drawn from the stored result), re-run on the same or the newest data, cancel, export (CSV, Excel, Parquet, PDF),
  share (same, re-masked, recomputed), promote to a snapshot or a report, keep longer, delete the result, schedule, confirm or discard.
  The rail's **Runs** link counts your active runs; `BI RUNS <GO>` and `g r` open the tab. Report visuals and board tiles ask with
  `Prefer: respond-async, wait=<inline wait>` (`B.ask` in bi-lib.js; the proxy passes it on and waits that plus 5 s): an answer in time is
  drawn as before; a slower one shows the **run card** (the estimate as a range, why, measured progress, Cancel, Open in Runs) and turns
  into the chart when its run finishes; a large question shows the **confirm card** (rows, days, basis, expected time; Run in background,
  Narrow the dates, Not now); a slicer, cross-filter or drill that would need a run says so at once (`DRS-9089`) with Run in background.
  Every state and code is said in words, the code in brackets. The bell and the inbox (a **Runs** tab) carry `bi-run` notices linking to
  the run. Admin → BI → **Runs** (`/admin/bi/runs`): the gate's slots per class, the queue per person, what runs (with Cancel), the result
  store, estimate accuracy, the inline rate and the rollup suggestions. CLI: `tools/biruns.py`, `drishti.py bi runs
  list|get|submit|estimate|wait|result|cancel|rerun|export|share|promote|keep|schedule|schedules|storage`, and `bi mq --async`,
  `bi sql --async`; completion follows. Help: `bi-runs` (docs/guides/BI_GUIDE.md, with three pictures) and the addresses `runs-tab`,
  `run-card`, `run-confirm`, `run-needed`, `snapshot-dataset`. Tests against a stand-in server (`tests/bi_runs_backend.py`):
  `test_bi_runs_page.py`, `test_bi_runs_inline.py`, `test_bi_runs_browser.py` (section 19.6, every theme, a phone),
  `tools/test_cli_biruns.py`. Works against the server's runs endpoints as they land; until then a page asks as before.
- **Chart any table (2.6.7, the console wiring; docs/architecture/TABLE_CHARTS.md section 24).** Every table can be drawn as a chart: a
  chart button in each table's heading and `K` on a focused table (`Shift`+`K` on a history page, where `k` is the previous day; `K` on a
  focused BI table or matrix, while `K` elsewhere on a report still toggles kiosk) open a wide dialog (full screen on a phone) with the
  chart already drawn from smart defaults: line, bar (grouped, stacked, 100%), area, pie or donut, scatter and combo; X with date buckets
  and gaps; up to six series with their aggregation and left or right axis; split by a column (12 at most); sort; Top N with Others.
  Search results, history and BI tables chart the server's raw values; a table with a Pivot tab its raw records; any other table its
  cells as displayed, said so. Masked columns are offered greyed and never charted (a crafted choice is refused); partly masked cells
  are left out and counted. **Chart all N** aggregates every match of a search on the server through its pack's search pivot, or reads
  every record of a table with a Pivot tab. View as table, PNG, SVG, CSV and Excel of the data as drawn; the summary sentence is the
  chart's accessible name and caption; points step with the arrow keys and are read out; every console theme (Terminal hues and light
  included), redrawn on a theme change, with a palette that never gives two series one colour. The scripts load at the first chart.
  Not yet: saved charts, Promote to Sutra, Open in BI and Chart all through BI runs (the server steps). `test_table_chart.py`,
  `test_table_chart_browser.py`; USER_GUIDE *Chart any table* with pictures; the `table-chart` help address.
- **Drishti\*net: gossip off the busy path (2.6.7).** A server busy with queries is never wrongly suspected. Each node opens a **gossip
  port** as it joins (node.yaml's new `gossip-port`: `auto` by default, a port number, or `off`), a second Tomcat connector with its own
  acceptor, connection limit and eight platform threads, advertised in its member entry (`gossipPort`) and serving only gossip, probes and
  digests. On both ports those three are answered by the first filter, from memory, past every guard and admission gate. The sender's
  round runs on a platform thread of its own, its exchanges and probes on a platform pool, through an HTTP/1.1 client of its own (two
  platform threads, short connect timeout), never the data client or its timeouts. A gossip port blocked by a firewall falls back to the
  server's port for 5 minutes with one warning; older nodes are gossiped with on their server port. New metric
  `drishti_net_gossip_exchange_seconds`; Admin → Health shows `gossipPort` and `peerProtocol`. NetGossipBusyTest: with every node's request
  threads saturated for 12 s, no suspicion (with `gossip-port: off`, every node suspected both peers); a node that died was suspect after
  3.0 s and dead after 7.0 s. TransportSettingsTest; DRISHTI_NET.md, NET.md, CONFIGURATION.md, API_GUIDE.md, config/net.examples/node.yaml.
- **Drishti\*net: HTTP/2 for peer data (2.6.7).** Forwarded views, peer documents, scatter-gather, peer history, state sync and the live
  relay are multiplexed over one HTTP/2 connection per peer (routing.yaml's new `peer-protocol: http2 | http1`, default `http2`): `h2c` by
  the upgrade on plain HTTP, ALPN on TLS, the server's port speaking both (`server.http2.enabled: true`, `DRISHTI_HTTP2`; 1,000 streams per
  connection). The first call to a peer is a lone signed ping so the upgrade happens once. A peer without HTTP/2 answers in HTTP/1.1 on
  the same call. NetHttp2Test; NetPeerProtocolBench (64 users, forwarded views, warm): 1 connection instead of 227, p99 117 ms instead of
  370 ms. DRISHTI_NET.md, NET.md, CONFIGURATION.md, config/net.examples/routing.yaml; `drishti.py net check` knows `gossip-port`,
  `peer-protocol`, `join-wait` and `join-grace`.
- **Mixed Delta and Iceberg storage: each source system's trades in Delta Lake or Apache Iceberg (2.6.7).**
  `tools/build_demo_lakes.py --store <system>=delta|iceberg` (repeatable, `all=` for every system; default every system in Delta, as
  before): `--store endur=delta --store calypso=iceberg` keeps ENDUR in Delta and puts CALYPSO in `data/iceberg/trading/trade_calypso`
  (beside `--lake`; `DRISHTI_ICEBERG_ROOT` moves it). The system is built as Delta (so its documents and promoted columns are a Delta
  build's), then streamed by the new `tools/lake/stores.py` into `IcebergLoader` (`engine: native`, started from the server's exec jar:
  no Maven, works on Windows), and its Delta table is removed. Its connector file `trade-<system>.yaml` is switched to `plugin: iceberg`
  with `table: {trade: trade_<system>}` (or back to the pack's Delta template; the old text kept in `<data>/connectors/history/`), so one
  connector serves each system; the closing lines list every system's store and what was done to each connector file. Works with
  `--only` (a `--store` moving a system the run does not rebuild adds `trades/<system>`), `--files-only` and `--source-dir --system`
  (your files staged as Delta under `<data>/build/iceberg-stage`, then copied), `--server` (told once, `trade`, the newest date) and
  `--dry-run`; a partial run keeps each system it does not name in its store; `lake demo` leaves a non-Delta connector file as it is.
  The Iceberg connector gained `table.<kind>` (a kind read from a named table, as the Delta connector's), BI's column `scan`,
  `dataVersion` (snapshot id and time; a day's files' fingerprint) and `latestDate`/`earliestDate`/`heldDates`, so BI reads a mixed union
  as columns (it fell back to reading documents one by one) and the history cache works on Iceberg trades (it was off).
  **Equality test** `tools/lake/stores_equality.py`: five synthetic days of 1,000 trades a system built all-Delta and mixed (ENDUR Delta,
  CALYPSO and MUREX Iceberg), one server on each in turn: six trade pages, `TRD <id> 10` for each, two counterparty-trades pages, three
  searches and a BI model query, **18 answers the same**. IcebergNamedTableTest; tools/lake/test_stores.py; test_build_demo_lakes.py;
  DEMO_DATA.md, ICEBERG_CONNECTOR.md, TOOLS.md 4.9, CLI_GUIDE.md, QA_ON_WINDOWS_WITH_CUSTOM_DATA.md step 3.3.

- **History cache default 64 → 256 MB (SOAK4-02).** Counted in real heap since SOAK3-02, 64 MB held only 63 to 208 answers, and the busiest soak node hit the cache 1 % of the time; `drishti.history.cache-mb` lowers it on a small heap.

- **Fixed (SOAK3-01, P2): a node that has just started or rejoined never says "no source holds" (`404 DRS-1001`) for what only its peers
  hold.** Until it has the digests of its alive peers (or for at most routing.yaml's new `join-grace`, 30 s) a node with seeds or saved
  members is *joining*; a read none of its sources holds then waits up to the new `join-wait` (2 s) for the digests and is answered from
  the peer, or says `502 DRS-5052` "this node is still joining Drishti*net …; try again in a moment". Histories and views of a kind not
  here do the same. The console tries such a read once on another server without counting it against the node. Admin → Health shows
  `state: joining`; a single server and a node with no seeds are never joining. NetRejoinMissTest (a restarted node asked 408 times from
  its first open port: 81 × 404 before, 0 after); NetFolderTest; test_cluster_failover; NET.md, DRISHTI_NET.md section 5.
- **History cache: `cache-mb` is real heap (SOAK3-02).** The cache was already one global, least-recently-used budget across every key
  and caller signature, but it sized an entry at 48 bytes a node, 2.3 to 3.2 times under the heap the days take, so `cache-mb: 64` held
  150 to 210 MB. An entry is now sized as the JVM lays it out (within a few per cent of the measured heap). The other per-signature caches
  (a view's shape, 100,000 entries, about 30 MB; the map panels' listings and documents, 32 and 8 entries for 60 s) are bounded by count.
  HistoryCacheBoundTest; HISTORY_QUERIES.md section 11; CONFIGURATION.md.
- **Soak: the checker asks the administrator and the viewer back to back, in both orders (SOAK2-01).** Each checked history range is
  asked in both roles, and the checker asks a history's twin (same entity, range and node, the other role) straight after it, so the
  class of SOAK2-01 is exercised every few seconds; `soak.json` `maskPairs` counts the pairs per order, peer-held, and wrong answers.
  `net_soak.py`; test_net_soak; DRISHTI_NET.md 17.1.
- **Fixed (QA4-07): `load-iceberg.sh`'s one-line error gives the real reason, never `: null`.** A REST catalog that could not be reached
  read *cannot reach the REST catalog at http://127.0.0.1:1: null (ClosedChannelException …)*: the exception has no message. The line
  (and the REST catalog's own error) now gives the first message in the cause chain that says something, else the cause in words: *(the
  connection was refused or closed before an answer (ClosedChannelException))* (`Reasons`). ICEBERG_CONNECTOR section 6.
  IcebergLoaderFailureTest.
- **Fixed (QA4-06): `build_demo_lakes.py --server` ends with what came of the signals.** It said *The server … was told* when nothing
  listened or every signal was refused (403); it now reads lake demo's own report of the server and says *was not told: nothing
  answered there*, *was not told: it refused the signals* (and the token to give), *did not answer in time*, *was told of only some
  tables*, or *was told* when every signal was taken; a dry run says *would be told*. TOOLS.md. test_build_demo_lakes.
- **Fixed (QA4-03): statements: notes wrap whole, and a date after the business date reads no misleading 0.** A card's note was cut
  (*Not available: DRS-9020 the as-of date 202…*) and a masked reader's table note too on paper (*Not sorted: 'MTM' is masked fo…*); notes
  now wrap over lines on the preview and the PDF, never cut. For a date later than the business date the Trades card read `0` above *Not
  available*: nothing was counted, so every card reads `–` there (a count still reads `0` on a day the data could hold). The preview's
  `rows` and the CLI's *N rows* are `0` when every band is empty, not the three empty cards. STATEMENTS.md. StatementApiTest,
  StatementLayoutTest.
- **Fixed (QA4-04): a connector file's `enabled` placeholder is listed as it resolves, and one that resolves to neither true nor false
  is refused.** `"${DRISHTI_LAKE_ENABLED:true}"` with the variable `false` read `enabled: true` beside `DISABLED` (the list used the
  file's text); `"${VAR:nope}"` switched the connector off silently while a literal `"nope"` was refused. Now the list, the form's
  checks and the disable confirmation use the resolved value, and `${VAR:nope}` is refused with the literal's message (`… not 'nope'
  (${VAR:nope} resolves to it)`) on a hot reload and at start. CONNECTOR_FILES.md. ConnectorManagerTest, ConnectorFilesTest.
- **Fixed (QA4-02): a map panel on a node that reads its kind only from a peer is drawn.** Its listing asked this node's sources only,
  so the map was empty and said *no economy entity matches ECON-{iso3}* though the entities exist. The listing now asks the peers a
  search of the kind asks (`GET /api/v1/net/list/{kind}`, for the caller, one hop), merged with this node's; the documents come through
  the peers, masked there for the caller, and both stay keyed per security signature. DRISHTI_NET.md N5. NetMapPanelTest (two servers,
  viewer and risk in both orders; it failed before the fix).
- **Fixed (QA4-01, QA3B-03, P2): a moved Iceberg table is DEGRADED on Java 25 too.** The plugin carries a failed load as a quiet
  cancellation and looked for it by type when the load was joined; Java 25's `CompletableFuture.join()` throws a new
  `CancellationException("join")` with it as the cause, so on Java 25 (QA's server; the tests ran on 21) no failure reached the
  table problems: Admin → Connectors said `UP`, Test found no dates, and every read answered a generic `502 DRS-1003` with a 36-line
  stack trace. The failure is now found through the join's wrappers on every JDK: the badge and Health say *degraded* with the moved
  table and the `relocate` to copy, a read answers *the table … names files that are not there* with one log line, and the connector's
  Test is not ok with the same text, each kind reading `cannot read: …` instead of *nothing found* (`listingProblem`). ICEBERG_CONNECTOR
  section 14. IcebergMovedConnectorFileTest now loads several domains and tables over ten dates with the loader, moves the folder and
  serves it through a connector file at start and one hot-added (it failed on Java 25 before the fix); IcebergMovedTableTest.
- **Fixed (QA3B-04): a `relocate` whose old folder matches nothing is said in Health** (for example a Windows pair on a Linux lake),
  also when several tables moved together are one sentence.
- **Fixed (QA4-05): an Iceberg connector whose `relocate` cannot be read no longer logs a NullPointerException at each retry**; the
  half-started connector closes quietly and the start's refusal is the one problem, logged in one line (a connector whose start refuses a
  setting no longer logs a stack trace). IcebergMovedTableTest, IcebergMovedConnectorFileTest.
- **Fixed: `build_demo_lakes.py` run with a Python that lacks `deltalake` failed every table with "no engine"**; it now stops at once and names the console's environment to use.
- **Fixed (SOAK2-01, P1): an administrator's history of a peer-held entity no longer shows a viewer's masks.** The history cache kept
  the days a peer answered (masked there for the first caller) as if they were unmasked, and served them to every later caller: after a
  viewer, an administrator got `PRICE` as `•••` in a column marked `masked: false`, with the price's changes missing, until the entry
  went. Days a peer answered are now kept under the caller's security signature (`Principal.securitySignature()`: sorted roles and
  embedding app, the live relay's partition too) and never served to a caller with another one; days this node holds stay one shared
  unmasked entry, masked per answer. A field that reads as the mask on any day (a peer's stricter `redact`) is `masked: true` and never
  "changed". The other caches on the history and net paths were checked; two more shared what peers read for one caller and are now
  per signature too (`SourceRouter.partition()`): the map panels' listing and documents (60 s), and a view's document-shape cache
  (a masked value's type is not the value's). HISTORY_QUERIES.md sections 11 and 13, DRISHTI_NET.md *Masks twice*. Tests: HistoryCacheMasksTest, NetHistoryMasksTest (three servers: viewer first and
  administrator first, two reading nodes, repeated within the cache's life; it failed before the fix).
- **Fixed (SOAK2-02): a connector file's `enabled: "false"` (quoted) switches the connector off.** It was refused (`'enabled' is true or
  false`) though `${VAR:false}` resolves to the same text; `"true"` and `"false"` in any case are now the booleans, anything else is
  refused naming the value. `net_soak.py` writes a YAML boolean. CONNECTOR_FILES.md; ConnectorFilesTest, test_net_soak.
- **Fixed (SOAK2-05): the refusal log says each thing about a node once a minute from the first refusal.** Pages that said a node
  "failed" and histories that said it was "not answering" alternated and logged a line each time (38 lines in the 2 s before the node
  was suspect); each is now one line, then the count a minute. A node gossip says is back whose digest has not arrived yet is named
  `(rejoining)` in a refusal, never `(alive)`. NET.md troubleshooting; RefusalLogTest.

- **Fixed (DOCS2-01): `build_demo_lakes.py`'s heartbeat named its own working folders** (`_drishti-lake/staging`, `locks`) instead of the table being written; it now names the table, as the Windows QA guide shows.

- **Fixed (QA3B-06): BI powers changed on a role reach its holders at once on every console worker.** With four workers the BI menu was wrong for up to 6 s after Admin, BI settings changed a role's powers (only the administrator's own copy was forgotten) and Admin, Roles forgot nothing. A role saved or deleted there now writes the console's shared stamp (`core/user_stamps.py`), so every worker reads every holder's BI powers, and their other per-user copies, again at their next page. `test_user_stamps_workers.py`, `test_bi.py`; BI_GUIDE (BI settings), CONFIGURATION (`server.workers`).

- **Fixed (QA3B-01): a figure on a statement is never cut with an ellipsis.** A seven-currency matrix on A4 portrait read `-428,350,58…` (a thousand times smaller than the figure) and the Notional card `3,617,068,619,773.…`, with no note. Now a number column is as wide as its widest figure (every row measured) and the text columns share the rest; when the figures do not fit, the table's font shrinks to a floor (three quarters of `fontSize`, at least 6 pt), then its number columns go on in parts below, each repeating the row labels (*… (part 2 of 2: NOK to NZD)*), then the text columns narrow. A card shrinks to the statement's font, then reads in compact units (`3.62tn`) with *Exactly 3,617,068,619,773.12* under it. Only a figure wider than the paper is cut, and then the page says so and the preview's `cut` lists it. Text may still be cut. `StatementFit`; `StatementLayoutTest` (the QA's matrix); STATEMENTS 3, REPORTS 22.
- **Fixed (QA3B-02, 08, 10, 09): a statement for a date without data says which date it read and where data is; an empty count reads 0 everywhere; Excel carries the PDF's notes; "1 page".** The hint said *No data is held for October 2026 (2026-10-01 to 2026-10-31)* for 2026-10-25 in a month with 14 days of data: with `dates: end` only the period's last day is read, and the hint now names it (*No data is held for 2026-10-25, the date this October 2026 statement reads … The nearest date with data is 2026-10-20 (before).*), the nearest dates coming from what the connectors keep (`SourcePlugin.heldDates`: Delta, file; else their first and newest dates). An empty count card read `–` on some dates and `0` on others: a count of nothing is `0` and a value of nothing `–` in the preview, the PDF and Excel, a date later than the business date included. The Excel statement's *About* sheet lists each sheet's notes and each sheet has its note beside the table (*Masked for you: MTM.*, *Not sorted: …*). The mail subject and the audit say *1 page*; the file carries `X-Statement-Hint`. `StatementApiTest`; STATEMENTS 3, 6, 7.

Java 21 accepts both flags. `tools/test_launcher_memory.py`; PERFORMANCE (*Resident memory*), OPERATIONS sections 4 and 7.2.
- **Fixed (QA3B-07): after a burst of data-load signals the BI layers settle.** 2,976 signals in rounds (8 clients, 60 dates) rebuilt each BI table 24 to 25 times per date, four rebuilds failed on a race (`DRS-9027 … part.parquet.….tmp is gone`, `cannot write the layer's metadata`), and 20 minutes later the server was at 1,000 to 1,600 % CPU with 588 full GCs. Each signal cleared the date's partitions (deleting their folders, under builds writing into them) and queued a rebuild, so every round rebuilt every date again; the latest's build and a date's build of one partition took different locks. Now a signal for a date whose stored partition was built from the data the connector holds now (its data version matches) changes nothing; a waiting rebuild runs only when the data changed since the one before it; two tables' background rebuilds run at once in the whole server; an invalidation removes a partition's metadata only (the Parquet file stays until a build replaces it, so a page reading it finishes and a build keeps its temporary file); and every build of a partition (on demand, background, a table's latest) checks, writes and records it under the partition's one lock, into a file of its own (`part-<id>.parquet`, named by the metadata; the replaced one goes ten minutes later), so a query reading the previous file finishes on it; a signal rebuilds in the background only the dates a page has read (a backfill's other dates are built when asked). Measured on a 3 GB server over the 66-table, 60-day demo lakes, 3,000 signals in 25 rounds (8 clients) with three model-query readers: 6,621 queries, none failed, slowest 1.7 s; no DRS-9027; CPU 500 to 950 % during the burst, 28 % 12 s after the last signal and 1 to 2 % from then on (7 minutes watched), no full GC, RSS 1.7 GB. With the coalescing alone (before the last two changes) the same burst left the server at about 1,000 % CPU and 587 full GCs seven minutes after the last signal, still reading every signalled date of twelve tables from the documents. An `after-load` dataset refresh has one running and one waiting with every signalled date, each once, skipping a date whose layers hold the data held now. `LoadBurstTest` (3,000 signals with three readers: none rebuilt for unchanged data, one more read for a date changed mid-burst, no failure without data versions), `DatasetRefresherTest`; DATA_LOADS (*On ready*).
- **Fixed (QA3B-12): `load-iceberg.sh` and `load-iceberg.ps1` end a failed load with one line, not a Java stack trace.** A REST catalog whose bucket was missing ended in `Exception in thread "main" java.io.UncheckedIOException … NoSuchBucketException` and eight frames. The loader now prints one line and exits 1: a missing bucket names the bucket (from `--warehouse` or the root), the endpoint and what to check; an unreachable catalog or object store names it; anything else is `iceberg: the load failed: <why>` (`-Ddrishti.loader.trace=true` adds the trace). The scripts add one line of their own, remove their input file, and the PowerShell twin no longer throws an error record on top. `IcebergLoaderFailureTest`, `tools/test_load_scripts.py`; ICEBERG_CONNECTOR section 6.
- **Fixed (QA3B-05): a Cassandra connector that cannot connect no longer leaks a driver session at every retry.** The session still connecting was left to close "when it connects", which a refusing cluster never does: each restart by the retry board added one more session with its own threads and reconnect WARNs (`too many session instances: 9 active`), and they went on after the connector file was deleted. A close (a retry, a stop, a deleted file) now cancels the session being built, so the driver stops reconnecting and closes it, and the connector's refresh task is stopped too. The driver's sessions, threads and log lines carry the connector's name (`[qa-cass-nocert] Error connecting …`) instead of `s2`, `s3`, …. `CassandraConnectFailureTest` counts the driver's sessions and threads over five restarts against a closed port; CASSANDRA_CONNECTOR section on diagnosing.
- **Fixed (QA3B-11): a Cassandra TLS refusal is named in Health.** `DOWN: connecting to Cassandra at …` read the same for a closed port and a TLS refusal; the cause was only in the driver's WARN. While the driver retries, the connector opens one connection of its own to the first contact point (at most every 30 s) and says what it found: no connection, the node asks for a client certificate, the client certificate refused, the node's certificate not trusted or not naming the host, `tls.enabled` against a plain port, or a node that requires TLS from a connector without it, each with the `tls.*` settings to set. `CassandraConnectFailureTest` (local TLS servers), `CassandraTlsTest` (Cassandra 5 with mutual TLS); CASSANDRA_CONNECTOR.
- **Fixed (QA3B-03, QA3B-04): a moved Iceberg table is "degraded" in Admin → Connectors with the `relocate` to copy, and `relocate` reads plain folders.** A domain written by `load-iceberg.sh --engine native`, moved and served through a connector file was DEGRADED in Health, but Admin → Connectors showed it as *running* (its badge read only DOWN and warnings), so the page said UP and hid the fix; each read answered `502 DRS-1003` with a full stack trace. `IcebergMovedTableTest` passed because it checked the plugin's own health, not the page. Now the badge is **degraded** with the health beside it; tables moved together are one sentence with one pair, given in the plain form to copy (`relocate: '/data/ice1 -> /data/ice2'`); the 502 says the table names files that are not there (no folder in it) and the log has one line. `relocate` accepts plain folders, Windows folders and shares, `file:` URIs in any spelling and `s3a://` for `s3://` (both sides are read into the metadata's `file:` form; whole folders only), says when its old folder holds nothing or its new folder lacks the files, and a pair that cannot be read fails the start naming it. `RelocationTest`, `IcebergMovedLoaderTableTest`, `IcebergMovedConnectorFileTest`, `ConnectorBadgeTest`; ICEBERG_CONNECTOR sections 14 and 15, CONNECTOR_FILES.
- **Design: fewer duplicate BI runs** (BI_RUNS.md 8.3a, product owner 2026-10-20): normalise questions before hashing, offer an existing result on older data before a heavy run, suggest a rollup to the model owner for heavy questions asked again and again (in 2.6.7), with reuse and join rates in Admin → Runs.

- **Design: BI runs (release 2.6.7).** New [BI_RUNS.md](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md#287-bi-runs-every-bi-query-as-a-bounded-visible-job), the product owner's decisions of 2026-10-20: super scale is the architecture at every data size; every BI query goes through one bounded asynchronous pipeline (submit, plan with a metadata-only estimate, admission, run, store, notify), drawn inline within about 2 s or shown as a visible job in a new Runs tab of the BI Workspace with a count on the bell; three tiers (interactive, known heavy from products and rollups, ad-hoc heavy as a background run); results stored as Parquet under the data folder, keyed by fingerprint, data version and security signature, re-masked or recomputed per recipient when shared; background class caps in admission, cancellation, restart and cluster rules; settings in `config/runs/runs.yaml`; codes DRS-9080 to DRS-9089; build steps R1 to R9 for two builders. The release order in IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN and BI_DESIGN 12.2 (2.6.6, 2.6.7, 2.7.0, 2.8.0, the real-life QA, 2.9.0, 3.0.0), SUPER_SCALE and the docs index follow.
- **Design: one Drishti database and the write-back decisions of 2026-10-20.** New [DATABASE.md](docs/architecture/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md#6-the-one-drishti-database-design-not-built) (2.7.0 item 0): all Drishti-owned relational state in one database (SQLite by default, PostgreSQL long term), no migrations (two complete schema files, a parity test, a version stamp, `drishti.py db copy`), configured in `config/db/database.yaml`. [WRITE_BACK.md](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md#31-collaboration-write-back-and-approvals): a durable shared edit log (`drishti_edit_lane`, `drishti_edit_log`) fenced by epoch, with SQLite, PostgreSQL, S3 and edit-primary fallbacks (`edit.log: auto`); the lane owner does every write, the lake is never written per edit, source commands go through the outbox; connector `writes:`; off by default at three levels and controlled by roles; W0 and cluster acceptance tests. IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN, BI_DESIGN 12.2 wave W and the docs index follow.
- **Fixed (QA3A-05, 07, 08): `build_demo_lakes.py` tells the server you name, once, says what it is waiting for, and ends with lines that fit the run.** `--server URL` (and `--token-file`, else `DRISHTI_TOKEN`) tells that server once at the end, one data-load signal per table for its newest date (`lake demo --signal-once`), never one per table and day; by default no server is told and the closing lines say to restart it or wait for its refresh. The heartbeat says `writing <table>` only while files land, else `nothing written for N s`; `lake demo` counts signals the server **refused** apart from those it **did not answer** in time (the token hint only for 401/403) and reports the build and the signals' time apart. After `--files-only --system calypso` the closing lines name a CALYPSO trade from your newest file and say no restart is needed. `test_build_demo_lakes.py`, `tools/lake/test_demo.py`; TOOLS 4.9, QA_ON_WINDOWS_WITH_CUSTOM_DATA 3.0.
- **Fixed (QA3A-02, 03, 04, 06): a change made through one console worker shows on every worker at once, in every browser of the user.** With `server.workers=4`, a pack choice came back as the old one on 17 of the next 20 pages, a saved layout flipped back and forth for a minute, a disabled user kept working for 10 s on the console the administrator used, and a second browser showed the old theme for 30 s: each worker kept its own copy and only the worker that made the change forgot its own. Now the change writes the user's stamp (one small file per user under `<console data>/user-stamps`; one for everyone when an administrator switches a pack), and every worker checks it (one `stat`) before reusing a copy of the user's settings, packs, view layouts, saved pivots, BI powers or session check. The browser cookie stamp stays as the fast path. The copies now live 10 s (`ui.user_cache_seconds`; settings were 30 s, packs, layouts and pivots 60 s), which bounds other consoles behind one address that share no data folder. `core/user_stamps.py`; `test_user_stamps_workers.py`; CONFIGURATION (`server.workers`, `ui.user_cache_seconds`, `auth.recheck_seconds`), OPERATIONS, USER_MANAGEMENT.
- **Fixed (QA3A-01, P1): a storm of data-load signals no longer drives the server out of memory.** A 60-day `--only` load sent 60 signals; each dropped the trade connectors' caches, cleared the BI layers and started a full read of every trade document beside the ones running, and reads whose caller had timed out stayed queued for a document-read slot (880,000 parked threads, then `OutOfMemoryError`). Now: signals for a connector refreshed less than `drishti.loads.refresh-window` (5 s) ago are merged into one more refresh at the end of the window (at most one running and one waiting per connector; the merged signal still looks for the newest table version); a purge of grouped pages keeps the build that runs and builds once more after it (`rebuild-delay`, 5 s, on disk), never two full reads at once; BI layer rebuilds run one date at a time per table, each date once; and the Delta, Iceberg, JDBC, DuckDB and MongoDB read slots are bounded (`max-queued-reads`, 4096 for documents) and drop a read whose caller has stopped waiting (`ReadSlots`, `ReadDeadline`). `AbandonedReadsTest`, `DerivedSourcePluginTest`, `QueryEngineTest`, `LoadsApiTest`; DATA_LOADS, DELTA_CONNECTOR, ICEBERG_CONNECTOR, CONFIGURATION.
- **Fixed: a BI table rebuilt on Windows failed with DRS-9027** (`part.parquet.tmp -> part.parquet`): Windows cannot replace a file anything holds open (a query reading the previous version, a virus scanner, the indexer). The new file is written under a name of its own (two builds never share one) and moved over the old one, tried again for about 5 s while it is held; past that the message says what held it. `FileSwapTest`. Found on the product owner's Windows machine.
- **Fixed: the server makes the folder `java.io.tmpdir` names when it is missing** (an IDE run configuration passes `-Djava.io.tmpdir=<data>/tmp/server` but cannot make it; on a fresh clone DuckDB, RocksDB and CatBoost then failed to unpack). The console never falls back to the system temp folder: without a setting its base is `<data dir>/tmp/console`, however it is started. `JvmTempDirTest`, `test_tmpdir.py`.
- **Fixed: `build_demo_lakes.py` no longer signals a running server for every table and day** (3,960 signals for 66 tables over 60 days, each making the server read the data again; QA3A-01/05). Restart the server after a build, or let it pick the tables up at its next refresh.
- **Fixed (SOAK-10): the soak configures only what its lakes hold.** Its servers retried `collateral-store`, `legal-store`,
  `market-store` and `risk-store` (about 8 WARN attempts each) and warned `deprecated: connector 'trade-…' is defined in the server's own
  configuration` because of the soak's own `--drishti.sources.connectors.*.enabled=false` flags. No server loads market-risk any more,
  and before each start the soak writes a connector file (the pack's template with `enabled: "false"`) for every Delta connector whose
  tables the node's lake lacks, the documented way; the flags are gone. `net_soak.connector_files`; test_net_soak; DRISHTI_NET
  section 17.1, TOOLS.
- **Fixed (SOAK-09): the soak's mask check covers something.** It checked 35 distinct histories, and no viewer trade history had a
  masked field (the default `drishti.security.redact` names `trader`, which the synthetic trades do not hold). The soak's servers now
  mask `PRICE`, `TRADER_ID` and `NAME`; a viewer's trade history must show `PRICE` and a counterparty's `NAME` as a masked column, the
  mask on every row and never a value in a diff, or the answer is wrong. The checked set holds `--history-sample` (40) trades per
  system (MUREX ones peer-only from a and b) and 20 counterparties, each asked as administrator and viewer with two of ten ranges (about
  140 distinct histories, 280 requests); the verdict's `masksExercised` fails unless the reference masks them in every viewer history.
  `soak_check.mask_missing`; test_net_soak; DRISHTI_NET section 17.1, TOOLS.
- **Fixed (SOAK-08): the soak keeps every wrong answer.** It kept five per kind, with no time for the others and the body cut at 600
  characters before `partial` and `problems`, which were what made them wrong. `soak.json`'s `wrong` now has the count per kind of
  request and per rule that failed (`byKind`, also in `soak-report.txt`), every wrong answer's time, node, request and rule (`all`), and
  the first 200 with the status, `partial` and `problems` whole, the rest of the body cut and a compact diff against the reference
  (`samples`). `soak_check.judge_history_why`, `WrongLog`; test_net_soak; DRISHTI_NET section 17.1, TOOLS.
- **Fixed (SOAK-07): the soak measures the console's memory.** It sampled the uvicorn parent alone (one thread, 50.7 MB on all 120
  samples of the 2026-10-20 soak); `tools/bench/net_soak.py` now samples the console's whole process tree from `/proc`: resident memory,
  threads and open files summed over the parent and its workers, `processes`, and each worker's own figures (`workers`), so the console's
  memory slope means something. test_net_soak; DRISHTI_NET section 17.1, TOOLS.
- **Fixed (SOAK-04): the soak's memory check tells a leak from a node taking over the load.** `tools/bench/net_soak.py` judges each
  process by its steady slope: only the samples outside the kill windows and `--settle` seconds (600) after each, fitted with a level per
  steady span, so a step when the console moves sessions to a node at a failover is not growth. The whole-run slope is reported beside
  it (`wholeRunSlopeMbPerHour`, `steadySpans`). On the 2026-10-20 soak's b (128 to 367 MB at c's kill, flat after) the whole-run slope
  is +166 MB/h and the steady one 0. `soak_check.memory_trend`; test_net_soak; DRISHTI_NET section 17.1, TOOLS.
- **Fixed (QA-OPEN-01): `tools/testdata/make_testdata.py` writes the same bytes on every Python.** 16 counterparty and netting-set
  change files differed in the sixth decimal of walked values between environments (`NET_MTM` 484329001.595759 vs .595758): a netting
  set's `NET_MTM` is the sum of its trades' MTM, and the built-in `sum()` of floats gives a different last bit on Python 3.13 and 3.14
  (597445765.99 vs 597445765.9899999), which the walk of earlier days carries into the sixth decimal. The banking generator's sums
  (`data_results.py`: `amount()`, whole numbers exactly, others by `math.fsum` to the cent; every other float sum by `math.fsum`) and the
  walk's drift (`samplegen/lake.py`) no longer use it; the pack samples are unchanged, data/testdata regenerated (63 files).
  `make_testdata.py --check` passes on 3.14 and 3.13. `tools/testdata/test_deterministic.py`; TOOLS, DEMO_DATA, DEVELOPER_GUIDE.
- **Investigated (SOAK-05): resident memory that creeps while the live heap is flat is the committed heap and glibc's malloc arenas,
  not a native leak.** Two runs under 20 users with Native Memory Tracking: metaspace, code, threads and direct buffers flat; RSS grows
  with G1's committed heap (to `-Xmx`) and, with the default allocator, 149 malloc arenas holding about 700 MB (about 200 MB with
  `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2`). PERFORMANCE.md *Resident memory* gives the numbers, the budget (`-Xmx` plus about 1 GB, or 0.4 GB with two
  arenas) and the settings `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2`, `-XX:MaxDirectMemorySize=256m`, `-XX:TrimNativeHeapInterval=60000`.
- **Fixed (SOAK-01): a complete history is no longer marked partial while a node is down.** A node that is down counts only for the
  business dates its last digest said it holds: each source of a digest now carries `earliestDate` beside `latestDate`
  (`SourcePlugin.earliestDate`, given by the Delta and Cassandra connectors), and `NetRouting.downHolders(kind, date)` names a down
  node only for a date inside one of its sources' ranges. A `range=3M` history of a CALYPSO trade or a counterparty asked while the
  MUREX holder is down is complete again, not `partial` with `DRS-5052 … drishti-c (dead): 54 days of the window may be held there`
  naming days before any lake's first day. DRISHTI_NET sections 6 and 7, HISTORY_QUERIES section 12, NET.md, API_GUIDE;
  HistoryPeersTest, NetPeerDownTest.
- **Fixed (SOAK-02): a history through a peer that just died answers `DRS-5052` naming it, never `502 DRS-1003 … ConnectException`.**
  A connection failure to a peer (refused, reset, no route) is that node being down for the read: the next holder is asked, and the dates
  no one answered are `DRS-5052` naming it (`… cannot be reached now: drishti-c (not answering: the connection failed)`), only for the
  dates it may hold; any other failure of a peer is `DRS-5052` too, as views say. A date one peer failed and another answered is no
  longer partial. `DRS-1014` stays for a time-out. The console never sets aside the server that answered for a problem about another
  node: `DRS-505x`, and a `DRS-1003` naming a peer from a 2.6.5 server, are its own answer (`peer_problem`), and `504 DRS-1014` never
  counts; the soak had 43 such set-asides of healthy servers. HISTORY_QUERIES sections 12 and 16, DRISHTI_NET 11.1, NET.md;
  HistoryPeersTest, NetPeerDownTest, test_cluster_failover.
- **Fixed (SOAK-03): a starting node joins Drishti\*net only once it is ready.** The node gossips itself alive on `ApplicationReadyEvent`
  (web server up, connectors started), no longer as soon as its net service is made, 12 to 19 s before its port opened, so peers no
  longer route to a closed port after a restart (`ConnectException`); a peer that refuses the connection passes the read to the next
  holder. The log says `this node joins once the server is ready`, then `joined Drishti*net` after `Tomcat started`. DRISHTI_NET
  sections 5 and 12, NET.md; NetJoinWhenReadyTest (a node held 4 s before its port opens: routed to while closed in 94 polls before,
  0 after).
- **Fixed (SOAK-06): expected refusals about another node are one short log line, not a stack trace each.** `DRS-5052`, `DRS-5053` and
  `DRS-1014` are logged once per change of what they say about a node (`drishti-c (suspect)`, then `(dead)`), then as a count once a
  minute (`request refused 6000 times in the last 60 s naming drishti-c (dead)`), never with a stack trace; unexpected errors keep
  theirs. While a node was down each server wrote about 11 MB of log a minute (68 MB in the soak's six-minute window). NET.md
  troubleshooting, HISTORY_QUERIES section 16; RefusalLogTest (10,000 refusals: 10,000 WARN lines with stack traces before, 2 short
  lines after).

A change now stamps the browser (`drishti_settings_at` cookie), and a worker re-reads the settings when its copy is older than the stamp; with four workers, 5 of 24 pages came back in the old theme before the fix and 0 after. `test_settings_workers.py`.   `MID` (it lay outside them on 59 of 60 days); a bond's `YIELD` moves against its `PRICE` by the modified duration, its `Z_SPREAD` with

Sixty days of `trade_endur` (five product types) were 300 commits, each replaying the whole log (98 s on Linux, far longer on Windows, where each log file is opened and scanned); now 60 commits with a short log, the same rows.
