- **Added:** **an outbound HTTP proxy for connectors, AI providers and MCP servers.** One shared mechanism (`com.ash.drishti.api.proxy`, next to the TLS module; the plugin SPI stays Spring-free): a `proxy:` block in a connector file's `settings:` (`url: http://host:port`, `username`, `password` as `${ENV}` only, `no-proxy` names, suffixes, addresses and CIDR blocks, `enabled`), or `proxy: none` to go direct; a **site default** `drishti.http.proxy.*` in `application.yaml` (`url`, `username`, `password`, `no-proxy`, `enabled`, `from-environment`; off by default, read at start) that every connector inherits unless it says otherwise; and, with `drishti.http.proxy.from-environment: true`, the standard `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` variables. `http://` targets are forwarded, `https://` targets are tunnelled with `CONNECT` and keep their `tls.*` end to end. **Covered:** REST, feeds, news, yfinance, S3 (the AWS SDK's proxy configuration; the Apache client is used when a proxy applies), Delta and Iceberg on S3 (SDK proxy configuration, Hadoop `fs.s3a.proxy.*`, the Iceberg REST catalog's `rest.client.proxy.*`), the Kafka **schema registry** (the brokers are not HTTP), the AI providers (OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic) and the Streamable HTTP MCP client, in the server (JDK HTTP client) and in the console (`httpx`, same rules, the `DRISHTI_HTTP_PROXY_*` environment variables as site default). **Not covered:** a proxy reached over TLS (refused with a message), NTLM, Kerberos or SOCKS proxies, PAC files, and the server's own non-connector clients (pack registry, report e-mail, OIDC, the collaboration bridge). Basic credentials never leak: the password is `***` in Admin, health, the API and logs; a literal `proxy.password` or a password inside the URL is refused on save and in AI and MCP files (`drishti.http.proxy.password` literal in a configuration file stops the server at start). **Admin → Connectors:** the connector page has a **Proxy** row (effective proxy, user, `password ***`, no-proxy, where it came from: connector, site default, environment or disabled), the editor has a **Proxy** section with the same line, and **Test connection** goes through the proxy and says so (with plain-words hints for 407, CONNECT refused and an unreachable proxy). Health ends `via proxy host:port (source)`, or says the host is on the no-proxy list. **Changed:** the console's AI and MCP `httpx` clients no longer pick up `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` by themselves (`trust_env` is off): set `DRISHTI_HTTP_PROXY_FROM_ENVIRONMENT=true` for that. The JDK refuses Basic credentials for a `CONNECT` tunnel by default; Drishti allows them (`jdk.http.auth.tunneling.disabledSchemes` unset) when a proxy with a login is configured. New settings: `drishti.http.proxy.*`. [PROXY.md](docs/guides/DATA_GUIDE.md#outbound-http-proxy-for-connectors-ai-providers-and-mcp-servers), [CONNECTOR_GUIDE.md](docs/guides/DATA_GUIDE.md#8-connectors), [CONNECTOR_FILES.md](docs/guides/DATA_GUIDE.md#9-connector-files-and-admin--connectors), each connector's "Outbound proxy" section, [CONFIGURATION.md](docs/admin/CONFIGURATION.md), [AI_PROVIDERS.md](docs/guides/AI_GUIDE.md#1-model-providers), [MCP_CLIENT.md](docs/guides/AI_GUIDE.md#2-the-mcp-client-other-servers-tools-behind-drishtis-policy), [TROUBLESHOOTING.md](docs/guides/OPERATIONS_GUIDE.md#21-troubleshooting). Tests (no real network; `FakeProxy` in `drishti-testkit` is a small forward proxy with HTTP forwarding, CONNECT and Basic `Proxy-Authorization` checks): `ProxySettingsTest`, `RestProxyTest`, `FeedProxyTest`, `NewsProxyTest`, `YFinanceProxyTest`, `S3ProxyTest`, `S3StorageProxyTest`, `HadoopLakeProxyTest`, `IcebergProxyTest`, `SchemaRegistryProxyTest`, `AiProxyTest`, `ConnectorProxyTest`, `SiteProxyEnvironmentPostProcessorTest`, `tests/test_ai_proxy.py`, `test_admin_detail_pages.py` and `test_admin_connectors_proxy_browser.py` (Chromium).
- **Added:** **Rūpaka phase 4: publishing and governance.** Every save of a dataset or report is a *saved state* (author, time, message), with a history list, a **side-by-side YAML diff** of any two states or versions and *restore as a new draft*; the published version stays pinned. **Review** extends publish-with-review: the reviewers (any `bi-steward`, and workspace members with `approve`) are told in the inbox, the review page shows the diff, Check, the impact and a **data preview** answered with the reviewer's own rows and masks, approve and reject keep their comments in the item's review record, four-eyes holds. **Certification** only by a steward, badges in the catalogue and search, and it **falls automatically** (with a warning and an inbox notice) when a dataset is published with a removed or renamed field, measure or hierarchy. **Lineage** (dataset: tables, pack kinds, connectors, reports; report: dataset and the names it uses) and **impact analysis** ("what breaks if I remove X"), used on review, publish and import: publishing a dataset change that breaks published reports is refused (`DRS-9040`) unless a `bi-admin` forces it. **Environments:** BI bundles (versions, sample flags, owners, audience, checksums) exported and imported with a dry run, workspace and owner mapping (`DRS-9041`, `9042`), at `/bi/environments`. Everything is audited. **API:** `/api/v1/bi/items/{id}/history|diff|review|lineage|impact`, `POST /bi/items/{id}/history/{n}/restore`, `publish` and `approve` with `force`, `GET /bi/bundle`, `POST /bi/bundle/import`. **Settings:** `drishti.bi.governance.*`. **Not built** (marked everywhere): BI content in a pack archive and rollback of an import, rename detection, impact on a changed meaning or type, lineage past the connector, threaded diff comments. [BI_GOVERNANCE.md](docs/guides/REPORTS_GUIDE.md#17-publishing-and-governance-versions-review-certification-lineage-impact-environments), [BI_GUIDE.md](docs/guides/REPORTS_GUIDE.md) section 17, [BI_TUTORIAL.md](docs/tutorials/08-reports-and-dashboards.md#part-a--your-first-bi-report) chapter 17, [API_GUIDE.md](docs/guides/API_REFERENCE.md), [CONFIGURATION.md](docs/admin/CONFIGURATION.md), [RUPAKA.md](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md#28-business-intelligence-on-the-table-layer) section 20.4. Tests: `BiGovernanceApiTest` (versions, review four-eyes, certification revoke, impact, bundle round trip, audit), `LineDiffTest`, console route tests and `test_bi_gov_browser.py` (Chromium, ports 18992/17992, phone).
- **Added:** **Connectors that are code, not a store.** Two new source plugins whose documents are computed when asked for. `news` (`plugins/drishti-plugin-news`) takes a name from the id (`NEWS-Federal_Reserve`, `@de-DE` for another edition, `~all` for no relevance filter), asks Google News RSS (no key), parses it with XXE off and a size limit, keeps only headlines whose title names the entity or an alias, applies publisher allow and deny lists, sorts newest first, removes duplicates, caches per name for a TTL in a bounded cache, retries with the shared backoff, and reports the steps that chose the headlines (`pipeline`) and a count by publisher. `yfinance` (`plugins/drishti-plugin-yfinance`) returns a quote (price, change, change %, currency, market state, day and 52-week ranges, volume, market cap when given) and price history for a ticker from Yahoo Finance's public chart endpoint (`range` and `interval` settings), with a bounded cache and the same failure handling. **Both are off as shipped**: the names and tickers leave the network, and Yahoo's endpoint is unofficial and restricted to samples and internal demonstrations. Two **sample packs** use them: `news-watch` (fifteen topics, each with headlines, a count by source, the selection steps and the unfiltered list) and `market-watch` (twenty listed companies, each with a quote, a closing-price chart and headlines; extends `news-watch`); their connector templates write `config/connectors/news.yaml` and `yfinance.yaml` disabled at first start, enable with `DRISHTI_NEWS_ENABLED` and `DRISHTI_YFINANCE_ENABLED` or live in Admin, Connectors (a new plugin jar needs a restart). A panel cell whose text is a web address is now a link that opens in a new tab. Pages that read these through `source:` need `drishti.graph.link-budget` above 40 ms or show *pending* on the first view. [NEWS.md](plugins/drishti-plugin-news/README.md), [YFINANCE.md](plugins/drishti-plugin-yfinance/README.md), [CONNECTOR_DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md](docs/guides/DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md#1011-connectors-that-compute-data-on-demand), [PACKS.md](docs/guides/BUILD_GUIDE.md#31-the-packs-that-ship-turning-them-on-who-sees-which). Tests never call Google or Yahoo: local fake servers serve canned RSS and JSON (an XXE attempt, bad JSON, oversized bodies, a slow response, 429 and 5xx then success, an unknown symbol); contract tests for both plugins; a Chromium test over the real server and console (ports 18993 and 17993) shows a company page and a topic page, and the same pages with the connectors off.

## 1.20.0 — BI you can use: datasets, reports and the designer; deep trades; real public data (2026-10-10)
- **Added:** **Rūpaka phase 3: reports, the designer and the Model view.** A *report* (YAML: pages on a 12-column grid, visuals bound to a dataset's fields and measures through wells, filters at report, page and visual level with basic, advanced and top-N, bookmarks,
  drill-through pages, a theme) is parsed, validated against its dataset (`DRS-9030` to `9035`) and written back the way a person writes it; publishing a report checks it. The viewer at `/bi/r/<id>[/<page>]` (`BI <report> <GO>` opens it) draws 21 visuals (bar, column, line, area,
  combo, scatter, pie, donut, waterfall, treemap, heatmap with ECharts; card, multi-row card, KPI, gauge; table, matrix with subtotals; list, dropdown and range slicers; text, image, button), each from one dataset query built on the server and run as the reader (row rules and masks),
  with cross-filter and highlight, drill-down along a hierarchy, drill-through to a page, show the rows, show as a table, open in the terminal, bookmarks, a business-date picker, the keyboard and a phone layout. The designer at `/bi/design/<draft>` has the Power BI panes (Fields with date
  parts and search, Visualizations with Build wells and Format, Filters, page tabs), a canvas to drag and resize on the grid and operate from the keyboard, a YAML tab that works both ways with suggestions, real data and the query time on every visual, Check (validation, accessibility,
  layout, performance), undo and redo; a field dropped on the canvas makes the best visual. The Model view at `/bi/m/<dataset>` draws tables as boxes and relationships as lines, relates by dragging a column onto another, accepts relationships proposed from the data, keeps positions under
  `layout:` and rewrites only the `relationships:` and `layout:` blocks. **API:** `/api/v1/bi/reports` (`GET /{id}`, `POST /{id}/query`, `/query`, `/validate`, `/format`, `GET /catalogue`, `/dataset`); `POST /datasets/validate` returns the parsed model. **Settings:** `drishti.bi.report.*`.
  Three sample reports in `config/bi/reports` (`trades-overview`, `counterparty-risk`, `cashflow-ladder`). **Not built** (marked everywhere): Perspective and live visuals, the map, funnel, histogram, box, bubble, Python and entity visuals (`DRS-9033`), the relative-date slicer, true totals
  for measures that do not add up, a report over several datasets, per-device layouts, a Check that runs expected values. [REPORTS.md](docs/guides/REPORTS_GUIDE.md#9-the-report-file-pages-visuals-filters-and-slicers), [BI_GUIDE.md](docs/guides/REPORTS_GUIDE.md) sections 14 to 16, [BI_TUTORIAL.md](docs/tutorials/08-reports-and-dashboards.md#part-a--your-first-bi-report) chapters 10 to 15,

- **Added:** **control values and column filters travel with a sent share.** A share now keeps the sender's *view state*: the `ctl.*` control values and the `f.<panel>.<column>` column filters, as query text in a new nullable `view_state` column on `drishti_share` (added by the schema script and, on SQLite, by `IdentityDatabase`; the file store reads old rows as having none; a share's hash is unchanged without one). The share dialog sends it (`view` in `POST /shares`, at most `drishti.collab.share.max-view-state`, default 4000, else `DRS-5001`), `GET /shares/{id}` returns it, the console opens the recipient on the same controls and filters, and the share's watermarked picture (and so the email's attachment) is built with the control values and shows only the rows the column filters leave (a server port of the console's filter grammar, applied after the recipients' masks; a masked cell never matches). There is no scheduled subscription yet, so none stores them. Arrow keys, `PageUp` / `PageDown`, `Home` / `End`, drag or press on the track; `role="slider"` with `aria-valuemin` / `-max` / `-now` / `-valuetext`; 44 px handles on touch; in the workbench Controls tab (Min, Max, Step, *Two handles*) and `RachanaSchema`. - **Added:** **Rūpaka phase 2: datasets and the query engine.** A *dataset* (YAML: tables from pack kinds by connector logical name across packs, columns with paths and types, calculated columns, relationships, measures in Rachana-EL extended with aggregation
  (`sum avg min max count distinct ratio percentile`, conditions, `[Measure]` references), hierarchies, row rules per role, masked columns, rollups) is parsed, validated (`DRS-9010` to `9013`) and queried: `POST /api/v1/bi/datasets/{id}/query` compiles a visual query to one **parameterised** SQL
  statement (names checked and quoted, every value bound, joins many-to-one from the measures' table, row rules the reader cannot remove, masks applied before aggregation) and runs it on an embedded DuckDB behind an `AnalyticEngine` interface. **Layers:** a typed Parquet **columns layer** per table per
  business date in the BI store (`drishti.bi.query.store-dir`), rebuilt for exactly the date a data-load signal names, and **rollups** with aggregate-aware routing (rollup, else columns, else the source); `direct` tables pushed into a SQL store; a minimal `live` snapshot. Answers as masked **Arrow IPC** or JSON, a
  result cache keyed by dataset version, query, the reader's rules and masks and the data generation, limits for time, rows, bytes and concurrency (`DRS-9020` to `9027`). **Connector SPI:** optional `scan(ScanRequest)` (column batches) and `sqlTarget()`; Delta, DuckDB, PostgreSQL (table mode) and file scan
  over their promoted columns, DuckDB and PostgreSQL expose a SQL target (`ColumnScans`). **Model from packs:** kinds become tables, the packs' link graph becomes relationships across packs, relationships are proposed by value matching with the match rate (`/bi/model/start|infer`). **Pages:** Datasets list, Start from packs,

The phase 0 query endpoint runs on the engine; the console serves static files
