## 1.19.0 — Connectors as files, TLS everywhere, query by form, Elements, no restarts, BI begins (2026-10-10)
- **Added:** the `BI` command keyword, working like `FORM`: `BI <GO>` the BI home, `BI WORKSPACE`, `BI CATALOGUE`, `BI <report-or-board>` by id or title (several matches open the catalogue searched), type-ahead after `BI ` offering the items the user may open; `RUPAKA` stays as an alias. `BI` is a reserved word beside `RUPAKA` and `FORM`: the pack loader and `drishti pack check` refuse a pack mnemonic named `BI` (no shipped pack uses it). Docs: BI_GUIDE, USER_GUIDE, PACK_DEVELOPER_GUIDE, RUPAKA.md section 4.
- **Changed:** query by form: an enum field with more than 6 values (asset class, product type, book, desk, currency) is one **multi-select dropdown** the size of a select
  instead of a wall of tick boxes: a summary ("All", "REPO", "3 selected: ABS, REPO, +1"), a search box, *Select all* / *Clear*, keyboard, 44 px rows on touch; up to 6 values stay
  a checkbox row; the address encoding is unchanged. One shared component, `static/js/multiselect.js` ([DEVELOPER_GUIDE 5.8a](docs/guides/DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md)), also draws the
  `multi-select` controls of Sutras and works inside `<drishti-view>`. Tests: `test_form_browser.py`.
- **Added:** **controls on a screen** (Rūpaka phase 0a, [RUPAKA.md 8.1](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md#289-reports-boards-and-controls)
  "as built"). A Sutra declares `controls:` (dropdown, multi-select, cascading, toggle, segmented, date, date-range, number-range, top-n, search; options from a list,
  an expression over the record such as `$.legs[*].id`, or an entity kind; `default`, `remember`, `required`, `placement` strip / header / side) and panels read the
  values as `ctl.<id>` in `rows`, `where`, `limit` and `title`. Rachana-EL gained `ctl.<id>`, the projection `[*]` and the functions `within` and `oneOf`; panels gained
  `where`, a `limit` that reads a control, and `on-select: { by, field, filter }` (a click or Enter on a row or bar sets a control: cross-filtering); problem codes
  `DRS-2034` to `DRS-2039`. The server evaluates with the request's `ctl.*` values (view and stream endpoints), builds only `&panels=a,b` when asked, reads options from the
  record as the caller may see it (a masked value is never listed and never matches) and builds live frames with the values the stream was opened with. Console: one script,
  `controls.js`, draws every kind (keyboard, 44 px on touch, both themes), asks `GET /v/{kind}/{id}/panels` for only the panels that read the control (whole view 17.0 ms and
  12.8 KB, one panel 10.1 ms and 5.5 KB on a warm local server), keeps the values in the address (`?ctl.legs=2&ctl.when=2026-10-01..2026-12-31`) and the Share link, moves the live
  subscription, and works inside `<drishti-view>` (a `controls` attribute and property, a composed `drishti:controls` event, `GET /embed/v1/views/{kind}/{id}/panels`; Chromium,
  Firefox, WebKit). The workbench has a **Controls** tab (cards, YAML two ways, one `setControls` operation, the real controls over the previewed sample). Shipped on
  `irs-fixfloat` (cashflows by leg and date range) and `netting-set` (member trades by asset class, product and how many, the asset-class bars selecting). `remember: user` is
  per browser (the server has no per-user view-preference store); not built: a `slider` kind, options from a dataset column, a view-level `title:` reading a control, the Pivot tab
  and CSV following the controls, control values stored with a *sent* share, picture or subscription (a copied link carries them). Docs:
  [RACHANA_REFERENCE](docs/guides/RACHANA_REFERENCE.md#controls), [USER_GUIDE](docs/guides/USER_GUIDE.md#controls-on-a-screen-choose-what-a-panel-shows),
  [SCREEN_DESIGNER](docs/guides/RACHANA_REFERENCE.md#the-controls-tab), [ELEMENTS](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md#30-the-client-renderer-and-drishti-elements). Tests: `ControlsTest`, `ControlsApiTest`, `ControlsLiveTest`,
  `test_controls_routes.py`, `test_controls_browser.py`, `test_workbench_controls_browser.py`, `test_embed_controls_browser.py`.
- **Added:** **Rūpaka phase 1: the BI shell and catalogue** ([BI guide](docs/guides/REPORTS_GUIDE.md)). A **BI** top-bar menu for people with the new `bi` power and the reserved `RUPAKA` keyword (`RUPAKA <GO>`, `RUPAKA WORKSPACE`, `RUPAKA CATALOGUE`, `RUPAKA <report>`; any case; type-ahead); packs and `pack check` refuse a mnemonic named `RUPAKA` or `FORM`. A `/bi` page with its own layout (rail, Home, Catalogue, Workspaces, items; keys `/`, `g h`, `g c`, `g w`, `?`; phone and every theme). Personal and shared workspaces (viewer, contributor, member, admin), typed items (dataset, report, board, notebook) with a stored, versioned, **not executed** YAML body, draft, proposed, published with restore, review reusing the `approve` power and four-eyes, promoted and certified endorsement, audiences of roles, users and packs enforced on the server, favourites, recents and views. Storage in the identity database; shipped read-only files in `drishti.bi.dir` (`config/bi`), **watched live with no restart** (`drishti.bi.watch`: auto, poll, off; a bad file keeps its last good version and shows in Admin, BI settings and on Health). Powers `bi`, `bi-author`, `bi-steward`, `bi-admin` on roles (`roles.<role>.bi`, `bi` on the role API); Admin, BI settings (powers per role, workspace creation policy); API `/api/v1/bi/**` with token scopes `bi:write`, `bi:approve`, `bi:admin`; every change audited; DRS-9001 to DRS-9006; `drishti.py bi workspace|catalogue list|get|publish`. Datasets, reports and the designer are not built yet (phases 2 and 3); the Phase 0 proof of concept stays for administrators under the BI menu (`bi.poc_enabled`). Settings: `drishti.bi.*`, console `bi.enabled` (`DRISHTI_BI_ENABLED`).
- **Added:** **retry with backoff, and nothing needs a restart.** Anything that failed to load or lost its connection is tried again by itself, so it works as soon as the cause is fixed. One mechanism (`RetryPolicy`, `RetryTracker`, `RetryBoard` in `drishti-common`; `core/retry.py` in the console): exponential backoff with jitter (`drishti.retry.*`: `initial` 5s, `factor` 2, `max` 5m, `jitter` 0.2, `permanent-after` 3, `enabled`, with per-area overrides `drishti.retry.packs|connectors|ai|mcp.*`; console `retry.*`). **Packs** refused (a clash, a missing `extends`, a bad file) are re-evaluated when the packs folder, the connector files, the sample-pack switch or the overlay change, and on the schedule: a pack loads after its conflict is removed with no change in its own folder. **Connectors** that fail to start, or whose plugin reports `DOWN`, are retried (started afresh after a few looks) and serve again as soon as the source is up. **AI providers** that cannot be built and **MCP servers** that cannot be set up or lost their connection are rebuilt / reconnected; the console's own AI and MCP layer now also reloads its files without a restart (`ai.poll_seconds`) and retries the same way. Errors retrying cannot fix are classed permanent after `permanent-after` repeats and slowed to `max`. State is visible: Admin -> Packs, Connectors, AI and Health show "failed - next retry in Ns (attempt k)" and the last error; `GET /api/v1/admin/retry`. **Retry now** (`POST /api/v1/admin/retry/{packs|connectors|ai|mcp|all}`, admin, audited, token scope `packs:admin`). Failures are logged and audited on attempts 1, 2, 4, 8, ... and every recovery always (`pack|connector|ai|mcp-retry-failed`, `-recovered`, `-retry-now`). See [OPERATIONS.md](docs/guides/OPERATIONS_GUIDE.md#138-retries-what-failed-is-tried-again-by-itself), [CONFIGURATION.md](docs/admin/CONFIGURATION.md#retry-settings).
- **Changed:** **no setting a pack contributes needs a restart any more.** Roles, the link graph (reference patterns, fields, badges, impact), search columns and pivots, formats, semantic hints, About pages and guides, kind routes and the demo connector's sample folders are now swapped in live by the pack reloader (`LiveSettings`: each is built from the new packs first, a refusal changes nothing, then all are swapped in one reload at a time and the cached view layouts are dropped); `restartFor` in the answer is always empty. The console's help library is rebuilt when a pack's version or `help.yaml` changes. OPERATIONS.md has a table of every artifact type, how a change is noticed and what a bad edit does ("What changes live (no restart)"). The AI registry no longer logs a line at every look at the folder.
- **Changed:** the holiday calendars (CAL-USNY, GBLO, EUTA, JPTO) name every holiday (New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Good Friday, Thanksgiving Day, ... and "(observed)" for a weekend substitute) instead of "Public holiday". Each holiday line is `{date, name, weekday, year, observed}` for 2026 and 2027; the `calendar` Sutra shows Holidays 2026 and 2027, the next holiday and its date, and a table of Date, Day, Holiday and Observed with every line on one page. `BusinessCalendar` (Java) has `holidayNames(year)`; a test pins the Java and Python calendars to the same dates (Python Boxing Day now follows the Java substitute rule).
- **Added:** **query by form** (`FORM <pack> <GO>`; [User guide](docs/guides/USER_GUIDE.md#search-with-a-form-form-pack)). A page of typed inputs for a kind (text with equals/contains/starts with/regex and a case toggle; number and amount with `=`, between, `>`, `<` and `10m`/`1bn`; date on/between/before/after or a business-day range such as `last 5 business days`; enum multi-select of the values in the data; one-or-many ids pasted as a list; yes/no) that the server compiles to the existing search grammar and runs as any search (masks, kinds per role, packs per user and sample visibility apply). The generated command is shown and copyable, the results are the console table with column filters, the key cell opens the view and Alt+Left returns to the form with the criteria (they are in the URL), and the search can be saved by name (`savedSearches` setting), watched as a monitor, scheduled as a report or shared as a link. `FORM` is a reserved command word with type-ahead for the packs and kinds you may open. API: `GET /api/v1/forms/{pack}`, `POST /api/v1/forms/{pack}/{kind}/compile`.
- **Added:** **hide the form** on `FORM <pack>`: a Hide form / Show form button (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`) and Alt+F fold the form to one line of its criteria (click it to reopen); after Search the form folds when results arrive (`form.collapse_on_submit` in `config/application.yaml`, default true), criteria kept; the state is in the address (`&form=hidden|shown`) and a hand-opened form stays open for the tab. [User guide](docs/guides/USER_GUIDE.md#give-the-results-the-room-hide-the-form).
- **Added:** the pack.yaml `form:` section ([Pack developer guide](docs/guides/BUILD_GUIDE.md#46-form-the-search-form-of-a-kind)): per kind, fields with `path`, `label`, `type` (text, number, amount, date, enum, id, bool), `operators`, `default`, `order`, `group`, `help`, `required`, `hidden`, `values`. A kind with none gets a form inferred from its search columns, Sutra match and strip fields and sample values, labelled from `about.yaml`. Every shipped pack declares forms (the generators write them, `--check` clean; `finance` and `logistics` by hand), `pack check` validates them (`DRS-2060` in the workbench), and `pack make` and New pack write one from samples and schemas.
- **Added:** **regular expressions in search, on a linear-time engine** (`SafeRegex`, written in-tree because the build is offline; RE2/J would be a drop-in). `matches(field, 'pattern')`, `matchesCase(field, 'pattern')` and `field matches 'pattern'` in any search and in Rachana-EL; back-references, look-around, atomic groups, possessive quantifiers and `\b` are refused with `DRS-4010`, as are patterns over 200 characters or 4,000 expanded steps; a value is cut to 8,192 characters and a match over 50 ms is `DRS-4011` (`drishti.search.regex.*`). A backslash in a quoted search string is now kept.
- **Added:** the workbench **Form tab** ([Screen designer](docs/guides/RACHANA_REFERENCE.md#the-form-tab)): the field palette of the samples, a card for each form field (type, operators, label, default, group, help, required, hidden), reordering by drag and by Alt+Up/Down, the YAML in both directions, a live preview of the form, the form kept as a step of the design's log (undo, redo, revisions), and a form change that travels with the proposal (reviewers see before and after) and is in force once approved.
- **Added:** **pluggable LLM providers and an MCP client** ([AI_PROVIDERS.md](docs/guides/AI_GUIDE.md#1-model-providers), [MCP_CLIENT.md](docs/guides/AI_GUIDE.md#2-the-mcp-client-other-servers-tools-behind-drishtis-policy)), off by default (`drishti.ai.enabled`, `drishti.mcp.enabled`). New module `drishti-ai` (no controllers; depends only on `drishti-api` and `drishti-common`; ArchUnit rule): Drishti's own interfaces `LlmProvider`, `LlmModel`, `EmbeddingModel`, `LlmRegistry`, `LlmPolicy` / `LlmGateway`, `ProviderFactory` (ServiceLoader or Spring bean: a new provider is one class and one registration). Providers are files, one YAML per provider in `config/ai/<name>.yaml` (`drishti.ai.dir`, `DRISHTI_AI_DIR`; type, `base-url`, `api-key: ${ENV}` only (a literal key is refused), models with logical names, timeouts, `tls.*`; live reload like connectors). Implementations: `openai` through Spring AI 1.0.3 (`spring-ai-starter-model-openai`, BOM in dependencyManagement, Java 17+ bytecode so the enforcer rule `maxJdkVersion 21` passes; any OpenAI-compatible endpoint incl. Azure, vLLM, Ollama `/v1`), `anthropic` (the existing Ask provider ported; Spring AI's Anthropic starter is not used, to keep one HTTP stack and the shared TLS), and `mock` (deterministic, no network: fixed, echo, rules, tool calls, latency, errors, usage). Policy: masking with `drishti.security.redact` and extra patterns, audit row per call (action `ai`, never the text), per-user/per-feature rate limits, daily cost limit, features per role. MCP client: `McpClient`, `McpRegistry`, `McpGateway` (roles/features per server and tool, masked arguments and results, audit), Streamable HTTP and mock transports, one YAML per server in `config/mcp/<name>.yaml` (`drishti.mcp.dir`, headers as `${ENV}`, `allowed-tools`); tested live against the SAJHA MCP server (`config/mcp/sajha.yaml.example`). REST: `GET /api/v1/admin/ai`, `GET /api/v1/admin/mcp/{server}/tools`, `POST /api/v1/admin/ai/test` (scope `ai:admin`, audited), `GET /api/v1/ai/models`, `POST /api/v1/ai/chat`, `POST /api/v1/ai/mcp/{server}/tools/{tool}` (scope `ai:use`); DRS-4015..4014. Console: `core/ai/` mirrors it with `typing.Protocol`s (providers `openai`, `anthropic`, `server` (recommended: keys stay on the server), `mock`; MCP `streamable-http`, `server`, `mock`), Admin -> AI (read-only), `POST /api/ai/chat`. **Ask now runs on the AI layer**; its `endpoint`/`api`/`api-key` settings still work as provider `ask` with a deprecation warning.
- **Changed:** **the product owner's layout.** The packs moved from `./packs` to `./config/packs` (`drishti.packs.dir`, `DRISHTI_PACKS_DIR`; the console's default is `../config/packs`), beside `config/connectors/` and the new `config/bi/` (`drishti.bi.dir`, `DRISHTI_BI_DIR`: `datasets/`, `reports/`, `python/` and a README; Rupaka content lives only there, never inside a pack). A new umbrella `drishti.data.dir` (`DRISHTI_DATA_DIR`, default `./data`) is the base of every runtime path (identity database, caches, loads, collab, designs, reports, governance, the pack overlay, installed packs, settings and samples-mode, the lake roots the packs suggest, and the plugins' and command-line tools' defaults); each path's own setting still overrides. For one release a missing packs folder falls back to `./packs` (the console to `../packs`) with a warning. Docs, tests, tools, Dockerfiles and CI follow ([CONFIGURATION.md](docs/admin/CONFIGURATION.md), "The data folder and the config folder").
- **Changed:** **generated packs name their connectors.** `tools/schemapack.py`, Build → New pack (`core/schemakit`) and `pack new --lake` write `connectors: [<pack>-store]`, the `routes`, and the connection settings as `connector-templates`, as [CONNECTOR_FILES.md](docs/guides/DATA_GUIDE.md#9-connector-files-and-admin--connectors) describes, instead of an inline definition; `pack bundle`, `pack diff`, `data ingest` and the lake tools read both forms.
- **Added:** **live pack reload** (no restart). The packs folder is watched (`drishti.packs.watch`: auto | poll | off, with `poll` and `reload-debounce`): a new pack folder is checked with the loaded packs and loaded (kinds, mnemonics, Sutras, connector templates become connector files by the usual rule); an edited `pack.yaml`, `about.yaml`, Sutra or sample is re-checked and swapped in; a deleted pack is unloaded, the connectors only it used stop and open views of its kinds say "pack removed". A bad edit keeps the last good version and the problem shows in Admin -> Packs and Health; a pack another loaded pack extends is never unloaded; bursts are debounced, one reload runs at a time, every change is audited. Admin -> Packs Load and Unload, archive deploy, registry install and rollback now use this path instead of restarting the server (`restarting` is always `false`; settings bound at start, such as roles, graph, search columns, formats and About pages, are reported in `restartFor`). See [PACKS.md](docs/guides/BUILD_GUIDE.md#292-loading-a-pack-while-the-server-runs).
- **Added:** **sample packs.** `sample: true` in `pack.yaml` (set on genomics, politics-society, logistics and economics) and `drishti.packs.samples` = `visible` (default) | `developers` (only authors and administrators see them; others get them filtered on the server as a pack switched off) | `hidden` (not loaded, their connectors do not start). Admin -> Packs shows a Sample badge and "Hide samples from business users", a saved setting that overrides the property, applied at once and audited (`pack-samples`); `GET`/`PUT /api/v1/admin/packs/samples`. See [PACKS.md](docs/guides/BUILD_GUIDE.md#315-sample-packs).
- **Fixed:** `POST /api/v1/admin/packs/deploy/{id}/connectors` is declared in the `packs:admin` token scope; the connector-files guide states that a connector's `kinds:` adds the kinds it serves to the routed ones, and that a shared connector folder lets a file left by another run merge into a connector defined in the server configuration; `RecentStoreApiTest` uses its own folder.
- **Added:** **Excel-style column filters on every table, matrix and pivot** (RUPAKA.md 8.1, delivery 1; no grammar change). A funnel in each column heading (hover or focus on a desktop, always shown and 44 px on touch) opens a menu: sort (A→Z, smallest→largest, oldest→newest), a search box over the column's distinct values with counts, *(Select all)* and *(Blanks)*, and conditions by the detected type: numbers (equals, does not equal, greater, less, between, top / bottom N, above / below average), dates (today, yesterday, this / last week and month, last 7 / 30 days, between, before, after) and text (equals, does not equal, contains, does not contain, begins / ends with); OK, Cancel, Clear. Filters combine across columns and with the *Filter rows* box; the funnel fills and its tooltip says what it does; the pager reads `12 of 840 rows (filtered)`, a *Clear filters* button and `Alt+Shift+X` clear them, and the counts are announced politely. They survive live patches (rows leave or enter), work with paging and zoom fit, and are part of the address (`?f.<panel>.<column>=in:a,b`, `gt:1m`, `bt:1~9`, `top:10`, `today` ...) so reload, share and snapshot reproduce them; remembering per user is off. Masked values are one *(masked)* entry and never match a condition; in a matrix a parent stays, open, when a row below it matches. Keyboard: Enter or Space opens the menu, arrows, Space and type-ahead in the list, Esc closes only the menu. Also inside `<drishti-view>` (`colfilter` joins the enhancers; the element sheet gains `colfilter.css`). New `static/js/colfilter.js`, `static/css/colfilter.css`; every table event `drishti:column-filter` is the hook for a server-paged table (none exists yet). USER_GUIDE "Filter a table like Excel" with pictures (`tools/docs/screenshots.py --guide colfilter`); tests `test_colfilter_browser.py` (Chromium, phone) and an element test in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
- **Changed:** a table's footer with a filter on reads `n of N rows (filtered)` (it read `a–b of n (filtered from N)`); sorting always puts blank cells last, ascending or descending; in a matrix a parent stays open when any row below it matches the filter box (it checked only its first child).
- **Added:** **TLS for the rest of the connectors** with the same shared `tls.*` settings ([TLS.md](docs/guides/DATA_GUIDE.md#connector-matrix)). Redis (`rediss://`, a private CA, mutual TLS; the Lettuce `verifyPeer` URI option still works, deprecated, with a warning), REST and the feeds' mirrors (HTTPS with a private CA or mutual TLS, the new `TlsHttp` helper in the plugin API), S3 (a private CA or client certificate for MinIO, Ceph or a gateway), MongoDB (TLS and `auth-mechanism: x509` certificate log-in), PostgreSQL through the JDBC connector (the module's context handed to the driver, `sslmode=verify-full`, certificate log-in with `pg_hba` `cert`; the other drivers keep their own URL options, documented), Aerospike (TLS policy, `tls-name`, `auth-mode: pki`), Delta (the native engine's S3 client) and Iceberg (S3FileIO for REST catalogs). Each checks at start (a wrong file or password, or `tls.*` beside an address that is not TLS, stops the connector naming the setting and the file), adds a certificate's expiry to the health text, and has a Security section with complete connector files, verification commands and real error messages. Integration tests run against real servers in Docker (Redis 8, MongoDB 7 with x.509, PostgreSQL 18) and in-process HTTPS servers; Aerospike's live check is a documented manual procedure (its TLS is Enterprise Edition). Not covered because the libraries have no hook: a private CA on Hadoop's S3A (`engine: hadoop`, `catalog: hadoop`) and the Iceberg REST catalog's own connection; both are refused or warned about at start and point to the JVM truststore.
- **Changed:** **the connector form's `tls.*` section is generated from the code that reads the settings** (`TlsSettings.settingSpecs`), with the real names, types, secret flags and help text (`tls.ca-file`, `tls.truststore`, `tls.cert-file`, ... instead of the earlier guessed `tls.truststore.path`); a test fails if the two ever differ. The Kafka settings (`flavour`, `security.protocol`, `sasl.*`, `schema-registry.*`, `schema-registry.tls.*`) are in the catalogue, so Admin -> Connectors validates and offers them. A `-file` twin (`tls.keystore-password-file`) holds a path and is no longer taken for a secret; a `${KEY}:${SECRET}` pair of references is accepted as a secret value. New secure examples in `config/connectors.examples/other/` (Kafka mutual TLS with PEM, Confluent Cloud, RabbitMQ `amqps://` with certificate log-in, ActiveMQ `ssl://`, PostgreSQL, Redis, MongoDB x.509, REST mutual TLS, S3, Delta, Iceberg, Aerospike).
- **Fixed:** **an embedded `<drishti-view>` no longer repaints when the stream's first look is a generation ahead of the page.** The element disposed and re-booted every enhancer one to three times within 100 ms of going live (resetting scroll, selection and focus, and flickering for the host). It now fetches the view again and applies only the differences as patches in place (also after a reconnect); a repaint (new `drishti:paint` event) happens only for a real change. Test: ten seconds of ticks, one paint per element, zoom/focus/scroll kept, three browsers.
- **Added:** **schema-driven Sutra generation** ([docs/guides/SCHEMA_TO_PACK.md](docs/guides/DATA_GUIDE.md#5-schema-to-pack-generate-a-pack-from-json-schema)). One or many JSON Schema files (draft 2020-12 and 07; `$ref`/`$defs`/`definitions`, `allOf`, `oneOf`/`anyOf` with or without a `discriminator`, nested objects, arrays of objects, enums, formats, `examples`, `required`, titles and descriptions, JSON or YAML) become a pack: the **kind** (from `x-drishti-kind`, a short title, the `$id` or the file name), the **key** (`x-drishti-role: key`, else the required id-like field, asking when it is ambiguous), **links** between the kinds (`x-drishti-link`, `*Id` fields that name another kind of the batch, or values that are another kind's keys), **labels and panel titles** from `title`, **formats** from `type`/`format`/`x-drishti-format` and a **strip** of the most important numbers (required and described first), a **Sutra per `oneOf` variant** (or per value of a chosen match column, with `match.where`), **About-this-page text** from the descriptions (`config/about.yaml`), enum fields as status fields and as **dropdown control suggestions** (a hook, ready for the controls feature), and **tests** from the schema's own `examples` or synthetic samples generated from it (named `sample-synthetic-N.json`, marked synthetic everywhere). Real JSON Lines documents win over synthetic ones; the schemas add labels, descriptions and links. The rules and every `x-drishti-*` annotation are in the new guide; the code is `drishti-console/core/schemakit/` (pure Python, shared by the console and the command line).
- **Added:** `drishti.py sutra design --schema FILE...` (the Sutras the schemas describe, printed or written under `--out` with their tests) and `drishti.py pack make --schema FILE|DIR... [DATA_FOLDER]` (alone or with a folder of JSON Lines; the same output folder, bundle, `README.txt` and `MANIFEST.json` as before, with many kinds). New flags: `--match none`, `--mnemonic`, `--strip`, `--count`, `--code`, `--description`, `--connector`, `--yes`. `pack make` without `--schema` is unchanged.
- **Added:** **Build → New pack** (`/build/pack/new`, a Build menu entry; the author power builds and downloads, an administrator deploys): five steps. 1 **Sources**: choose or drop many schema files and/or a folder of JSON / JSON Lines; the browser streams and samples them (reservoir, deterministic; file count, rows, size and per-file progress shown, caps configurable) and sends only the sample and the counts. 2 **Kinds**: one card per kind with the detected key, links (and a graph of the kinds), match column (with the number of Sutras it creates), business date and mnemonic, all editable; a kind another pack already defines is flagged. 3 **Pack**: name, code, title, version, connector names and templates per kind (a pack refers to its sources by logical name only), mnemonic conflicts. 4 **Preview**: every Sutra drafted by the server as a background job (progress, cancel) and rendered on its samples (real, example or synthetic, labelled), with its YAML, the About text it carries, its samples and a panel-by-sample check; any Sutra opens in the workbench. 5 **Output**: the bundle in the format of `pack bundle` (checksum, manifest), or **Deploy**: handed to Admin → Packs → Deploy archive, whose checks and preview come first and whose rollback is unchanged. The wizard's state is kept as a draft (a design named `New pack: <name>`) and resumed. New settings `builder.pack_*` and `builder.tools_dir`.
- **Added:** `GET /api/v1/studio/settings` also answers `author` (the caller's role has the author power, whether or not saving is on). Admin → Packs accepts `?bundle=<job>` to take a bundle from New pack.
- **Added:** **TLS for connectors, one set of settings, and Kafka with every security option.** A shared module in the plugin API (`com.ash.drishti.api.tls`: `TlsSettings`, `TlsContexts`, `TlsMaterial`, `Secrets`; pure JDK) reads `tls.*` settings (`enabled`, `ca-file`, `truststore`, `trust-jvm-default`, `cert-file`, `key-file`, `keystore`, `key-alias`, `protocols`, `cipher-suites`, `verify-hostname`, `insecure-trust-all`) and builds the `SSLContext`, key and trust managers and `SSLParameters`: trust from a PEM bundle, a PKCS12 or JKS truststore, the JVM default, or any merge; a client identity (mutual TLS) from PEM files (PKCS#8, PKCS#1 RSA, SEC1 EC, encrypted PKCS#8) or a keystore with an alias; passwords as `${ENV}` placeholders or `-file` paths; hostname verification on, `verify-hostname: false` warns at every start; `insecure-trust-all` refused unless `DRISHTI_ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS=true`. A wrong file, password or key/certificate pair stops the connector at start naming the setting, the file and the reason; a certificate within 30 days of expiry (or expired) is warned about and adds a sentence to the source's health text (Admin → Health). Reference: [docs/connectors/TLS.md](docs/guides/DATA_GUIDE.md#10-tls-and-the-outbound-proxy) (every setting, openssl/keytool conversions, rotation, troubleshooting); for plugin authors: [CONNECTOR_DEVELOPER_GUIDE](docs/guides/DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md#108-tls-for-a-connector-the-shared-module). The other connectors will take the module on in a later change; `drishti-testkit` gains `TestPki` (certificates generated at test time).
- **Added:** **Kafka: `security.protocol` (PLAINTEXT, SSL, SASL_PLAINTEXT, SASL_SSL), `tls.*`, `sasl.*` (PLAIN, SCRAM-SHA-256/512, OAUTHBEARER client credentials, GSSAPI/Kerberos), `flavour: confluent` and Schema Registry.** First-class settings translate to Kafka client properties (PEM becomes `ssl.keystore.type=PEM` / `ssl.truststore.type=PEM`; stores are handed over as they are); `client.<property>` is still passed through and wins. The Confluent preset sets `SASL_SSL`, `PLAIN` with `api-key` / `api-secret`, `client.dns.lookup=use_all_dns_ips` and tuned timeouts. With `schema-registry.url` (basic or bearer auth, TLS through `schema-registry.tls.*`) the connector strips the Confluent wire format (zero byte and 4-byte schema id) and reads JSON Schema payloads as they are and Avro payloads decoded with the writer schema fetched by id (Apache Avro 1.12, Apache-2.0, added to the Kafka plugin) as JSON; Protobuf is not supported yet; an unreadable message is skipped and logged, never read as a delete. Tested against Apache Kafka 3.9 in Docker (mutual TLS in PEM and PKCS12/JKS forms, SASL_SSL SCRAM-SHA-512, refusals) plus unit tests of every property combination and of the wire format with recorded bytes. [KAFKA_CONNECTOR.md › Security: TLS, SASL and Confluent](plugins/drishti-plugin-kafka/README.md#security-tls-sasl-and-confluent).
- **Added:** **ActiveMQ over `ssl://` and RabbitMQ over `amqps://` with the shared `tls.*` settings**, no JVM-wide `-Djavax.net.ssl.*` properties needed: a private CA, truststores, a client certificate (PEM or keystore), hostname verification. RabbitMQ also takes `auth-mechanism: external` to log in with the client certificate (SASL EXTERNAL). The whole message-source contract runs over TLS in the tests against ActiveMQ Classic 6.1.7 and RabbitMQ 4.1 in Docker, with a client certificate required. [ACTIVEMQ_CONNECTOR.md › Security](plugins/drishti-plugin-activemq/README.md#security), [RABBITMQ_CONNECTOR.md › Security](plugins/drishti-plugin-rabbitmq/README.md#security).
- **Added:** **connector files** ([CONNECTOR_FILES.md](docs/guides/DATA_GUIDE.md#9-connector-files-and-admin--connectors)). A connector is now a site resource: one YAML file per connector in `config/connectors/<name>.yaml`, the file name being the connector's name (`plugin`, `enabled`, `kinds`, `description`, `settings`; `${VAR:default}` and `file:` references, secrets never written in clear). Settings `drishti.sources.connectors-dir` (`DRISHTI_CONNECTORS_DIR`), `connectors-watch` (`auto`, `poll`, `off`), `connectors-poll` (5s), `connectors-drain` (3s) and `connectors-generate` (true). Every earlier text of a file is kept in `.history/`.
- **Added:** **live reload.** The folder is watched (file events with a polling safety net); only the connector whose file changed is started, restarted or stopped, and reads in flight get `connectors-drain` to finish. A bad file keeps the last good configuration running and appears in Admin -> Health (`connectors` block: `badFiles`, `watch`, `deprecated`) and in the UI.
- **Changed:** **packs name connectors and suggest templates.** A pack lists the connectors it reads through and routes its kinds to them; its `connectors:` mapping is read as TEMPLATES. At the first start the server writes a file from a template when none exists (never overwrites); a file replaces a template wholesale. A route to a connector with no file loads the pack and says so (`DRS-1011` on a read; pack rows in Health show `connectorsNotConfigured`; the deploy preview lists missing connectors).
- **Added:** **Admin -> Connectors** (`/admin/connectors`): list, a form generated from the plugin's settings, a YAML tab, test connection, save with versions, enable and disable, reset to the pack's template, delete, history with diff and restore. Scope `packs:admin` also covers writes to `/api/v1/admin/connectors/**`; audit actions `connector-saved`, `-deleted`, `-reset`, `-enabled`, `-disabled`, `-restored`, `-tested`, `-generated`, `-migrated`.
- **Added:** **connector API and CLI.** `/api/v1/admin/connectors` (list, plugins, get, put with ETag, delete, reset, enable, test, history, restore) and `drishti.py connector list|get|apply|delete|test|plugins|enable|disable|reset|history`.
- **Changed:** the Admin -> Packs **Data source** panel is a read-only view of the pack's connectors, with links to Admin -> Connectors; the `PUT`, `DELETE` and `test` calls of `/admin/packs/{name}/datasource` and `drishti.py server packs datasource set|test|reset` are gone.
- **Changed (migration):** the old per-pack data-source overrides (`data/packs/settings/<pack>.yaml`, `drishti.packs.settings-dir`, `DRISHTI_PACKS_SETTINGS`) are migrated once at start into connector files; the originals are kept in `data/packs/settings/.migrated/`; an override that cannot be placed is left in place and reported.
- **Deprecated:** `drishti.sources.connectors` in `application.yaml` (and in profiles and `DRISHTI_SOURCES_CONNECTORS_*` variables) and the per-store profiles (`postgres`, `duckdb`, `aerospike`, `mongodb`, `iceberg`, `redis`, `files`) still work, with a start-up warning that names the equivalent file; examples for every store are in `config/connectors.examples/`.
- **Added:** error codes `DRS-1011` (a read routed to a connector that has no file), `DRS-5031`, `DRS-5032` and `DRS-5033` (connector file and API errors; see TROUBLESHOOTING).
- **Added:** plugin `settingSpecs()` in the `SourcePlugin` SPI: a plugin declares the settings it reads for the connector form and validator (the server falls back to its catalogue for the shipped plugins).
- **Fixed:** an embedded view that repaints (a refresh, when the stream's first look is newer than the page fetched) **keeps a zoomed panel zoomed** (and its focus), and disposing its charts no longer raises Trusted Types violations on a strict host (ECharts' SVG painter emptied its elements with `innerHTML = ''`). The zoom browser tests click again if a click straddled the swap.
- **Added:** **Rūpaka phase 0 proof of concept, off by default** (`drishti.bi.poc.enabled`, console `bi.poc_enabled`; `docs/archive/RUPAKA_POC.md`). Throw-away code that tests the risky parts of the BI design: `POST /api/v1/bi/poc/query` (a masked aggregation from embedded DuckDB over a generated Parquet lake, answered as Apache Arrow IPC), `GET /api/v1/bi/poc/rows` (live rows for Perspective, on the console's one live channel), `GET /api/v1/bi/poc/bench` (JSON column vs typed columns vs rollup); the console page `/bi/poc` (top-bar **BI** entry and the reserved command `RUPAKA <GO>`) with Perspective (vendored, 3.9 MB), DuckDB-Wasm (installed by `tools/fetch-duckdb-wasm.sh`, 36 MB, not committed) and a masks-proven panel; `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` and Perspective's style hashes on that one page only.
- **Added:** **Sign in and Sign out are easy to find.** With sign-in on, the landing page's navigation shows **Sign in** (to `/login?next=<this page>`, the target checked as a path on this console) to anyone not signed in, and your name with a small menu (Open the terminal, My account, Sign out) once signed in. With sign-in off, the top bar's user menu says **Sign-in is off on this server** with a **How to turn it on** link (USER_MANAGEMENT, "Signing in and out"), and `/login` says so and offers the terminal instead of a form that cannot work. `/login` links back to the home page; **Sign out** lands on the landing page with a "Signed out" notice. Tests: `test_sign_links.py`, `test_sign_links_browser.py`.
- **Changed:** a zoomed panel's table **fits the height**: the pager gets a temporary *Fit (n)* page size (panel height over the real row height, at least 5) that keeps the top row on screen, follows window resizes, tab switches and live row changes, yields to an explicit choice until restore, and is never saved; restore puts back the previous size and page. Also inside `<drishti-view>`.
- **Added:** **zoom a panel.** Every panel's heading has a zoom button (`aria-pressed`, *Expand/Restore <title>*) and `Z` on a focused panel expands it over the view area, under the top bar and above the function keys, with page scroll locked, the other panels inert, live patches still applied and charts redrawn at the new size; `Esc` (after any open drawer or popover) or the button restores it and returns the focus to the button. The state is the URL hash `#zoom=<panel>` (reload or share; an unknown id is ignored), not your saved layout; layout mode and zoom exclude each other; `Shift+Z` asks for true full screen; on a phone the button is 44 pixels and the zoomed panel fills the screen; print shows the zoomed panel alone. Inside `<drishti-view>` the panel fills the element's own box (`static/js/zoom.js`, a root-scoped enhancer). USER_GUIDE "Zoom a panel", pictures by `tools/docs/screenshots.py --guide zoom`.
- **Changed:** the favicon and app icons are the logo mark (braces and eye) filling the icon, generated in every size by `tools/make_icons.py`; `/favicon.ico` is served.
- **Added:** **the full `<drishti-view>`** (Drishti Elements step 9). The library is now ES modules under `web/embed/` (served as `/embed/v1/m/<name>.js`, one `<script type="module">` line still loads it). Server markup goes through an allow-list sanitiser (no scripts, iframes, `on*`, inline styles or `javascript:` links reach the shadow root) and one Trusted Types policy, `drishti-elements`, so a host with `require-trusted-types-for 'script'; trusted-types drishti-elements` works. New: `loading`/`empty`/`error` slots for host content, `density` and a reserved `panel` attribute, the `drishti:token-needed` event, a token provider set late reloads elements that failed with a 401, and tokens are renewed early enough for short lifetimes (a 30 s token at 18 s). The About drawer's body is written through `options.setHtml` (the console's own pages are unchanged). Browser tests (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit) cover the sanitiser, Trusted Types, live token renewal past the first token's expiry and slots.
- **Added:** **Admin → Embedding** (Drishti Elements step 10): `/admin/embedding` lists the host applications with origins, sign-in method, scopes and kinds, status and usage (tokens issued, calls, live streams, refusals by code, last use); *New application* shows the client secret once, *Rotate secret* shows the new one once, *Disable* and *Enable* stop and resume an application without deleting it, *Delete* confirms first. Applications can be declared in configuration (`drishti.embed.apps`, GitOps: only the secret's SHA-256 is written) and are read-only, marked *from config*. The server counts usage in memory (`GET /api/v1/admin/embed/usage`, Micrometer `drishti.embed.*` by `app`), and has `POST /api/v1/admin/embed/apps/{id}/disable` and `/enable`.
- **Added:** **embedded views, the console's embed API** (Drishti Elements step 7). The proof of concept's `/embed/v1/poc/*` routes are now the versioned API under `/embed/v1` (views, About at `/views/{kind}/{id}/about`, pivot rows at `/views/{kind}/{id}/panels/{panel}/records`, `/resolve`, the live `/channel`; the `poc` paths are gone). `EmbedAuth` verifies the server's ES256 embed token in the console (key set from `/api/v1/embed/jwks`, cached, one throttled refetch on an unknown key id; expiry, audience, the token's own origins) before the token is passed on to the server, which still decides. A live stream outlives its token: at expiry the console sends `event: token`, the element posts a fresh token to `POST /embed/v1/channel/{cid}/token` and nothing repaints; with none within `embed.token_grace_seconds` the stream ends `DRS-8001`; the server is re-asked every `embed.recheck_seconds`. New console settings `embed.rate_per_minute` (`429 DRS-8004` with `Retry-After`), `embed.max_streams`, `embed.jwks_ttl_seconds`, `embed.jwks_min_refetch_seconds`, `embed.audiences`, `embed.recheck_seconds`, `embed.token_grace_seconds`, `embed.compress_min_bytes`; a `Drishti-Embed-Api` major other than 1 is `410 DRS-8006`; payloads are gzip or Brotli compressed. The console now needs the `cryptography` package (`brotli` optional).
- **Changed:** the console listens on every interface (`0.0.0.0`) by default, so it opens from other machines and phones; `DRISHTI_CONSOLE_HOST=127.0.0.1` keeps it to this machine.
- **Changed (mobile friendly):** `<drishti-view>` answers to its own width, not the host page's viewport: the element is a size container and the generated sheet rewrites the console's width `@media` rules to `@container drishti (...)` (non-width media are kept; `test_element_sheet.py` fails if a width `@media` is left). In a 360 px sidebar of a desktop page a view takes the narrow layout; on a phone it has no sideways scroll, panels stack, controls are at least 44 px, hints open by tap, tables scroll inside their panel and the About drawer is a bottom sheet when the element is narrow (tests in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit). The sample host page is responsive too. The console's page-width sweep (390, 1600, 2560 px) now includes the data loads pages, collaboration admin, the inbox, the no-access share page and the landing page's way back. Documented in `ELEMENTS.md` and the developer guide.
- **Changed (touch):** on touch devices (`pointer: coarse`) every control the console shows is at least 44 px in both directions (top bar, function keys, table pagers and filters, inputs, buttons, link lists, help contents), from a new last-loaded `css/touch.css` (also in the element sheet); desktop sizes are unchanged. Code examples in the help scroll sideways inside their box instead of being cut off. `test_page_widths_browser.py` gained a 390 px touch sweep over all pages against the real server (skipped without the built jar): every page shows content rather than a problem page, no tap target is under 44 px (running-text links excepted), no text is clipped.
- **Added:** **embedded views, server side** (Drishti Elements steps 1 to 3; off by default, `drishti.embed.enabled`). Host applications are registered by an administrator (`/api/v1/admin/embed/apps`: exact origins, a client secret shown once and/or public keys, kinds, scopes, token lifetime, rates; audited) and their backends buy short embed tokens by the RFC 8693 token exchange (`POST /api/v1/embed/token`: client secret or `private_key_jwt`, and the user's OIDC ID token or a JWT the host signs about the user; there is no plain-username path). The token is an ES256 JWT of the server's own key (`/api/v1/embed/jwks`), audience-bound, 5 minutes, read-only (`embed:view`, `embed:about`). Every embed call re-checks the token, the host application, the user, the `Origin`, the scope, the kind and the rates, and **always masks** whatever the user's roles say; the access log says `embed:<app>`. `provenance.masked` and `provenance.maskedPanels` count what a caller's masks hid in every ViewModel and live frame. New codes `DRS-8001` to `DRS-8006`. The console's dev-only token path of the proof of concept is gone: `tools/elements-demo` now signs a user assertion and exchanges it at the server.
- **Changed (Elements build steps 4, 5 and 8, no change to the console's behaviour):** the live channel is a class, `core/channel.py` `ChannelSession`, shared by `/api/channel` and the embed stream (identity passed in, owner = user plus host application); the view's title, strip, panels and provenance banners are macros (`templates/_macros/view.html`) used by the full page and the embed payload, so both render a panel with the same template; `<drishti-view>`'s stylesheet is generated by `python3 tools/elements_sheet.py` into `drishti-console/web/elements/` (versioned by content hash, only the Bootstrap Icons glyphs the macros use: 80.2 KB, 15.7 KB gzipped, down from 30.5 KB) and a test fails when it is stale or a macro uses a glyph it lacks.
- **Changed:** the console's view scripts (`tables`, `tree-rows`, `pivot`, `view`, `charts`, `about`, `about-hints`) are root-scoped modules: each exposes `init(root, options)` (root = the document or a ShadowRoot) and the console calls `init(document)`, so it behaves as before. `<drishti-view>` now uses the same copies for sorting and paging, tree rows, pivots (no saving), charts, panel `?` popovers and the About drawer; keys are bound to the element, not the host page (Elements, step 6).
- **Added (proof of concept, off by default):** `<drishti-view>`, a live Drishti view inside another web application's page in a Shadow DOM, no iframe: the console's `/embed/v1/` (view as per-panel HTML, one channel, resolve, the element's script and sheet; `embed.poc.*`, exact-origin CORS, always masked) and a sample host application on its own origin (`tools/elements-demo/`). Acceptance runs in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit; results in `docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md`, step 0. The token path is a dev-only stand-in for the planned RFC 8693 exchange.
- **Added:** Admin menu → **Data loads** (`/admin/loads`): every loaded pack at a glance (today's expectations, latest loads, what needs attention); the Admin menu also lists **Collaboration**. Both were reachable only from tabs or a row button before.
- **Docs:** design for **Drishti Elements** (`docs/architecture/ELEMENTS.md`, proposed): live Drishti views inside other web applications without iframes, as a `<drishti-view>` Web Component fed by HTML over the wire from the console, with embed tokens by token exchange (RFC 8693), the decisions and a build plan.

## 1.18.0 — Data loads: the batch-landed signal, expectations and late data (2026-10-06)
- **Added:** **data loads**, the "batch landed" signal. Drishti does not ingest (that stays with your ETL or DishtaYantra); what only it can do is act on new data. `POST /api/v1/packs/{pack}/loads {kind, businessDate|asOf, status ready|failed, rows, rejected, source, batchId, note}` (idempotent per pack, kind, date and batch; a later `failed` or a re-load is recorded as such; an administrator, or a personal token with the new least-privilege scope `loads:write` whose user's roles open the kind; `DRS-5011` unknown pack, `DRS-5012` unknown kind) records the load, drops the caches of the connectors that serve the kind, verifies the kind has entities on the date (`verified` or `not-found`), evaluates the alert rules on the kind for that business date, optionally opens N sample entities, and tells the people the pack names (inbox, bell, and an email through the outbox when asked), each as a step with its own result. **Expectations** per pack and kind (`loads:` in `pack.yaml` plus an administrator's override file, like the data source: due time, zone, business-day calendar) flag late and missing loads once (a notice, and `data late: my-bank/trade 2026-10-06` on Admin → Health, which turns DEGRADED) and clear when the load lands. New Admin → Packs → **Data loads** page per pack (history with step results, expectations with today's state, filters, settings; keyboard, phone, themes), `drishti.py data landed` (exit 1 when not verified) and `data loads`, settings `drishti.loads.*`, audit rows `data-load-*`. New guide [DATA_LOADS.md](docs/guides/DATA_GUIDE.md#1-telling-drishti-new-data-has-landed) (concepts, API, CLI, configuration, Airflow, cron and DishtaYantra recipes, troubleshooting, FAQ); OPERATIONALISING, DEMO_DATA and CLI_GUIDE now say plainly that `data ingest`, `--watch` and `pack make` are for staging, small setups and proofs of concept, not production ETL.

## 1.17.1 — The logo leads home and back, hot reload by polling, a nine-minute drill (2026-10-06)
- **Fixed:** Sutra hot reload no longer stops when the operating system has no file watches left (Linux *User limit of inotify watches reached*): it polls the Sutra files instead (`drishti.rachana.watch: auto|poll`, `poll-interval`); Health shows `hotReload: POLLING`. Before, edits were ignored until a restart.
- **Changed:** the drill is about 2.5 times faster with the same tests: Maven test classes run in parallel forks (`drishti.test.forks`), the console suite on pytest-xdist workers, the Java 25 verify (in a copy of the committed tree) beside the console and tool tests; `tools/drill.sh --docs` (chosen by itself when only documentation changed) is the light drill and `--no-push` verifies without pushing; a browser wait that timed out on `net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED` reloads the page once. Tests that depended on the order they ran in were fixed (the stand-in server's state is restored per test, `PackDeployApiTest` restores the pack folders it changed, a bridge test ignores the JDK's own HTTP server log). See the developer guide, section 2.6.
- **Changed:** the name and logo in the top bar lead to the landing page from every page, signed in or not; a signed-in visitor gets **← Back to …** (Alt+B) to the page they came from (same-site paths only).

## 1.17.0 — JSON Lines to a deployed pack: the drishti.py command line, pack make, admin deploy (2026-10-05)
- **Added:** Admin → Packs **Deploy an archive**, **History and roll back**, and per-pack **Data source**. An archive (the pack only, never data; the `.tar.gz` of `pack bundle`, or a `.zip`) is uploaded as the raw body (`POST /api/v1/admin/packs/deploy`, 413 above `drishti.packs.deploy.max-archive-mb`), checked by the server (SHA-256, optional Ed25519 signature by a `registry.trusted-keys` publisher, tar/zip slip, links, size and file-count limits, `MANIFEST.json` checksums as `pack verify`, required server version, Sutra lint and tests by the same checker, parent packs) and previewed against the running version with the same four levels as `pack diff` (breaking, selection, layout, change; the Java and Python rule sets share test cases). Confirming swaps it into `drishti.packs.installed-dir`, keeps the replaced version (`keep-versions`, 5), restarts in place with the existing automatic undo, and records the deployment (`deploy-history.jsonl`, audit rows); `POST /admin/packs/{name}/rollback` goes back to a kept version or to the shipped copy. The data source of a pack (view, edit, **Test connection** with business dates and row counts per kind, reset) is saved to `data/packs/settings/<pack>.yaml`, never into the pack, so redeploys keep it; precedence environment > override file > pack; credentials only as `${ENV}` references; shown in the console as pack default / overridden / set by the site. Token scope `packs:admin` covers all of it. CLI: `drishti.py server packs deploy|history|rollback|datasource get|set|test|reset`. Docs: OPERATIONALISING section 17, PACKS, CLI_GUIDE, API_GUIDE, CONFIGURATION.
- **Added:** `GET /api/v1/me/token` (the calling token's id, scopes and expiry; 404 for a session), used by `drishti.py doctor`; `SourcePlugin.inventory` (dates and row counts, implemented by the Delta and file connectors); `DRISHTI_DOCTOR_PORTS` to check other ports than 18480/17480.
- **Fixed:** the explain API's match trace now includes the chosen Sutra (`candidates[].chosen`), so `view explain` shows the whole trace exactly; the CLI_GUIDE captures of `server smoke`, `doctor` (no false red "jar missing") and `view get|explain` were retaken.
- **Added:** pack authoring tools in `drishti.py`: `data profile` (streaming, bounded memory: every field with types, coverage, distinct count and examples, candidate key, date and match columns with an explained score, and a ready `pack make` line), `pack regenerate PACK INPUTS` (generates again and three-way merges into the pack against a baseline that `pack new`/`pack make` now store in `<pack>/.generated/`: new groups added, untouched files refreshed, your edits kept, edits on both sides merged line by line or marked as conflicts and listed, exit 1; `--dry-run`; nothing of yours is overwritten), `pack diff OLD NEW` (folders or bundles: Sutras added/removed/changed, kinds and mnemonics removed or renamed flagged BREAKING, match where/priority flagged "screen selection changes", about, glossary and data layout changes; `--unified`, `--fail-on breaking|any|none`), `pack catalogue` (Markdown or one HTML page for business review: kinds, glossary, every Sutra with match rule and panels, optional `sutra preview` snapshots) and `pack i18n export|import` (About text through a CSV into `config/about.<lang>.yaml`, reporting missing and extra keys). Bundles leave `.generated/` out. Tests `tools/test_pack_authoring.py` (in the drill); CLI_GUIDE sections with real output; PyCharm `.run/` samples.
- **Added:** five CLI commands. `drishti.py server smoke` (health, packs loaded and enabled, no Sutra problems, then sample views of every kind on the latest and an earlier business date with timings; exit 1 on any failure), `doctor` (green/yellow/red checks of Java 21+, the server jar, Python and optional libraries, directories, ports 18480/17480 and, with `--server`, the token and its scopes, each with a fix), `data ingest --watch DIR` (a drop folder: stable-size check, each file once through a state file written after success, `--done-dir`, `--once` for cron, `--interval`), `view get|explain KIND/ID [--date D]` (the rendered view and the About answer as text tables, with the caller's masks) and `completion bash|zsh|powershell` (generated from the command tree). CLI_GUIDE has a section for each with real output; `.run/` has PyCharm configurations for smoke, doctor and view get.
- **Added:** `drishti.py pack make INPUT --kind K --match COL --name N`: one command from a folder (or file) of JSON Lines to ONE folder to deploy: `pack/<name>/` (Sutras, tests, about), the data in `data/delta` (or `data/files`) partitioned by business date, a checksummed `bundle/`, `config/drishti-site.yaml`, `run-server.sh`/`.ps1`, `MANIFEST.json` and a plain-text `README.txt` (deploy, verify, lifting the data from Delta, new days, rollback, troubleshooting) with the real kind, ids and dates filled in. It detects `--key` (present and unique in every document) and `--date` (a date field in at least 95% of the documents) when not given, says why, then runs `pack check` and `pack verify`. `pack new` gained `--version`. CLI_GUIDE has a "Quickest path" section and a much fuller PyCharm section (interpreter, a run configuration per task, debugging, sharing through `.run/`, with sample `.run/*.run.xml` files).
- **Fixed:** `sutra lint` and `sutra test` (and `drishti.py pack check`) load the packs their command line names, so a pack is checked with its own About text and glossary whatever `DRISHTI_PACKS` says; a pack outside `packs/` is read from its parent folder. Before, market-risk and the other banking packs showed false help-coverage failures from the command line.
- **Added:** personal API tokens (`drk_…`) may carry write scopes so tools, CI and GitOps can act: `design:write`, `design:approve`, `packs:admin` (config `drishti.security.token-scopes`; no `admin` or `data:admin` scope, and users, roles, tokens, sign-in and personal or collaboration state stay closed via `token-never`). Chosen on My account → API tokens (or `POST /me/tokens {scopes}`), stored with the token, enforced in one place (`TokenScopes` in the token filter) as scope **and** the user's current roles; a write token must expire (`token-write-max-days`, 90); every write is audited as `token-write` (token id, never the secret) and each refusal as `token-denied`. Existing tokens keep reading only. `TokenScopeGuardTest` fails when a non-GET endpoint declares no scope. CLI_GUIDE, API_GUIDE, CLIENTS, USER_MANAGEMENT and CONFIGURATION updated.
- **Added:** `tools/drishti.py`, one command line (stdlib + PyYAML) for `sutra shape|design|gen|lint|test|preview`, `pack new|check|about-check|publish|keygen|verify|install`, `data ingest|load`, `server health|packs list|load|unload|on|off`, `design list|create|get|save|check|propose|approve|reject|export|import|bind` (REST, token from `DRISHTI_TOKEN` or `--token-file`) and `docs shots`, with `--json`, exit codes 0/1/2 and `pack new --load --server`; the generated `pack.yaml` `ingest:` block is documented as an optional tooling key the server ignores; new guide `docs/guides/CLI_GUIDE.md` (every command with real output, recipes, running it from PyCharm).

- **Added:** the offline path to production: `drishti.py pack bundle` (a reproducible `<name>-<version>.tar.gz` with `.sha256` and a MANIFEST of checksums, kinds, required server version and data layout), `pack verify` (archive and file checksums, schema, server version, `sutra lint`/`test`; also checks a deployed folder for drift), `pack deploy` (atomic copy into a packs folder, previous version kept in a backup folder, `--dry-run`, never touches a running server) and `pack rollback`, with `tools/packbundle.py`, `tools/test_pack_bundle.py` and the guide docs/guides/OPERATIONALISING.md (artifacts and where each goes, promotion by copying the same bundle, data, CI, permissions, Docker/Kubernetes, Windows, troubleshooting). `pack verify --registry` is the old registry check.- **Added:** `tools/drishti.py`, one command line (stdlib + PyYAML) for `sutra shape|design|gen|lint|test|preview`, `pack new|check|about-check|publish|keygen|verify|install`, `data ingest|load`, `server health|packs list|load|unload|on|off`, `design list|create|get|save|check|propose|approve|reject|export|import|bind` (REST, token from `DRISHTI_TOKEN` or `--token-file`) and `docs shots`, with `--json`, exit codes 0/1/2 and `pack new --load --server`; the generated `pack.yaml` `ingest:` block is documented as an optional tooling key the server ignores; new guide `docs/guides/CLI_GUIDE.md` (every command with real output, recipes, running it from PyCharm).
- **Added:** `sutra design --each <dir>` (one draft per subfolder of samples in one JVM), `tools/sutragen.py` (Sutras from JSONL, one per match-field value, `--date`, samples across dates), `tools/packgen/pack_from_jsonl.py` (a complete dated pack from JSONL, linted and tested) and `tools/ingest_jsonl.py` (JSONL into a Delta lake or the File connector's files, idempotent per business date); inputs are folders or single files. See PACK_DEVELOPER_GUIDE "Generating a pack from JSON Lines".
- **Changed:** the console module is `drishti-console/` (was `console/`), named like the other modules. Recreate its virtual environment once: `rm -rf drishti-console/.venv` and follow QUICKSTART step 3; point IDE run configurations at `drishti-console/run_drishti_web.py` and `drishti-console/.venv`.

## 1.16.0 — Java 21 for production, About this page, Share and Discussion (2026-10-05)

- **Collaboration behaviour pass (B3):** Admin > Collaboration gets a mail outbox view (tries, last error, dead letters, send again, test mail), bridge rows show tries and last error, and a share that asks for email while the mail server is failing says so; revision history, comments and shares use the person's Clock time zone (pictures use the business zone); error lines print the code once and `Retry-After` reaches the browser; the bridge Test waits for the bridge (`collab.bridge_test_timeout_seconds`) and names the right setting; the Edit button goes when the window closes and the message says "the 15-minute edit window"; the Discussion box fits a 390 px phone; a lone email notice goes after 10 s (`email.coalesce-window`) instead of 2 minutes; the compliance export streams through the console; `GET /admin/collab/threads/hidden` lists hidden comments for the admin page.

- **Data safety QA fixes (2026-10-05):** no oracle for masked values (an author without `raw` gets no warning or refusal, reads their own text as written, each hit is audited as `collab.masked-copy`); copies are matched case-insensitively after NFKC, spacing, zero-width and look-alike folding; emails and chat posts carry values rendered per recipient (quotes filled in share emails and bridges too; `link-only` unchanged); share pictures freeze their rights profile at share time and can only narrow later; tamper evidence covers the live comment row, the thread head, holds and the audit trail (`drishti_collab_seal`), and `verify` reports unreadable rows instead of failing; tokens of deleted or disabled users are refused (`drishti.security.registered-users-only`); email templates drop their licence comment; `/collab` reports real email availability; names lose control characters.
- **Watermarked snapshots (collaboration step 10):** off by default (`drishti.collab.snapshots.enabled`, per pack `packs.<pack>.snapshots.enabled`); a share may include a server-drawn PNG (Java2D, headless) of the view or panel, made for the most restrictive recipient (masks of anyone without `raw`, panels any recipient may not open left out), watermarked with sender, recipients, time, data date, generation and link; limits (`snapshots.width|max-height|max-panels|max-rows|max-bytes|timeout`), a cache, `DRS-7015`/`DRS-7016`, an access-log `export` row per picture, `POST /shares/preview-picture`, `GET /shares/{id}/picture`, an email attachment under `email.content: comment`, and the share dialog's *Include a picture* with a preview.
- **Collaboration server polish:** the file inbox and outbox never reuse a sequence number (a high-water mark is kept before rows are purged); bridge posts also write an access-log row; several notices for one person inside `drishti.collab.email.coalesce-window` (default 2m, `0` = off) go out as one digest email; the compliance export adds `inbox.ndjson` and `outbox.ndjson` (no message bodies); `drishti.collab.share.post-to-thread` is the server default when a share request does not say.
- **Collaboration console polish:** the share dialog's tick *Also start a discussion on the view* (default from `drishti.collab.share.post-to-thread`), a reply box on the shared view's banner for the share's sender and recipients, **Admin > Collaboration** (threads and moderation, legal holds, compliance export, chain verify, retention dry run, bridges, role-gated as the API), every collaboration time in the top bar's zone with its label, and quoted values drawn as the page formats the field (`•••` stays for readers without raw). No server change.
- Java 21 is the production runtime: docs, pom enforcer message, Windows script and server Dockerfile (default `eclipse-temurin:21-jre`) no longer say "25 recommended"; Java 25 stays supported (compact object headers there only).
- **Fixed:** in a workspace pane, Alt+0..4 moved the focus again: the view's own date attribute (`data-page-asof`, added with Discussion) no longer looks like the top bar's date form, which made `app.js` stop before its pane keys; `app.js` now looks for the form only.
- **Build:** `mvn package` fails when any runtime dependency needs a JVM newer than Java 21 (`enforceBytecodeVersion`, `maxJdkVersion` 21), so the product always runs on Java 21, the production runtime.
- **Changed (docs):** collaboration documents reconciled to what was built (build step 8): the worked example *Share and Discussion, end to end* ([HOW_IT_FITS.md §3.10](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md#3111-share-and-discussion-end-to-end)) on MX-20000001 with screenshots (`tools/docs/shots/collab.py`, `docs/guides/img/collab/`), ADR-020, the console guide *Sharing and discussion* (the inbox's help page), moderation and compliance in USER_MANAGEMENT, backups in OPERATIONS, two TROUBLESHOOTING entries, and the as-built differences in COLLABORATION.md (inbox rows are not yet purged by `inbox.keep-days`; `share.post-to-thread` is only reported by `/collab`).
- **Changed (tests):** the drill's Java 21 run skips the container tests (they run on Java 25); the console's browser tests share one live server and console per session instead of one per file; builders run only the tests their change touches, the drill is the one full gate.
- **Changed (drill):** a console test that fails is re-run once; one that then passes is reported as `FLAKY` and logged in `target/drill-flakes.log`, one that fails twice still stops the drill. Browser waits that time out now report the page state, JavaScript errors, failed requests and HTTP errors.
- **Added:** Retention, legal holds and the compliance export ([COLLABORATION.md](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md#31-collaboration-write-back-and-approvals), build step 7, server): `drishti.collab.retention` (`keep-days`, per-kind `kinds`, per-pack `packs.<pack>.retention-days`, default keep forever) with a scheduled purge that removes whole old threads and shares and never what an active legal hold covers; legal holds placed and released by the `compliance` role (scope entity, kind, user, thread or all, with an optional date range, audited); an asynchronous eDiscovery export (JSON Lines in a zip with every revision, the hash-chain proof and a manifest of SHA-256 checksums, streamed in bounded memory, once-only download, audited); `GET /admin/collab/verify` to find a tampered chain; admin search and `/admin/collab/retention/run`; `DRS-7010` for removing a held thread. API only: the admin console page is not built yet. See [OPERATIONS.md](docs/guides/OPERATIONS_GUIDE.md#123-retention-legal-holds-and-the-compliance-export).
- **Added:** Ask about this page ([CONTEXT_HELP.md](docs/guides/RACHANA_REFERENCE.md#about-this-page-the-design-of-context-help), build step 9), optional and **off by default**: `POST /api/v1/views/{kind}/{id}/ask` and a question box at the end of the About drawer, drawn only for packs listed in `drishti.explain.ask.packs`. The server builds the prompt from the caller's own explain answer, its glossary and the pack guide (labels only unless `values: shown`; a masked value is never sent; data and pack text are marked untrusted with a per-request id; no tools), calls an OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic Messages endpoint with a key from `DRISHTI_ASK_KEY`, and limits questions per user (`DRS-4009`), time (`DRS-4008`) and size; questions go to the access log (`ask`), answers are not stored. `DRS-4007` to `DRS-4009` are now live. See [CONFIGURATION.md](docs/admin/CONFIGURATION.md) and the privacy note in [OPERATIONS.md](docs/guides/OPERATIONS_GUIDE.md).
- **Added:** Discussion, the console ([COLLABORATION.md](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md#31-collaboration-write-back-and-approvals), build step 6): **Discussion** (`Alt+N`) is a second tab of the view's side drawer beside About (`?` and `F1` still open About, arrow keys switch tabs; a bottom sheet on a phone). Threads on the whole view, a panel (a comment count beside its `?`) or a field; `@` mentions of people and roles and `{` value quotes (masked values read as •••); reply, edit within the window, retract, resolve, follow and mute, administrator hide and lock; each comment's pin with **Open as it was**; new comments announced live. The old Notes drawer is gone (old notes appear as threads). The account page gains the email opt-outs (share, mention, reply).
- **Fixed (threads):** a note imported from the old Notes is checked for masked values when it is read (it was never checked when written), so a value such as a trader's name typed into an old note shows as ••• to readers without raw; when the entity cannot be read the whole text is hidden from them.
- **Added:** Chat bridges and mail follow-ups ([COLLABORATION.md](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md#31-collaboration-write-back-and-approvals), build step 9): admin-configured bridges (`drishti.collab.bridges`) post a share, comment or mention as "comment + link" to a signed generic webhook, a Microsoft Teams incoming webhook or Workflows, or a Slack incoming webhook, through the outbox (retries, backoff, dead letters), with routing rules per pack, kind and event, URLs and secrets from environment variables only, an allow-list, a per-minute limit, no redirects, never a data value (the note is written as the `render-as` role would read it, quotes read as their paths), audit entries, `GET /admin/collab/bridges` and a test post (`DRS-7013`, `DRS-7014`); also emails for @mentions and replies, panel titles instead of ids in emails, and `inbox.keep-days` now purges old inbox rows.

A share writes an outbox row per recipient in its own transaction (`drishti_outbox`, JPA or files, one contract test); a worker claims due rows under a lease, builds the message for the recipient's rights at send time (the kind, id, panel, date, the note with masked values as `•••`, and the link; never a data value; `link-only` per pack with `packs.<pack>.email.content`; text and HTML templates, product name from `drishti.branding.product`, overridable with `email.templates-dir`), sends through `spring-boot-starter-mail`, retries with doubling backoff and makes dead letters, visible and retryable at `GET /api/v1/admin/collab/outbox` and `POST .../outbox/{seq}/retry`; `POST .../mail-test` mails the administrator; `notify.email.{share,mention,reply}` in `/me/settings` opts a person out; metrics `drishti.collab.mail` and `drishti.collab.outbox`. Tests: `OutboxDispatcherTest`, `MailRenderTest`, `ShareMail*Test` against an in-process SMTP server (GreenMail).
- **Added:** Share with a note, the console ([COLLABORATION.md](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md#31-collaboration-write-back-and-approvals), build step 3): **Share** (`Alt+S`) opens a dialog (the view or one panel, the pinned date shown, people and roles by type-ahead from the directory, a note, `Ctrl+Enter` to send, *Copy link* kept) that posts to the step 2 API and reports who was reached and who was not; `/share/{id}` opens the view as it was pinned (date, "known at", generation, panel) with a *Shared by* banner and the note, or a clean no-access page (nothing about the entity; *Switch on <pack>* when the pack is off; a stranger's link looks like no link); the view call carries `X-Drishti-Share`; the bell counts unread notices and alerts (toast on a `notice`, count from `/api/inbox/count`) and opens `/inbox` (`Alt+I`), a page of rows rendered for the reader now with filters, mark read and mark all read; keyboard, phone full-screen sheet, all seven themes; see [USER_GUIDE.md](docs/guides/USER_GUIDE.md#share-a-view-with-a-note).

- **Changed:** Drishti now supports Java 21 and newer (25 stays recommended): the build targets Java 21 bytecode (`maven.compiler.release` 21), the enforcer rule is `[21,)` and says "Drishti needs Java 21 or newer (any vendor; 25 recommended)", `-XX:+UseCompactObjectHeaders` is used only on Java 25+ (the Docker image, the Windows start script and the docs; Java 21 refuses to start with it), and synchronized blocks that did I/O (the DuckDB file check, the Redis loader's journal and dictionary training, the Iceberg run cleanup) use a `ReentrantLock` so they do not pin virtual threads on Java 21. `NoBlockingUnderSynchronizedTest` fails if main code blocks inside `synchronized`. `tools/drill.sh` runs the tests on Java 21 as well. Load test of the connectors on both Javas: [PERFORMANCE.md](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md#14-concurrency-and-performance).

- **Docs:** [CONNECTOR_DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md](docs/guides/DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md#10-connectors-choosing-combining-and-writing-one) replaces `PLUGIN_GUIDE.md` and `CONNECTOR_GUIDE.md`: which connector, the `SourcePlugin` SPI, testing with the testkit contracts, a worked teaching plugin (`docs/guides/examples/connector/`, built and contract-tested, not shipped) and one short section per connector; each connector's walk-through and worked examples moved into its own `*_CONNECTOR.md`, de-duplicated.
- **Docs:** [PACK_DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md](docs/guides/BUILD_GUIDE.md) (build a pack end to end, with a help-desk pack) takes the developer half of `PACKS.md` and the in-app `build-a-pack` tutorial; `PACKS.md` keeps the user and admin content.

- **Docs:** [PANEL_DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md](docs/guides/RACHANA_REFERENCE.md#developing-a-panel-kind) (adding a panel kind end to end, worked through the real `metric` tile, with an ordered checklist and the guard tests) and [PANEL_KINDS.md](docs/guides/RACHANA_REFERENCE.md#panels-the-twenty-two-kinds-and-developing-a-new-one) (the catalogue of all twenty-one kinds, where F1 lands) replace PANELS.md, the in-app panel-kinds guide and DEVELOPER_GUIDE §5.4; screenshots are generated per guide by `tools/docs/screenshots.py --guide <name>` (the unreproducible `static/img/guide/kind-*.png` are gone).
