## 1.14.1 — LZ4 Delta tables, clean 413 for oversized requests, masking of copied values (2026-10-03)
- **Added:** Delta: LZ4 and LZ4_RAW Parquet pages are read by both engines. The native engine decodes LZ4_RAW (one block) and the deprecated LZ4 codec the way Arrow does (Hadoop framing when the lengths add up exactly, else one raw block) with lz4-java's safe decoder (`lz4-decoder: fast` for the fastest available); the `hadoop` engine reads LZ4 files, which parquet-java's Hadoop codec cannot when Arrow or pyarrow wrote them, through the native decoder (a per-file footer check; `lz4-via-native: false` turns it off). An LZ4 table is `UP` and lists and searches normally; only BROTLI, LZO and pages that do not decode are `DEGRADED`, naming the table, file and codec. Tests use real delta-rs/pyarrow fixtures (`plugins/drishti-plugin-delta/src/test/resources/lake-codecs`) compared value by value with the uncompressed copy on both engines. Supersedes the DATA-13 advice to rewrite LZ4 dates.

- Oversized builder requests get a clean `413` `DRS-5005` naming the size and the limit (declared or chunked, before the body is read; Tomcat drains a bounded remainder so there is no reset), the console says "This file is too large: X MB; the limit is Y MB"; new opt-in `drishti.security.mask-copies` scrubs exact copies of masked values inside other text of the same document, dotted `redact` entries mask by path, and the shipped setting also masks `lifecycle.timeline.description` (QA S2-08, S2-11).

## 1.14.0 — The Build workbench, and two rounds of adversarial QA closed (2026-10-03)
- **Fixed:** QA round 2 of the Build workbench (usability), every finding. Adding and removing panels is obvious: a **+ Add panel** button in the bar on every tab (a chooser of all 20 kinds), a filterable kind grid, a grip and resize handles, an *Add your first panel* call to action, Studio addresses open in Split view; panels are removed by a trash button, the inspector, a right-click menu or the palette, with a toast *Undo*. A design of your own kind has no false "not a valid kind" problem; a mistyped expression is a located Problem (code once) and the other panels still draw (the console cuts the failing panels out of a preview-only copy; the schema now carries per-kind options). The inspector edits every option: numbers, `expand` (number or all), selects for fixed sets (graph `layout`, tabs `layout`, surface `view`), `markers`, the table `pivot` object, the pivot `by` list and a tab `body`. DRS codes appear once on every Build page; a **Notes** tab (markdown preview, licence comment hidden); no sideways scroll at 390 px; a skip link and `G` then `C` to the canvas, Esc returns from the inspector; one live region; F1 and links send a pending edit first; in-page dialogs instead of `confirm()`/`prompt()`; unknown `?example=`/`?design=`/`?sutra=` say so; palette `go to sample` by file name, plus Auto-design, Split, Phone, Theme, Bind and Remove; guide pictures regenerated, `docs/qa/2026-10-03/ux/FINDINGS.md` marks each row.
- **Docs:** `docs/archive/HOW_IT_FITS.md`, "How Drishti fits together": how kinds, mnemonics, packs, connectors, Sutras, links and roles refer to each other, and the runtime path of `TRD MX-20000001` from the command box through the console, server, source router, Sutra matcher, layout, binder and ViewModel to the live patches, with real files and outputs, a second example in the genomics pack, the no-Sutra case, how the Build workbench adds a screen, and a where-to-change-what table; linked from the docs map, ARCHITECTURE, QUICKSTART and Help → Developers.
- **Tests:** jqwik removed; property tests are plain JUnit with seeded generators (`-Ddrishti.test.seed` overrides the base seed; failures print case index, seed and input).
- **Fixed:** QA round 2, governance and safety. Development file binding (S2-01, S2-05, S2-06, S2-07, S2-13) writes only to your own folder under `drishti.builder.dev-dir`, which must lie outside the loaded Sutra directories, so *Save to file* can no longer make a Sutra live without review; symbolic links are never followed, writes go through an exclusively created temporary file, bad names and oversize bodies are clean `400`/`413` problems, `sync` is a POST, and the binding info shows no absolute path to non-administrators.
- **Fixed:** a Design publishes `name@(latest+1)` and never rewrites a version; an unrelated Design over an existing `name@version` (a pack's included) is refused at propose time with `DRS-2028` (M-1). When the base Sutra gets a newer version the Design flags it and *Rebase* replays its operations on it, reporting what cannot be replayed (M-2).
- **Fixed:** limits. The synthetic sampler is bounded by `drishti.builder.sample-max-*` and clamps with a problem (S2-02); Sutra, notes and tests count in the design and user size and have their own caps (S2-03); a long text no longer reads as "nested too deep" (S2-08); scratch designs have a cap of their own, never fill the named quota, are evicted oldest first and have a bulk delete (UX-05); the console enforces body limits while streaming chunked bodies and answers an over-limit import with 413 (S2-09).
- **Fixed:** `GET /studio?...` no longer creates a design: it shows a confirmation whose button POSTs (S2-04). Proposal evidence and share links show reference sample names as `kind (reference)` to viewers who may not open the kind, and the notes only to the author and approvers (S2-10); four-eyes compares canonical user names (S2-14); the stateless builder endpoints and `sutra design --kind` validate `kind` (L-7); the `sutra` CLI keeps the input size limit, stays inside its input and never prints a stack trace (S2-12); masking of free text is documented precisely (S2-11).
- **Fixed:** QA round 2, data and engine (2026-10-03). Shape: bounds beyond 2^53 are exact and non-finite numbers carry none, sparse optional sections are no longer read as maps, `markdown` accepts `source:`. Pack fragments: notes live in `NOTES.md` (no growth on re-import) and sample names keep their Unicode. `sutra test`: the JUnit file is always written, invalid/BOM/empty samples are failed cases, `expect.yaml` typos fail, `.jsonl` is read. Synthetic samples honour `pattern`, `oneOf`, `patternProperties`, `prefixItems` and recursion limits, and refuse dangling `$ref`. Auto-design: monthly series, tenor grids, single-root trees, year/version/number codes not formatted as amounts, no always-empty links panel, stable key order, gauges for shares (`fraction-names`), tabs for short four-field lists. Operations refuse lists/mappings for single-value options and `setStrip` keeps its comments. Tree tables skip non-record children; oversize uploads answer `413`; messages say MiB, a text `baseRev` says "whole number", expression problems state their code once.
- **Added:** Build workbench step 8, ship and scale. **Propose with evidence:** the workbench's *Submit for review* (`POST /api/v1/builder/designs/{id}/propose`) sends the check matrix, the sample names, the notes and the design's identity with the proposal; reviewers see them on `/build/reviews/{id}`; approval makes the design `live(vN)` (shown beside its title and on *My designs*), rejection returns it to `draft`.
- **Added:** pack fragments: *Ship → Export as a pack fragment* downloads a zip (`pack.yaml` stub with the kind, a mnemonic and the id field, the Sutra, `tests/<sutra>/*.json` + `expect.yaml`, three samples, a README) that loads as a pack and passes `sutra test`; *New screen → Or import a pack* turns a pack folder or zip into designs, one per Sutra, with its samples and notes.
- **Added:** development file binding (`drishti.builder.file-binding`, default off): a design bound to a file under `drishti.rachana.dirs` saves by writing the file, and an edit made in an IDE comes back into the design (polled every few seconds); a clash with unsynced edits is `409 DRS-5007`.
- **Added:** read-only share links (*Ship → Create a read-only link*, `/build/d/{id}?share=token`): the Sutra, the operations and the sample names, never sample contents or notes; the recipient previews against their own JSON or a stored entity they may open; revocable at once.
- **Added:** the screen designer guide is finished: an end-to-end walkthrough (folder, design, check, propose, approve, live), pack fragments, sharing, the command line and CI, file binding, troubleshooting, limits and a keyboard reference for shipping, with eight new screenshots (`tools/docs/screenshots.py` now also runs against a scratch server with saving and binding on).
- **Fixed:** the workbench reloaded an empty Sutra after a 409 or an auto-design (it read `yaml` from a design that answers `sutra`); and `tools/docs/screenshots.py` never started its scratch servers because an HTTP error counted as "nothing listens".
- **Fixed:** in a narrow `status` or `kv` panel two labels ran into each other ("Confirmation" into "Clearing"): labels now wrap (`overflow-wrap`), and a very narrow panel (under 15rem) stacks them one per row; pinned by `test_panel_polish_browser.py` at four widths.
- **Fixed:** a waterfall's value labels overlapped at small widths: the labels now fit their columns when they can, turn to read upward (with room made above the bars) when the columns are narrow, and are left out when not even that fits; the chart is laid out again on resize (`drishtiCharts.labelFit`).
- **Fixed:** the all-panels showcase (and `linked-sources`) opened as a copy with "Problems 2" although nothing was wrong. Causes: the light YAML check read a flow map written over several lines (`- { id: explain, ...,` then `rows: ...}`) as cut at the line end and said `rows` was missing (`studio-yaml.js` now joins the continuation lines); the Problems tab flagged `children: "@.children"` of a tree table as present in only some samples (a tree's `children` is rare by nature, now skipped); and the schema typed `limit` as a whole number for every panel kind though an area's is an expression (`exposure-profile` was told "limit is a whole number"). Every example now opens with an empty Problems tab (`test_showcase_clean_browser.py`; kind and entity messages of the banking packs aside).
- **Fixed:** a `source:` link to an entity no store holds said "waiting for NOPE-1" like one still being fetched; it now says "NOPE-1 not found" (`SourceRouter.fetchAll` reports the refs no source holds; "waiting for" stays for a source that failed or timed out).
- **Fixed:** `test_live_tabs_browser.py[leader]` was timing-sensitive (failed once in a full run): the election, the single shared connection and the takeover after the leader closes are now waited for as conditions.
- **Changed:** Build workbench step 7, Studio folded in: Sutra Studio has no page of its own any more. Every `/studio` address (`?example=`, `?sutra=name@v`, `?kind=&id=`, `?design=&sample=`, `?build=1`) answers a 302 into the workbench (`/build/d/{id}`, a new design started for it: a scratch copy of the showcase, a copy of the example, a design that edits that Sutra with Studio's test entities carried over as stored-entity samples, or a stored entity as the sample), and `/studio/reviews[/{id}]` into `/build/reviews[/{id}]`. The workbench has Studio's keys (Ctrl+S saves or says why not, Ctrl+Enter previews), a File menu (open a `.yaml` or `.json`, or an example as a copy), Save or Submit for review under the same rights as before (designing open to everyone, saving needs the author right), a **command palette** (Ctrl+K: add or go to a panel, next sample, run the check, switch tab, undo, save, guide), and a **Versions** tab that diffs the design against the Sutra it came from or any earlier step of its log and restores one as an operation (`GET /api/v1/builder/designs/{id}/versions[/{n}]`). The Build menu is Create, Govern (Reviews, with the number waiting) and Learn; the *Sutra Studio* tutorial redirects to the screen designer guide, which gains four chapters.
- **Added:** headless Sutra CLI: `java -jar drishti-server-*-exec.jar sutra lint|test|shape|design|preview <path>` runs the workbench engine without a web server (exit codes 0/1/2, `--junit` XML, `--out` HTML snapshots), with the `packs/<p>/tests/<sutra>/*.json` + `expect.yaml` convention (`noErrors`, `nonEmpty`, per-sample overrides); `SutraCliTest` runs `sutra test` over every shipped pack's tests and the ten examples (docs/guides/SUTRA_CLI.md).
- **Fixed:** the shape extractor wrote a schema that rejected its own sample when a list of records held `null` items (`{"c":{"name":[null,{"x y":false}],"x y":204}}`): the nulls were folded into the record, so the record turned nullable while the tree's `items` `$ref` did not allow null. The null items now belong to the list (`items` is `anyOf` the record or null) and the record keeps its own nullability; found by `ShapePropertyTest`, pinned by `ShapeSelfValidationTest`.
- **Fixed:** the linked-sources example previewed with "waiting for NS-SUMMIT-NY" in tests: a pasted document already fetches its `source:` entities like a stored one (same pipeline, link budget and open-rights); the entities were simply not held because the banking packs were not enabled. `ExamplePreviewTest` runs every example and a Studio paste of linked-sources with the packs enabled and no longer tolerates "waiting for".
- **Added:** Build workbench step 6, the visual canvas: a design's page (`/build/d/{id}`) is now the workbench. Data on the left (samples, the 20-kind palette, the shape tree whose fields can be dragged), **Design / YAML / Summary** in the middle (split view), **Inspector / Problems / Tests** on the right, a status bar with the sample switcher, desktop or phone width, theme, the check result, the revision, undo and redo and *Preview with a file…*. The Design tab draws the real preview with an editing layer: click to select a panel, the title or the strip; drag a panel by its heading to move it (a bar shows where it lands), drag its edges to size it on the 12-column grid, Delete removes it; drag a palette kind to add a panel, drag a shape field to bind it to a panel or to get ranked panel kinds with reasons; every change is one operation sent with its base revision (a stale one is a 409, reloaded and said). The inspector is generated from the Rachana schema (required options first, selects, switches, expression fields that complete `$.`/`@.` paths and functions, reorderable lists). Typing in the YAML tab is a Text operation; Problems lists YAML, operation (DRS-502x), binding and check problems with a jump to each; the Tests tab re-checks every sample 0.8 s after the last change. Everything has a keyboard path (arrows select, Alt+arrows move, Shift+arrows size, `N` adds, `B` binds, Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Shift+Z) announced in a live region; the move/size keys are one shared module (`build/grid-keys.js`) used by layout mode too. New guide `docs/guides/SCREEN_DESIGNER.md` with screenshots made by `tools/docs/screenshots.py` (F1 on any Build page, *Build → Learn*, Help → Examples "Open in the workbench"); the help centre serves pictures under `docs/` at `/help/files/`.
- **Added:** Build workbench step 4, Designs: your work on a screen is kept on the server as a *design*, owned by you alone (others get `404 DRS-5006`): `/api/v1/builder/designs` (create, list, read, rename, delete, duplicate; samples as files, references to stored entities re-read with your current rights and masks, or synthetic documents generated from a JSON Schema; `/shape`, `/preview?sample=`, `/autodesign`), in files (`data/designs/<user>/<id>/`, owner-only permissions) or the identity database (`drishti.builder.designs.store`), with quotas (50 designs, 50 samples and 25 MB each, 250 MB in all; limits answer `413 DRS-5005`) and expiry (scratch 1 day, named 90 days, warning from 75; a sweeper deletes them). Console: **Build → New screen** (`/build/new`: files, a folder, a schema, stored entities, examples as your own copies, an existing Sutra; start from auto-design, that Sutra or an empty one), **My designs** (`/build`) and a design's page (`/build/d/{id}`: data and shape tree, Sutra, preview with a sample switcher, Open in Studio). Replaces the console's in-memory sample sets (`builder.ttl_hours` is gone); `/build/shape` redirects to `/build/new#files`. Studio, `/studio?example=` and the help centre examples are unchanged.
- **Changed:** designing and trying are open to every signed-in user; only deploying stays permission-based. Studio, its preview/check/inference against a pasted document, File → Open and the examples, and the Screen Builder (`/build/shape`, `POST /api/v1/builder/shape`, `/design`, `/suggest`) no longer need the `author` power or the right to the pasted document's kind (it is a label, not a permission). Saving, proposing, approving and deleting are unchanged (403 without the right); Studio disables Save/Propose with "Designing is open to everyone; saving needs the author right". Previewing a stored entity (kind + id) still requires the right to its kind and the field masks.
- **Security:** a panel with `source: link(id, kind)` bound against the linked entity's document even when the viewer could not open that kind (links were disabled, sourced data was not). The view pipeline now takes the caller's open-right alongside the redactor and never fetches or binds a sourced or linked entity of a kind the caller may not open: the panel shows "no access to <kind>" (no data, no error) in views, stored and pasted previews, the Pivot tab's records (403), live stream rebuilds, monitors and builder previews.
- **Fixed (DOC-01..22):** documentation brought in line with the code: JDK 25 check, the Calc runtime step (`tools/fetch-pyodide.sh`), `--trades`, key list, error-code tables (DRS-3001 reserved), plugin lists (15), `extends`, and the settings documented nowhere (`drishti.branding`, `drishti.identity`, console `ui.*`, `layouts.min_span`, delta `warm-dates`). New tests keep them honest: `test_docs_error_codes.py`, `test_docs_plugins.py`, `test_docs_settings.py`.
- **Added:** Screen Builder step 1, the shape extractor: `POST /api/v1/builder/shape` (authors) merges up to 50 sample JSON documents into one JSON Schema (required/optional with presence, nullable, conflicts as `oneOf`, maps, merged array items, recursive trees as `$ref`, enums, formats, number ranges) with a role and reason per path (id, link, measure, dimension, status, date, series, ohlc, distribution, grid, steps, graph, tree, events, text) and a report of conflicts and rare fields; limits under `drishti.builder.*`, refused with the new `413 DRS-5005`.
- **Added:** Screen Builder step 2, the shape extractor page: `/build/shape` (Build → Screen Builder; authors) takes up to 50 `.json`/`.jsonl` files by picker or drag-and-drop, refuses over-limit uploads cleanly in the console (`builder.max_samples`, `max_file_mb`, `max_total_mb`) and reports unusable files without failing the rest, then shows conflicts and rare fields first and a keyboard-accessible schema tree (type, role with reason, presence, examples, filter, counts). Download `shape.json` or the plain JSON Schema, copy it, or **Open in Studio** with the first sample pasted. The last set is kept per user in the console's memory for `builder.ttl_hours` (24); nothing is stored or logged but counts. New guide `screen-builder` in the help centre.
- **Added:** Screen Builder step 3, auto-design and suggest: `POST /api/v1/builder/design` (authors) drafts a complete Sutra from sample documents or a shape (title, a strip of at most six figures ranked by role, presence and variety, panels from the fields' roles including pivots with row groups, tree tables, candlesticks, waterfalls and gauges, keys for links, charts side by side), with a reason for every decision, ranked alternatives per panel with their options filled, and pruning: the draft is previewed against every sample and a panel or figure empty or failing for more than `drishti.builder.prune-share` (0.5) of them is demoted or dropped and listed. `POST /api/v1/builder/suggest` ranks panel kinds for one field or a dimension and measure pair. Runtime inference now shares its packing, panel recipes and column rules with it (`LayoutPacker`, `PanelRecipes`; output unchanged). `/build/shape` gains **Draft a screen** and **Open in Studio** with the drafted Sutra. New settings `prune-share`, `strip-max`, `max-panels`, `max-side-panels`, `line-min-points`, `max-alternatives`, `limit-names`.
- **Fixed:** Studio's preview draws expandable row groups (▸/▾ in tree tables and nested pivots): it now loads the same tree and pivot scripts as a view; the all-panels showcase has a desk → book → trade tree table.
- **Fixed (UX-11, UX-14, UX-15, UX-17, UX-18, UX-19, SEC-17):** console polish from the 2026-10-01 QA. Error pages advise to fit the DRS code (`ui.error_advice`), an unknown kind says so, and an unknown console URL gets the console's own 404 (a JSON problem under `/api`). Layout mode keeps a minimum width (`layouts.min_span`, 3), refuses to hide the last visible panel, and announces the height it keeps. Studio marks a preview stale after a failed one, has a heading and a labelled editor, and the review of an approved proposal shows its diff. The function-key bar shows whole panel titles on hover and focus. A help page has one `<h1>`. Calc's SyntaxError shows your code only (full traceback behind Details). Calc's worker can fetch only static files and the Python runtime, so its code cannot call console routes with your session.
- **Fixed:** connectors serving one kind are consulted in the order they are written in the config (after the kind's `routes` entry); the connector map lost that order (`Map.copyOf`). Tests: `SourceRouterTest` (three-plus stores, a rebuild, bound config). Docs: DEVELOPER_GUIDE 2.7, CONNECTOR_GUIDE.
- **Fixed:** `PostgresLoader` names a bad line (invalid JSON, a missing field, `\u0000` in an id, document or column) with its line number and id before anything is published, and a duplicate id in a day is loaded once, the last line winning, as in the JSON-lines connector (the first ten duplicates are named on standard error). Test: `PostgresLoaderRowsTest` (Testcontainers). Docs: POSTGRES_CONNECTOR.
- **Fixed (UX-12):** the Delta connector warms its newest `warm-dates` (3, `0` turns off) in the background after start, and a console page answers a timeout with 504 (the console's own wait too, as `DRS-1004`), not 502. Cold past-date read measured 37-68 ms against 5-13 ms warm on the samples. Tests: `DeltaWarmUpTest`, `test_timeouts.py`.
- **Fixed (UX-16):** a fresh start logs 1-2 WARN lines instead of 126: `spring.jpa.open-in-view` is off, the Delta log-listing, Hibernate incubating and springdoc notices are not warnings (`DRISHTI_API_DOCS`). Test: `QuietStartTest`.
- **Added (SEC-15):** personal API tokens may call the `POST`s that only read, listed in `drishti.security.token-read-posts` (`/api/v1/search/pivot/**`, `/api/v1/command`); every other write stays refused. Test: `IdentityApiTest`.
- **Changed (SEC-16):** `deploy/compose.yaml` requires `DRISHTI_ADMIN_USER` and `DRISHTI_ADMIN_PASSWORD` (the first administrator, via the new `DRISHTI_SEED_USERNAME` / `DRISHTI_SEED_PASSWORD`; the development admin is not created), publishes the server on `127.0.0.1` only; `compose.data.yaml` binds `127.0.0.1`. Only the built-in default password shows the default-password warning. Test: `UserServiceTest`.
- **Docs (SEC-13):** OPERATIONS 9a-1 says plainly that the token secret is a master key, how to protect and rotate it, and the alternatives; the production checklist has the new items.
- **Added:** `source` on every panel kind that reads data, not only `line`: a pivot, candlestick, tabs, graph or any other panel can read a linked entity's document (`source: "link($.desk, 'desk')"`), fetched with the view's sources, business date and field masks; a table's Pivot tab reads it too.
- **Fixed (SEC-12):** the console's `/readyz` calls the server with the console's service identity, so it reports UP with security on (it was always DOWN: the call carried no token).
- **Fixed (SEC-10):** a missing query parameter answers `400 DRS-5001` naming it (it was a 401), and a parameter of the wrong type or a date that is not one (`/search/compare?from=xx`) answers `400 DRS-5001` with no stack trace (it was a 500), both as RFC 7807 problems.
- **Fixed (SEC-11):** Sutra problems name their files relative to the Sutra root (`/api/v1/sutras/problems` and save/preview errors); the absolute paths stay in the server log.
- **Fixed (UX-13):** a console endpoint that reads JSON answers a body that is not JSON, or JSON that is not an object, with a 400 or 415 problem, never a plain 500 (`json_body` checks the shape; `test_json_bodies.py` covers every such route).
- **Fixed (UX-10):** a DRS code appears once in a message: one shared helper (`drs_message` in Python, `drsMessage` in the browser) does not prefix a message that already starts with the code and drops repeats inside it; the missing-entity page, the alerts page and the other pages use it.
- **Fixed (DOC-18):** in-app help links open: repository documents not in the catalogue open at a slug made from their path, anchors are made the way GitHub makes them (`delta--delta-lake`, headings with `<kind>` in them), and `drishti-console/tests/test_help_links.py` finds no dead internal help link.
- **Added:** expandable row groups in Sutra panels. A `pivot` panel's `by` may be a list (`by: [desk, book, productType]`): the rows nest, each group row shows its subtotal and a ▸/▾ toggle, `expand` (a whole number, default 1, or `all`) sets the levels open at first; a single `by` is unchanged. `table` and `ladder` take `children` (an expression per row, such as `"@.children"`) and `expand`: rows with children expand in place, indented, to any depth; columns read each child with `@`, `total: true` sums the leaf rows only, and the filter keeps the ancestors of a match. Bad option types are located `DRS-2029` problems; `drishti.panels.tree-depth` and `tree-rows` bound a tree. The console draws nested pivots with the Pivot tab's grid (`pivot-grid.js`, via the new `tree-rows.js`), keyboard accessible; CSV export lists every row. Tests: `ChartPanelsTest`, `StrictSutraTest`, `test_tree_rows.py` (headless Chromium, skipped without one). Docs: RACHANA_REFERENCE, PANELS, RACHANA_GUIDE, panel-kinds guide, CONFIGURATION.
- **Added (examples):** `docs/guides/examples/`: ten small working Sutras (`all-panels-showcase`, `pivot-row-groups`, `tree-table`, `market-charts`, `risk-distribution`, `pnl-explain`, `relationships`, `operations-status`, `exposure-profile`, `linked-sources`), each with a self-contained JSON document and a note (the last reads live linked entities with `source`), together using all twenty panel kinds, nested pivot groups and tree rows. Studio opens on `all-panels-showcase` (`ui.studio_example`; falls back to the old behaviour), has **File → Open** (`.yaml`/`.yml` and/or `.json`, read in the browser, then previewed) and `/studio?example=<name>`, served by `/studio/example/<name>` from `studio.examples_dir` for names of complete sets only; **Help → Examples** lists each with its note, YAML, JSON and an *Open in Studio* link. Tests: `test_examples.py` (the set covers all twenty kinds, a nested pivot and a tree table; names cannot traverse paths). Docs: QUICKSTART, RACHANA_GUIDE, CONFIGURATION.
- **Docs:** QUICKSTART builds and runs with a system `mvn`, from IntelliJ IDEA and PyCharm, and with a different config (`--spring.config.additional-location`, profiles, the console's local file, env vars, arguments); CONFIGURATION explains the `${NAME:default}` placeholders (precedence, relaxed names, nesting) with a table of every one in both `application.yaml` files, kept in step by `drishti-console/tests/test_docs_placeholders.py`; the developer guide has a tried example config with two file, two Delta, two JDBC and one Kafka connector and how kinds route across them.
- **Fixed (UX-05):** example entities come from the packs switched on, not the finance pack. Plain `/studio` previewed `trade/IRS-48213` with `irs-vanilla@3` and opened on a red `DRS-1001` with any other packs; it now opens on the first example entity of the user's packs (their `console.examples`, as on `/t`) with a Sutra of its kind, or, when no pack names one, empty with a hint (no preview, no error). The new-Sutra template binds no pack's fields. The landing page's hero commands and *Keyboard first* card use the packs' examples (`ui.landing_examples`, 4), a showcase caption names its command only when that pack is installed (`ui.showcase`, now configuration), and the server's `DRS-4001` names the mnemonics it has loaded instead of `TRD IRS-48213`. Tests: `test_samples.py`, `CommandParserTest`. Docs: USER_GUIDE, sutra-studio guide, CONFIGURATION, TROUBLESHOOTING.
- **Fixed (UX-06):** workspaces can be made with any packs. `/w` has **New workspace** (a name, then **Create**: a blank workspace from `blank` in `drishti-console/config/workspaces.yaml`, two empty panes), says so when the packs bring no starters, and `/w/<name>` for a name not yet used offers **Create it** (`?new=1`). Tests: `test_workspaces.py`. Docs: workspaces guide, USER_GUIDE, QUICKSTART, CONFIGURATION.
- **Fixed (UX-07):** `Alt+1`…`Alt+4` move between workspace panes wherever the focus is: a pane (an embedded view, or its error page) hands `Alt+0`…`Alt+4` to the workspace by a same-origin message, and the workspace acts only on messages from its own panes. `Alt+0` returns from a pane to the workspace's bar, so keyboard users are never stuck in a pane; an empty pane takes the focus in its command box. Test: `test_workspace_keys_browser.py` (Chromium; skipped without Playwright). Docs: workspaces guide, USER_GUIDE, PYTHON_CALC, QUICKSTART.
- **Fixed (UX-08):** a picked date that no dated store holds no longer passes current data off as that date. The view said *murex-rates is not a dated source* (the kind has a dated store; it lacked the date) and, in the top bar and in workspace panes, *Live*. It now says *No data held for <date>: no dated store has <id> for that date*, names the undated source whose current data is shown instead, as a still snapshot (no live updates in a page or pane, the top bar says *Static*), with *Back to live*. Tests: `test_terminal.py`. Docs: USER_GUIDE, GETTING_STARTED, QUICKSTART, TROUBLESHOOTING, the connector guides, ADR-012.
- **Fixed (UX-09):** pivot groups of numbers read `4.240872601E7` on a search pivot. Numbers as group keys are written plainly, to at most 15 significant digits (`42408726.01`, `0.3`, never an exponent), the same by the server (`PivotCube.key`) and the client engine (`pivot-engine.js`), so a panel's pivot and a search's agree. Tests: `PivotCubeTest`, `test_pivot.py`. Docs: USER_GUIDE, pivot-tab guide.
- **Fixed (GRAM-04):** field names in searches and pick lists are case-insensitive, as QUICKSTART and the search page promised: `trd producttype=revolver` matches what `TRD productType=Revolver` does (`COUNTERPARTY.NAME`, `LEGS[0].Rate` too), and the result columns use the kind's own spelling. A field no entity of the kind has is `400 DRS-4004 no trade has a field 'nosuchfield'; did you mean …?` instead of an empty result. Names are resolved in one place (`FieldNames`): against the kind's promoted columns and key fields first (so the columnar search still answers), then the documents the search read; a name is not reported when the scan was partial. The search pivot reads names the same way. Test: `SearchFieldNamesTest`. Docs: QUICKSTART, USER_GUIDE, API_GUIDE, TROUBLESHOOTING.
- **Fixed (GRAM-05):** invalid Sutras are no longer accepted silently. New `DRS-2033` for YAML that would not be read as written: a key written twice in one mapping (YAML kept the last), a second document after `---` (ignored), a tag other than the core ones (`!panel`, `!!binary`). `match.kind: 42`, `match.where` that is not text and `match.priority: high` / `1e99` are `DRS-2012`; a written `title` without `id` is `DRS-2010`; table `rows: 5` (and `each`, `nodes`, `edges`, `source` not written as text), table `limit: many` / `-5` / `"6"`, table and ladder `search: maybe`, `kv`/`status` `fields: 5`, `area` `series: 5` and markdown `text: [1, 2]` are `DRS-2029`; all with line and column. The JSON Schema says the same (title needs `id`, table `limit` an integer from 1, `fields` and `series` lists). The finance pack's `book-pnl` Sutra had `rachana: 1` twice; fixed. Test: `StrictSutraTest`. Docs: RACHANA_REFERENCE (problem codes, top level, title, options), TROUBLESHOOTING.
- **Fixed (GRAM-06):** `limit 999999999999` in a search no longer leaks a Java error ("For input string …"), and `limit 0` no longer quietly becomes 1 (nor `limit 5000` 1000): a limit outside 1 to 1000, or not a number, is `400 DRS-4004 limit must be a whole number from 1 to 1000, not '0'`. The console passes a typed `limit <anything>` on for the server to check. Test: `SearchFieldNamesTest.aLimitOutsideItsRangeSaysTheRange`. Docs: USER_GUIDE, API_GUIDE, TROUBLESHOOTING.
- **Fixed (GRAM-07):** clearer messages. A search condition that stops short (`TRD where mtm >`) says `the condition ends early: something is missing after '>'` instead of `unexpected '' at 7`, and Rachana-EL says `the expression ends early: a value is missing` / `expected ']' but the expression ends`; an out-of-range Sutra `version` (`99999999999999999999`) is `DRS-2020 version must be a positive integer up to 2147483647`, not YAML syntax (`DRS-2001`); the unknown-function message lists the functions alphabetically without brackets; Studio's check says `line 7 is indented with a tab: YAML allows only spaces` instead of "needs a colon"; a phrase search without a kind suggests `a kind such as counterparty (CPTY), trade (TRD)` instead of a bracketed list with guessed plurals. Tests: `StrictSutraTest.expressionMessagesSayWhatIsWrong`, `StrictSutraTest.anOutOfRangeVersionIsAVersionProblemNotYamlSyntax`, `SearchFieldNamesTest.aConditionThatStopsShortSaysSo`, `PhraseParserTest`, `test_studio_check_js.py`. Docs: RACHANA_REFERENCE, RACHANA_GUIDE, USER_GUIDE, API_GUIDE, TROUBLESHOOTING.
- **Fixed (GRAM-08):** `POST /api/v1/studio/preview` with `{"yaml": null}` answered 500 (a NullPointerException); a body that is not JSON, empty, or JSON of the wrong shape answered Spring's bare 400. Now each is `400 DRS-5001` problem+json saying what is missing (`'yaml' is required: the Sutra text to preview`, `'kind' …`, `'id' …` without a pasted `document`) or `the request body is not valid JSON` — on every endpoint for unreadable bodies. The console's `/studio/preview` and `/studio/test` check the body the same way. Tests: `StudioTest.aPreviewRequestThatCannotBeReadIsACleanProblem`, `test_gram_inputs.py`. Docs: API_GUIDE.
- **Fixed (GRAM-09):** an invalid or out-of-range business date (`9999-99-99`, `2026-02-30`, `2030-01-01`, `1900-01-01`) picked through `/asof` was stored in the `drishti_asof` cookie and made every page a `DRS-4003` error for 12 hours. The console now checks it first (a real date, not after today in the server's business zone, not before its history window) and stays on the current date with *Pick a business date from <earliest> to today*; a stored date the server refuses (say, after the history window moved on) is ignored, the page is live and says so, and the cookie is cleared. Tests: `test_gram_inputs.py`. Docs: USER_GUIDE, TROUBLESHOOTING.
- **Fixed (DATA-07):** a promoted JSON-lines field that is a number on most lines and text on others (`"mtm": "N/A"`) made searches answered from columns disagree with documents: the column became text, ordered lexicographically (`'999478'` before `'1.2e22'`), a condition above 1e19 matched nothing, and `1e20` was stored as `9223372036854775807`. Such a field is now a mixed column (`ColumnSet.mixed`) holding each value as the document does, numbers unclamped; searches order and compare it as documents do (one total order: numbers by value, then text), and impact and derived sums read its numbers.
- **Fixed (DATA-08):** file connector reverse lookups skipped every `effective`-mode kind, so Impact (F8) of a netting set on the `files` profile lacked the counterparty and credit-limit groups other stores show. Effective kinds are now looked up in each entity's version on the date (days newest first, each entity in its newest line, `max-load-rows` lines in all).
- **Fixed (DATA-12):** a store that holds a date is authoritative for it. A recent store that dropped a trade no longer has it brought back from the lake behind (view 200 from the lake while search said 0): the read is `404 DRS-1001 <store> holds trade for <date> and does not list …`, a search lists the kind only up to that store, and columns come from it or from documents. Only dates the store does not hold pass on; a failing store still stops the read with `DRS-1003`. Plugins say what they hold through `SourcePlugin.coverage(kind, asOf)` (`DateCoverage`); the file connector does for dated JSON-lines snapshot days.
- **Fixed (DATA-15):** `knownAt` was silently ignored by stores without time travel (the files store answered 200 with today's data). A dated store that keeps no earlier versions (`SourcePlugin.timeTravel()` false; Delta Lake and Iceberg are true) and may hold the date now refuses with `400 DRS-1007` naming it; a search is `partial` and names it in `failed`. Never today's data.
- **Fixed (DATA-16):** after a row was deleted in place with a deletion vector (Databricks or Spark `DELETE`), type-ahead still offered its id and opening it gave 404: the Delta connector's id map read the id column as stored. A file that carries a deletion vector is now read through Kernel with the vector applied (id column only, both the native and the hadoop engine); files without one are read as before. The test fixture that writes deletion vectors now names the file's current vector in its `remove` and keeps the rows earlier deletes removed, so sequential deletes make a valid log. Tests: `DeltaDeletionVectorTest` (`theIdMapLeavesOutDeletedRows`, `twoSequentialDeletesFromOneFile`, type-ahead in `aRowDeletedWithADeletionVectorIsGone`). DELTA_CONNECTOR § 6.2, 12.
- **Fixed (DATA-17):** ordered searches had no tie-break, so on PostgreSQL and JDBC query mode (rows in physical order) a `limit` kept different tied rows from run to run. Every path now orders equal values by id (entities without the sort value last).
- **Fixed (DATA-21):** ids containing `/` could not be opened through the API (`%2F` is refused in a path). Every `{kind}/{id}` endpoint now also takes `~` in place of the id and the id as the `id` query parameter (`GET /api/v1/views/trade/~?id=sl%2Fash-6`); the console, its entity pages and the Python client use it when an id needs it. Encoded slashes in paths stay refused (SEC-02).
- **Fixed (DATA-19):** JDBC query mode. One failing part query made every view of the kind fail with a generic `DRS-1003 … failed reading` (the SQL error only in the log); the error now names the query: `… trade MX-1 cannot be read: its query query.trade.legs failed (SQL state 42703); Admin → Health and the server log say more` (its SQL and the database's message are not shown to readers; they go to the server log, once per distinct failure, and to Health, `DEGRADED: query.trade.legs failed: …`, until it runs again). A `columns.<kind>` query that returns an id more than once (a join with a child table) has each id counted once, with its first row, and is reported in the log and in Health (`UP (columns.trade returned 5 rows for 2 entities …)`), instead of multiplying search counts and impact totals. A statement that fails on a live connection no longer marks the source `DOWN … (reconnecting)` (only a lost connection does). Test: `QueryModeProblemsTest`. [JDBC_QUERIES § 5, 7, 12, 13](plugins/drishti-plugin-jdbc/README.md#query-mode-parts).
- **Changed (DATA-11): `RedisLoader` now REPLACES each business day it loads; `--merge` restores the old behaviour.** Upgrade note: a load of part of a day, or an intraday correction (`--publish`), must now pass `--merge`, or it replaces the day with that part (a replacement that would drop more than `--max-drop-share`, 0.5, of a day's entities is refused, nothing switched, unless `--force-drop`). Before, every load merged, so a trade dropped from the book could never be removed by reloading (the 10,000-trade book then the 8,000-trade book left 10,000 on the day). Replacing is atomic for readers, like the PostgreSQL, DuckDB and file loaders: the day's documents and columns are written under a generation of the load that no reader looks at, then each day is switched in one step (one script sets `{<domain>:<kind>:days}:gens` and the kind's days), and the replaced generation expires `--keep-replaced-seconds` (120) later; readers see the old day or the new one, never a mix (before, documents were overwritten as they arrived, even with `--replace`). A replacing load that dies switches nothing and the next load deletes what it wrote. Days loaded before keep working (no generation: the keys without a suffix). The connector reads each day in its current generation (an effective kind now takes two round trips: `ZREVRANGEBYSCORE`, then `MGET`; the read script is gone, so the connector's ACL no longer needs `EVAL`/`EVALSHA`, the loader does). `tools/load-redis.sh` passes `--merge`/`--keep-replaced-seconds` and merges the samples when it also loads a bulk book. Tests: `RedisLoaderReplaceTest` (`aLoadReplacesEachDayByDefault`, `whileADayIsReplacedReadersSeeTheOldDayThenTheNewOneNeverAMix`, `mergeAddsToADayAndKeepsWhatTheStreamDoesNotCarry`, `replacingADayWithAFewOfItsEntitiesNeedsForceDrop`). [REDIS_CONNECTOR § 2, 4, 5](plugins/drishti-plugin-redis/README.md#loading), DEMO_DATA, CONNECTOR_GUIDE.
- **Fixed (DATA-22):** with Redis down, each read waited for its timeout (a 504 after 2 s through the server, 3 s in the test) and each search 8 s. The Redis connector now fails fast while its health says the store is down (the connection dropped, a read or column read failed, the catalogue could not be read): reads and column reads fail at once with `DRS-1003 … the Redis store is not reachable; reads fail at once until it answers again …` (no host or credentials), searches are `partial` at once, and reverse lookups answer none. One check every `recheck-ms` (1000) pings Redis and resumes reads as soon as it answers. Settings `fail-fast` (true) and `recheck-ms`. Tests: `RedisFailFastTest` (Redis paused and resumed; Redis stopped). REDIS_CONNECTOR § 11-12, PLUGIN_GUIDE, OPERATIONS.
- **Fixed (flaky test):** `DiskCacheTest.storesReadsDeletesAndClears` failed intermittently with "Failed to delete temp directory … gen-…". A cleared disk-cache generation is closed and deleted by a task on the scheduler; when that task had not run yet, `DiskCache.close()` returned with the old generation's RocksDB still open and its background threads still writing into its directory (and `shutdownNow` could drop the task, leaving it open for good). `close()` now disposes of every cleared generation nobody is inside before it returns; each generation is disposed of exactly once, by the scheduler or by `close()`. Test: `closeDisposesOfClearedGenerationsBeforeReturning` (a busy scheduler); the test class passed 20 consecutive runs.
- **Fixed (flaky test):** `tools/samplegen/test_layout.py` could hang the drill for good (once 30 minutes, 63 threads in futex wait): `bulk_trades.py` forked its worker pool from a process where pyarrow and deltalake had already started threads, so a child could inherit a lock no thread would ever release (Python's "os.fork() was called … multi-threaded" warning). Its pools now use the `spawn` start method, and `tools/drill.sh` runs the two lake test files under a 10-minute `timeout`, so a hang fails the drill instead of blocking it. Test: `test_workers_are_spawned_not_forked_from_a_threaded_process` (no fork warning with a thread alive). DEVELOPER_GUIDE § 2.6.
- **Fixed (DATA-14):** `drishti.quant.year_fraction` follows the ISDA 2006 definitions. `30E/360` (`EUROBOND`) caps both the start and the end day at 30 (2026-01-15 to 2026-03-31 is 75/360, 2026-02-28 to 2026-08-31 182/360; it was computed as US 30/360, which `30/360` and `BOND` still are); `ACT/ACT`, `ACT/ACT ISDA` and `AA` split the period by calendar year, each year's days over 365 or 366 (a calendar year is exactly 1.0; it was days/365.25). Tests: `test_30e_360_moves_the_31st_to_the_30th_on_both_dates`, `test_act_act_isda_splits_the_period_by_calendar_year`. [PYTHON_CALC § 17](docs/guides/USER_GUIDE.md#calc-python-on-any-view).
- **Fixed (DATA-20):** `drishti.quant` edge cases. Black-Scholes, Black-76 (and Garman-Kohlhagen) and Bachelier at expiry or with zero vol price the discounted intrinsic value of the forward, 0 at the money, instead of NaN; `norm_ppf` takes its Halley step's residual on the near tail, so `norm_ppf(1 - 1e-12)` is exact to 1e-16 (it was off by 1e-9), and its docstring states the measured bound (relative error below 1e-15 outside 0.4..0.6, absolute below 1e-14 everywhere); `month_code_years` is 0, not negative, in the contract month once its middle has passed (`V6` on 2026-10-20). Tests: `test_options_at_expiry_or_zero_vol_are_worth_their_intrinsic_value`, `test_norm_ppf_is_accurate_in_the_far_tails`, `test_a_month_code_for_the_current_month_is_never_negative`.
- **Fixed (UX-02):** no console page scrolls sideways on a phone. At 390 px every page with the top bar was 419 px wide, with Live and the avatar cut off; admin pages were 603 px (the tab row) and My account 646 px (its tables). Below 640 px the top bar tightens: the command line shrinks first, the date input is compact, Live shows its dot (the word stays for screen readers), and the date controls wrap when time travel adds more; below 480 px the brand shows its mark only. The admin tab row wraps and the account tables scroll inside their own container. Test: `test_page_widths_browser.py` (Chromium through Playwright: every console page and help guide at 390, 1600 and 2560 px; skipped without Playwright). Docs: USER_GUIDE (On a phone), ARCHITECTURE, DEVELOPER_GUIDE.
- **Fixed (UX-03):** help-centre screenshots fit their column at every width and keep their shape (they were up to 1440 px wide, pushing guides to 1922 px at 1600 px); each opens full size in a new tab. Tests: `test_help.py::test_guide_screenshots_fit_their_column_and_open_full_size`, `test_page_widths_browser.py`.
- **Fixed (UX-04):** every theme's text meets WCAG AA contrast. `--d-faint` (the footer, "No data available", placeholders, key notes) read at 2.6–4.4:1 in six of seven themes and the light theme's amber, used as text, at 3.35–3.98:1. Each theme's faint is now the dimmest shade of its hue that reads at 4.5:1 on all four of its grounds, the light theme's amber and ok green are a shade deeper, and a new token, `--d-on-accent`, gives accent buttons a label that reads on them (white on parchment amber and crimson, whose buttons were 2.5:1). Placeholders use faint; Bootstrap's pink inline code and grey outline buttons take the theme's colours. `test_contrast.py` checks every text colour on every ground in all seven themes, labels on accent fills, that the CSS colours text only with checked tokens, and the light fallback. Docs: USER_GUIDE (Themes), PANELS, ARCHITECTURE.
- **Fixed (UX-01):** six tabs on live views no longer freeze a seventh page. Browsers allow six connections to a site over HTTP/1.1 and each tab held its own live channel, so the next page of the console never loaded, with no message. Now each **browser** holds one live channel, whatever the number of tabs and workspace panes: `channel.js` hands every tab's subscriptions to a hub (`live-hub.js`) in a SharedWorker, or, without one, in a tab elected with a Web Lock that relays over a BroadcastChannel (another tab takes over when it closes). A view open in several tabs is subscribed once; a later tab gets the view's opening events at once. Frames are still built by the console for the signed-in user (permissions and field masks): pages carry their session's fingerprint (`<meta name="drishti-live">`), the channel's first event says whose session it runs as (`who`), and the hub serves only matching tabs (`GET /api/channel/who` settles a sign-in in another tab). Page loads never wait for live updates; a channel that cannot be had within 10 s shows `Reconnecting…`, and a refused one is retried. Reconnect after a restart, hidden tabs, the Live pill and `deleted` frames work as before. A browser follows at most `live.max_subscriptions` (32, console configuration) live things; one more is told so (`gone`, `DRS-5003`) instead of silently not ticking. Tests: `test_live_tabs_browser.py` (Chromium: eight live tabs and a four-pane workspace, with and without SharedWorker; skipped without Playwright), `test_live_hub.py` (the hub protocol in Node, and the console's side). Docs: LIVE.md, USER_GUIDE, ARCHITECTURE, CONFIGURATION, OPERATIONS, TROUBLESHOOTING, DEVELOPER_GUIDE, the live-latency runbook, the workspaces guide.
- **Fixed (SEC-02):** the server's token filter could be skipped by spelling an API path differently: `/api/v1;x/…` and `/api/%761/…` were served as `/api/v1/…` but the filter tested the raw request line, so about, packs, sources, Sutras, the Rachana schema, the business date, live stats and alert suggestions answered without a token. Filters now decide on the decoded path the dispatcher serves (`RequestPaths.routed`; the management guard on `/actuator` and `/api/docs` too), and a new `PathGuard` refuses, security on or off, any request line under `/api` or `/actuator` that does not spell that path plainly (a `;` path parameter, a percent-encoded letter, digit, `- . _ ~`, `/` or `\`, a malformed escape, a dot or empty segment) with `400 DRS-5001` problem+json. Encoded spaces, `;`, `%`, parentheses and non-ASCII letters in names and ids still work. [API_GUIDE](docs/guides/DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md#114-who-you-are-authentication), TROUBLESHOOTING.
- **Adversarial QA of 1.13.0** ([docs/qa/2026-10-01](CHANGELOG.md)): security and access control, data correctness and connectors, UX, grammar and documentation; 10 high, 33 medium, 36 low and 15 informational findings with activity logs, reproduction scripts and a proposed fix order. Nothing fixed yet.
- **Fixed (DATA-02):** one unreadable line no longer erases a JSON-lines day. The file connector skips and counts a truncated line, a line that is not a JSON object or has no id, a line longer than `max-document-mb` (new, 64 MB; a 25 MB trade document is read) or nested deeper than `max-nesting-depth` (new, 1000), with line numbers and why; logs it once per version of the file; shows it in Health (`UP (1 unreadable line in trading/2026-09-30/trade.jsonl (line 201: …))`) and the cache statistics (`unreadableLines`, `unreadableFiles`, `indexBuilds`); and the day's columns say why they may be missing entities (`ColumnSet.incomplete()`, new in the plugin API). `NaN` and `Infinity`, as Python's `json.dumps` writes them, are read as no value. A file that cannot be read is indexed once, until it changes, instead of on every request ([FILE_CONNECTOR.md › 3](plugins/drishti-plugin-file/README.md#data-structure)).
- **Fixed (DATA-06):** JSON-lines rows whose `doc` is a JSON object and that carry no `columns` now have their promoted fields read from the document, as rows with `doc` as a string always had; searches, pick lists and derived kinds over such files were empty.
- **Fixed (DATA-09):** an id on several lines of a JSON-lines day is one entity, its last line (as a reload leaves it): the view, searches, columns, derived kinds and reverse lookups agree and count it once. The ids repeated are counted (`duplicateIds`) and named in Health.
- **Fixed (DATA-10):** a read racing an atomic replace of a JSON-lines file no longer fails (502) or reads with the old file's offsets: a day's index holds the file it read open, and a read that finds the file rewritten in place builds the index again and reads again.
- **Roadmap: server-side pricing.** A design for a QuantLib pricing service behind the Drishti server ([QUANT_SERVICE.md](docs/guides/AI_GUIDE.md#4-server-side-pricing-the-quant-service-proposed), [ADR-019](docs/architecture/adr/019-pricing-is-a-quantlib-service-behind-the-server.md), proposed), now first on the roadmap in [IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md](docs/architecture/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md#roadmap).
- **Fixed:** the server no longer opens an unused MongoDB client to `localhost:27017` at every start (and logs connection errors when no MongoDB runs). The MongoDB driver ships for the `mongodb` plugin, which makes its own client only when configured; Spring Boot's MongoDB auto-configuration is now excluded.
- **Fixed (DATA-04):** loaders never leave a business day empty or half loaded for readers. `PostgresLoader` COPYs into a stage nobody reads and publishes each (kind, business date) in one transaction (delete, insert, `entity_dates`); `--recreate` builds a shadow schema swapped in in one transaction; a load that fails or is killed leaves every day as it was (the next load drops its stage), two loads of one day are serialised, and the table catalogue re-reads a day's columns that were loaded again while it read them. Reloads of 10,000 trades × 3 days cost about a tenth more (1.65–1.96 s against 1.52–1.81 s). `RedisLoader` journals each id before its document, so the next load (or the failing one) deletes documents a dead load wrote that no day's columns list, and gains `--replace` (merging, still the default, is documented). `MongoLoader` hides a new day in `<domain>_loading` until its load has finished. DuckDB, Iceberg and the JSON-lines files were already atomic per day (checked).
- **Fixed (DATA-05):** one mis-dated row can no longer wipe a store's history. Every loader (PostgreSQL, DuckDB, MongoDB, Redis, Iceberg, Aerospike, JSON-lines files) quarantines rows dated after tomorrow in the business zone (`--future-days`, `--zone`) and ends with an error naming them; retention (`--keep-months`, `--keep-days`, `--ttl-days`, `IcebergMaintenance --keep-days`, `maintain.py keep-business-days`) counts back from `--as-of` (today), never from the newest date loaded; and a run that would drop more than `--max-drop-share` (0.5) of a table drops nothing unless `--force-drop` (`maintain.py`: `max-drop-share`, `--force-drop`, `--as-of`).
- **Checked:** a lake maintained by `tools/lake/maintain.py` (compaction, re-sorting, checkpoints, vacuum) reads identically through the native Delta engine: the same documents and search rows as the unmaintained lake.
- **Fixed (DATA-01):** a source that failed or timed out while a kind was listed or read made a search look exact and empty (`matched 0, scanned 0, partial: false`). The router now reports each source that failed, timed out or says its listing is incomplete (`SourcePlugin.listingProblem`), with why; searches, pivots and the pack overview are then partial, and the answer's new `failed` list (`[{source, reason}]`) names them, as the console's search page does (*Incomplete: 1 source could not be read*). A column set a source marks `incomplete` counts the same way (Calc columns and impact groups carry the reason). A Delta table whose ids cannot be re-indexed keeps the ids it listed before, logs it and shows it in Health, instead of dropping the kind from type-ahead.
- **Fixed (DATA-03):** a store that failed could still count as "not held", so the next store answered with different data (and views and searches disagreed): the file connector took any unreadable day's file for one that went away; the DuckDB, PostgreSQL (table mode) and MongoDB connectors answered "not held" for every read until their first catalogue read succeeded. They now fail the read (`DRS-1003` naming the connector, as CONNECTOR_GUIDE §1 says); only a store that knows it does not hold the entity passes the read on. A JSON-lines day whose file cannot be read at all fails reads and makes searches partial (its columns are not replaced by another store's); a day with some unreadable lines is served without them, partial (DATA-02). PLUGIN_GUIDE says when to return empty and when to throw.
- **Fixed (DATA-13):** a Delta date with LZ4 Parquet pages failed with a generic `502 DRS-1003 … failed reading`; the codec and the advice were only logged. The error now says it (`…: trade 2026-09-30 cannot be read: the native Delta engine does not decompress LZ4 Parquet pages …; rewrite the date with Snappy or ZSTD (tools/lake/maintain.py relayout --force --dates <date>)`), on either engine, and Health names the table and date. DELTA_CONNECTOR §16 no longer advises `engine: hadoop`: it cannot read delta-rs/Arrow LZ4 either (it reads `LZ4_RAW`); `maintain.py relayout --force` rewrites the date in Snappy, which both engines read (tested).
- **Fixed (DATA-18):** Health said `UP` for Delta tables it could not read (a broken log, a truncated Parquet file, an unsupported codec). A Delta connector is now `DEGRADED: cannot read <kind> <date|log>: <why>` until a read of it succeeds or the table gets a new version; Admin → Health shows degraded connectors in amber, counts them (`summary.sourcesDegraded`) and the overall status is `DEGRADED`. A Redis connector is `DOWN` as soon as its connection drops or a read fails, not at its next refresh (about 20 s later before).
- **Fixed (GRAM-01):** a Sutra with a deeply nested expression (hundreds of parentheses) no longer stops the server from starting. Rachana-EL expressions are bounded (`drishti.rachana.max-expression-depth`, 200 levels; `max-expression-length`, 10,000 characters) and one beyond the bounds is a located `DRS-2101` problem; any other failure while reading one Sutra file is that file's problem (`DRS-2032`, logged), never a failed start ([RACHANA_REFERENCE › Size limits](docs/guides/RACHANA_REFERENCE.md#size-limits)).
- **Fixed (GRAM-02):** such a file no longer silently kills Sutra hot reload: the watcher survives any failure in one file, reports it in `GET /api/v1/sutras/problems` and the log, and keeps loading later edits. `GET /api/v1/admin/health` shows `sutras.hotReload` (`WATCHING`, `OFF`, or `STOPPED: <reason>`, which makes the overall status `DEGRADED`).
- **Fixed (GRAM-03):** a very long expression (a 5000-term `+` chain) is refused at load (`DRS-2101`) instead of loading and failing its view with HTTP 500; alert rules, search conditions, history paths and Studio previews refuse it with a 4xx and a code. Should a panel's evaluation still fail (limits raised far beyond the default), that panel shows `DRS-2102` and the rest of the view renders.
- **Fixed (SEC-01):** disabling or demoting a user now ends or narrows their console session. Each console sign-in is a session the server keeps (`drishti_session`, by a SHA-256 of its id; `POST`/`GET`/`DELETE /api/v1/auth/sessions`, for the console's service identity only); the console checks it per request and takes the user's roles, enabled flag and password-change flag from the server, not the cookie, reusing an answer for `auth.recheck_seconds` (10 s, `DRISHTI_SESSION_RECHECK_SECONDS`) and forgetting it at once when an administrator changes the user on that console. Disabling, deleting or resetting the password of a user ends all their sessions (enabling them again revives none), and a disabled user can no longer create API tokens (`403`). Cookies from before carry no session: everyone signs in once more after the upgrade; upgrade the server and the console together.
- **Fixed (SEC-05):** sign-out ends the session on the server, so a copy of the old cookie no longer signs anyone in (`signed-out` in the audit log).
- **Fixed (SEC-06):** "must change password at first sign-in" is enforced: until the password is changed, the console answers only *My account*, the password change and sign-out; other pages lead back to *My account* and console API calls answer `403 DRS-6010` (new code). *My account* then shows only the password form, and opens the terminal once it is changed.
- **Fixed (SEC-08):** console state-changing requests (`POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`) whose `Origin` (or `Referer`) is another site are refused (`403 DRS-5002`); `auth.allowed_origins` adds origins for a proxy that changes the `Host` header. JSON routes refuse a body not sent as `application/json` (`415`), and sign-out is a `POST` (the user menu posts a form; `GET /logout` only asks). Documented in OPERATIONS 8.4.
- **Fixed (SEC-03):** field masks mean the same everywhere. A field in `drishti.security.redact` (for roles without `raw`) was masked in raw JSON, search, CSV, compare, history, Calc and pivots but shown in views: the header strip (`MTM (USD) +1,875,863`), the title (`Meridian Reinsurance Ltd`), tables, the Pivot tab's panel records, the live stream, monitors and the console's panel CSV export. The server now masks documents in one place (`Entitlements.redactor`) before the view pipeline, its records, live rebuilds, monitors and Studio previews read them; the Sutra and layout are still chosen from the document as stored. The mask stands for the whole field (`counterparty.name` reads `•••` when `counterparty` is masked) and Rachana-EL carries it through: anything computed from it is `•••` (`fmt`, arithmetic, `link`, `sum`), every format shows `•••`, a condition on it is never true (`!` included), a table total or pivot-panel value over it reads `•••` and a chart leaves it out. CONFIGURATION, USER_GUIDE, API_GUIDE, PYTHON_CALC, USER_MANAGEMENT, ARCHITECTURE, OPERATIONS, PACKS and RACHANA_REFERENCE state the policy ([CONFIGURATION › Field masks](docs/admin/CONFIGURATION.md#field-masks)). Alert rules now see the document as their owner may (a rule on a masked field never fires, a message shows `•••`), and phrase search names no values of a masked field.
- **Fixed (SEC-04):** Impact (F8) honours field masks. A user who sees `counterparty` masked found no trades of `CP-MERIDIAN-RE` by search, but Impact listed 200 with their MTM and a total of −1,047,715,039. An entity tied to the analysed one only through a masked field is no longer a dependent for that user (when some reference fields are masked and others not, each dependent's document is checked); a masked measure reads `•••`, and so does its group's total (never added up); a masked follow field rolls nothing up.
- **Fixed (SEC-07):** the type-ahead no longer shows or matches masked values. For a user with masks, each entity suggestion is described from its view title as the user sees it (`Rates · Interest rate swap (fixed/float) · •••` instead of the source's `… · Meridian Reinsurance Ltd · AUD 242m`) and kept only when the text typed is in its id or that description: typing `Meridian` no longer finds `MX-20000001` through its masked counterparty.
- **Fixed (SEC-14):** a pivot on a field under a masked one (`counterparty.name` with `counterparty` masked) grouped under `(blank)`; it now groups under `•••`, lists the field in `masked`, and is never added up, as the documentation says.
- **Fixed (SEC-09):** the file connector confined an entity file to the feed root but not to its kind's folder, so an id such as `../other-kind/x` (or a kind such as `trade/../other-kind`) could read another kind's file. A kind is now one folder name directly under the root or a day folder, and an id's file must lie inside that folder; JSON-lines files are `<kind>.jsonl` beside the day only. Over HTTP such ids were already refused earlier (hardening). Test: `FileSourcePluginTest.anIdCannotReachAnotherKindsFolder`. Docs: PLUGIN_GUIDE.

## 1.13.0 — A million trades a day, eight stores, Calc, pivots, twenty panel kinds and JDK 25 (2026-10-01)
- **Fixed:** an area chart's dashed limit line was not drawn when the limit was above (or below) every value, because the axis was scaled to the series only. The axis now reaches the limit, and the label sits inside the plot.
- **Every panel kind, by example** ([RACHANA_GUIDE.md › 10](docs/guides/RACHANA_REFERENCE.md#panels-the-twenty-two-kinds-and-developing-a-new-one)).
  The Rachana tutorial has a contents list and a new chapter with a complete, minimal Sutra for each of the twenty
  panel kinds, each on a sample entity that ships with the banking packs (`TRD BBG-60000001`, `NSET NS-NORTHBRIDGE-FRA`,
  `CPTY CP-NORTHBRIDGE`, `VAR VAR-COMM`, `CMDV CMDV-BRENT`, `PNL PNL-COMM-1`, `LE LE-FRA`, `CMD CMD-BRENT`,
  `DESK DESK-COMM`): what the kind is for, each option it uses, what you should see (read from the server), and one
  common mistake with its problem code. Then the layout keys (`area`, `span`, `height`, and the comma trap in a
  one-line panel), and the twenty kinds together on seven screens, the largest a government bond trade with twelve
  kinds arranged on the grid. The in-app Sutra guide's *The twenty panel kinds* gains the seven newer kinds it lacked
  and a new section 8 with each kind as a complete Sutra and three screenshots of the combined screens. Every example
  was previewed through Studio on a scratch server with no problem and no empty panel, and `DocumentedSutrasTest`
  checks them all. The reference now says 20 kinds where it said 13, and that `heat: "yes"` (not an unquoted `yes`,
  which YAML reads as `true`) is `DRS-2029`.
- **Calc without JavaScript Promise Integration, run in a real Firefox** ([PYTHON_CALC.md › Reading data](docs/guides/USER_GUIDE.md#52-reading-data)).
  The `_async` fallback had never run outside Chromium. Run in Firefox 155 (Playwright's build) on the sample data,
  with JSPI on and with it switched off (`javascript.options.wasm_js_promise_integration: false`; Firefox 155 has it on
  by default): the panel detects its absence, `view` works, the `_async` reads work, and now every starter snippet runs
  too. Changes: the two pack snippets that read (`desk_pnl_by_book.py`, `mtm_concentration.py`, from
  `tools/packgen/banking/calc_snippets.py`) use `await drishti.search_async(...)`, so they run in every browser; a plain
  read without JSPI says exactly how to write it (*write `await drishti.get_async('trade', 'MX-20000001')` instead*);
  a last line that is an un-awaited `_async` read is awaited; a "'coroutine' object" error says to add `await`; and
  the panel says how to read before a run fails (a note beside the output tabs, and a line in its empty state).
  A console test imports the module with Pyodide stood in as a browser without JSPI would answer, and another keeps
  every pack snippet on the `_async` forms.
- **A review shows moved panels as moves** ([USER_GUIDE.md › Layout mode](docs/guides/USER_GUIDE.md#layout-mode-arrange-a-view-your-way)).
  A layout promotion (Sutra version N against N+1) used to show a moved panel block as a deleted block and an added one,
  hiding the one real edit in it. The review page and the promote drawer now list each moved panel in words, *moved:
  DV01 by tenor (USD) from position 3 to 1 (side → main)* (positions within the column), and show only the real edits
  as a line diff; **Full line diff** keeps the plain diff one click away. `drishti-console/core/sutra_diff.py` matches panel
  blocks by id (with the comments above them), finds the ones out of order with a longest common subsequence per
  column, and diffs the old text with its blocks in the new order. A Sutra it cannot read as a panel list (a flow
  list, duplicate ids) gets the full diff, so nothing is hidden. `GET /api/layout/{sutra}/{kind}/promotion` adds
  `moves` and `edits` beside `diff`. The review's diff no longer shows a blank line between every two lines.
- **Waterfalls rise green and fall red** ([PANELS.md › waterfall](docs/guides/RACHANA_REFERENCE.md#waterfall)). Steps now
  take the theme's good and bad colours (`--d-ok`, `--d-bad`) in every theme, light and dark, and totals are a neutral
  grey (`--d-muted`) instead of the link blue. A new option, `colors: gain-loss | theme` (default `gain-loss`), keeps
  the theme's positive and negative colours (blue and orange, which readers with red-green colour blindness tell
  apart). Any other value is `DRS-2029`; the Rachana schema lists both values, so Studio completes and checks them.
  Bars are solid now, and a contrast test holds every theme's waterfall colours to 3:1 against the panel.
- **Deletes reach open views** ([LIVE.md › Deleted entities](docs/architecture/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md#deleted-entities)). A Kafka
  tombstone (or an envelope with `"doc": null`) and an ActiveMQ or RabbitMQ delete used to remove the entity from the
  store while open views kept showing it, and Kafka kept the id in type-ahead until a restart. Now the connector pushes
  the deletion through the view's existing subscription, the server sends it on the live stream as a `deleted` patch
  with the time of the delete, and the console greys the view under a banner, *"MX-29000001 was deleted at 1 Oct 2026,
  09:30:05 by its source"*, with `Deleted` in the top bar; it is not an error page. An entity that comes back repaints
  the view (a `restored` patch). The id leaves type-ahead at once, and the command line's "recent" list too.
  - **SPI:** `EntityDocument` gains `deleted()` and `EntityDocument.deleted(ref, provenance)`; the old three-argument
    constructor stays, so every plugin compiles unchanged and a plugin that never deletes needs nothing. Listeners that
    do not care skip deleted documents (the alert engine does).
  - **`HitIndex.remove(ref)`:** a cheap removal at any size (dropped from the pending list, or marked removed and folded
    out every 4,096 removals). `MessageStateSource` uses it instead of rebuilding the whole type-ahead index on the
    consumer thread for every delete; it also forgets a deleted entity's cache weight. The Kafka connector also clears
    an envelope-deleted entity's disk-cache entry at once.
  - **Tests:** the Kafka plugin (both message shapes, type-ahead, re-creation), the message-queue contract run against
    ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ in Docker, `HitIndex` removal (a million entities), the server's SSE stream with an embedded
    Kafka (`deleted` then `restored`), the mailbox's merge order, and `live.js` run under Node.
- **A scale benchmark for every store** ([BENCHMARK.md section 9](docs/admin/BENCHMARK.md#9-the-stores-compared-10000-to-50000-trades-a-day)). `tools/bench/scale.sh
  <store> <trades-a-day>` starts the store (a container for PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis and Aerospike, capped in memory),
  loads it with the project's loader, starts a server with the store's profile, measures over HTTP with
  `tools/bench/measure.py` (median and p95 of 25 requests, requests per second with 8 clients, load time, size, start,
  live heap after a full GC, and that every search is exact) and removes everything; `tools/bench/report.py` turns the
  JSON lines into tables with a linear fit per measure and its value at a million trades a day, labelled as an
  extrapolation. Run on 2026-10-01 for Delta Lake (native), PostgreSQL, DuckDB, files, MongoDB, Redis, Aerospike and
  Iceberg at 10,000, 25,000 and 50,000 trades a day over three days (raw results in
  `tools/bench/results/2026-10-01.jsonl`); every search exact. Each connector document's measured results gain the
  curve; the earlier million-trade measurements (Delta Lake, PostgreSQL, Aerospike, Redis) are kept with their date, and
  the other stores' million figures are now labelled extrapolations or estimates.
  - **Fixed: Redis lost the last partial chunk of a day's columns.** The loader counted chunks with Java's truncating
    division, so a day whose size was not a multiple of 10,000 (25,000 trades: two chunks, not three) was written short,
    and every search on it read documents. `DayColumns.chunks` uses `Math.ceilDiv` (`DayColumnsTest`); the Aerospike
    scan's partition ranges use it too (more than 4,096 `scan-threads` looped forever).
- **A library of Calc snippets for the banking packs, and `drishti.quant`** ([PYTHON_CALC.md › Snippet catalogue](docs/guides/USER_GUIDE.md#18-snippet-catalogue)).

  structures), vol surfaces (calendar and butterfly arbitrage checks, SVI fits), equities and commodities (realised

    Kupiec, drawdown, Sharpe, HHI, hazard rates, survival, CVA and the FRTB aggregation formulas. The worker fetches it

- **The Pivot tab: an Excel-style pivot, only where a Sutra or pack asks for it**

- **Delta Lake without Hadoop; Drishti on Windows** ([DELTA_CONNECTOR.md › Engines](plugins/drishti-plugin-delta/README.md#engines-native-and-hadoop),
  [WINDOWS.md](docs/guides/OPERATIONS_GUIDE.md#4-drishti-on-windows)). A new module, `drishti-deltalake`, is a Delta Kernel engine (`NativeEngine`)
  that never touches Hadoop's file systems: local lakes through `java.nio` (drive letters, backslashes and UNC shares),
  S3 through the AWS SDK v2, Parquet through parquet-java over its own input files (row groups pruned by statistics
  for `id = X`, only the asked columns decoded, its own Snappy/ZSTD/GZIP page codecs, no Hadoop `Configuration`), commit
  JSON and expressions through Kernel's Hadoop-free handlers; checkpoints, time travel and deletion vectors read as
  before. It only reads.
  - **The Delta connector's `engine` setting:** `native` (the default), `hadoop` (Kernel's default engine; also
    `abfs://`, `gs://`, HDFS) or `auto` (native on Windows); `DRISHTI_DELTA_ENGINE` sets it for every connector.
    Health says `UP (engine: native)`; the cache stats carry `engine`.
  - **Tests:** every Delta test runs on both engines (the dated-source contract, the layout, S3 in Docker, a maintained
    lake), plus a comparison of both engines' documents, id maps, columns, reverse lookups and time travel; deletion
    vectors written by the protocol; and the connector run in a class loader that refuses Hadoop's `FileSystem`,
    `Shell` and `Configuration`. Measured on a 10,000-trade lake, the native engine matches Hadoop's (a single read
    4.4 ms against 5.6 ms median; a cold id map 225 ms against 190–285 ms).
  - **Windows:** `tools/windows/start-server.ps1`, `start-console.ps1`, `load-delta.ps1`; a `windows` GitHub Actions
    job (windows-latest, Temurin 25) that runs the engine's, the connector's and the server's tests and checks a view,
    a search and a past date on a running server. Iceberg stays on Hadoop and is not supported on Windows (it is off
    unless the `iceberg` profile is used).
  - `DatedSourceContract` accepts a health of `UP (detail)`, as the server always has.
- **Layout mode: arrange a view your way** ([USER_GUIDE.md](docs/guides/USER_GUIDE.md#layout-mode-arrange-a-view-your-way)).
  `Alt+L` (or the footer's **Layout** key) turns a view into a 12-column grid per column: drag a panel by its heading
  to another place or the other column (a dashed placeholder shows where it lands), drag its right edge for its width
  in columns and its bottom edge for its height in rows, hide it and show it again, reset to the Sutra's layout. Pointer
  Events, so mouse, pen and touch alike; no drag library. Every move has a key (`↑` `↓` move, `←` `→` main or side
  column, `Shift`+arrows size, `H` hide, `A` natural height), each announced to screen readers; `Esc` cancels,
  `Ctrl+Enter` saves.
  - **Personal layouts:** saved per user and Sutra (and the kind it lays out) as an overlay (order, column, `span`,
    `height`, `hidden`), never changing the Sutra: `/api/v1/me/layouts/**` in `drishti_preference` (namespace `layouts`,
    at most 50), validated against the Sutra's panels; when the Sutra changes, removed panels are dropped and new ones
    appended. The console applies a layout when it draws the user's view (screen, print and workspace panes alike; the
    server's view, live updates, exports and the API stay the Sutra's), and live updates keep the user's sizes.
  - **Promote to Sutra:** an author turns their layout into the next version of the Sutra, written from its text (order,
    `area: right`, `span`, `height`; comments and every other key kept), shown as the changes in words and a diff,
    optionally without the hidden panels, and proposed through review like a Studio save. A review of a new version now
    shows the diff against the version before it (`previousText`).
  - **Rachana:** two optional keys every panel takes, `span` (1-12 columns of the grid) and `height` (1-24 rows of
    2.5 rem), with problem code `DRS-2030`; in the JSON Schema, Studio's completion and checking, and the view model
    (`PanelView.span`, `.height`; `provenance.sutra` names the Sutra). Not `rows`, which already names a panel's data.
  - **A role power, `layout`:** on for every role unless it says `layout: false`; the bundled `viewer` does not have it.
    Admin → Roles has a tick box (*Customise layouts*, ticked for a new role); kept as a `no-layout` row in
    `drishti_role_power` so existing roles keep the default. Without it the key is greyed with the reason and the
    endpoints answer `403`. `drishti.layouts.enabled` / `layouts.enabled` (`DRISHTI_LAYOUTS_ENABLED`) switch it off.
- **Workspaces: drag and drop, and dividers** ([workspaces guide](docs/guides/USER_GUIDE.md#workspaces)). Drag a suggestion
  (or a recent view) from the command line onto a pane, or a pane's number onto another pane, to show that view there;
  drag the dividers between columns and rows (or move them with the arrow keys) to resize the panes. Workspaces keep
  their `sizes` (`{"cols": [...], "rows": [...]}`, validated per layout).
- **Fixed:** a view in a workspace pane threw a script error when it loaded its notes (the notes count is not shown in
  panes).
- **Calc: Python on any view** ([PYTHON_CALC.md](docs/guides/USER_GUIDE.md#calc-python-on-any-view)). `Alt+C` opens a drawer like F9's with a
  Python editor (CodeMirror, Python mode), Run (`Ctrl+Enter`), Stop, the output and a history of runs. The code runs in
  the browser, in Pyodide 314.0.7 (CPython 3.14 on WebAssembly) inside a Web Worker, with numpy, pandas, scipy,
  statsmodels and matplotlib; nothing runs on the server.
  - **The `drishti` module:** `view` (the screen: `doc`, `tables` as DataFrames for every panel that holds rows,
    `panels`, `business_date`), `get`, `search`, `columns` (whole columns of a day) and `history`, each an ordinary read
    with the user's session (roles and masking apply), with `_async` forms for browsers without JavaScript Promise
    Integration; `show()` (tables paged like Drishti's), `chart()` (ECharts in the theme), matplotlib figures as PNG;
    output capped per run.
  - **Packs opt in:** `python: { enabled: true, snippets: [...] }` in `pack.yaml` and `python/*.py` files; the server's
    pack model reads them and `/packs` carries them. The five banking packs ship starters (rate shift on a trade, MTM
    concentration on netting sets and counterparties, VaR and ES from the scenario P&L, a desk's P&L pivot, curve
    interpolation), generated from `tools/packgen/banking/calc_snippets.py`; `finance` has two inline ones.
  - **A role power, `calc`:** granted to `author`, `approver`, `admin` and the analysts' roles of the packs that offer
    Calc (`trader`, `risk`, `market-risk`, `credit-risk`), not to `viewer`; Admin → Roles has a tick box. Kept in a new
    table, `drishti_role_power`, created at start on existing databases.
  - **Server:** `GET /api/v1/calc/settings`, the user's snippets (`/api/v1/me/calc-snippets`, at most 50, in
    `drishti_preference`), and `GET /api/v1/search/columns/{kind}?paths=` (a day's promoted columns, redacted as a search,
    access-logged); `drishti.calc.*` settings.
  - **The runtime is not in git:** `tools/fetch-pyodide.sh` downloads the pinned release once, checks its SHA-256 and
    keeps only what Calc needs (53 MB); the console serves it at `/pyodide/<version>/` (cached for good), the console
